Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Minimum Ignition Timing (Coolant)
table.description:
Lowest timing the ECU will fire, by coolant temperature, used with the pedal pressed and the throttle between about 3 % and 46 % open; otherwise Minimum Ignition Timing applies. Lowering it allows more retard.
Details: 0x0D9E40 (read): floor for final timing FFF8A744, looked up from coolant FFF88A44 while the accelerator is pressed (FFF886AB bit 5 clear) and the throttle opening FFF8CD74 (706 = 100 %, Phase 17) lies within cal 0x2FC6C (20, about 2.8 %)... cal 0x2FC6A (328, about 46 %) (0x0D9EC0-0x0D9ED4); otherwise the floor is Minimum Ignition Timing. Confidence: read.

table.name: Minimum Ignition Timing
table.description:
Lowest timing the ECU will ever fire when Minimum Ignition Timing (Coolant) does not apply. Final timing is never allowed below this.
Details: 0x0D9E40 (read): the timing floor used outside the coolant-table conditions. Confidence: read.

table.name: Ignition Dwell Time
table.description:
Coil charge (dwell) time in milliseconds by rpm and battery voltage, used whenever the engine runs. More dwell gives a stronger spark but heats the coils.
Details: When used: always while running. 0x0DC960 (read): FFF8A762 = this(rpm FFF8CD54, battery FFF9DD61); FFF8A762 is passed to the ignition output layer (0x1DB782 -> FFF8D0C6, used by the timer D compare scheduling in 0x1DBD94) and converted by 0x0DC88C into the dwell angle FFF8A761 = x x rpm >> 12 (+ cal 0x37E46 briefly after a fuel-mode change, clamped cal 0x2FC7F..0x2FC7E; fixed cal 0x2FC80 in engine state 2) (read). Falls with battery voltage, as a coil dwell does (inferred). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Base Timing IAT Compensation
table.description:
Timing added (negative = retard) for hot intake air, by intake air temperature, scaled by Base Timing IAT Compensation Multiplier. Applied once the engine is running above about 800 rpm and feeds into base timing.
Details: When used: FFF8A782 = rate-limited (cals 0x32DE2/0x32DE4 = 65535, i.e. none) value, enabled once FFF8CD5C >= cal 0x37F9E (800 rpm) in running mode FFF8866C = 3 (0x0E0184, read; cal 0x239AE bit 3 clear, so the knock-limit min() is not applied). FFF8A782 is added to the torque-model base timing FFF8A645 (0x0C2C08, A-D path with FFF8A787; E/F path with FFF8A788; my research notes, Ghidra stack args) and to the timing request FFF8A78A/FFF8B10E -> FFF8A789 (0x0E0A30, register args, read), which becomes the spark target FFF8A72A (0x0D9088). It is not a separate term of the final timing sum FFF8A744, but it reaches the fired timing through FFF8A645 (FFF8A645 -> FFF8A76A -> FFF8A76D -> FFF8A74B -> FFF8A744, 0x0DD568 / 0x0DD760 / 0x0DA600 / 0x0D9E40, read). Value = this(IAT FFF88A48) x Base Timing IAT Compensation Multiplier(rpm, load) / 128 (read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing IAT Compensation Multiplier
table.description:
Scales Base Timing IAT Compensation by rpm and load: 0 = no intake-temperature timing correction, 1.0 = the full amount.
Details: When used: multiplies Base Timing IAT Compensation, /128 (0x0E0184, read). FFF8A782 = rate-limited (cals 0x32DE2/0x32DE4 = 65535, i.e. none) value, enabled once FFF8CD5C >= cal 0x37F9E (800 rpm) in running mode FFF8866C = 3 (0x0E0184, read; cal 0x239AE bit 3 clear, so the knock-limit min() is not applied). FFF8A782 is added to the torque-model base timing FFF8A645 (0x0C2C08, A-D path with FFF8A787; E/F path with FFF8A788; my research notes, Ghidra stack args) and to the timing request FFF8A78A/FFF8B10E -> FFF8A789 (0x0E0A30, register args, read), which becomes the spark target FFF8A72A (0x0D9088). It is not a separate term of the final timing sum FFF8A744, but it reaches the fired timing through FFF8A645 (FFF8A645 -> FFF8A76A -> FFF8A76D -> FFF8A74B -> FFF8A744, 0x0DD568 / 0x0DD760 / 0x0DA600 / 0x0D9E40, read). Axes rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing Coolant Compensation (TGV Open)
table.description:
Timing added to base timing on a cold engine, by coolant temperature, for the TGV-open side; scaled by Base Timing Coolant Compensation Weight (TGV Open) and blended with the TGV Closed table by how far the TGVs are open. Active above about 800 rpm.
Details: When used: TGV-open side, weighted by the TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 and Base Timing Coolant Compensation Weight (TGV Open). 0x0E0584 (read): in running mode FFF8866C = 3 and once FFF8CD5C >= cal 0x37F9E (800 rpm, latched) and load >= cal 0x38120, FFF8A787 = FFF8A765 (EGR term, 128 = none) + the compensation - 128. With cal 0x31E38 bit 0 set the compensation = [TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 x Weight (TGV Open)(rpm, load) x Comp (TGV Open)(coolant) + (1 - fraction) x 05BCF4(rpm, load; 100 % flat) x Comp (TGV Closed)(coolant)] x 0.1 x 0.01 degrees; with bit 0 clear the half-degree alternate tables are used instead. FFF8A787 is added to the torque-model base timing FFF8A645 (0x0C2C08, A-D path) and the timing request (0x0E0A30) (read); it is not a separate term of the final timing sum FFF8A744 but reaches it through FFF8A645 (0x0DD568 / 0x0DD760 / 0x0DA600, read), and FFF8A787 <= 0 is one of the conditions for the fixed closed-pedal timing in 0x0D9E40. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing Coolant Compensation (TGV Closed)
table.description:
Timing added to base timing on a cold engine, by coolant temperature, for the TGV-closed side, blended with the TGV Open table by how far the TGVs are open. Active above about 800 rpm. Keep consistent with Base Timing Coolant Compensation (TGV Open).
Details: When used: TGV-closed side. 0x0E0584 (read): in running mode FFF8866C = 3 and once FFF8CD5C >= cal 0x37F9E (800 rpm, latched) and load >= cal 0x38120, FFF8A787 = FFF8A765 (EGR term, 128 = none) + the compensation - 128. With cal 0x31E38 bit 0 set the compensation = [TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 x Weight (TGV Open)(rpm, load) x Comp (TGV Open)(coolant) + (1 - fraction) x 05BCF4(rpm, load; 100 % flat) x Comp (TGV Closed)(coolant)] x 0.1 x 0.01 degrees; with bit 0 clear the half-degree alternate tables are used instead. FFF8A787 is added to the torque-model base timing FFF8A645 (0x0C2C08, A-D path) and the timing request (0x0E0A30) (read); it is not a separate term of the final timing sum FFF8A744 but reaches it through FFF8A645 (0x0DD568 / 0x0DD760 / 0x0DA600, read), and FFF8A787 <= 0 is one of the conditions for the fixed closed-pedal timing in 0x0D9E40. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing Coolant Compensation Weight (TGV Open)
table.description:
Percentage (by rpm and load) of Base Timing Coolant Compensation (TGV Open) actually applied. Lower values reduce the cold-engine timing correction in that area.
Details: When used: percentage applied to Base Timing Coolant Compensation (TGV Open). 0x0E0584 (read): in running mode FFF8866C = 3 and once FFF8CD5C >= cal 0x37F9E (800 rpm, latched) and load >= cal 0x38120, FFF8A787 = FFF8A765 (EGR term, 128 = none) + the compensation - 128. With cal 0x31E38 bit 0 set the compensation = [TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 x Weight (TGV Open)(rpm, load) x Comp (TGV Open)(coolant) + (1 - fraction) x 05BCF4(rpm, load; 100 % flat) x Comp (TGV Closed)(coolant)] x 0.1 x 0.01 degrees; with bit 0 clear the half-degree alternate tables are used instead. FFF8A787 is added to the torque-model base timing FFF8A645 (0x0C2C08, A-D path) and the timing request (0x0E0A30) (read); it is not a separate term of the final timing sum FFF8A744 but reaches it through FFF8A645 (0x0DD568 / 0x0DD760 / 0x0DA600, read), and FFF8A787 <= 0 is one of the conditions for the fixed closed-pedal timing in 0x0D9E40. Axes FFF8CD5C (rpm/25) x load FFF8A616. Confidence: read.

table.name: Timing Request Enrichment Retard
table.description:
Retard ramped into the timing request while open-loop power enrichment is active, by load and rpm. The ECU fires the lower of Base Timing and request + knock advance.
Details: When used: 0x0E0910 (read; my research notes section 5): while FFF8A655 bit 0 is set, or the open-loop enrichment FFF8A684 is between 1 and FFF8A681, and FFF8A8A3 bit 6 / FFF8A8A4 bit 7 are clear, FFF84848 ramps toward (this - 128) x 64 at cal 0x3107C (4) per pass and back to 0 at cal 0x3107E otherwise; FFF8A77A = FFF84848/64 + 128 is added to the timing request: FFF8A789 = FFF8B10E + FFF8A77A + cal 0x23CE6 - 256 (read). FFF8A789 becomes the normal-mode spark target FFF8A72A (0x0D9088) and is the request side of the P050B monitor; it is not a term of the final timing sum 0x0D9E40, but it lowers the request side of the fired-timing limit (0x0C13B4 -> FFF8AF22 -> 0x0C39DC / 0x0DD568: fired base = min(Base Timing + comps, request + KCA + FLKC); read, min() form computed), so it retards the spark at the coil wherever the request is the lower side. Axes load FFF8A616 (50/100/150 %) x rpm FFF8CD54. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing Coolant Compensation (Alternate, Below 5000 RPM)
table.description:
Alternate cold-engine timing correction by coolant temperature, used below 5000 rpm only when a calibration switch selects the alternate tables.
Details: When used: only with cal 0x31E38 bit 0 clear, below 5000 rpm (FFF8CD5C < cal 0x38122 = 200, hysteresis to 192). 0x0E0584 (read): in running mode FFF8866C = 3 and once FFF8CD5C >= cal 0x37F9E (800 rpm, latched) and load >= cal 0x38120, FFF8A787 = FFF8A765 (EGR term, 128 = none) + the compensation - 128. With cal 0x31E38 bit 0 set the compensation = [TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 x Weight (TGV Open)(rpm, load) x Comp (TGV Open)(coolant) + (1 - fraction) x 05BCF4(rpm, load; 100 % flat) x Comp (TGV Closed)(coolant)] x 0.1 x 0.01 degrees; with bit 0 clear the half-degree alternate tables are used instead. FFF8A787 is added to the torque-model base timing FFF8A645 (0x0C2C08, A-D path) and the timing request (0x0E0A30) (read); but FFF8A787 <= 0 is one of the conditions for the fixed closed-pedal timing in 0x0D9E40. Confidence: read.

table.name: Filtered RPM Rate Timing Term
table.description:
Timing added or removed according to how fast engine speed is changing, which looks like an rpm-oscillation (surge) damper.
0x0DB888 (called from 0x0DF0B8 with FFF8AA85 bit 1 and FFF8A8A1 bit 7, read): while FFF8AA85 bit 1 is set (set by 0x07FA1A when the surge damping trigger FFF8A7A1 bit 2 and FFF8A8A2 bit 6 are clear, the request is not being shaped (FFF8AEC2 <= FFF8AEBE), FFF8CEC1 bits 0-4 (rpm and load window flags) are set, speed >= cal 0x57576, gear FFF8A621 within cals 0x57577..0x57578, and FFF886AB bit 7 or FFF8A88F), FFF8A757 = clamp((this(FFF88CA4) + cal 0x2FEDE (s8 -3) x (rpm k passes ago - filtered rpm k passes ago) >> 7) x 100 >> 8, cal 0x2FEDD.. cal 0x2FEDC); k = 05B784/05B790(gear FFF8A621) + 1 (both all 0, so k = 1); rpm history FFF88CAC.. and the filtered-rpm history FFF88CC8.. (FFF8CE9A, a second lag of FFF8CEB2) (read). A757 is added to the base timing sum FFF8A74B (0x0DA600, read). Axis: FFF88CA4 = change of the lag-filtered rpm FFF8CEB2 between passes of 0x07E96C (read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Knock Correction Advance Max A (TGV Open)
table.description:
First part of the knock correction advance (timing added as DAM rises), by rpm and load, for TGVs open; blended with the TGV Closed table and scaled by KCA DAM Curve A. It is added to the Primary Ignition request, not to the Base Timing map: the ECU fires the lower of Base Timing and Primary + knock advance + fine learning, so raising it adds timing only where that sum is still below Base Timing.
Details: Knock correction advance (0x0E71FC and 0x0E1FD8, read). Two components, A and B, are each looked up by rpm (FFF8CD54) x load (FFF8ADE4) and blended by the TGV open fraction v = FFF8B3E8: A = 05C078 x (1 - v) + 05C08C x v (FFF8A7A4), B = 05C0A0 x (1 - v) + 05C0B4 x v (FFF8A7A6), and the maximum FFF8A7A5 = A + B (capped at 255). With cal 0x35509 bit 0 set (it is, in both images) the applied advance FFF8A791 = (A x KCA DAM Curve A(DAM) + B x KCA DAM Curve B(DAM)) / 128; otherwise it is A7A5 x DAM / 16. One count = 0.3516 degrees (x 180 >> 8 in 0x0C13B4 / 0x0DB3D4, x 90 / 128 in 0x0D9088, read). Where it goes (read, knock routing review 2026-10-31): FFF8A791 is not a term of the fired-timing sum 0x0D9E40 (FBKC FFF8A79A is the only knock term there). It reaches the coil through the timing request: 0x0C13B4 (combustion modes FFF8A85C = 3/4, i.e. normal running) forms the request retard r = max(0, FFF8A645 - (FFF8A789 - 32 + (FFF8A791 + FLKC FFF8A7A7) x 180 / 256)) and FFF8AF22 = Ignition Efficiency vs Retard(r); 0x0C39DC folds AF22 (times the torque-cap ratio) into FFF8A64B, and 0x0DD568 sets the spark angle FFF8A76A = FFF8A645 - Torque Reduction Spark Retard(max(A64B, 102) x 128) - tip-in retard (AF22 >> 7 directly with the pedal released or a cylinder cut active). Torque Reduction Spark Retard is the exact inverse of Ignition Efficiency vs Retard, so in effect FFF8A76A = min(base timing FFF8A645, timing request + KCA + FLKC) less any torque-reduction retard; it then rate-limits (0x0DD760) into the base sum FFF8A74B (0x0DA600) and the fired timing FFF8A744 (min() form computed from the inverse tables). In limit states FFF8A639 = 0x0B/0x0C/0x19/0x1A/0x1B the spark target FFF8A72A (0x0D9088: request + 0.3516 deg x (A791 + A7A7) with the pedal pressed) replaces FFF8A645 outright. The total FFF8A77B (0x0DFA88) has one reader, 0x0DDBBC, and the headroom term of 0x0DB3D4 (A7A5 - A791 into FFF8A754) is capped at cal 0x2FEC2 = 0. So the advance is fired only where Primary Ignition (+ compensations + EGR Timing Advance) + KCA + FLKC is below the Base Timing map; it can never lift the fired timing above Base Timing. Component A, TGVs open (weight v). Confidence: read.

table.name: FBKC Maximum Retard
table.description:
Largest amount of timing feedback knock correction can pull. The live knock retard never goes below minus this value, and it applies to all cylinders at once. Raising it allows more protective retard.
Details: Feedback knock correction (0x0E2BE4, read): FFF8A79A is an s8 integrator kept at or below 0 and added directly to the fired timing (x 0.3516 degrees, 0x0D9E40): it is the only knock term of that sum, and FFF8A79A is one value for the whole engine, so a knock event on any cylinder retards all four (the fired timing FFF8A744 is recomputed per event for the next cylinder, but no per-cylinder knock retard exists; read). The state FFF8A79C (set once per combustion event by 0x0E2F94 from that event's knock results FFF8A7AD / FFF8A7B5; FFF8A7C1 is the knock-window-length flag (1 = extended window), used there only to reload per-cylinder hold counters FFF84920...FFF84930 from cal 0x27014 when it changes, purpose inferred) picks the action: states 0x0E, 0x0D, 7 and 6 subtract a step (floor = minus FBKC Maximum Retard); states 0x0C, 2, 0 (outside the rpm window) and the other non-knock states (0x0A outside the window, 0x0B) add the recovery step 0x1C271; 0x10 (inside the rpm window, no knock, fewer than cal 0x1C288 = 100 events since the last knock) holds the correction unchanged; 0x0F (inside the window, no knock, >= 100 events) adds 0x1C270, 8/9 add 0x1C272 (capped at 0); 5 = FFF8A79B x 0x1C26E / 128; 3 and 4 load the fixed values 0x1C26F / 0x1C278; 1 = 0. States (0x0E2F94, read, in priority order): 1 = knock control off (cal 0x56EE7 bit 7); 2 = FFF886AB bit 5 or load FFF8ADE4 <= cal 0x1C27E (0); 3 / 4 = FFF88E29 bit 3 / FFF88E2A bit 6 (fixed -14 counts = -4.9 degrees, inferred knock-sensor fault default); 5 = engine speed above FBKC Window RPM Maximum (hold); inside the rpm window: 6 / 0x0D = knock A with / without FFF8AA85 bit 0, 7 / 0x0E = knock B (FFF8A7B5, intensity > Knock Threshold, the active one); 0x0F = no knock and FFF8B130 (events since the last knock, 0x0E7C7C) >= cal 0x1C288 (100), 0x10 = no knock, fewer events; 8 / 9 hold; 0x0A / 0x0B / 0x0C other conditions (0x0B: A/F FFF88AF6 above a lambda threshold). This is the floor: the integrator never goes below minus this value. Confidence: read.

table.name: FBKC Window RPM Maximum
table.description:
Upper rpm limit for feedback knock correction. Above it the current knock retard is held: no new retard and no recovery. Raise this if you raise the rev limit.
Details: 0x0E8128 / 0x0E2F94 (read): upper end of the FBKC working range. While rpm FFF8CE9C is above this (with hysteresis cal 0x1C27C), FFF8A7AE is clear and FBKC goes to state 5, which holds the current correction (x cal 0x1C26E / 128 = 1.0): no new knock retard and no recovery. Inside the window (FBKC Window RPM Minimum...this, and FFF8A7AF set) the knock retard states 0x0D/0x0E, the hold state 0x10 (no knock, fewer than 100 events since the last knock) and the recovery state 0x0F are used. Confidence: read.

table.name: FBKC Window RPM Minimum
table.description:
Lower rpm limit for feedback knock correction: below it no new knock retard is taken, and any existing knock retard is given back by FBKC Recovery Step each combustion event.
Details: Lower end of the FBKC working range: below it no knock retard or recovery steps are taken (see FBKC Window RPM Maximum). 0x0E2BE4 (read): the second window flag is true while rpm FFF8CE9C >= this (once true, it stays until rpm < this - 0x1C286). Confidence: read.

table.name: DAM Step Gain (FLKC Cell)

scaling.units: FLKC cell (5 x rpm range + load range)

table.description:
How strongly each fine-knock-learning step moves DAM, per FLKC learning cell (index = 5 x rpm range + load range, 0-34; index 0 is the lowest rpm and load cell). Larger values make DAM move faster when the ECU learns knock in that cell; 0 means that cell never moves DAM. Purpose is inferred.
Details: When used: every combustion event while the DAM state FFF8A7AA is 8 (0x0E7AEC: FFF8A7CF set and no other state applies, read). 0x0E792C (read): DAM x 256 += this(FLKC cell FFF8A790) x FFF8A799 x 90 >> 16, clamped 0..256 (DAM 0..1); FFF8A799 is the signed step chosen by the FLKC state (-23/-24/-14 in states 8/9/10, +6/+3 in states 5/6, 0x0E2ABC). So DAM moves by this x step count; a larger value makes DAM react more to learning in that cell. Index = FLKC cell FFF8A790 = 5 x rpm range + load range, 0..34 (0x0E1C58, read; 0x0E1F90 reads the learned value FFF81414[A790]), so index 0 is the lowest rpm / lowest load cell and is used. With the -23 step of state 8 that is -0.10..-0.24 DAM per step (computed). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: FLKC Advance Learning Inhibit Zones

scaling.units: zone index (5 x rpm band + load band)

table.description:
Per rpm/load zone switch: 1 stops fine knock learning from learning timing back upward there, so it can only learn retard (inferred). These zones use their own rpm/load boundaries, not the FLKC cell boundaries.
Details: When used: every combustion event (0x0E74B0 <- 0x0E402C <- 0x07D0E0, crank task, read). Zone index FFF8A7A8 = 5 x rpm band + load band: rpm bands <=2100, 2100-3000, 3000-3400, 3400-3800, 3800-4300, 4300-8000, >8000 rpm (FFF8CE9C, cals 0x26FBC..0x26FC6, hysteresis cal 0x26FC8 = 50 rpm); load bands <=1.42, 1.42-1.68, 1.68-1.94, 1.94-2.20, >2.20 g/rev (<=110, 110-130, 130-150, 150-170, >170 %) (FFF8ADE4, cals 0x26FB2..0x26FB8, hysteresis cal 0x26FBA = 2.5 %) (read). FFF8A7A9 = this(zone). With 1 the fine-learning state machine 0x0E1A38 cannot enter states 4-7, which include the positive learning steps (FFF8A799 = +cal 0x1C269 / 0x1C268 in states 5/6, 0x0E2ABC), and 0x0E9970 sets the latch FFF8A7D0 (read). So in the flagged zones FLKC learns only downward (inferred from the step signs). Zone boundaries differ from the FLKC cell boundaries. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: FLKC Range Boundary Load 1
table.description:
One of the four load boundaries that split fine learning knock correction (FLKC) into load ranges; each learning cell covers one rpm range by one load range. Moving it changes which conditions share a learned correction. Keep them in increasing order.
Details: Fine learning knock correction cells (0x0E1C58, read): the cell FFF8A790 = 5 x rpm range + load range (0...34). Seven rpm ranges are split at the six boundaries 0x1C24A...0x1C254 on FFF8CE9C, five load ranges at the four boundaries 0x1C240...0x1C246 on FFF8ADE4, each with a hysteresis band (0x1C256 rpm, 0x1C248 load). The learned value for the cell is FFF81414[cell] (s16, x 256); 0x0E73CC applies FFF8A7A7 = min(that, KCA Max x (16 - DAM) x 16) / 256, in 0.3516 degree counts; it is not added to the fired timing directly: like KCA it enters the timing request (0x0C13B4 -> FFF8AF22 -> 0x0C39DC / 0x0DD568), so fired base timing = min(Base Timing + comps, request + KCA + FLKC), and in limit states 0x0B/0x0C/0x19/0x1A/0x1B through the spark target FFF8A72A (0x0D9088). A negative learned value therefore retards the spark only where the request side is the lower one; where Base Timing is lower it is hidden until it pulls the request below Base Timing. Feedback knock correction is the only knock term added directly (0x0D9E40). load boundary. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend (DAM 0)
table.description:
Timing offset added to base timing only at high pedal, blended by DAM with Base Timing DAM Blend (DAM 1); this table applies at DAM 0. 32 = no change, 0.5-degree steps. Not the knock correction advance (renamed from Knock Correction Advance DAM 0/1).
Details: When used: only while the AVCS high-pedal latch FFF8A8A4 bit 7 (0x11C15C) is set; otherwise the blend is 32 = no change (0x0DA600, caller 0x0DF0B8, read). 0x0DA600 blends this table with its pair, weighted (16 - w)/16 where w = FFF811AE (FFF8B128 >> 4, a 0..256 learned value stepped up and down by the knock-learning logic at 0x0E792C: DAM x 256, inferred). The blend is added to the base timing sum FFF8A74B. Base Timing DAM Blend B uses the other high-pedal latch, FFF8A8A4 bit 6 (0x11C0C4, the one that selects Injection Timing (High Pedal)). Not the knock correction advance itself: that is Knock Correction Advance Max A/B with the KCA DAM curves (0x0E1FD8, read). Renamed from "Knock Correction Advance (DAM 0/1)". Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend B (DAM 0)
table.description:
Timing offset added to base timing in a high-pedal, enrichment-limited condition in one combustion mode, blended with Base Timing DAM Blend B (DAM 1) by DAM; this table applies at DAM 0. 32 = no change, 0.5-degree steps.
Details: When used: while FFF8A8A3 bit 6 is set; weight (16 - DAM)/16 (the DAM 0 table). 0x0D9D48 (per combustion event, from 0x0DF0B8) blends the two tables by DAM FFF811AE (0..16): FFF8A741 = (DAM 1 table x DAM + DAM 0 table x (16 - DAM))/16, 32 = no change; then 0x0D9B28 sets FFF8A73C = FFF8A741 when FFF8A8A3 bit 6 is set, else 32, and 0x0DA600 adds FFF8A73C - 32 (0.5-degree units) to the base timing sum FFF8A74B (read). FFF8A8A3 bit 6 (0x11C04C, read) = combustion mode FFF8A85C = 4, coolant within cal 0x36502..0x36500 (all), DAM >= cal 0x364FE (0). Axes rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4 (same as Base Timing DAM Blend). Confidence: read.

table.name: FBKC Retard Step (Secondary Knock, State 0x0D)
table.description:
Timing pulled per event by feedback knock correction when the secondary knock detector fires.
Details: Feedback knock correction (0x0E2BE4, read): FFF8A79A is an s8 integrator kept at or below 0 and added directly to the fired timing (x 0.3516 degrees, 0x0D9E40): it is the only knock term of that sum, and FFF8A79A is one value for the whole engine, so a knock event on any cylinder retards all four (the fired timing FFF8A744 is recomputed per event for the next cylinder, but no per-cylinder knock retard exists; read). The state FFF8A79C (set once per combustion event by 0x0E2F94 from that event's knock results FFF8A7AD / FFF8A7B5; FFF8A7C1 is the knock-window-length flag (1 = extended window), used there only to reload per-cylinder hold counters FFF84920...FFF84930 from cal 0x27014 when it changes, purpose inferred) picks the action: states 0x0E, 0x0D, 7 and 6 subtract a step (floor = minus FBKC Maximum Retard); states 0x0C, 2, 0 (outside the rpm window) and the other non-knock states (0x0A outside the window, 0x0B) add the recovery step 0x1C271; 0x10 (inside the rpm window, no knock, fewer than cal 0x1C288 = 100 events since the last knock) holds the correction unchanged; 0x0F (inside the window, no knock, >= 100 events) adds 0x1C270, 8/9 add 0x1C272 (capped at 0); 5 = FFF8A79B x 0x1C26E / 128; 3 and 4 load the fixed values 0x1C26F / 0x1C278; 1 = 0. States (0x0E2F94, read, in priority order): 1 = knock control off (cal 0x56EE7 bit 7); 2 = FFF886AB bit 5 or load FFF8ADE4 <= cal 0x1C27E (0); 3 / 4 = FFF88E29 bit 3 / FFF88E2A bit 6 (fixed -14 counts = -4.9 degrees, inferred knock-sensor fault default); 5 = engine speed above FBKC Window RPM Maximum (hold); inside the rpm window: 6 / 0x0D = knock A with / without FFF8AA85 bit 0, 7 / 0x0E = knock B (FFF8A7B5, intensity > Knock Threshold, the active one); 0x0F = no knock and FFF8B130 (events since the last knock, 0x0E7C7C) >= cal 0x1C288 (100), 0x10 = no knock, fewer events; 8 / 9 hold; 0x0A / 0x0B / 0x0C other conditions (0x0B: A/F FFF88AF6 above a lambda threshold). Subtracted per pass in state 0x0D. p16 (read): the FBKC logic 0x0E2F94 (0x0E402C <- 0x07D0E0 <- 0x1E1CBC) is crank-synchronous: one pass per combustion event (180 deg CA, dispatched at tooth position 70 via the ATU-J0 software interrupt 0x0A7390), not per time. Confidence: read.

table.name: FLKC Counted-Cell Learned Value Threshold
table.description:
By DAM: a fine-knock-learning cell is counted when its learned value is at or above this, and the count sets an internal flag.
0x0E7DF8 (read): one cell per pass, it counts the FLKC cells whose flag FFF811AF[cell] is 1 and whose learned value FFF81414[cell] is at or above this(DAM FFF811AE); after all 35 cells the count goes to FFF8A792 and FFF8A7A3 bit 1 = count >= cal 0x1C699 (4). 0x0E7D0C (read) uses that bit only together with DAM inside cal 0x1C698..0x1C697 (32..48 in DAM x 16 units), which DAM (0..16) never reaches. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (DAM 0)
table.description:
Alternate DAM-blended timing offset (DAM 0 side) for base timing. 32 = no change.
Weighted (16 - DAM)/16. 0x0D9BD4 (read): FFF8A73F = ((16 - DAM) x 05B54C + DAM x 05B560) / 16 in the 32-offset half-degree frame, DAM = FFF811AE (0..16), tables by rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4. 0x0D9CA0: FFF8A73E = (A73F + FFF8A73B - 32) x FFF8B0D2 / 256 + 32, and FFF8A740 = A73E when FFF8A8A5 bit 4 is set, else A73D (the 05B574/05B588 path) (read). FFF8A73E/A73F have no other readers. With cal 0x32DEA = 'Z' the base timing term FFF8A73C would ramp toward A740 (cal 0x32DEC per pass) and enter the base timing sum FFF8A74B (0x0DA600). Confidence: read.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 1, Full Window)
table.description:
Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 1 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the extended (full) knock window is in use. Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 1 is has not been mapped.
Details: Knock decision (0x0E8654 / 0x0E80B4, read): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4) the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot] (output of the signal processing 0x0E51E4) is compared with two thresholds. Knock B, FFF8A7B5 = intensity > Knock Threshold (this family, FFF8C1CC[slot] by 0x0E77E0) or FFF8CDC4[slot] >= cal 0x1BD92 (65535, off). Knock A, FFF8A7AD = intensity > Secondary Knock Threshold (FFF8C1D4[slot] by 0x0E78E4). Each event also sets bits of FFF8A79D (0x10/0x20/0x30/0x40 by slot). Slot vs cylinder number not mapped. Knock Threshold (0x0E77E0, read): looked up by rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500) and load FFF8A616 for each event slot; set A (05C104/118/12C/140) while FFF8A7C1 = 0, i.e. the nominal (short) window; set B (05C154/168/17C/190) while A7C1 = 1, i.e. the extended window (0x0E77E0 at 0x0E7836-0x0E784A; flag polarity read in 0x0E20E0 at 0x0E21AA-0x0E21EC; corrected 2026-10-30, the earlier names had the two sets swapped). A higher value needs a larger knock signal to count as knock (less sensitive). Set B (extended / full window). Confidence: read.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 3, Short Window)
table.description:
Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 3 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the nominal (short) knock window is in use. Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 3 is has not been mapped.
Details: Knock decision (0x0E8654 / 0x0E80B4, read): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4) the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot] (output of the signal processing 0x0E51E4) is compared with two thresholds. Knock B, FFF8A7B5 = intensity > Knock Threshold (this family, FFF8C1CC[slot] by 0x0E77E0) or FFF8CDC4[slot] >= cal 0x1BD92 (65535, off). Knock A, FFF8A7AD = intensity > Secondary Knock Threshold (FFF8C1D4[slot] by 0x0E78E4). Each event also sets bits of FFF8A79D (0x10/0x20/0x30/0x40 by slot). Slot vs cylinder number not mapped. Knock Threshold (0x0E77E0, read): looked up by rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500) and load FFF8A616 for each event slot; set A (05C104/118/12C/140) while FFF8A7C1 = 0, i.e. the nominal (short) window; set B (05C154/168/17C/190) while A7C1 = 1, i.e. the extended window (0x0E77E0 at 0x0E7836-0x0E784A; flag polarity read in 0x0E20E0 at 0x0E21AA-0x0E21EC; corrected 2026-10-30, the earlier names had the two sets swapped). A higher value needs a larger knock signal to count as knock (less sensitive). Set A (nominal / short window). Confidence: read.

table.name: Secondary Knock Threshold (Event 1)
table.description:
Second knock detector level by rpm for event slot 1; a signal above it triggers the secondary knock retard steps. Unit: sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background (3.0 = all at background).
Details: Knock decision (0x0E8654 / 0x0E80B4, read): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4) the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot] (output of the signal processing 0x0E51E4) is compared with two thresholds. Knock B, FFF8A7B5 = intensity > Knock Threshold (this family, FFF8C1CC[slot] by 0x0E77E0) or FFF8CDC4[slot] >= cal 0x1BD92 (65535, off). Knock A, FFF8A7AD = intensity > Secondary Knock Threshold (FFF8C1D4[slot] by 0x0E78E4). Each event also sets bits of FFF8A79D (0x10/0x20/0x30/0x40 by slot). Slot vs cylinder number not mapped. 0x0E78E4 looks this 16-point curve up by FFF8CDC2 with the implicit-axis routine 0x7304 (0...240 in steps of 16 = 500...8,000 rpm, read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Knock Window Start
table.description:
Crank angle (probably degrees after top dead centre) at which the ECU starts listening for knock, by rpm; limited by Knock Window Start Minimum and Maximum.
Details: Knock window (0x0E2090 / 0x0E20E0, read): window start FFF8B118 = clamp(Knock Window Start(rpm), 0x1C210...0x1C212); nominal length FFF8B11C = Knock Window Length(rpm). The length used, FFF8B11A, is the nominal length plus Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 is at or below Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold (with hysteresis; MOVRT at 0x0E216E) and the extended window end (0x0E20E0 computes it from nominal + extension with the same formula 0x0E7CB0 uses for the window end FFF8A7AB) ends before the per-event angle FFF8C0E8 (built by 0x0E39C0 from FFF88860/FFF81478, inferred to be the next spark); if either fails the nominal length is used. Either way the length used is clamped to Knock Window Length Minimum...Maximum (0x1C1EC...0x1C1EE; 0x0E211E-0x0E2130 for the extended length, 0x0E21C0-0x0E21E8 for the nominal one, read). FFF8A7C1 / FFF8A7C2...C5 = 1 while the extended length is used (read, 0x0E20E0 at 0x0E21AA-0x0E21EC; corrected 2026-10-30). 0x0E7C00 / 0x0E7C24 scale start and length by FFF8CD46 into FFF8B12A / FFF8B12C for the window timer (1E5202, read). The rpm axis is FFF8CDC2 (rpm = x x 31.25 + 500, read). Degrees are crank degrees after the firing cylinder's TDC (reference inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: Knock Window Length
table.description:
Normal length of the knock listening window in crank degrees, by rpm; Knock Window Length Extension may be added at low timing.
Details: Knock window (0x0E2090 / 0x0E20E0, read): window start FFF8B118 = clamp(Knock Window Start(rpm), 0x1C210...0x1C212); nominal length FFF8B11C = Knock Window Length(rpm). The length used, FFF8B11A, is the nominal length plus Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 is at or below Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold (with hysteresis; MOVRT at 0x0E216E) and the extended window end (0x0E20E0 computes it from nominal + extension with the same formula 0x0E7CB0 uses for the window end FFF8A7AB) ends before the per-event angle FFF8C0E8 (built by 0x0E39C0 from FFF88860/FFF81478, inferred to be the next spark); if either fails the nominal length is used. Either way the length used is clamped to Knock Window Length Minimum...Maximum (0x1C1EC...0x1C1EE; 0x0E211E-0x0E2130 for the extended length, 0x0E21C0-0x0E21E8 for the nominal one, read). FFF8A7C1 / FFF8A7C2...C5 = 1 while the extended length is used (read, 0x0E20E0 at 0x0E21AA-0x0E21EC; corrected 2026-10-30). 0x0E7C00 / 0x0E7C24 scale start and length by FFF8CD46 into FFF8B12A / FFF8B12C for the window timer (1E5202, read). The rpm axis is FFF8CDC2 (rpm = x x 31.25 + 500, read). Degrees are crank degrees after the firing cylinder's TDC (reference inferred). Nominal length before the extension. Confidence: read.

table.name: Knock Window Overlap Margin (Event 1)
table.description:
For knock event slot 1, by rpm: how many degrees the knock window may run past the next event angle before the ECU flags an overlap, which changes how the knock signal background is adapted. Which cylinder slot 1 is has not been mapped.
Details: Knock window (0x0E2090 / 0x0E20E0, read): window start FFF8B118 = clamp(Knock Window Start(rpm), 0x1C210...0x1C212); nominal length FFF8B11C = Knock Window Length(rpm). The length used, FFF8B11A, is the nominal length plus Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 is at or below Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold (with hysteresis; MOVRT at 0x0E216E) and the extended window end (0x0E20E0 computes it from nominal + extension with the same formula 0x0E7CB0 uses for the window end FFF8A7AB) ends before the per-event angle FFF8C0E8 (built by 0x0E39C0 from FFF88860/FFF81478, inferred to be the next spark); if either fails the nominal length is used. Either way the length used is clamped to Knock Window Length Minimum...Maximum (0x1C1EC...0x1C1EE; 0x0E211E-0x0E2130 for the extended length, 0x0E21C0-0x0E21E8 for the nominal one, read). FFF8A7C1 / FFF8A7C2...C5 = 1 while the extended length is used (read, 0x0E20E0 at 0x0E21AA-0x0E21EC; corrected 2026-10-30). 0x0E7C00 / 0x0E7C24 scale start and length by FFF8CD46 into FFF8B12A / FFF8B12C for the window timer (1E5202, read). The rpm axis is FFF8CDC2 (rpm = x x 31.25 + 500, read). Degrees are crank degrees after the firing cylinder's TDC (reference inferred). 0x0E7328 loads this for event slot FFF8A798 = 1 into FFF8C1C8[0]; 0x0E9AF8-0x0E9C48 set the flag FFF8A7D2 when the window end passes the event angle by more than this many degrees (read). The flags feed the knock signal-processing block 0x0E4500 / 0x0E51E4: when a slot's flag changes while its window is nominal, 0x0E51E4 skips the background step and sets the background gain to the gain curve (flag 0 -> 1) or min(1024/gain, cal 0x26FAF) (1 -> 0) (read, Phase 18 review). Event slot vs cylinder number is not mapped. Confidence: read.

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 1, Channel 2)
table.description:
This software version (function 0x0D6B88, read against the longer version of the function): the table is the step only on the pass where the window flag sets. On the pass where it clears, the longer version subtracts the table; this one adds the fixed value at cal 0x026B6E instead (s16; the row for the event is Knock Background Clear Step (Event 1)).
Knock signal processing for event slot 1, channel 2 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock. Larger = that event less likely to count as knock. Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.
Details: When used: event slot FFF8CDC0 = 1 (Event 1), knock channel 2 of 8, on the knock window where FFF8A7C2 changes. Background step for this channel, added to (window extended) or subtracted from (window back to nominal) the channel background FFF8C180[1] for that one event; overlap-flag FFF8A7D2, gain curve cal 0x26F6F. Knock signal processing 0x0E51E4 (read; called once per knock window from 0x0E43B8 with load FFF8A616, after the event chain 0x0E433C): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4, the slot of the Knock Threshold tables) each of 8 knock channels i gets a reference ref_i = 32 x step_i + g x background_i, and the channel ratio is 256 x FFF8CDB0[i] / (ref_i / 32), i.e. measured / reference with 256 = equal (0x0E51E4 tail, read). Channels with their bit set in cal 0x1B97C..0x1B97F give 0; a channel flagged in FFF8CEED (driver flag, value at its lower limit, inferred) gives 256. The ratios are sorted and the largest min(cal 0x1B988, 5) = 3 are summed into the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot], which 0x0E80B4/0x0E8654 compare with Knock Threshold (read). The measured channels come from the knock sensor ADC: 0x1E7868 DMA-collects 32-sample blocks, 0x1E725A runs FFT-style butterflies, 0x1E73A4 takes sqrt(re^2+im^2) of 8 selected bins (pointer tables 0x34A88/0x34AA8), and 0x1E7724 sums them over the window into FFF8D1D4[8] -> FFF8CDB0[8] (read), so the 8 channels are 8 frequency bins of the knock sensor signal (inferred). background_i is the per-slot channel background FFF8C180.. (slot 1) / C190.. / C1A0.. / C1B0.. (slot 4), a lag filter of the measured channel kept by 0x0E4500 when the event is not knocking, floored at the per-channel rpm curve FFF8C0D8 (0x0E22A4) (read). step_i is this table family: it is non-zero only on the one event where the slot's window-length flag changes: +table when the flag goes 0 -> 1 (window switched to the extended length) and -table when it goes 1 -> 0 (back to the nominal length); on that event the reference is also floored at 32 x FFF8C0D8[i] (read). The flag is set when the extended knock window is used (0x0E20E0, read: B11A = nominal + Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 <= Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold and the extended window ends before the event angle). The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). Axes: rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500, 500-4000 rpm) x load FFF8A616 (read). Confidence: inferred.

On the pass where it clears, the longer version subtracts the table; this one adds the fixed value at cal 0x026B7E instead (s16; the row for the event is Knock Background Clear Step (Event 2)).
Knock signal processing for event slot 2, channel 2 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.
Details: When used: event slot FFF8CDC0 = 2 (Event 2), knock channel 2 of 8, on the knock window where FFF8A7C3 changes. Background step for this channel, added to (window extended) or subtracted from (window back to nominal) the channel background FFF8C190[1] for that one event; overlap-flag FFF8A7D3, gain curve cal 0x26F7F. Knock signal processing 0x0E51E4 (read; called once per knock window from 0x0E43B8 with load FFF8A616, after the event chain 0x0E433C): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4, the slot of the Knock Threshold tables) each of 8 knock channels i gets a reference ref_i = 32 x step_i + g x background_i, and the channel ratio is 256 x FFF8CDB0[i] / (ref_i / 32), i.e. measured / reference with 256 = equal (0x0E51E4 tail, read). Channels with their bit set in cal 0x1B97C..0x1B97F give 0; a channel flagged in FFF8CEED (driver flag, value at its lower limit, inferred) gives 256. The ratios are sorted and the largest min(cal 0x1B988, 5) = 3 are summed into the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot], which 0x0E80B4/0x0E8654 compare with Knock Threshold (read). The measured channels come from the knock sensor ADC: 0x1E7868 DMA-collects 32-sample blocks, 0x1E725A runs FFT-style butterflies, 0x1E73A4 takes sqrt(re^2+im^2) of 8 selected bins (pointer tables 0x34A88/0x34AA8), and 0x1E7724 sums them over the window into FFF8D1D4[8] -> FFF8CDB0[8] (read), so the 8 channels are 8 frequency bins of the knock sensor signal (inferred). background_i is the per-slot channel background FFF8C180.. (slot 1) / C190.. / C1A0.. / C1B0.. (slot 4), a lag filter of the measured channel kept by 0x0E4500 when the event is not knocking, floored at the per-channel rpm curve FFF8C0D8 (0x0E22A4) (read). step_i is this table family: it is non-zero only on the one event where the slot's window-length flag changes: +table when the flag goes 0 -> 1 (window switched to the extended length) and -table when it goes 1 -> 0 (back to the nominal length); on that event the reference is also floored at 32 x FFF8C0D8[i] (read). The flag is set when the extended knock window is used (0x0E20E0, read: B11A = nominal + Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 <= Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold and the extended window ends before the event angle). The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). Axes: rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500, 500-4000 rpm) x load FFF8A616 (read). Confidence: inferred.

On the pass where it clears, the longer version subtracts the table; this one adds the fixed value at cal 0x026B92 instead (s16; the row for the event is Knock Background Clear Step (Event 3)).
Knock signal processing for event slot 3, channel 4 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.
Details: When used: event slot FFF8CDC0 = 3 (Event 3), knock channel 4 of 8, on the knock window where FFF8A7C4 changes. Background step for this channel, added to (window extended) or subtracted from (window back to nominal) the channel background FFF8C1A0[3] for that one event; overlap-flag FFF8A7D4, gain curve cal 0x26F8F. Knock signal processing 0x0E51E4 (read; called once per knock window from 0x0E43B8 with load FFF8A616, after the event chain 0x0E433C): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4, the slot of the Knock Threshold tables) each of 8 knock channels i gets a reference ref_i = 32 x step_i + g x background_i, and the channel ratio is 256 x FFF8CDB0[i] / (ref_i / 32), i.e. measured / reference with 256 = equal (0x0E51E4 tail, read). Channels with their bit set in cal 0x1B97C..0x1B97F give 0; a channel flagged in FFF8CEED (driver flag, value at its lower limit, inferred) gives 256. The ratios are sorted and the largest min(cal 0x1B988, 5) = 3 are summed into the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot], which 0x0E80B4/0x0E8654 compare with Knock Threshold (read). The measured channels come from the knock sensor ADC: 0x1E7868 DMA-collects 32-sample blocks, 0x1E725A runs FFT-style butterflies, 0x1E73A4 takes sqrt(re^2+im^2) of 8 selected bins (pointer tables 0x34A88/0x34AA8), and 0x1E7724 sums them over the window into FFF8D1D4[8] -> FFF8CDB0[8] (read), so the 8 channels are 8 frequency bins of the knock sensor signal (inferred). background_i is the per-slot channel background FFF8C180.. (slot 1) / C190.. / C1A0.. / C1B0.. (slot 4), a lag filter of the measured channel kept by 0x0E4500 when the event is not knocking, floored at the per-channel rpm curve FFF8C0D8 (0x0E22A4) (read). step_i is this table family: it is non-zero only on the one event where the slot's window-length flag changes: +table when the flag goes 0 -> 1 (window switched to the extended length) and -table when it goes 1 -> 0 (back to the nominal length); on that event the reference is also floored at 32 x FFF8C0D8[i] (read). The flag is set when the extended knock window is used (0x0E20E0, read: B11A = nominal + Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 <= Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold and the extended window ends before the event angle). The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). Axes: rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500, 500-4000 rpm) x load FFF8A616 (read). Confidence: inferred.

On the pass where it clears, the longer version subtracts the table; this one adds the fixed value at cal 0x026BA6 instead (s16; the row for the event is Knock Background Clear Step (Event 4)).
Knock signal processing for event slot 4, channel 6 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.
Details: When used: event slot FFF8CDC0 = 4 (Event 4), knock channel 6 of 8, on the knock window where FFF8A7C5 changes. Background step for this channel, added to (window extended) or subtracted from (window back to nominal) the channel background FFF8C1B0[5] for that one event; overlap-flag FFF8A7D5, gain curve cal 0x26F9F. Knock signal processing 0x0E51E4 (read; called once per knock window from 0x0E43B8 with load FFF8A616, after the event chain 0x0E433C): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4, the slot of the Knock Threshold tables) each of 8 knock channels i gets a reference ref_i = 32 x step_i + g x background_i, and the channel ratio is 256 x FFF8CDB0[i] / (ref_i / 32), i.e. measured / reference with 256 = equal (0x0E51E4 tail, read). Channels with their bit set in cal 0x1B97C..0x1B97F give 0; a channel flagged in FFF8CEED (driver flag, value at its lower limit, inferred) gives 256. The ratios are sorted and the largest min(cal 0x1B988, 5) = 3 are summed into the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot], which 0x0E80B4/0x0E8654 compare with Knock Threshold (read). The measured channels come from the knock sensor ADC: 0x1E7868 DMA-collects 32-sample blocks, 0x1E725A runs FFT-style butterflies, 0x1E73A4 takes sqrt(re^2+im^2) of 8 selected bins (pointer tables 0x34A88/0x34AA8), and 0x1E7724 sums them over the window into FFF8D1D4[8] -> FFF8CDB0[8] (read), so the 8 channels are 8 frequency bins of the knock sensor signal (inferred). background_i is the per-slot channel background FFF8C180.. (slot 1) / C190.. / C1A0.. / C1B0.. (slot 4), a lag filter of the measured channel kept by 0x0E4500 when the event is not knocking, floored at the per-channel rpm curve FFF8C0D8 (0x0E22A4) (read). step_i is this table family: it is non-zero only on the one event where the slot's window-length flag changes: +table when the flag goes 0 -> 1 (window switched to the extended length) and -table when it goes 1 -> 0 (back to the nominal length); on that event the reference is also floored at 32 x FFF8C0D8[i] (read). The flag is set when the extended knock window is used (0x0E20E0, read: B11A = nominal + Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 <= Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold and the extended window ends before the event angle). The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). Axes: rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500, 500-4000 rpm) x load FFF8A616 (read). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Timing Retard High Load (1st Gear)
table.description:
Timing pulled at high load in 1st gear (by rpm and load), used only above about 2800 rpm and 0.84 g/rev (65 % load) and not in neutral. Raising values adds retard. Not used if knock control is switched off.
Details: When used: 0x0DF3EC (called from 0x0DF0B8, args read): FFF8A779 = -(cal 0x2FE3E (23) x value >> 7) half-degrees, a retard term in the final timing sum FFF8A744 of 0x0D9E40 (read). Normal path: the table for the current gear FFF8A621 (1-5; gear 6 and 0 give 0) is used only while rpm FFF8CD54 >= cal 0x2FE44 (2800 rpm, hysteresis cal 0x2FE46 = 100 rpm) and load FFF8ADE4 >= cal 0x2FE40 (65 %, hysteresis cal 0x2FE42 = 15 %), and is forced to 0 while FFF88ADA bit 6 (neutral switch, discrete input FFF8A29E bit 5 = pin PH5, Phase 16) is set (read). Fault path: while FFF88E2B bit 1 (set by the failed status of U0073/U0101/U0122/U0140/U0402/U0416/U0422/U0423/U0155 = CAN communication faults, 0x080B96 area, read) or (manual coding FFF886AB bit 7 and FFF88E28 bit 0 = P0500/P2158 vehicle-speed faults) is set, the 3rd-gear table is used at every gear, rpm and load. All of it is 0 while cal 0x56EE7 bit 7 (knock control off) is set (read). Axes rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4 (2000-5600 rpm, 80-160 %). Scaling assumes cal 0x2FE3E = 23. Gear meaning of FFF8A621 inferred. p16 (read): confirmed - FFF88E2B bit 1 is the OR of the test-failed bits FFF81315 b0-b6 / FFF8131E b2-b3 (0x080B96) = U0422/U0140/U0402/U0101/U0416/U0122/U0073/U0423/U0155. Confidence: read.

Details: When used: 0x0DF3EC (called from 0x0DF0B8, args read): FFF8A779 = -(cal 0x2FE3E (23) x value >> 7) half-degrees, a retard term in the final timing sum FFF8A744 of 0x0D9E40 (read). Normal path: the table for the current gear FFF8A621 (1-5; gear 6 and 0 give 0) is used only while rpm FFF8CD54 >= cal 0x2FE44 (2800 rpm, hysteresis cal 0x2FE46 = 100 rpm) and load FFF8ADE4 >= cal 0x2FE40 (65 %, hysteresis cal 0x2FE42 = 15 %), and is forced to 0 while FFF88ADA bit 6 (neutral switch, discrete input FFF8A29E bit 5 = pin PH5, Phase 16) is set (read). Fault path: while FFF88E2B bit 1 (set by the failed status of U0073/U0101/U0122/U0140/U0402/U0416/U0422/U0423/U0155 = CAN communication faults, 0x080B96 area, read) or (manual coding FFF886AB bit 7 and FFF88E28 bit 0 = P0500/P2158 vehicle-speed faults) is set, the 3rd-gear table is used at every gear, rpm and load. All of it is 0 while cal 0x56EE7 bit 7 (knock control off) is set (read). Axes rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4 (2000-5600 rpm, 80-160 %). Scaling assumes cal 0x2FE3E = 23. Gear meaning of FFF8A621 inferred. p16 (read): confirmed - FFF88E2B bit 1 is the OR of the test-failed bits FFF81315 b0-b6 / FFF8131E b2-b3 (0x080B96) = U0422/U0140/U0402/U0101/U0416/U0122/U0073/U0423/U0155. Confidence: read.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard Start (Below 200 km/h)
table.description:
Delay, in 10 ms steps after a sudden throttle opening (tip-in), before the tip-in timing retard starts, by rpm; used below 200 km/h.
Details: When used: speed FFF99835 below cal 0x37EF4 (200 km/h), latched on the pass where the tip-in code FFF8A619 appears. First 10 ms pass of the retard window (retard applies from this pass count up to the End table), by rpm FFF8CD5C (x25) (read). Tip-in timing retard 0x0DDD94 (10 ms module 0x0DE0E0; args engine state FFF8866C, speed FFF99835, FFF886AB bit 5, rpm/25 FFF8CD5C, coolant FFF8CD65, tip-in code FFF8A619, second intake temperature FFF888CF, events-per-pass FFF8A760, rpm FFF8CE9C; stack args checked at 0x0DDDA0..0x0DDDB2: s0 coolant, s4 code, s8 FFF888CF, s12 FFF8A760, s16 rpm, read). On the pass where the tip-in code FFF8A619 appears the window start (05BB50 / 05BB5C) and end (Tip-In Timing Retard End) are latched by rpm/25. FFF8A772 = amount while start <= passes < end, engine state 3, rpm within cal 0x37EF8..0x37EF6 (3900-6375 rpm), coolant FFF8CD65 within cal 0x37EFB..0x37EFA and speed below 200 km/h or 200-250 km/h; amount = code cal 0x37EFD..0x37F00 (below 200 km/h) or 0x37F01..0x37F04 (200-250 km/h) + Tip-In Timing Retard Temperature Adder. Afterwards FFF8A772 falls each pass by min(255, decay table(rpm/25) x FFF8A760), FFF8A760 = combustion events since the previous pass (0x0DC7E8 on the per-event counter FFF8A780, 0x0DFEF8), i.e. by the table value per combustion event. 0x0DD568 subtracts FFF8A772 (0.5-degree units) from the timing request FFF8A76A (read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard Decay (Below 200 km/h)
table.description:
How fast the tip-in timing retard is removed once its window ends, in degrees per combustion event by rpm; used below 200 km/h. Larger values give timing back faster.
Details: When used: speed FFF99835 below cal 0x37EF4 (200 km/h), every pass (looked up by rpm/25 FFF8CD5C, R5 at 0x0DDDBE, read); acts once the retard window has ended or its conditions fail. Ramp-out of the tip-in retard in degrees per combustion event. Tip-in timing retard 0x0DDD94 (10 ms module 0x0DE0E0; args engine state FFF8866C, speed FFF99835, FFF886AB bit 5, rpm/25 FFF8CD5C, coolant FFF8CD65, tip-in code FFF8A619, second intake temperature FFF888CF, events-per-pass FFF8A760, rpm FFF8CE9C; stack args checked at 0x0DDDA0..0x0DDDB2: s0 coolant, s4 code, s8 FFF888CF, s12 FFF8A760, s16 rpm, read). FFF8A772 = amount while start <= passes < end, engine state 3, rpm within cal 0x37EF8..0x37EF6 (3900-6375 rpm), coolant FFF8CD65 within cal 0x37EFB..0x37EFA and speed below 200 km/h or 200-250 km/h; amount = code cal 0x37EFD..0x37F00 (below 200 km/h) or 0x37F01..0x37F04 (200-250 km/h) + Tip-In Timing Retard Temperature Adder. table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard End (Below 200 km/h)
table.description:
How long the tip-in timing retard lasts after a sudden throttle opening, in 10 ms steps by rpm; used below 200 km/h between about 3900 and 6375 rpm.
Details: When used: speed FFF99835 below cal 0x37EF4 (200 km/h). End of the tip-in retard window, in 10 ms passes since the tip-in code FFF8A619 appeared, by rpm FFF8CD5C (x25). 0x0DDD94 (called from the 10 ms module 0x0DE0E0; args read: engine state FFF8866C, speed FFF99835, pedal released FFF886AB bit 5, rpm/25 FFF8CD5C, coolant FFF8CD65, tip-in code FFF8A619, FFF888CF, FFF8A760, rpm FFF8CE9C, outputs FFF8A772/A773/A771). On the pass where FFF8A619 becomes non-zero the window start (05BB50 / 05BB5C) and end (05BB68 / 05BB74) are looked up by rpm/25; the second table of each pair is used when speed >= cal 0x37EF4 (200 km/h). FFF8A772 = amount while start <= passes since the code appeared < end, with engine state 3, pedal not fully released, rpm FFF8CE9C within cal 0x37EF8..0x37EF6 (3900-6375 rpm), coolant FFF8CD65 within cal 0x37EFB..0x37EFA (20..255) and speed within cal 0x37EF5..0x37EFC; afterwards it decays by 05BB8C/05BB80(rpm/25) x FFF8A760 per pass. Amount = cal 0x37EFD..0x37F00 (below 200 km/h) or 0x37F01..0x37F04 (200-250 km/h) by code 1-4 + 05BB44(FFF888CF) (read). 0x0DD568 subtracts FFF8A772 from the timing request FFF8A76A (0.5-degree units), which reaches the base timing sum through FFF8A76D (0x0DD760, 0x0DA600) (read). FFF8A619 (0x0B86A0 via 0x0B8618, read) is a tip-in code: active while the pedal is off its released position and the throttle byte FFF8CD74>>2 has risen by >= cal 0x3497C (6 counts, about 3.4 %) over the last 40 ms (5-deep 10 ms history FFF8CD78..CD7C); 0x40 = from below 0594A8(rpm) to above 0594B4(rpm) with a rise >= cal 0x3497F (8); 0x30 / 0x20 = peak rise >= cal 0x3497E (10) / 0x3497D (5); else 0x10 (read). It clears when the throttle closes by cal 0x34980 (4) or the pedal is released. Unit: passes of the 10 ms module (read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard Temperature Adder
table.description:
Extra tip-in timing retard added by intake air temperature (from what is probably the second intake air temperature sensor).
Details: When used: on every pass with a tip-in code, added to the code amount (0x0DDD94: FFF8A771 = this(FFF888CF), FFF8A7EC = code cal + this, capped at 255; argument s8 = FFF888CF passed in the delay slot at 0x0DDE3C, read). FFF888CF is the second intake air temperature (degC + 50 from Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling, 0x06B304; sensor identity inferred). Tip-in timing retard 0x0DDD94 (10 ms module 0x0DE0E0; args engine state FFF8866C, speed FFF99835, FFF886AB bit 5, rpm/25 FFF8CD5C, coolant FFF8CD65, tip-in code FFF8A619, second intake temperature FFF888CF, events-per-pass FFF8A760, rpm FFF8CE9C; stack args checked at 0x0DDDA0..0x0DDDB2: s0 coolant, s4 code, s8 FFF888CF, s12 FFF8A760, s16 rpm, read). table.name: Tip-In Retard Class 4 Start Throttle Maximum
table.description:
Tip-in classification by rpm: for the strongest tip-in class (4), the throttle before the stab must be below this. Together with Tip-In Retard Class 4 Throttle Minimum it defines a big low-to-high throttle jump.
Details: When used: during a tip-in event (0x0B86A0, read): class 4 needs the throttle before the event (held FFF8CD77) below this(rpm FFF8CE9C). Tip-in classifier 0x0B86A0 (called by 0x0B8618, read): active while running (FFF8906B = 3), accelerator not released, throttle rising (CD7C < CD78) and FFF8CD77 - its value 40 ms earlier (CD7B) >= cal 0x3497C (6 = 3.4 %); it ends when the throttle closes by cal 0x34980 (4) or the pedal is released. Class FFF8A619: 0x40 if the throttle before the event < Tip-In Retard Class 4 Start Throttle Maximum, the peak 40 ms rise >= cal 0x3497F (8) and the throttle now >= Tip-In Retard Class 4 Throttle Minimum; else 0x30 / 0x20 for a peak rise >= cal 0x3497E (10) / 0x3497D (5) unless frozen (see Tip-In Retard Class Hold Throttle); else 0x10. 0x0DDD94 (read) turns class n into the retard FFF8A772 = cal 0x37EFC+n (or 0x37F00+n by speed) + 05BB44(FFF888CF), subtracted from FFF8A76A in 0x0DD568. Confidence: read.

table.name: Tip-In Retard Class 4 Throttle Minimum
table.description:
Tip-in classification by rpm: for the strongest tip-in class (4), the throttle after the stab must be at or above this.
Details: When used: during a tip-in event (0x0B86A0, read): class 4 needs the current throttle FFF8CD77 at or above this(rpm FFF8CE9C). Tip-in classifier 0x0B86A0 (called by 0x0B8618, read): active while running (FFF8906B = 3), accelerator not released, throttle rising (CD7C < CD78) and FFF8CD77 - its value 40 ms earlier (CD7B) >= cal 0x3497C (6 = 3.4 %); it ends when the throttle closes by cal 0x34980 (4) or the pedal is released. Class FFF8A619: 0x40 if the throttle before the event < Tip-In Retard Class 4 Start Throttle Maximum, the peak 40 ms rise >= cal 0x3497F (8) and the throttle now >= Tip-In Retard Class 4 Throttle Minimum; else 0x30 / 0x20 for a peak rise >= cal 0x3497E (10) / 0x3497D (5) unless frozen (see Tip-In Retard Class Hold Throttle); else 0x10. 0x0DDD94 (read) turns class n into the retard FFF8A772 = cal 0x37EFC+n (or 0x37F00+n by speed) + 05BB44(FFF888CF), subtracted from FFF8A76A in 0x0DD568. Confidence: read.

table.name: Tip-In Retard Class Hold Throttle
table.description:
Tip-in classification by rpm: once the pedal has been pressed for a short while and throttle is at or above this, the tip-in class is held rather than reassigned to classes 2/3 or dropped back to 1.
Details: When used: during a tip-in event (0x0B86A0, read): once the accelerator has been pressed for more than 10 passes and the current throttle FFF8CD77 is at or above this(rpm FFF8CE9C), classes 2/3 are no longer assigned and the class keeps its last value instead of falling back to 1. Tip-in classifier 0x0B86A0 (called by 0x0B8618, read): active while running (FFF8906B = 3), accelerator not released, throttle rising (CD7C < CD78) and FFF8CD77 - its value 40 ms earlier (CD7B) >= cal 0x3497C (6 = 3.4 %); it ends when the throttle closes by cal 0x34980 (4) or the pedal is released. Class FFF8A619: 0x40 if the throttle before the event < Tip-In Retard Class 4 Start Throttle Maximum, the peak 40 ms rise >= cal 0x3497F (8) and the throttle now >= Tip-In Retard Class 4 Throttle Minimum; else 0x30 / 0x20 for a peak rise >= cal 0x3497E (10) / 0x3497D (5) unless frozen (see Tip-In Retard Class Hold Throttle); else 0x10. 0x0DDD94 (read) turns class n into the retard FFF8A772 = cal 0x37EFC+n (or 0x37F00+n by speed) + 05BB44(FFF888CF), subtracted from FFF8A76A in 0x0DD568. Confidence: read.

table.name: Tip-Out Timing Retard
table.description:
Timing pulled, by gear and manifold pressure, when rpm rises shortly after lifting off the pedal on a warm engine above walking speed; probably damps driveline shunt or coasting downshift jolts. Latched on the event and removed at once afterwards.
Details: When used: within cal 0x1B8F0 (100 passes of the 10 ms task = 1 s, inferred) after the accelerator is released, once the trigger FFF8A774 bit 5 sets. Bit 5 (0x0E0F3C) is set while: pedal released, rpm rate FFF8CEA6 >= cal 0x1B8E6 (26), rpm FFF8CE9C <= cal 0x1B8E8 (6600 rpm, hyst. cal 0x1B8EA), coolant FFF88A44 >= cal 0x1B8EC (158 F / 70 C), vehicle speed FFF88BE8 >= cal 0x1B8EE (178 = 10 km/h) and FFF8A8AE bit 7 and FFF88E62 bit 0 (not identified) (0x0E0F3C, read); bit 4 (0x0E0EA8, read) passes bit 5 on only within cal 0x1B8F0 passes of the pedal release and while rpm FFF8CE9C >= cal 0x1B8F2. 0x0DDB2C (read): on the rising edge of FFF8A774 bit 4 this table (gear FFF8A621 x manifold pressure FFF88A34) is latched into FFF8A76F and held while the bit stays set; when it clears the value decays by cal 0x1B8F4 (51200 = 200 half-degrees per pass, i.e. at once). FFF8A76F is subtracted from the final timing sum FFF8A744 (0x0D9E40, read). So a retard when the rpm rises right after a lift-off (driveline shunt / coasting downshift damping, inferred). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Timing Request Recovery Rate After Tip-Out
table.description:
Limits how fast the timing request may climb back to the closed-pedal target just after the pedal is released, by rpm. Lower values give a softer return.
Details: When used: 0x0E0A30 (read): while the accelerator is released (FFF8A774 bit 0), for the first part of the release (counter FFF8484C, incremented by FFF8A760 per pass, below cal 0x30FD0 = 3072) and while the closed-pedal target is more than cal 0x30FD2 - 32 (20 half-degrees) above the current request, the timing request FFF8B10E may rise by at most (this - 32) half-degrees per pass (rpm FFF8CDC2 axis); otherwise it follows the target at once. FFF8B10E feeds FFF8A789 (0x0E0910) and the spark target FFF8A72A. Confidence: read.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Resume Timing Retard
table.description:
Short timing retard by coolant temperature, applied for a few combustion events when fuel comes back after decel fuel cut because rpm fell to the resume point with the pedal still closed; then ramped out. Softens the fuel-return bump. 128 = no change.
Details: When used: 0x0DAFD4 (called per combustion event from 0x0DF02C <- 0x07D0E0, the crank-synchronous task; args read: accelerator released FFF88C64 bit 5, FFF8A774 bit 3, MT coding FFF88ADA bit 7, FFF88ADA bit 6, engine stopped FFF88A2D bit 0). Event (read): with the pedal released, the engine running and the rpm change per event FFF8CEA6 >= cal 0x2FF56 (s16 -154 = -30 rpm per event; signed CMP/GE at 0x0DB000), an event starts when FFF8A774 bit 3 is set and rpm FFF8CE9C/128 (rpm/25) is below FFF8A62E. After cal 0x2FF50 (1) event with no change, FFF8B0DA = this table(coolant FFF88A44) << 7 for cal 0x2FF4F (10) combustion events; afterwards B0DA ramps back toward 0x4000 (no change) by cal 0x2FF58 - 0x4000 = 179/16384 per event (0.7 degrees per event). Pressing the pedal or a fast rpm drop cancels it (B0DA = 0x4000) (read). 0x0DB374: FFF8A753 = min(B0DA, B0DC) >> 7, the more retarding of this term and the 0x0DB21C term (05B718/05B724), and A753 is added in the 128-offset half-degree frame to the final timing sum (0x0D9E40, read). Trigger meaning: FFF8A774 bit 3 is set by 0x0E1628 when the limit state FFF8A638 steps from 8 to 9 while cylinders were cut on the previous pass (FFF8A643 != 0), and cleared by FFF8A78E (read). 0x0BD684 enters state 8 while FFF8A63D bit 0 holds past the 059D44 hold count and goes to 9 when it drops (read). FFF8A63D bit 0 comes from bit 2, which 0x0C06F0 clears when the pedal is released and rpm/25 >= FFF8A62E (plus start-time and fault conditions) (read). So state 8 is the deceleration fuel cut and FFF8A62E its rpm threshold in 25 rpm units (inferred from the cut-cylinder count and the closed-pedal rpm test), and this table is a short retard when fuel returns because rpm fell to that threshold with the pedal still closed (read in Phase 19: limit state 8 is the staged decel fuel cut, A63D bit 0 held for 059D44 passes). 128 = no change, one count = 0.5 degree, negative = retard. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Recovery Timing Ramp (Closed-Pedal Resume)
table.description:
How fast, in degrees per combustion event by rpm, the -5 degree decel-fuel-cut timing offset is removed after the cut ends with the pedal still released.
Details: When used: state 2 after a cut that ended with the pedal still released or rpm/25 below the resume threshold FFF8A62E (latch FFF84762 = FFF8A78D, set on the falling edge of FFF8A64C bit 2 in that case, read). Decel fuel cut timing offset FFF8B0DC, 0x0DB21C (per combustion event, from 0x0DF0B8 <- 0x07D0E0; args A64C bit 2, FFF88C64 bit 5, read). State FFF8A76E (0x0DD7E8, 10 ms): 3 while cylinders are cut (FFF8A64C bit 2 = cut active in limit state 8, 0x0C5170), 4 once the cut has lasted cal 0x2FF48 (1 s) with coolant >= cal 0x2FF4A (70 C), load FFF8A616 < cal 0x2FF4E (77 %), rpm FFF8CD54 < cal 0x2FF4C (2500 rpm), combustion mode 4 and FFF8881E < cal 0x2FF46; after the cut 1 (hold) while those conditions last, at most cal 0x2FF44 (3 s), then 2. B0DC = 0x4000 (no change) in state 3, cal 0x2FF12 << 7 (118: -5 degrees) in state 4, held in state 1, and in state 2 it climbs back to 0x4000 by (table(rpm FFF8CD54) - 0x4000) per event. FFF8A753 = min(Decel Fuel Cut Resume Timing Retard term B0DA, B0DC) >> 7 is added to the final timing sum (0x0DB374, 0x0D9E40), 128 = no change (read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Recovery Timing Ramp (Pedal Resume)
table.description:

Details: When used: state 2 after a cut that ended with the pedal pressed and rpm/25 at or above the resume threshold FFF8A62E (latch FFF84762 clear, read). Decel fuel cut timing offset FFF8B0DC, 0x0DB21C (per combustion event, from 0x0DF0B8 <- 0x07D0E0; args A64C bit 2, FFF88C64 bit 5, read). State FFF8A76E (0x0DD7E8, 10 ms): 3 while cylinders are cut (FFF8A64C bit 2 = cut active in limit state 8, 0x0C5170), 4 once the cut has lasted cal 0x2FF48 (1 s) with coolant >= cal 0x2FF4A (70 C), load FFF8A616 < cal 0x2FF4E (77 %), rpm FFF8CD54 < cal 0x2FF4C (2500 rpm), combustion mode 4 and FFF8881E < cal 0x2FF46; after the cut 1 (hold) while those conditions last, at most cal 0x2FF44 (3 s), then 2. table.name: A/C Cut Timing Retard Hold (RPM)
table.description:
When the A/C compressor switches off near standstill, the ECU retards timing 5 degrees for this many combustion events (one per 180 degrees of crank rotation), by rpm, then ramps the retard out. Probably smooths the idle load change.
Details: When used: 0x0D8E3C (called from 0x0DF02C, args read): on the falling edge of FFF8A9A2 bit 6 (A/C compressor engaged, inferred in my research notes) while FFF88A3C < cal 0x2FE88, vehicle speed FFF99835 < cal 0x2FE90 (4 km/h), rpm FFF8CE9C within cal 0x2FE8E..0x2FE8C (500 rpm..max) and coolant >= cal 0x2FE8A, a hold counter FFF8A75D is loaded from this table (by rpm FFF8CE9C) and counted down per pass. While it runs, FFF8B0CC = cal 0x2FE82 (2560 = 10 half-degrees = 5 degrees); afterwards B0CC decays by cal 0x2FE84 (51) per pass. B0CC >> 8 is subtracted from the final timing sum FFF8A744 (0x0D9E40, read). Off while FFF88A2D bit 0 (engine stopped) or FFF8A65F bit 7. The alternate per-step table 05B410 (by FFF8A8C7) replaces cal 0x2FE82 only with cal 0x1D0AE bit 0 set. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Curve (Gear 1)
table.description:
Manual transmission, gear 1: timing correction (negative = retard) by the size of the throttle-flow change after a throttle step, scaled by the surge phase, coolant and mode factors. Appears to damp driveline surge (shuffle) by retarding while rpm swings up.
Details: When used: gear FFF88FCE = 1 on the MT coding (0x0DBB20, read; the AT/CVT curves 05B898/05B8B0/05B8C8/05B8E0 are flat -20 deg, 05B880 and the gear 6 curves 05B8F8/05B904 are 0). Full-scale timing correction (degrees, negative = retard) by the largest throttle-flow change FFF8B0EE since the trigger FFF8A7A1 bit 2 set (0x0DBB20 holds the maximum in FFF8B0F0 and resets it to 0 while the trigger is clear, read), before the phase, coolant, mode and cal factors (read). Surge damping term FFF8A758 (0x0DBB20, called from the 10 ms module 0x0DE0E0; stack args verified with callers.py: s0 = gear FFF88FCE, s4 = MT coding FFF88ADA bit 7, s8 = FFF8B0EE, s12 = rpm FFF8CE9C, s16 = FFF88C64 bit 5, s20 = combustion mode FFF8A85C, read): A758 = Curve(FFF8B0EE) x PhaseFactor(FFF8A75E) x CoolantFactor FFF8A75C x ModeFactor(A85C) x cal factor (MT coding: cal 0x306E5 = 254, or cal 0x306E7 = 128 once FFF88C64 bit 5 has been clear for cal 0x306E8 = 150 passes) / 255^4, in 0.5-degree units, capped at +63.5 degrees, and 0 when the trigger FFF8A7A1 bit 2 is clear or when the current swing count has lasted longer than its time cal 0x306EA..0x306FA (100/20/100/10/100/5/100/100/100 passes of 10 ms for counts 0..8) (read). A758 is added to the final timing sum in 0x0D9E40 (read), so negative values retard. Trigger (read): 0x0DC1E8 counts passes while FFF8A7A1 bit 3 is set, the throttle-flow change FFF8B0EE >= cal 0x3084E (131 = 0.4 % per 20 ms, MT; hysteresis 0x3084C) and FFF8B112 (0x0E0D14 of FFF88A3A) <= cal 0x30842; 0x0E1350 sets FFF8A7A1 bit 2 when that count exceeds a per-gear, per-rpm-band threshold (cals 0x30F62..0x30FAC); it is dropped after cal 0x30850 (90) active passes. FFF8A75E counts rpm swings (0x0DC324, see p17p_surge_phase). FFF88FCE is the gear: on the MT coding 0x08254C copies FFF8A8B6, which 0x11422C derives from the ratio gear FFF8A623 (read). Reading: a timing intervention after a throttle step that retards while rpm swings up and releases while it swings down, i.e. driveline surge (shuffle) damping. Confidence: inferred.

Manual transmission, gear 3, below 1800 rpm: how much of the surge damping timing correction is applied at each step of the rpm swing count (0 = none, 1.0 = full). Appears to target the rpm-rising part of a driveline surge.
Details: When used: gear FFF88FCE = 3 on the MT coding (FFF88ADA bit 7) with rpm FFF8CE9C below cal 0x306E2 (9216 = 1800 rpm) (0x0DBB20, read). Phase factor (x/255) by the rpm swing count FFF8A75E. With gear FFF88FCE = 0 or above 6 no table is read and the last factor is held (read). Surge damping term FFF8A758 (0x0DBB20, called from the 10 ms module 0x0DE0E0; stack args verified with callers.py: s0 = gear FFF88FCE, s4 = MT coding FFF88ADA bit 7, s8 = FFF8B0EE, s12 = rpm FFF8CE9C, s16 = FFF88C64 bit 5, s20 = combustion mode FFF8A85C, read): A758 = Curve(FFF8B0EE) x PhaseFactor(FFF8A75E) x CoolantFactor FFF8A75C x ModeFactor(A85C) x cal factor (MT coding: cal 0x306E5 = 254, or cal 0x306E7 = 128 once FFF88C64 bit 5 has been clear for cal 0x306E8 = 150 passes) / 255^4, in 0.5-degree units, capped at +63.5 degrees, and 0 when the trigger FFF8A7A1 bit 2 is clear or when the current swing count has lasted longer than its time cal 0x306EA..0x306FA (100/20/100/10/100/5/100/100/100 passes of 10 ms for counts 0..8) (read). A758 is added to the final timing sum in 0x0D9E40 (read), so negative values retard. Trigger (read): 0x0DC1E8 counts passes while FFF8A7A1 bit 3 is set, the throttle-flow change FFF8B0EE >= cal 0x3084E (131 = 0.4 % per 20 ms, MT; hysteresis 0x3084C) and FFF8B112 (0x0E0D14 of FFF88A3A) <= cal 0x30842; 0x0E1350 sets FFF8A7A1 bit 2 when that count exceeds a per-gear, per-rpm-band threshold (cals 0x30F62..0x30FAC); it is dropped after cal 0x30850 (90) active passes. FFF8A75E counts rpm swings (0x0DC324, see p17p_surge_phase). FFF88FCE is the gear: on the MT coding 0x08254C copies FFF8A8B6, which 0x11422C derives from the ratio gear FFF8A623 (read). Reading: a timing intervention after a throttle step that retards while rpm swings up and releases while it swings down, i.e. driveline surge (shuffle) damping. Confidence: inferred.
