table.name: A/C Cut Timing Retard Step (Alternate Logic)
table.description:
Alternate A/C-switch timing retard amount, by an unidentified input.
0x0D8E3C (called from 0x0DF02C; args read: FFF88A2D bit 0, cal 0x1D0AE bit 0, FFF8A9A3 bit 0, FFF8A9A2 bit 6, FFF8A65F bit 7) loads FFF8B0CC with this table (by FFF8A8C7) instead of cal 0x2FE82 (2560 = 5 degrees) only when its second argument, the calibration bit 0x1D0AE bit 0, is set. With that bit set the trigger also changes from the A/C engagement edge (FFF8A9A2 bit 6) to FFF8A9A3 bit 0. B0CC >> 8 is subtracted from the final timing sum (0x0D9E40) while the A/C Cut Timing Retard Hold counter runs, then decays (read). Axis FFF8A8C7 is not identified: 0x116034 writes it as a latched copy of FFF8A8C6 (latch conditions involve FFF88B8B bit 0 and FFF8A9A3 bit 1; not worked out in detail), and FFF8A8C6 comes from 0x115F80, which takes it from FFF88B91 (a received input byte, meaning not identified); FFF8A8C6 is read by several other functions together with the same cal bit 0x1D0AE bit 0 (read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Torque Reduction Spark Retard
table.description:
Turns a torque or efficiency shortfall back into spark retard on base timing. Besides torque reduction, it is how the ECU pulls fired timing down to Primary Ignition (or the closed-pedal target) plus knock correction advance where that is below Base Timing, so it must stay the inverse of Ignition Efficiency vs Retard; don't edit one without the other. Not used in the rev/overboost-cut states.
Details: When used: on the FFF8A76A spark path (normal fuel mode; the catalyst-heating paths FFF8A76B / FFF8A76C use the sibling Catalyst Heating Spark Retard tables, inferred), except in limit states 0x0B / 0x0C / 0x19 / 0x1A with their Limit-State Spark bits set and in state 0x1B. 0x0DD568 (read): spark angle FFF8A76A = base timing FFF8A645 - this(max(FFF8A64B, cal 0x2FDE4 = 102) x 128) + per-cylinder trim - tip-in retard FFF8A772, capped at cal 0x1B83C (120); FFF8A76A then rate-limits into the fired timing (0x0DD760 -> 0x0DA600 -> FFF8A744). FFF8A64B (0x0C39DC) is the torque cap over the air torque times the request efficiency, the share of torque the spark must still deliver (inferred), so this is the torque-reduction (and efficiency) retard. Same form as Catalyst Heating Spark Retard (0x0DD4EC). Not used by the rev limiter. The floor applies only on the normal path: when FFF8866C = 3 and either FFF8A649 != -128 or (param 5 = FFF88C64 bit 5 set and the state is not 2), outside state 0x18 with A649 = -128, the input is FFF8AF22 >> 7 instead (no floor, read). FFF8AF22 (0x0C13B4, read) = Ignition Efficiency vs Retard(max(0, FFF8A645 - (FFF8A789 - 32 [+ 0.3516 deg x (KCA FFF8A791 + FLKC FFF8A7A7) in combustion modes 3/4]))), the efficiency of the timing request relative to base timing, and 0x0C39DC builds FFF8A64B = min(255, torque-cap ratio x AF22 / 128). This table is the exact inverse of Ignition Efficiency vs Retard (axis and data mirrored), so on both paths FFF8A76A = min(base timing, timing request + KCA + FLKC) less the torque-cap retard: this is the mechanism by which Primary Ignition (or Closed-Pedal Timing Target) and the knock correction advance limit the fired timing (read; min() form computed). Keep it the inverse of Ignition Efficiency vs Retard. Because FFF8A64B is capped at 255, the pedal-pressed path always takes at least 1 count (0.5 degree) from this table even at full torque (255 x 128 = 32640 -> 1 by the truncating lookup 0x1AB8BC; computed), and the input is always capped at 256 = 100 % (read). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Open)
table.description:
Base ignition timing map for the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration) with the TGVs open; from 1200 rpm up its rows equal Base Timing (EGR Off, TGV Open). It is only an upper limit: the ECU fires the lower of this map and Closed-Pedal Timing Target (plus its corrections).
Details: When used: Used while the accelerator is fully released (FFF8A774 bit 0, see Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Closed)), TGVs not forced closed. From 1200 rpm up its rows equal Base Timing (EGR Off, TGV Open). Base ignition timing. 0x0C2C08 uses this 16x16 table when cal 0x1071E bit 0 and FFF8A774 bit 0 are both set, and F2 clear (F2 = FFF8A881 bit 4). The result is rate-limited (cals 0x1058C / 0x1058E) and the IAT compensation FFF8A782 and Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation FFF8A788 are added (0x0C2C08) to give base timing FFF8A645, which is only the upper limit of the fired timing: with the pedal released 0x0DD568 sets FFF8A76A = FFF8A645 - Torque Reduction Spark Retard(FFF8AF22 >> 7), where FFF8AF22 (0x0C13B4) is the efficiency of the closed-pedal timing request (Closed-Pedal Timing Target + FFF8A788 + FFF8A782 + Post-Start Closed-Pedal Timing Advance, 0x0E0A30) plus KCA + FLKC, so in effect FFF8A76A = min(FFF8A645, that request + KCA + FLKC) (read; min() form computed from the inverse tables). FFF8A76A then goes through 0x0DD760, 0x0DA600 and 0x0D9E40 to FFF8A744. The F2 selector is FFF8A881 bit 4, set by the TGV module 0x10CAE0 (0x10DEFC) - set = TGVs closed (see below). TGV polarity (read): 0x0D952C blends its Closed and Open ignition sets as Closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + Open x FFF8B3E8, so FFF8B3E8 is the TGV open fraction; 0x10C948 drives it toward 0 while FFF8A881 bit 4 is set, so that bit set = TGVs closed. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Maximum timing allowed with the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration), by rpm and load, TGV-closed side; blended with Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Open) by how far the TGVs are open. Never limits timing with the pedal pressed. The rpm axis ends at 4,000 rpm.
Details: 0x0D9E40 (read): final timing FFF8A744 = min(max(timing sum, floor), cap). The cap is this table x (1 - TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8) + Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Open) x FFF8B3E8 (rpm FFF8CE9C x load FFF8A616), used only while the accelerator is fully released (FFF886AB bit 5), the latch FFF8A774 bit 6 is set (set by FFF8A7E0 bit 4, cleared while the engine is stopped, 0x0E1258, read) and vehicle speed FFF88BE8 <= cal 0x32DF2 (17778 = 1000 km/h, i.e. always); otherwise the cap is cal 0x2FC66 (120 = 60 degrees, no cap). So it is a closed-pedal (deceleration / idle) cap; it never limits timing with the pedal pressed. The rpm axis ends at 4,000 rpm. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Open)
table.description:
Maximum timing allowed with the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration), by rpm and load, TGV-open side; blended with Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Closed) by how far the TGVs are open. Never limits timing with the pedal pressed.
Details: TGV-open partner of Ignition Timing Cap (TGV Closed), blended by the TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 (0x0D9E40, read). Same activation condition. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Closed-Pedal Timing Target
table.description:
Ignition timing target by rpm with the pedal released (idle and coasting) on this manual car; coolant, intake-air and post-start corrections are added. The ECU fires the lower of this and the Pedal Released Base Timing map; it is also fired directly during a scan-tool timing check.
Details: When used: on the manual-transmission coding (FFF886AB bit 7 forces FFF8CE63 = 0, 0x06B68C, so the debounced state FFF8A7D9 is 0; read). 0x0D948C: FFF8A72F = this(FFF8CD5C = rpm/25) (the rpm x load table 05B48C replaces it only below cal 0x23834 = 0 rpm, i.e. never). FFF8A72F is the base of the pedal-released timing target in 0x0E0A30 (FFF8A72F + A788 + A782 + A755, blended with the pedal-pressed request by FFF8A72E; its rise after tip-out is limited by Timing Request Recovery Rate After Tip-Out) (read). In addition, in 0x0D9E40 the final timing FFF8A744 is set to FFF8A72F - 32 directly while FFF99845 bit 5 (a scan-tool control, cleared by 0x1CE6DE when the pedal is pressed, FFF8A787 > 0 or rpm > 2000) is set (read). table.name: Closed-Pedal Timing Target (AT Drive Range)
table.description:
AT version of Closed-Pedal Timing Target, used with the pedal released while the transmission is probably in a drive range.
Details: When used: only with the automatic coding (FFF886AB bit 7 clear), while the debounced range state FFF8A7D9 (0x0EA0E0 from FFF8CE63, which 0x06B68C builds from the discrete inputs FFF8A2A1) is 1 or 2 (in a drive range, inferred). table.name: Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation
table.description:

table.name: Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation RPM Multiplier

table.name: Post-Start Closed-Pedal Timing Advance (Coolant at Start)
table.description:
Extra closed-pedal timing for the first moments after a start (stationary, pedal released, low rpm), by the coolant temperature at start, then ramped out. It raises the closed-pedal timing target. Not applied below about -3 C start coolant.
Details: When used: 0x0DB71C (read): while the car is stationary (FFF88BE8 <= 18), within cal 0x31468 (30 counts of FFF88A76 = 0.3 s since start; 10 ms per count, p16) and at or below cal 0x31466 (1000 rpm), FFF8A756 = this(coolant at start FFF88A46) x 05B76C/256; afterwards it decays by cal 0x31464 (-12.8 half-degrees per pass; 0x0DB71C runs from 0x0DF0B8 in the crank-synchronous task, so one pass = one combustion event, inferred from the call chain), limited to cal 0x31462..0x31463 (0..30). 0 when the start coolant is below cal 0x3146A (-3 C). That target is the request side of the closed-pedal timing limit, so this advance reaches the fired timing whenever the target is below Base Timing (Pedal Released)fired base = min(Base Timing (Pedal Released) + comps, Closed-Pedal Timing Target + comps + this + KCA + FLKC) via 0x0C13B4 -> FFF8AF22 -> 0x0DD568 (read; min() form computed). table.name: Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1)
table.description:
Base spark target by rpm and coolant for the cold-start / catalyst-heating mode (pedal released, car stopped, below 4000 rpm); the manual-car set. Torque, run-time and re-entry adders go on top. It feeds the torque model and cold-start monitors; the fired spark probably follows other paths.
Details: When used: set A7E2 bit 0 set, FFF899D7 bit 0 clear (the manual-car case). Base term. 0x108BAC (catalyst-heating module, read) writes FFF8A854, which 0x0C3200 selects as the spark target FFF8A647 in fuel mode FFF8A852 = 2 (combustion mode FFF8A85C 1 or 3, 0x108B08). A647 is the spark the torque model compensates for (0x0C2514, 0x0C1EA8) and the reference of the cold-start retard monitors (0x1CB70C, 0x132568: A72A - A854) (read); the fired spark in this mode follows FFF8A74C/FFF8A76B (0x0DA428), not A854 (read). In combustion mode 1 (A85C < 2), at <= 4000 rpm (cal 0x1CBD8), with the pedal released (FFF886AB bit 5) and speed below cal 0x2A0C1 (2 km/h): A854 = Base(rpm FFF8CD5C, coolant) + Torque Adder(FFF8A85E, coolant) + Run-Time Adder(passes since the engine state became running, coolant) + Re-Entry Adder(passes since mode 1 was re-entered from normal mode 4, coolant), saturated to a byte; the set is chosen by FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (set = the manual tables, clear = the "AT/CVT" tables; always set on the manual coding, Phase 14) and FFF899D7 bit 0 (set = the "Warm-Up Fallback" tables): a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch set by 0x081EFC only when cal 0x59134 bit 0 is set. Otherwise in mode 1 A854 = 05D0BC x 05D0A8 / 256 + FFF8A789 - 32; in mode 3 A854 = A72A (normal target) (read). with cal 0x2996C bit 6 set A854 is forced to cal 0x2A0C0. Units: A854 is compared with A72A and final timing in 0.5 degree units (inferred). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Boost
table.description:
Boost target in absolute pressure, by rpm and the ECU's target torque (the driver's request after the torque limits). Corrected for barometric pressure and intake temperature, then the wastegate control chases it. Raise with Boost Limit.
Details: Target Torque axis (FFF8AECA): the torque the ECU is aiming for, i.e. the driver's request from the Requested Torque tables (pedal x rpm, set chosen by drive mode) after the Maximum Torque (IAT) and (DAM) limits, the external (CAN) torque limit and the gear/rpm rate shaping (torque module 0x0BE694, read). It is a request, not a measured torque; 16000 = 0 ft-lb. 0x108678 -> FFF8B3AC, the boost target before compensation: rpm (FFF8CD54) x target torque FFF8AECA (Nm). Target pressure = this, scaled about absolute zero by the baro and IAT compensations. cal 0x290A8 = 1 would replace it with cal 0x290A6. Chain (0x107654, read): Target Boost(rpm, target torque FFF8AECA) -> FFF8B3AC; FFF8B3B0 = (B3AC + 3404.8) x f - 3404 with f = Baro Comp x IAT Comp x A84B (128 = x1 each); error = B3B0 - measured FFF89264; PI terms from the step tables; duty = min(Initial x Duty Comp + P + I, Maximum x Duty Comp), then the state/fault overrides in 0x107D1C/0x1088B4 and the PWM output FFF8B3B8 (0x1E417C, channel E11). Units: see the scaling note (read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Boost Limit
table.description:
Boost ceiling by rpm that the torque/throttle model uses as its full-load manifold pressure: the model's target MAP is (torque request / full-load reference torque) x this, and it also scales the throttle-area input. It is not an overboost cut (see Overboost Limit). Raise it together with Target Boost so the model's full-load pressure matches the boost you run.
Details: 0x1086F8 (20 ms boost task) -> FFF8A84F (raw) and FFF8A84E = (raw + 13.3) x f - 13, where f is the target's baro/IAT factor: the compensated boost ceiling (read). The torque-model task 0x0C3D14 copies it to FFF8AFAE = A84E << 8 (0x0C3D0C, read). AFAE is the full-load manifold pressure of the throttle/torque model. Target MAP FFF8AF6A = (torque request / full-load reference torque) x this (0x0C2F0C). FFF8AF8A = Throttle Required Area column input AFA8 x this (0x0C3408). The pressure ratio AF6C = AF8A / this (0x0C2F9C) selects the high-pressure spark-compensation filter above 0.85 (all read). Also read by the airflow/torque model 0x111AB8 (role there not decoded). It is not an overboost cut; see Overboost Limit for that. Raise it with Target Boost. Confidence: read.

table.name: Wastegate Duty Initial
table.description:
Base (feed-forward) wastegate duty by rpm and target torque, before boost feedback is added. Higher duty = more boost. It is scaled by the wastegate duty baro and IAT compensations and the total is capped by Wastegate Duty Maximum. Faults force 0 % duty.
Details: Target Torque axis (FFF8AECA): the torque the ECU is aiming for, i.e. the driver's request from the Requested Torque tables (pedal x rpm, set chosen by drive mode) after the Maximum Torque (IAT) and (DAM) limits, the external (CAN) torque limit and the gear/rpm rate shaping (torque module 0x0BE694, read). It is a request, not a measured torque; 16000 = 0 ft-lb. 0x107D3C -> FFF8B38C: base duty on rpm x target torque FFF8AECA (Nm). Output FFF8B3A8 = min(this x FFF8B3B6/32768 + P + I, Maximum x FFF8B3B6/32768) (0x108098, read), where FFF8B3B6 = Wastegate Duty Baro Compensation x Wastegate Duty IAT Compensation. Chain (0x107654, read): Target Boost(rpm, target torque FFF8AECA) -> FFF8B3AC; FFF8B3B0 = (B3AC + 3404.8) x f - 3404 with f = Baro Comp x IAT Comp x A84B (128 = x1 each); error = B3B0 - measured FFF89264; PI terms from the step tables; duty = min(Initial x Duty Comp + P + I, Maximum x Duty Comp), then the state/fault overrides in 0x107D1C/0x1088B4 and the PWM output FFF8B3B8 (0x1E417C, channel E11). Higher duty = more boost: faults force 0 % (0x1088B4, read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Wastegate Duty Maximum
table.description:
Ceiling on wastegate duty (Initial plus feedback) by rpm and target torque, scaled by the same baro and IAT compensations. Also stops the boost integral from growing once duty reaches it. Raise it if feedback runs out of authority.
Details: Target Torque axis (FFF8AECA): the torque the ECU is aiming for, i.e. the driver's request from the Requested Torque tables (pedal x rpm, set chosen by drive mode) after the Maximum Torque (IAT) and (DAM) limits, the external (CAN) torque limit and the gear/rpm rate shaping (torque module 0x0BE694, read). It is a request, not a measured torque; 16000 = 0 ft-lb. 0x107F24 -> FFF8B39E raw, FFF8B39C = this x FFF8B3B6/32768: the cap on Initial + feedback (0x108098) and the limit that stops the positive integral (0x1080E4) (read). Chain (0x107654, read): Target Boost(rpm, target torque FFF8AECA) -> FFF8B3AC; FFF8B3B0 = (B3AC + 3404.8) x f - 3404 with f = Baro Comp x IAT Comp x A84B (128 = x1 each); error = B3B0 - measured FFF89264; PI terms from the step tables; duty = min(Initial x Duty Comp + P + I, Maximum x Duty Comp), then the state/fault overrides in 0x107D1C/0x1088B4 and the PWM output FFF8B3B8 (0x1E417C, channel E11). Confidence: read.

table.name: Target Boost IAT Compensation
table.description:
Multiplier on Target Boost and Boost Limit by intake air temperature (1.0 = no change).
Details: 0x108778: FFF8B3B2 = 2 x Target Boost Baro Compensation x this x FFF8A84B / 128 (32768 = x1), the factor on the absolute boost target and Boost Limit (read). Implicit 16-point u8 table (boot lookup 0x71E0, axis 0..240 step 16) on FFF88663 = (IAT_c50 x 410 - 3972) / 256 from 0x06AF58, where IAT_c50 = FFF88662 = intake air temperature + 50 degC (the OBD IAT source, read); axis = -40.3 + 9.99 x n degC, shown in degF. 128 = x1.0. Confidence: read.

table.name: Target Boost Baro Compensation
table.description:
Multiplier on Target Boost (and Boost Limit) by rpm and barometric pressure (1.0 = no change).
Details: 0x10865C -> FFF8A84C: rpm x barometric pressure FFF88668 (kPa x 256 absolute), 128 = x1.0. Multiplies the absolute target together with the IAT compensation (0x108778: B3B2 = 2 x A84C x IAT comp x A84B, 32768 = x1). Chain (0x107654, read): Target Boost(rpm, target torque FFF8AECA) -> FFF8B3AC; FFF8B3B0 = (B3AC + 3404.8) x f - 3404 with f = Baro Comp x IAT Comp x A84B (128 = x1 each); error = B3B0 - measured FFF89264; PI terms from the step tables; duty = min(Initial x Duty Comp + P + I, Maximum x Duty Comp), then the state/fault overrides in 0x107D1C/0x1088B4 and the PWM output FFF8B3B8 (0x1E417C, channel E11). Confidence: read.

table.name: Wastegate Duty IAT Compensation
table.description:
Multiplier on Wastegate Duty Initial and Maximum by intake air temperature (1.0 = no change).

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default)
table.description:
Drive mode 1: the default set (used when no SI-Drive request is received; the only set on cars without SI-Drive). Main driver demand map for drive mode 1 (the default and fallback): torque requested from rpm and pedal; sets how much torque (and so throttle and boost) a given pedal gives. Edit together with Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, Monitor) or expect a throttle plausibility fault.

Driver-requested torque from rpm and pedal (0x0BB670, read): FFF8AEB4 = A x FFF8AE26/32768 + B x (1 - FFF8AE26/32768), torque above the zero point, into FFF8AEB4; FFF8AE26 ramps between 0 and 32768 under a condition (0x0B9C78). Table A of map set 2 = Drive Mode 1, Default (0x0BDBD8 combines the four sets by the drive-mode byte FFF8A8C1 and per-mode scale cals 0x1FAFE-0x1FB00; SI-Drive positions: mode 4 = Sport Sharp, mode 2 = Sport, mode 3 = Intelligent (least torque for a given pedal in both images), mode 1 = the default used when no valid SI-Drive request is received, and the only set on cars without SI-Drive). table.name: Accelerator Pedal Scaling
table.description:
Shapes the accelerator pedal position before it goes into the Requested Torque maps (role inferred). Editing this also changes the second pedal channel, which reads the same data.

table.name: Accelerator Pedal Span
table.description:
Pedal sensor voltage travel that counts as 100 % pedal. Normally leave alone; change only for a different pedal sensor.
Details: Pedal voltage travel that equals 100 % (0x09EE9E, read); cal 0x573BC is used instead under flag FFF88B7B bit 2. Volts assume the 65536 = 5 V sensor scale. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default)
table.description:
Tip-in smoothing for drive mode 1 (the default and fallback mode): how fast the target torque may rise per 10 ms in the first, slow stage of a tip-in, by gear and rpm (scaled by gear and by Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier). Raise for sharper throttle response, lower for smoother.
Details: When used: drive mode other than 2/3/4, FFF88ADA bit 7 set or FFF8AE0A below cal 0x1FC96. Step1, by gear x rpm, before the gear and pedal factors. 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1 and pedal FFF8AF00): with prev = FFF8AEC6, if prev + Step1 < Stage 2 Torque the shaped value is max(Start Torque, prev + Step1), otherwise max(Stage 2 Torque, prev + Step2); Step2 the same with cal 0x1FCA2.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; the gear factors apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set (else 255 = x1). FFF8AEBE = min(request FFF8AEC2, shaped value). No shaping (FFF8AEBE = request) while the request is below Start Torque, vehicle speed FFF88BE8 is below cal 0x1FCAC (89, about 5 km/h, hysteresis 0x1FCAE), or FFF88ADA bit 6 / FFF88E62 bit 0 is set. So these limit how fast the driver's torque request may rise (tip-in), in two stages. FFF8AEBE goes on through FFF8AEC6 = max(FFF8AEBE, FFF8AEA8) (0x0BD3F0) to the target torque FFF8AECA that indexes boost target and wastegate duty (my research notes). The torque monitor (0x1877B4) reads the same bytes through its own descriptor, so it stays consistent. Drive mode = FFF8A8C1 (2, 3, 4 or other; which value is which SI-Drive position: see the Requested Torque entries, see my research notes). Same data bytes are also referenced by descriptor(s) 05F6B0. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description:
AT/CVT version of Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default). Only used on an AT/CVT-coded car, so it has no effect on a manual.

Main path: with prev = FFF8AEC6, if prev + Step1 < Stage 2 Torque the shaped value is max(Start Torque, prev + Step1), otherwise max(Stage 2 Torque, prev + Step2); Step2 the same with cal 0x1FCA2.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; the gear factors apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set (else x1). FFF8AEBE = min(request FFF8AEC2, shaped value). No shaping (FFF8AEBE = request) while the request is below Start Torque, vehicle speed FFF88BE8 is below cal 0x1FCAC (hysteresis 0x1FCAE), or FFF88ADA bit 6 / FFF88E62 bit 0 is set. FFF8AEBE goes on through FFF8AEC6 = max(FFF8AEBE, FFF8AEA8) (0x0BD3F0) to the target torque FFF8AECA (boost target / wastegate duty axis). Its rpm axis (0x2000A) differs from the manual table's. The torque monitor 0x1877B4 reads the same data bytes through its own descriptor (05F674), so it stays consistent. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Ceiling (Normal)
table.description:
Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is the Ceiling, by gear and rpm, for the normal set: the smoothing only acts when the request is below it.
Details: When used: when the torque request drops (tip-out). Ceiling (Normal set). 0x0BB2A4 (read; called with the previous output FFF8AEC6, the rise-shaped request FFF8AEBE, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54 and vehicle speed FFF99835): x = FFF8AEC6 - Step A; if x is still >= Threshold, FFF8AEA8 = min(Ceiling, x), else FFF8AEA8 = min(Threshold, FFF8AEC6 - Step B). FFF8AEA8 is used only while FFF8AEBE < Ceiling and FFF88ADA bit 6, FFF88E62 bit 0, FFF8A89F bits 1/2 are clear (else FFF8AEA8 = FFF8AEBE); 0x0BD3F0 sets FFF8AEC6 = max(FFF8AEBE, FFF8AEA8). So when the request drops below Ceiling, the target torque falls by Step A per pass down to Threshold and then by the small Step B: the tip-out ramp (inferred driveline-lash shaping). Table set: vehicle speed < cal 0x20A64 (4 km/h) -> Low Speed set; else FFF8A9A2 bit 7 (latched while FFF8A63E bit 2; not identified) clear -> Normal set, set -> Alternate set. The torque monitor (0x187104) reads the same bytes through its own descriptor. Values in the 16000-centred torque unit; steps in Nm per pass. Same data bytes are also referenced by descriptor(s) 05F520. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Threshold (Normal)
table.description:
Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is the Threshold, by gear and rpm, for the normal set: where the fast fall (Step A) switches to the slow fall (Step B).
Details: When used: when the torque request drops (tip-out). Threshold (Normal set). 0x0BB2A4 (read; called with the previous output FFF8AEC6, the rise-shaped request FFF8AEBE, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54 and vehicle speed FFF99835): x = FFF8AEC6 - Step A; if x is still >= Threshold, FFF8AEA8 = min(Ceiling, x), else FFF8AEA8 = min(Threshold, FFF8AEC6 - Step B). FFF8AEA8 is used only while FFF8AEBE < Ceiling and FFF88ADA bit 6, FFF88E62 bit 0, FFF8A89F bits 1/2 are clear (else FFF8AEA8 = FFF8AEBE); 0x0BD3F0 sets FFF8AEC6 = max(FFF8AEBE, FFF8AEA8). So when the request drops below Ceiling, the target torque falls by Step A per pass down to Threshold and then by the small Step B: the tip-out ramp (inferred driveline-lash shaping). Table set: vehicle speed < cal 0x20A64 (4 km/h) -> Low Speed set; else FFF8A9A2 bit 7 (latched while FFF8A63E bit 2; not identified) clear -> Normal set, set -> Alternate set. The torque monitor (0x187104) reads the same bytes through its own descriptor. Values in the 16000-centred torque unit; steps in Nm per pass. Same data bytes are also referenced by descriptor(s) 05F50C. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Path B Coolant Rise
table.description:
Part of the condition that lets Path B tip-in smoothing act, based on how much the coolant has warmed since start.
Details: When used: only matters with Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B set. Gate of Path B (0x0BBA32..0x0BBA90, read): the warm condition is FFF80B96 >= cal 0x22A0C (16384 = 0 degC) and coolant at start FFF89224 >= cal 0x22A0A (50 = 0 degC, degC + 50 unit); while it holds, Path B stays available if clamp(FFF80B96 - FFF89224) < this(FFF89224). FFF80B96 is a copy of coolant FFF88A44 taken by 0x082F7E / 0x082FB0 under start/state conditions (read); which moment it captures is not identified. Data = coolant difference in the 409.6-per-degC unit offset by 0x4000 (40 degC) (read). 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module 0x0BE694 at 0x0BF612 with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1, pedal FFF8AF00 and, as stack argument 11, cal 0x23704 bit 6; argument order checked in the disassembly). Path B (read, 0x0BB958 0x0BCEFE..0x0BCF96): a second rise-shaping path evaluated after the main one. It acts only while Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B (cal 0x23704 bit 6) is set, FFF88BAA >= cal 0x22A08 (80; hysteresis 0x22A09), rpm FFF8CD54 <= cal 0x22A04, and the Path B gate is open. The gate is open unless all three hold: FFF8AE64 <= Target Torque Rise Path B Pedal-Released Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), FFF8AF1C <=...Path B Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), and (the warm condition is false or FFF80B96 - coolant at start FFF89224 >=...Path B Coolant Rise(FFF89224)). Step1B = (Path B Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear cal 0x229F0 + 2(g-1) x Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier (Path B)(FFF8AF00) / 65025; Step2B the same with cal 0x229FA.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Path B Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; gear cals apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set. With prev = FFF8AEC6: if prev + Step2B >= Path B Stage 2 Torque the shaped value becomes prev + Step2B; then, if prev + Step1B < Path B Stage 2 Torque, it becomes max(Path B Start Torque, prev + Step1B); otherwise the main path's value stands. Whenever the cal bit is set, a request below Path B Start Torque also passes unshaped. Tables are selected by drive mode FFF8A8C1 (2, 3, 4, other = 1) and, for the step tables, by AT/CVT Coding as in the main path. The torque monitor 0x1877B4 reads the same data bytes and is passed the same cal bit, so it stays consistent. The torque monitor 0x1877B4 reads the same data bytes through its own descriptor (05FA54), so it stays consistent. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Stage 2 Torque (Path B, Drive Mode 1, Default)

table.name: Rev Limit RPM
table.description:
The rev limit: above it the ECU cuts fuel to all four cylinders on every firing and closes the throttle; spark is not cut or retarded. To move the limit, set this, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 lower.
Details: When used: always. The rev limit: above this rpm the rev latch sets and the ECU enters limit state 0x0B (part 1). It is also the level stage 2 of the throttle cap holds above (part 5). Rev limiter and limit-state cuts (LF75404S; read unless marked). The rev limiter is a fuel cut. (1) Limit state, 0x0BE140 (10 ms torque module 0x0BE694): the rev latch FFF8416A sets when rpm FFF8CD54 > Rev Limit RPM (the comparator FFF84169 then uses Rev Limit Reset RPM) and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Reset RPM and MAP FFF88FF4 < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. The overboost latch FFF84167 sets when MAP >= Overboost Limit (compensated, FFF8A851) + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) and releases below that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). Either latch gives limit state FFF8A639 = 0x0B. Priority: not running = 1, FFF8A640 bit 0 = 0x19, latch FFF8416C = 0x1B (cals 0x22FB2-0x22FBC, not decoded), then 0x0B, then the vehicle-speed latch = 0x0C (see Vehicle Speed Limit). (2) Full-cut latch, 0x0BAE98: FFF840C4 sets when rpm >= Rev Limit Full Cut RPM and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM and MAP < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. In state 0x0B the final torque cap FFF8AE54 (0x0B9DC8) is limited to FFF8AE8A: zero indicated torque (32000 - losses FFF8AF62) while this latch or the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) is set, otherwise FFF8AF3A = the current air torque minus losses, i.e. no reduction. (3) Fuel: 0x0C4BA0 turns the cap into the torque ratio FFF8A64F; in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C and 0x18-0x1B, 0x0C1AC8 turns the ratio into the number of cylinders to cut FFF8A643 (Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio thresholds; a zero cap gives 4). Once per combustion event (crank-synchronous list 0x07D0E0) 0x0C4B84 makes a cut decision FFF8A648 from the count and the last three decisions (4 = every event, 3 = three in four, 2 = every second, 1 = one in four; the pattern is in code, not a cal). 0x0C88C8 (list 0x07D1C2) latches it into the cut flag of the cylinder being scheduled (FFF8A6F5-FFF8A6F8). For a flagged cylinder the fuel time is 0 (0x0D1D7C/0x0D1FB8) and both start angles are 0x1FE (0x0CB394/0x0CB604), which the injector driver 0x1DCA04 treats as no pulse. So the cut is a true injector cut, all four cylinders, every event. (4) Spark is neither cut nor retarded: the coil scheduler 0x1DB804 only checks FFF8C6F4 (set at the first injection after sync, cleared only on stop), and with Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut set 0x0DD568 uses the normal spark target FFF8A72A in state 0x0B instead of Torque Reduction Spark Retard. (5) Throttle: with Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable set 0x0BDA84 caps the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C in state 0x0B by 0x0BAFA8: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Stage 1) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM (held while > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold)) or MAP FFF8AF70 > Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 MAP (held while > Stage 1 Reset MAP); else (Stage 2) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) (held while > Rev Limit RPM) or MAP > Stage 1 Reset MAP (held while > Stage 2 Hold MAP); else (Base). The torque monitor (0x186F0C) repeats this with the same data. A hard cut; stage 2 is never selected because its thresholds equal stage 1's. To move the limit, set Rev Limit RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 rpm lower. Setting the Full Cut pair above Rev Limit RPM gives a throttle-only soft stage between them (inferred). The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. Confidence: read.

table.description:
Set it to your rev limit with the other Rev Limit rpm values.
Details: When used: always. During state 0x0B the throttle-side cap switches to Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Stage 1) above this rpm (part 5). Rev limiter and limit-state cuts (LF75404S; read unless marked). The rev limiter is a fuel cut. (1) Limit state, 0x0BE140 (10 ms torque module 0x0BE694): the rev latch FFF8416A sets when rpm FFF8CD54 > Rev Limit RPM (the comparator FFF84169 then uses Rev Limit Reset RPM) and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Reset RPM and MAP FFF88FF4 < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. The overboost latch FFF84167 sets when MAP >= Overboost Limit (compensated, FFF8A851) + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) and releases below that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). Either latch gives limit state FFF8A639 = 0x0B. Priority: not running = 1, FFF8A640 bit 0 = 0x19, latch FFF8416C = 0x1B (cals 0x22FB2-0x22FBC, not decoded), then 0x0B, then the vehicle-speed latch = 0x0C (see Vehicle Speed Limit). (2) Full-cut latch, 0x0BAE98: FFF840C4 sets when rpm >= Rev Limit Full Cut RPM and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM and MAP < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. In state 0x0B the final torque cap FFF8AE54 (0x0B9DC8) is limited to FFF8AE8A: zero indicated torque (32000 - losses FFF8AF62) while this latch or the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) is set, otherwise FFF8AF3A = the current air torque minus losses, i.e. no reduction. (3) Fuel: 0x0C4BA0 turns the cap into the torque ratio FFF8A64F; in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C and 0x18-0x1B, 0x0C1AC8 turns the ratio into the number of cylinders to cut FFF8A643 (Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio thresholds; a zero cap gives 4). Once per combustion event (crank-synchronous list 0x07D0E0) 0x0C4B84 makes a cut decision FFF8A648 from the count and the last three decisions (4 = every event, 3 = three in four, 2 = every second, 1 = one in four; the pattern is in code, not a cal). 0x0C88C8 (list 0x07D1C2) latches it into the cut flag of the cylinder being scheduled (FFF8A6F5-FFF8A6F8). For a flagged cylinder the fuel time is 0 (0x0D1D7C/0x0D1FB8) and both start angles are 0x1FE (0x0CB394/0x0CB604), which the injector driver 0x1DCA04 treats as no pulse. So the cut is a true injector cut, all four cylinders, every event. (4) Spark is neither cut nor retarded: the coil scheduler 0x1DB804 only checks FFF8C6F4 (set at the first injection after sync, cleared only on stop), and with Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut set 0x0DD568 uses the normal spark target FFF8A72A in state 0x0B instead of Torque Reduction Spark Retard. (5) Throttle: with Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable set 0x0BDA84 caps the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C in state 0x0B by 0x0BAFA8: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Stage 1) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM (held while > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold)) or MAP FFF8AF70 > Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 MAP (held while > Stage 1 Reset MAP); else (Stage 2) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) (held while > Rev Limit RPM) or MAP > Stage 1 Reset MAP (held while > Stage 2 Hold MAP); else (Base). The torque monitor (0x186F0C) repeats this with the same data. A hard cut; stage 2 is never selected because its thresholds equal stage 1's. To move the limit, set Rev Limit RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 rpm lower. Setting the Full Cut pair above Rev Limit RPM gives a throttle-only soft stage between them (inferred). The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. Confidence: read.

table.name: Maximum Torque (IAT)
table.description:
Maximum target torque by rpm and intake air temperature. The ECU uses the lowest of this, Maximum Torque (DAM) and other limits, and the result drives the boost target.
Details: 0x0BD078 -> FFF8AEC8: the limited target FFF8AEC2 = min(FFF8AEA6, this(rpm FFF8CD54, IAT FFF88A48), Maximum Torque (DAM), FFF8AF0C, FFF8AE5A) (read). Target-torque chain (0x0BE694, read): Requested Torque sets -> drive-mode select (0x0BDBD8) -> FFF8AEFC -> + additive torque (0x0BB53C) -> external/fault limit (0x0BB1AC) -> FFF8AEA6 -> min with Maximum Torque (IAT), Maximum Torque (DAM) and two other limits (0x0BD078) -> FFF8AEC2 -> gear-dependent rate shaping (0x0BB958) -> FFF8AEBE -> max with a floor (0x0BD3F0) -> FFF8AEC6 -> max with idle/cruise floors (0x0BB4A8) -> FFF8AEAA -> + 059D18 offset (0x0BD404) -> FFF8AECA, the target-torque axis of Target Boost and the wastegate duty tables. Confidence: read.

table.name: Maximum Torque (DAM)
table.description:
Maximum target torque by DAM (knock learning) and rpm, in the same lowest-wins limit as Maximum Torque (IAT). Losing DAM lowers the torque target and so the boost target.
Details: 0x0BD078 -> FFF8AEDE: second limit in the same min() (read). Row input FFF8A637 = FFF811AE copied by 0x0BD67C, the DAM-like knock value (x16); columns rpm. Target-torque chain (0x0BE694, read): Requested Torque sets -> drive-mode select (0x0BDBD8) -> FFF8AEFC -> + additive torque (0x0BB53C) -> external/fault limit (0x0BB1AC) -> FFF8AEA6 -> min with Maximum Torque (IAT), Maximum Torque (DAM) and two other limits (0x0BD078) -> FFF8AEC2 -> gear-dependent rate shaping (0x0BB958) -> FFF8AEBE -> max with a floor (0x0BD3F0) -> FFF8AEC6 -> max with idle/cruise floors (0x0BB4A8) -> FFF8AEAA -> + 059D18 offset (0x0BD404) -> FFF8AECA, the target-torque axis of Target Boost and the wastegate duty tables. Confidence: read.

table.name: Overboost Limit
table.description:
Overboost limit by rpm, compensated for baro and intake temperature like the boost target. Boost 26.7 kPa over it for 2 s sets the overboost flag, and 33 kPa over it starts the overboost cut (throttle cap, then a full fuel cut once the flag is set). Raise it when raising boost targets. Note: the boost-control pressure reading stops at about 269 kPa absolute, so an Overboost Limit above about 236 kPa absolute (269 minus the 33 kPa cut margin) can never trigger the overboost cut.
Details: When used: always. 0x1087D4 (20 ms boost task) -> FFF8A850 (raw) and FFF8A851 = (raw + 13.3) x f - 13, f = the boost target's baro/IAT factor FFF8B3B2/32768. Two overboost reactions use FFF8A851 (read): (a) 0x0C0FE0 (10 ms): MAP FFF88FF4 >= this + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay passes in a row sets the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6, cleared when MAP <= this + Overboost Flag Reset Margin; (b) 0x0BE140: MAP >= this + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) puts the ECU in limit state 0x0B, which caps the throttle at once. The flag makes the state-0x0B cut a full fuel cut on all four cylinders (see Rev Limit RPM); on its own, outside state 0x0B, it reduces nothing. It also feeds a diagnostic 0x1B8310. Raise it with Target Boost. Confidence: read.

Once per combustion event (crank-synchronous list 0x07D0E0) 0x0C4B84 makes a cut decision FFF8A648 from the count and the last three decisions (4 = every event, 3 = three in four, 2 = every second, 1 = one in four; the pattern is in code, not a cal). 0x0C88C8 (list 0x07D1C2) latches it into the cut flag of the cylinder being scheduled (FFF8A6F5-FFF8A6F8). For a flagged cylinder the fuel time is 0 (0x0D1D7C/0x0D1FB8) and both start angles are 0x1FE (0x0CB394/0x0CB604), which the injector driver 0x1DCA04 treats as no pulse. Setting the Full Cut pair above Rev Limit RPM gives a throttle-only soft stage between them (inferred). The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable
table.description:
Lets the rev limiter and overboost cut close the throttle (the Rev/Boost Limit Torque tables).
With this bit set, 0x0BDA84 replaces the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C by the Rev/Boost Limit Torque cap FFF8AE8C (0x0BAFA8) in limit state 0x0B; the torque monitor 0x189488 reads the same bit (read). Cleared, the rev limiter and the overboost cut become fuel-only: no throttle closing during the cut (inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: Overboost Margin
table.description:
How far above Overboost Limit boost must be before overboost time is counted toward the overboost flag, which makes the overboost cut a full fuel cut.
Details: When used: always. 0x0C0FE0: overboost time is counted while MAP FFF88FF4 >= Overboost Limit + this (read); after Overboost Delay the flag FFF8A63A bit 6 sets. The flag makes the limit-state overboost cut (Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State)) a full fuel cut on all four cylinders; it has no effect outside that state (read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Overboost Delay
table.description:
How long boost must stay above Overboost Limit plus Overboost Margin before the overboost flag sets and the overboost cut becomes a full fuel cut.
Details: When used: always. 0x0C0FE0: consecutive 10 ms passes with MAP >= Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin before the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 sets (read); the count restarts when MAP drops below that level. The flag turns the limit-state overboost cut into a full fuel cut on all four cylinders (see Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State)). Confidence: read.

table.name: Overboost Flag Reset Margin
table.description:
Once set, the overboost flag clears only when boost falls to Overboost Limit plus this.
Details: When used: always. 0x0C0FE0 (read): once set, the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) stays set until MAP FFF88FF4 <= Overboost Limit + this. The flag forces the zero torque cap in the overboost/rev cut state (0x0BAE98 -> FFF8AE8A, applied in limit state 0x0B; Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State)) and also feeds 0x1B8310 (0x1B828C / 0x1B83CC, the overboost diagnostic, inferred in my research notes), so this margin also sets how long that monitor sees overboost. Confidence: read.

table.name: Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State)
table.description:
Boost above Overboost Limit plus this enters the overboost cut state: the throttle is capped at once, and fuel to all cylinders is cut only if the 2-second overboost flag is also set.
Details: When used: always. Overboost latch FFF84167 (0x0BE140, read): sets when MAP FFF88FF4 >= Overboost Limit (the baro/IAT-compensated FFF8A851) + this, and releases when MAP < that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). While set (and no higher state) the limit state FFF8A639 is 0x0B, the same state as the rev limiter (see Rev Limit RPM). In that state the throttle-side request is capped at once (Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Base) by rpm, or the stage tables above 256 kPa abs); fuel is cut on all four cylinders every event only once the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 is also set or rpm reaches Rev Limit Full Cut RPM; spark is not retarded. When MAP falls below the release level the state ends and fuel returns even if the flag is still set (inferred from the state gating, read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State)
table.description:
How far boost must fall below the overboost cut level before the overboost cut state ends.
Details: When used: always. Subtracted from the overboost latch level while the latch FFF84167 is set (0x0BE208-0x0BE222, read): the overboost cut state 0x0B releases when MAP FFF88FF4 < Overboost Limit + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) - this. See Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) for what the state does. Confidence: read.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit
table.description:
Vehicle speed limiter. It needs this speed, Vehicle Speed Limit Minimum RPM and Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed to act, and then cuts fuel to all cylinders without closing the throttle.
Details: When used: always. Set speed of the vehicle-speed latch FFF84168 (0x0BE140, read): it sets when vehicle speed FFF99835 >= this minus Vehicle Speed Limit Offset and engine speed FFF8CD5C (rpm/25) >= Vehicle Speed Limit Minimum RPM, and holds until speed is below that level and MAP FFF88FF4 <= Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP. While it is set (and no higher state), the limit state FFF8A639 is 0x0C. State 0x0C does not reduce torque by itself: the final torque cap FFF8AE54 is limited (0x0B9DC8) to FFF8AF1A (0x0C058C), which is zero torque only while speed >= Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed (then all four injectors are cut every event through the cylinder-cut count FFF8A643, see Rev Limit RPM part 3), otherwise the current torque. There is no throttle cap in state 0x0C (0x0BDA84 caps only state 0x0B) and the spark stays on its normal target (Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Speed Limit). A working speed limiter needs this, Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed and Vehicle Speed Limit Minimum RPM (inferred); it is then a hard fuel cut. Limit-state priority: not running 1, FFF8A640 bit 0 0x19, latch FFF8416C 0x1B, rev/overboost 0x0B, speed 0x0C (0x0BE37E-0x0BE476, read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Minimum RPM
table.description:
The speed limiter only starts at or above this engine speed.
Details: When used: always. The vehicle-speed latch (state 0x0C, see Vehicle Speed Limit) sets only while engine speed FFF8CD5C (rpm/25) >= this (0x0BE1E8-0x0BE1F4, read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed
table.description:
Speed at which the active speed limiter cuts fuel to all cylinders; without it the limiter does nothing.
Details: When used: only in limit state 0x0C (vehicle-speed latch, see Vehicle Speed Limit). 0x0C058C (read): latch FFF84188 sets when vehicle speed FFF99835 >= this (minus Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed Hysteresis while above it) and holds until speed is below and MAP <= Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP; while set, FFF8AF1A = zero torque, which in state 0x0C cuts fuel on all four cylinders every event (0x0B9DC8, 0x0C1AC8). Without it state 0x0C reduces nothing. Confidence: read.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed Hysteresis
table.description:
How far speed must fall below Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed before the fuel cut ends.
Details: When used: only in limit state 0x0C. Subtracted from Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed after a pass at or above it (FFF8418A), so the full cut holds down to that speed (0x0C058C, read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Offset
table.description:
Subtracted from Vehicle Speed Limit to give the speed where the limiter state starts; it is not a release hysteresis.
Details: When used: always. Subtracted from Vehicle Speed Limit in the set test of the speed latch FFF84168 (0x0BE1CA-0x0BE1E4, read), so the latch sets at Vehicle Speed Limit minus this. It is not a release hysteresis: the latch releases when speed is below the same level and MAP <= Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP (read). See Vehicle Speed Limit for what the latch does (state 0x0C). Confidence: read.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP
table.description:
The speed limiter cannot release while manifold pressure is above this.
Details: When used: always. Neither the vehicle-speed latch FFF84168 (0x0BE140) nor the speed full-cut latch FFF84188 (0x0C058C) releases while MAP FFF88FF4 is above this, even below its speed (read). Plays the role Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP has for the rev limiter. Confidence: read.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP Hysteresis
table.description:
Hysteresis on Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP.
Details: When used: always. Added to Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP after a pass with MAP at or below it (FFF84165 / FFF84189), saturating (0x0BE270-0x0BE28E, 0x0C058C, read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold Hysteresis
table.description:
Extra speed needed above Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold before the switch.
Added to Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold (saturating at 255) while the normal (low-speed) pair is in use, so the speed must exceed threshold + this to switch to the high-speed pair (0x0BAEEA-0x0BAF04). Rev limiter and limit-state cuts (LF75404S; read unless marked). The rev limiter is a fuel cut. (1) Limit state, 0x0BE140 (10 ms torque module 0x0BE694): the rev latch FFF8416A sets when rpm FFF8CD54 > Rev Limit RPM (the comparator FFF84169 then uses Rev Limit Reset RPM) and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Reset RPM and MAP FFF88FF4 < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. The overboost latch FFF84167 sets when MAP >= Overboost Limit (compensated, FFF8A851) + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) and releases below that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). Either latch gives limit state FFF8A639 = 0x0B. Priority: not running = 1, FFF8A640 bit 0 = 0x19, latch FFF8416C = 0x1B (cals 0x22FB2-0x22FBC, not decoded), then 0x0B, then the vehicle-speed latch = 0x0C (see Vehicle Speed Limit). (2) Full-cut latch, 0x0BAE98: FFF840C4 sets when rpm >= Rev Limit Full Cut RPM and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM and MAP < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. In state 0x0B the final torque cap FFF8AE54 (0x0B9DC8) is limited to FFF8AE8A: zero indicated torque (32000 - losses FFF8AF62) while this latch or the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) is set, otherwise FFF8AF3A = the current air torque minus losses, i.e. no reduction. (3) Fuel: 0x0C4BA0 turns the cap into the torque ratio FFF8A64F; in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C and 0x18-0x1B, 0x0C1AC8 turns the ratio into the number of cylinders to cut FFF8A643 (Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio thresholds; a zero cap gives 4). Once per combustion event (crank-synchronous list 0x07D0E0) 0x0C4B84 makes a cut decision FFF8A648 from the count and the last three decisions (4 = every event, 3 = three in four, 2 = every second, 1 = one in four; the pattern is in code, not a cal). 0x0C88C8 (list 0x07D1C2) latches it into the cut flag of the cylinder being scheduled (FFF8A6F5-FFF8A6F8). For a flagged cylinder the fuel time is 0 (0x0D1D7C/0x0D1FB8) and both start angles are 0x1FE (0x0CB394/0x0CB604), which the injector driver 0x1DCA04 treats as no pulse. So the cut is a true injector cut, all four cylinders, every event. (4) Spark is neither cut nor retarded: the coil scheduler 0x1DB804 only checks FFF8C6F4 (set at the first injection after sync, cleared only on stop), and with Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut set 0x0DD568 uses the normal spark target FFF8A72A in state 0x0B instead of Torque Reduction Spark Retard. (5) Throttle: with Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable set 0x0BDA84 caps the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C in state 0x0B by 0x0BAFA8: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Stage 1) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM (held while > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold)) or MAP FFF8AF70 > Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 MAP (held while > Stage 1 Reset MAP); else (Stage 2) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) (held while > Rev Limit RPM) or MAP > Stage 1 Reset MAP (held while > Stage 2 Hold MAP); else (Base). The torque monitor (0x186F0C) repeats this with the same data. A hard cut; stage 2 is never selected because its thresholds equal stage 1's. To move the limit, set Rev Limit RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 rpm lower. Setting the Full Cut pair above Rev Limit RPM gives a throttle-only soft stage between them (inferred). The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. Confidence: read.

table.name: Fail-Safe Rev Limit (Rail Pressure Fault)
table.description:
Rev limit used only while a fuel-rail pressure fault is active: above it fuel to all cylinders is cut.
Details: When used: only while fault flag FFF88EDA bit 5 or 7 (set by 0x080B96 from rail-pressure monitor bits FFF89BDE 0-3, next to the P0087/P0088 bits, inferred) or FFF88E2C bit 2 (pending P0192/P0193, rail pressure sensor) is set. 0x0C1AC8 (read): limit FFF8AF4C = the lowest of this and the other active Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (65535 when none), and FFF8AF4A = max(FFF8AF4C, idle target FFF8B236 + Fail-Safe Rev Limit Minimum Above Idle Target). While rpm >= FFF8AF4A (release Fail-Safe Rev Limit Hysteresis lower) the cylinder-cut count FFF8A643 is forced to 4: all four injectors are cut every event, in any limit state (same injector path as Rev Limit RPM part 3). Precisely (0x0C1AC8, read): while the fail-safe comparator FFF841F9 is set the count is cal 0x38248, not a literal 4; and it is overridden when FFF89BFE bit 2 is set (the count then comes from cals 0x23D58-0x23D5F, not yet defined). Confidence: read.

table.name: Fail-Safe Rev Limit (Injector Driver Fault)
table.description:
Rev limit used only while an injector-driver fault has put the fuel system in its low-pressure fail-safe: above it fuel to all cylinders is cut.
Details: When used: only while FFF88F4A bit 1 is set (0x080B96, from the P062D / P2146 injector-driver monitors; the same flag selects Rail Pressure Fail-Safe Target A and the Injector Latency Adder, read). Otherwise as Fail-Safe Rev Limit (Rail Pressure Fault): rpm at or above the lowest active fail-safe limit cuts fuel on all four cylinders (0x0C1AC8, read). Precisely (0x0C1AC8, read): while the fail-safe comparator FFF841F9 is set the count is cal 0x38248, not a literal 4; and it is overridden when FFF89BFE bit 2 is set (the count then comes from cals 0x23D58-0x23D5F, not yet defined). Confidence: read.

table.name: Fail-Safe Rev Limit (Unused Fault Flag)
table.description: Details: When used: only while FFF88F4A bit 2 is set. Otherwise as Fail-Safe Rev Limit (Rail Pressure Fault) (0x0C1AC8, read). Precisely (0x0C1AC8, read): while the fail-safe comparator FFF841F9 is set the count is cal 0x38248, not a literal 4; and it is overridden when FFF89BFE bit 2 is set (the count then comes from cals 0x23D58-0x23D5F, not yet defined). Confidence: read.

table.name: Fail-Safe Rev Limit Hysteresis
table.description:
How far rpm must fall below an active fail-safe rev limit before fuel returns.
Details: When used: only while a fail-safe rev limit is active. Once the fail-safe cut is on (FFF841F9), it stays on until rpm drops this far below the limit FFF8AF4A (0x0C1C72-0x0C1C8C, read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Fail-Safe Rev Limit Minimum Above Idle Target
table.description:
A fail-safe rev limit is never set lower than the idle target plus this.
Details: When used: only while a fail-safe rev limit is active. The fail-safe limit is never below the idle target FFF8B236 plus this (0x0C1C02-0x0C1C16, read; saturating). Confidence: read.

table.name: Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Speed Limit
table.description:
Keeps normal spark timing during the vehicle-speed limiter.
Same as Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut for limit state 0x0C (vehicle-speed limiter) (0x0DD568, read). Bits 5 and 4 do the same for states 0x19 and 0x1A (not decoded); state 0x1B always uses the normal target. Leave set. Confidence: read.

table.name: Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut
table.description:
Keeps normal spark timing during the rev limiter and overboost cut instead of retarding it.
In limit state 0x0B (rev limiter, overboost cut) 0x0DD568 sets the spark angle FFF8A76A to the normal spark target FFF8A72A instead of base timing FFF8A645 minus Torque Reduction Spark Retard (asm 0x0DD5F8-0x0DD62A, read), so the limiter does not retard the spark. Cleared, the full cut would ask for about 34 degrees of retard (ratio floor cal 0x2FDE4 = 102, inferred from the table). Leave set. Confidence: read.

table.name: External Torque Limit Baro Factor
table.description:
Air-density correction (barometric part) applied to a torque limit received over CAN, probably from the transmission controller.
Details: When used: only with cal 0x20F04 = 1, 2 or 3. Barometric part of the air density factor FFF8AE9E. 0x0BB0A4 (read): FFF8AE9E = Baro Factor(FFF88A36) x IAT Factor(FFF88A48) / 16384. 0x0BB0EC / 0x0BB118 copy it to FFF8AEA0 / FFF8AEA2 only when cal 0x20F04 is 1 or 3 / 1 or 2 and FFF88E28 bit 2 / FFF88E2A bit 0 are clear, else 16384 (x1.0). FFF8AEA2 divides the external (CAN) torque limit in 0x0BB1AC: limit = 16000 + FFF88DF6 x 160 x 16384 / FFF8AEA2 (read; the limit byte is inferred to come from another controller, my research notes); FFF8AEA0 goes to 0x116158. The product is the air density relative to 101.3 kPa and 25 degC. p16 (read): FFF88DF6 = CAN 0x149 byte 4 (mailbox 1, TCM frame group: decoding gated by the U0101/U0402 status and forced off by the MT coding FFF886AB b7, which then loads cal 0x572D0), decoder 0x085D20. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: External Torque Limit IAT Factor
table.description:
Air-density correction (intake temperature part) applied to a torque limit received over CAN, probably from the transmission controller.
Details: When used: only with cal 0x20F04 = 1, 2 or 3. Intake-air-temperature part of the air density factor FFF8AE9E. 0x0BB0A4 (read): FFF8AE9E = Baro Factor(FFF88A36) x IAT Factor(FFF88A48) / 16384. 0x0BB0EC / 0x0BB118 copy it to FFF8AEA0 / FFF8AEA2 only when cal 0x20F04 is 1 or 3 / 1 or 2 and FFF88E28 bit 2 / FFF88E2A bit 0 are clear, else 16384 (x1.0). FFF8AEA2 divides the external (CAN) torque limit in 0x0BB1AC: limit = 16000 + FFF88DF6 x 160 x 16384 / FFF8AEA2 (read; the limit byte is inferred to come from another controller, my research notes); FFF8AEA0 goes to 0x116158. The product is the air density relative to 101.3 kPa and 25 degC. p16 (read): FFF88DF6 = CAN 0x149 byte 4 (mailbox 1, TCM frame group: decoding gated by the U0101/U0402 status and forced off by the MT coding FFF886AB b7, which then loads cal 0x572D0), decoder 0x085D20. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio (1 Cylinder)
table.description:
When a cut state asks for less torque than this share of the engine's current torque, one cylinder in four is cut. Also sets the first decel fuel cut stage.
Details: When used: in the cut limit states (decel fuel cut, rev/overboost/speed cuts). Below this torque ratio at least 1 cylinder is cut. 0x0C1AC8 (read): in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x18 (unless FFF8A638 = 2) and 0x19-0x1B the torque ratio FFF8A64F (capped / unreduced torque, 0x0C4BA0) is compared with four thresholds: cylinders cut FFF8A643 = 0 if the ratio >= the 1-cylinder threshold, 1 if >= the 2-cylinder threshold, 2 if >= the 3-cylinder threshold, 3 if >= the 4-cylinder threshold, else 4 (each threshold minus Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio Hysteresis while it is crossed). Once per event 0x0C4B84 then skips n of every 4 injections. The same four cals set the torque level of each decel fuel cut stage (0x0B9EF0), so changing them also changes the decel cut. The rev limiter and the overboost full cut use a zero cap (ratio 0, 4 cylinders) and do not depend on them. Further gating in 0x0C1AC8 (read): the ratio comparison also runs outside those states while FFF8A63B bit 0 or FFF899EC bit 1 / bit 4 is set; while FFF89BFE bit 2 is set (a fault latch from 0x09FE44, meaning not decoded) the count is instead taken from cals 0x23D58-0x23D5F by rpm FFF8CD62 and speed FFF99835 (not yet defined) and overrides both this ratio and the Fail-Safe Rev Limit; and with engine state FFF99844 = 4, or FFF8A65F bit 7 set while FFF89066 bit 0 is clear, the count is cal 0x38248 (the cylinder count, 4), i.e. all cylinders. Confidence: read.

Details: When used: with the four Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio thresholds. table.name: Throttle Opening Map Reference Torque
table.description:
Torque by rpm that counts as 100 % in the Throttle Opening from Target Torque maps: at or above it they give wide-open throttle. Raise it together with Full-Load Reference Brake Torque for a higher-torque tune. Edit together with Throttle Opening Map Reference Torque (Monitor).
Details: 0x0C0010 (read): normalises the target brake torque FFF8AECA into the column index of the eight Throttle Opening from Target Torque tables (idx = 255 x AECA / this); at or above this torque every table gives 100 % (wide open). Raising it with 05A054 keeps the WOT point of the opening tables and the full-load excess term (0x0BDAA0) together. Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Opening Map Reference Torque (Monitor)
table.description:
Throttle-monitor copy of Throttle Opening Map Reference Torque. Keep identical to the main table, or expect the monitor to disagree with the main path (plausibility fault inferred).
Details: When used: always, in the throttle monitor. 0x18A790 (from 0x189DF0, read) is the monitor copy of 0x0C0010: column index = 255 x monitor target torque FFF8BBC8 / 05FBB0(rpm), the eight tables are looked up on (rpm FFF8CD54, index) and blended with the same TGV FFF8B3E8 and EGR FFF8B290 weights into FFF8BBEE, the monitor's opening request. This is the normaliser of the index (the copy of 059DD0; data 0x045336, axis 0x04530C). The throttle-monitor module (0x18620C / 0x189DF0 / 0x186290, run from 0x07C408 on one pass in four, each right after its primary 0x0C3D14 / 0x0BE694 / 0x0C3E34, read) repeats the primary computation into its own FFF8BBxx variables with a separate copy of the data and axes. Edit both together, or expect the monitor to disagree with the main path (plausibility fault inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Closed)
table.description:
This is where part-throttle feel is set: the commanded throttle opening is essentially this map (by rpm and target torque) plus the idle air. Used with the TGVs closed and no EGR (blended by TGV position and EGR amount). Edit together with Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Closed, Monitor).
Details: 0x0C0010 (called from torque module 0x0BE694): column index = 255 x target torque FFF8AECA / Throttle Opening Map Reference Torque 059DD0(rpm); result blended by TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 and EGR realisation FFF8B290 (min 256) into FFF8AF12, which 059D2C/059D64/05A148/05A0BC turn back into the commanded throttle, so at part throttle the commanded opening is essentially this map plus the idle area (read, numeric check in TD.md). Weight (1 - TGV open) x (1 - EGR) on the normal (non-cruise) path. THIS is where part-throttle feel is set: the commanded opening is about this table plus the idle area (end-to-end model, my research notes). Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Closed, Monitor)
table.description:
Throttle-monitor copy of Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Closed). Make the same edit here as on the main table, or expect a plausibility fault (inferred).
Details: When used: as the original, in the throttle monitor. 0x18A790 (from 0x189DF0, read) is the monitor copy of 0x0C0010: column index = 255 x monitor target torque FFF8BBC8 / 05FBB0(rpm), the eight tables are looked up on (rpm FFF8CD54, index) and blended with the same TGV FFF8B3E8 and EGR FFF8B290 weights into FFF8BBEE, the monitor's opening request. Copy of Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Closed) 059DDC (data 0x044EEC, own axes). If you edit the part-throttle opening map, make the same edit here. The throttle-monitor module (0x18620C / 0x189DF0 / 0x186290, run from 0x07C408 on one pass in four, each right after its primary 0x0C3D14 / 0x0BE694 / 0x0C3E34, read) repeats the primary computation into its own FFF8BBxx variables with a separate copy of the data and axes. Edit both together, or expect the monitor to disagree with the main path (plausibility fault inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Open)
table.description:
This is where part-throttle feel is set: the commanded throttle opening is essentially this map (by rpm and target torque) plus the idle air. Used with the TGVs open and no EGR; probably the table a warm car mostly uses at part load. Edit together with Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Open, Monitor).
Details: 0x0C0010 (called from torque module 0x0BE694): column index = 255 x target torque FFF8AECA / Throttle Opening Map Reference Torque 059DD0(rpm); result blended by TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 and EGR realisation FFF8B290 (min 256) into FFF8AF12, which 059D2C/059D64/05A148/05A0BC turn back into the commanded throttle, so at part throttle the commanded opening is essentially this map plus the idle area (read, numeric check in TD.md). Weight TGV open x (1 - EGR) on the normal path; TGV polarity from FFF8B3E8 (read). The table a warm car at part load mostly uses (inferred). THIS is where part-throttle feel is set: the commanded opening is about this table plus the idle area (end-to-end model, my research notes). Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Open, Monitor)
table.description:
Throttle-monitor copy of Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Open). Make the same edit here as on the main table, or expect a plausibility fault (inferred).
Details: When used: as the original, in the throttle monitor. 0x18A790 (from 0x189DF0, read) is the monitor copy of 0x0C0010: column index = 255 x monitor target torque FFF8BBC8 / 05FBB0(rpm), the eight tables are looked up on (rpm FFF8CD54, index) and blended with the same TGV FFF8B3E8 and EGR FFF8B290 weights into FFF8BBEE, the monitor's opening request. The throttle-monitor module (0x18620C / 0x189DF0 / 0x186290, run from 0x07C408 on one pass in four, each right after its primary 0x0C3D14 / 0x0BE694 / 0x0C3E34, read) repeats the primary computation into its own FFF8BBxx variables with a separate copy of the data and axes. Edit both together, or expect the monitor to disagree with the main path (plausibility fault inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Closed, EGR)
table.description:
This is where part-throttle feel is set: the commanded throttle opening is essentially this map (by rpm and target torque) plus the idle air. Used with the TGVs closed and EGR active (blended by TGV position and EGR amount). Edit together with Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Closed, EGR, Monitor).
Details: 0x0C0010 (called from torque module 0x0BE694): column index = 255 x target torque FFF8AECA / Throttle Opening Map Reference Torque 059DD0(rpm); result blended by TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 and EGR realisation FFF8B290 (min 256) into FFF8AF12, which 059D2C/059D64/05A148/05A0BC turn back into the commanded throttle, so at part throttle the commanded opening is essentially this map plus the idle area (read, numeric check in TD.md). Weight (1 - TGV open) x EGR realisation (B290/256, inferred EGR at target) on the normal path. Typically 1-2 % more opening than 059DDC at mid columns. THIS is where part-throttle feel is set: the commanded opening is about this table plus the idle area (end-to-end model, my research notes). Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Closed, EGR, Monitor)
table.description:
