table.name: Throttle Opening (Required Area)
table.description:
Converts the required throttle area into commanded throttle opening (%). It is the exact inverse of Throttle Area from Opening; keep the two consistent, and edit Throttle Opening (Monitor) too. Leave alone unless the throttle body changes. Area is in mm^2 of effective throttle opening (about 2,150 mm^2 wide open).
Details: 0x0C326C (read): commanded throttle FFF8AF84 = this(max(Throttle Required Area output FFF8AFB4, idle area FFF8AE00)) x 400 / cal 0x3826E (706); 25600 = 100 % (OBD PID 0x4C, SSM 0x15, logger J11). The accelerator pedal FFF88824 x 100/256 is added only with the engine stopped (state 1) or with cal 0x23D0C bit 0 set, never while running. It is the exact inverse of Throttle Area from Opening; keep the two consistent. The same data is also read as 05A170 (idle floor) and 060B10. The monitor copy Throttle Opening (Monitor) (05F3FC, data 0x048EE6) must be edited too. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Throttle Opening (Monitor)
table.description:
Throttle-monitor copy of Throttle Opening (Required Area). Area is in mm^2 of effective throttle opening (about 2,150 mm^2 wide open).
Details: 0x185DD8 (read): separate copy (data 0x048EE6, axis 0x048F06) of Throttle Opening 05A0BC with its own divisor cal 0x48F5A (706). Edit together with 05A0BC. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Required Area
table.description:
Throttle area needed for a given fraction of full-load torque, by rpm. At part throttle it cancels out against Torque Fraction from Throttle Area, so part-throttle feel is set by the Throttle Opening from Target Torque maps instead. If you edit it, edit it with Torque Fraction from Throttle Area and Throttle Required Area (Monitor). Area is in mm^2 of effective throttle opening (about 2,150 mm^2 wide open).
Details: Columns: FFF8AFA8 = (torque request + losses) / (full-load reference torque) x spark compensation (0x0C37D8, read), i.e. the requested fraction of full-load torque (1.0 = full load). 0x0C3408 multiplies the same value by the Boost Limit to form the model's pressure AF8A (read). Rows: rpm. 0x0C4D84 (read): FFF8AFB4 = this(rpm, AFA8) in engine states 1/3/4; during cranking (FFF8906B = 2) FFF8AFB4 = FFF8AED6 instead. AFB4 goes through Throttle Opening (Required Area) in 0x0C326C to the commanded throttle FFF8AF84. The last column (AFA8 = 1.0) is 21468 = wide open in every row. At part throttle this table and Torque Fraction from Throttle Area cancel (one is the inverse of the other within interpolation), so the opening is set by the Throttle Opening from Target Torque tables. If you edit it at all, edit it with Torque Fraction from Throttle Area. The same data is also read as 05A15C. The monitor copy Throttle Required Area (Monitor) (05F3E8, data 0x049552) must be edited too. See my research notes. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Throttle Required Area (Monitor)
table.description:
Throttle-monitor copy of Throttle Required Area. Area is in mm^2 of effective throttle opening (about 2,150 mm^2 wide open).
Details: 0x185DD8 in the throttle monitor 0x186290 (read). Edit together with 05A148. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Area from Opening
table.description:
Converts a throttle opening (%) into throttle area; the exact inverse of Throttle Opening (Required Area). Also gives the required area during cranking. Keep the two consistent; leave alone unless the throttle body changes. Area is in mm^2 of effective throttle opening (about 2,150 mm^2 wide open).
Details: 0x0BD5CC (read): FFF8AED6 = FFF8AE00 + this(FFF8AF12), FFF8ADFC = this(AF12). Its axis in % equals the Throttle Opening data and its data equals the Throttle Opening axis, point for point: it is the exact inverse of 05A0BC. AED6 is the required area used during cranking (0x0C4D84). AF12 comes from 0x0C0010 (inferred: a torque-model opening). Keep consistent with 05A0BC. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Area from Opening (Monitor)
table.description:
Throttle-monitor copy of Throttle Area from Opening. Keep it identical to the main table (and the inverse of Throttle Opening), or expect a plausibility fault (inferred). Area is in mm^2 of effective throttle opening (about 2,150 mm^2 wide open).
Details: When used: always, in the throttle monitor. 0x189458 (read): FFF8BBCA = FFF8BB5E + this(FFF8BBEE), the copy of FFF8AED6 = AE00 + 059D2C(AF12) in 0x0BD5CC; BBEE is the monitor's opening from 0x18A790. Copy of Throttle Area from Opening 059D2C (data 0x044A04, axis 0x044A24). Keep it the inverse of Throttle Opening as for the original. The throttle-monitor module (0x18620C / 0x189DF0 / 0x186290, run from 0x07C408 on one pass in four, each right after its primary 0x0C3D14 / 0x0BE694 / 0x0C3E34, read) repeats the primary computation into its own FFF8BBxx variables with a separate copy of the data and axes. Edit both together, or expect the monitor to disagree with the main path (plausibility fault inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: Torque Fraction from Throttle Area
table.description:
Fraction of full-load torque expected from a given throttle area, by rpm; used to build the throttle torque request. The inverse of Throttle Required Area: if you edit one, edit the other, and Torque Fraction from Throttle Area (Monitor). Area is in mm^2 of effective throttle opening (about 2,150 mm^2 wide open).
Details: 0x0BDB00: FFF8AEE8 = AF64 x this(rpm, AED6), where AED6 = idle area AE00 + 059D2C(air request AF12 from the target torque, 0x0C0010). 0x0B9D08 then makes the throttle brake-torque request AE4C = AEE8 + max(AECA + AF62 - AF64, 0) - AF62, which becomes FFF8AEDA, the numerator source of 0x0C37D8. Shares its data (0x01C6F4) with 059D78. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: read.

table.name: Torque Fraction from Throttle Area (Monitor)
table.description:
Throttle-monitor copy of Torque Fraction from Throttle Area. Keep identical, or expect a plausibility fault (inferred). Area is in mm^2 of effective throttle opening (about 2,150 mm^2 wide open).
Details: When used: always, in the throttle monitor. 0x189500 (read): FFF8BBD2 = BB38 x this(rpm, area FFF8BBCA), the copy of FFF8AEE8 in 0x0BDB00. Copy of Torque Fraction from Throttle Area 059D64 (data 0x046E84, axes 0x047304/0x047334; the original's data is also read as 059D78). The throttle-monitor module (0x18620C / 0x189DF0 / 0x186290, run from 0x07C408 on one pass in four, each right after its primary 0x0C3D14 / 0x0BE694 / 0x0C3E34, read) repeats the primary computation into its own FFF8BBxx variables with a separate copy of the data and axes. Edit both together, or expect the monitor to disagree with the main path (plausibility fault inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Air Request Limit (Coolant)
table.description:
Upper limit, by coolant temperature, on the idle air request (probably from idle speed control) before it is converted to throttle area.
Details: 0x0B9394 (read): FFF8AE00 = 0594F0(min(FFF8B202, this(coolant))). B202 is written by the idle module (call in seg 0x0E0000) and read as the idle airflow request (inferred). Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Air Request to Throttle Area
table.description:
Converts the idle air request into throttle area, which is added to the pedal-driven opening and sets the idle throttle floor. Edit together with Idle Air Request to Throttle Area (Monitor). Area is in mm^2 of effective throttle opening (about 2,150 mm^2 wide open).
Details: 0x0B9394: FFF8AE00 = this(min(B202, Idle Air Request Limit)). AE00 adds to the pedal area (AED6), forms the idle-only area (AED8) and gives the idle throttle floor FFF8AFB8 via 05A170 (0x0C4E18). Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Air Request to Throttle Area (Monitor)
table.description:
Throttle-monitor copy of Idle Air Request to Throttle Area. Keep identical, or expect a plausibility fault (inferred). Area is in mm^2 of effective throttle opening (about 2,150 mm^2 wide open).
Details: When used: always, in the throttle monitor. 0x186ACC (from 0x189DF0, read): FFF8BB5E = this(min(FFF8B202, 05F474(coolant FFF88A44))), the copy of FFF8AE00 in 0x0B9394. Copy of Idle Air Request to Throttle Area 0594F0 (data 0x045380, axis 0x045360). The throttle-monitor module (0x18620C / 0x189DF0 / 0x186290, run from 0x07C408 on one pass in four, each right after its primary 0x0C3D14 / 0x0BE694 / 0x0C3E34, read) repeats the primary computation into its own FFF8BBxx variables with a separate copy of the data and axes. Edit both together, or expect the monitor to disagree with the main path (plausibility fault inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: Start Throttle Opening Add (Coolant)
table.description:
Extra throttle opening during engine start (cranking, car stopped), by coolant temperature. Edit together with Start Throttle Opening Add (Monitor).
Details: 0x0C4E5C (read): FFF8AF9E = this(coolant), clamped to 0xAD3A, added to the idle-area opening while rpm <= 10 (until rpm > 300), speed < 4 km/h, counter FFF88A76 < 200, FFF8A64E bit0 set, bit1 clear, FFF88ADA bit6 set and FFF8A6E7 != 3; AFBA = max(T, AFB8 x 1.057 + AF9E). Monitor copy 05F45C (data 0x048F6A) must be edited too. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: read.

table.name: Start Throttle Opening Add (Monitor)
table.description:
Throttle-monitor copy of Start Throttle Opening Add (Coolant).
Details: 0x186704, the monitor copy of 0x0C4E5C (read). The monitor's four caps 05F450/05F42C/05F438/05F444 share data with 05A17C/05A1A0/05A194/05A188. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Torque Request Cap
table.description:
Cap on the torque request (plus engine losses) that the throttle model works from. Raise it for high-torque tunes.
Details: 0x0C1414 (read): the torque request plus losses that the throttle model works from (FFF8AF24 -> AF2C) is capped at this. Raise it for high-torque tunes; see my research notes. Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Limit (Rail Pressure Deviation)
table.description:
Throttle opening cap by rpm for a rail-pressure-deviation fault mode.
Details: 0x0C4E5C (read): AFBA = min(this(rpm), T) while FFF8A9C9 bit 2 is set; 0x1296A8 sets it when rail pressure FFF88884 exceeds FFF8B9A0 by cal 0x38B00 for 05DA3C(rpm) passes, only if cal 0x38AD4 bit 0 - which is 0. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). p16 (read): 0x1296A8 (<- 0x1289AC <- 0x1E0AE8) counts 20 ms passes. Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Limit (Fuel Pressure Fault)
table.description:
Limp-mode throttle cap by rpm while a fuel pressure fault (P0087, P0088, P0192/P0193 and related codes) is pending; probably meant to limit speed with a high-pressure fuel fault.
Details: 0x0C4E5C (read): AFBA = min(this(rpm), T) while FFF88E2C bit 2 (pending P0192/P0193) or bit 4 (pending P0087, P0088, P062D, P1261-P1264, P0192/P0193) is set (0x080B96, codes by slot). Overridden only by 05A188. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Limit (Injector Circuit Fault)
table.description:
Limp-mode throttle cap by rpm while an injector or injector-driver fault (P1261-P1264, P2146, P062D) is set.
Details: 0x0C4E5C (read): AFBA = min(this(rpm), T) while FFF88F4A bit 3 is set; 0x080B96 sets it for DTC-enabled results in FFF89CD1 bits 1-4 (P1261-P1264), FFF89CF2 bits 6/7 (P2146 mask) and FFF89B67 bits 0-3 (P062D mask). Priority below 05A194/05A188, above 05A17C. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Offset Step IAT Factor
table.description:
Intake-temperature factor on the step rate of a small throttle offset ramp.
Details: 0x0C30F8: FFF8AF7E = cal 0x11ACE x this(IAT) x 05A080(baro) >> 14, the per-pass step of the AF9C throttle offset ramp (0x0C3700). Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). p16 (read): this torque-model function (0x0C3E34 subtree) runs every 10 ms (0x07C408 <- 0x1DFE3C); 'pass' = 10 ms. Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Offset Step Baro Factor
table.description:
Barometric factor on the step rate of a small throttle offset ramp.
Details: 0x0C30F8: second factor of FFF8AF7E (see 05A074). Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Offset Limit IAT Factor
table.description:
Intake-temperature factor on the lower limit of a small throttle offset ramp.
Details: 0x0C3150: FFF8AF80 = cal 0x11AD0 x this(IAT) x 05A098(baro) >> 14, the lower clamp of the AF9C ramp (0x0C3700). Shares data 0x011AEC with 05A0A4. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Offset Limit Baro Factor
table.description:
Barometric factor on the lower limit of a small throttle offset ramp.
Details: 0x0C3150: second factor of FFF8AF80. Shares data 0x011AE4 with 05A0B0. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Offset RPM Threshold (Coolant)
table.description:
Engine speed, by coolant temperature, below which a throttle offset ramp acts (probably a cold / low-speed throttle offset).
Details: 0x0C3700: while this(coolant) (less cal 0x10870 hysteresis) exceeds FFF8AF66 (= engine speed FFF8CE9C), FFF8AF9C follows a ramp (step AF7E, clamped AF80..AF82) or cal 0x11AD2; otherwise cal 0x1080C. AF9C goes to the throttle shaping 0x0C4E5C (a cold/low-speed throttle offset, inferred). Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Throttle Air Spark Compensation Limit
table.description:
Caps, by actual ignition timing, how much the throttle model may add air to make up for retarded timing. Shares data with two other entries: editing one edits all three.
Details: 0x0C37D8 (read): FFF8AFA8 = 32768 x (AF2C/AF64) x min(this(final timing FFF8A642), AF56)/8192; the result indexes Throttle Required Area 05A148. It caps the spark-efficiency air compensation (AF56, normally ~1.0) as a function of the actual final timing. Shares its data (0x0107E8) with 05A124 and 05F414 (0x185FFC): editing one edits all three. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Throttle Limit (Unused Mode)
table.description:
Highest-priority throttle cap by rpm for a fault mode that nothing in this ROM ever sets, so it has no effect.
Details: 0x0C4E5C (read): highest-priority cap, AFBA = min(this(rpm), T) while FFF88F4A bit 2 is set. No code in LF75404S sets that bit (0x080B96 sets bits 0, 1, 3 only), so the table is unused in this image. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Command Rate Term

scaling.units: % per pass (change of throttle command, FFF8AF84 unit)

table.description:
Has no effect: the ECU calculates a value from it that nothing reads.
Details: Unused in this ROM: 0x0B7FA0 (read) writes FFF8ADE8 = 059490(commanded throttle FFF8AF84) + this(|change of FFF8AF84 since the previous pass|); ram_xref finds no reader of FFF8ADE8 (writers 0x0B7EB4 init and 0x0B7FA0 only), so the result is never used. Editing it has no effect. Axis: FFF8AF84 in its own unit, 25600 = 100 % (x/256; corrected in Phase 19). Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Command Term
table.description:
Has no effect: the ECU calculates a value from it that nothing reads.
Details: Unused in this ROM: 0x0B7FA0 (read; called once from 0x0B7E00) writes FFF8ADE8 = this(commanded throttle FFF8AF84) + Throttle Command Rate Term(|change of FFF8AF84 since the previous pass|), capped at 65535. ram_xref finds no reader of FFF8ADE8 (writers 0x0B7EB4 init and 0x0B7FA0 only), and the address appears in the ROM only in those two functions' literal pools (0x0B7E84 caller, 0x0B7EE8 init), so the result is never used. Editing it has no effect. Confidence: read.

table.name: Engine Torque from Load (DAM 1.0, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Engine torque the ECU expects at a given rpm and load; probably shapes the estimated/reported torque, not throttle or boost. This is the full-DAM set, for TGVs closed, no EGR (blended by TGV position and EGR amount).
Details: When used: every pass of the 0x110000 torque module. Weight (1 - TGV open) x (1 - EGR). 0x118318 (DAM 1 set -> FFF8B490) and 0x1186A4 (DAM 0 set -> FFF8B4A2), called from 0x110000 with rpm FFF8CE9C, load FFF8A616, TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 and EGR realisation FFF8B290 (read): closed = TGV-closed x (1 - w) + TGV-closed-EGR x w, open = TGV-open x (1 - w) + TGV-open-EGR x w with w = B290/256, result = closed x (1 - B3E8) + open x B3E8, all above the 16000 zero point (read; same blend as the Throttle Opening from Target Torque tables in 0x0C0010). 0x10ED6C interpolates the two sets by DAM: FFF8B48A = B490 x DAM + B4A2 x (1 - DAM) with FFF811AE = DAM x 16 (read), and 0x118A40 subtracts (B490 - B4A2) x (1 - DAM) from the torque it reports as FFF8B4B2 (0.1 ft-lb, 0.1 Nm, 10000 = 0) (read). So these are the engine torque the ECU expects from the air charge, at full and at zero knock-learning advance (inferred from the DAM interpolation). They do not set the throttle or boost; they shape the estimated/reported engine torque (inferred). Axes: rpm FFF8CE9C x load % FFF8A616. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Full-Load Reference Brake Torque
table.description:
Full-load torque by rpm (density corrected) that the throttle/boost model divides every request by. It does not change part-throttle opening; it moves the full-load handover, target MAP and torque limits (raising it lowers target MAP for the same torque). Keep it equal to Throttle Opening Map Reference Torque from 2000 rpm, and edit the (Monitor) copy too.
Details: CORRECTION (end-to-end model, read arithmetic): at part throttle this table does NOT change the commanded opening (scaling it by 0.9 changes part-throttle opening by 0.00 %); it moves the full-load handover point and the target-MAP / torque-limit behaviour. 0x0C2E70: scaled by FFF8AF52 = baro/101.3 kPa x 059F00(IAT) and added to 05A048 into FFF8AF64, the full-load indicated torque. The throttle opens in proportion to request / AF64, and target MAP = request/AF64 x boost ceiling (0x0C2F0C), so raising this table closes the throttle and lowers target MAP for the same torque. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: read.

table.name: Full-Load Reference Brake Torque (Monitor)
table.description:
Throttle-monitor copy of Full-Load Reference Brake Torque. Keep identical, or expect the monitor to disagree with the main path (plausibility fault inferred).
Details: When used: always, in the throttle monitor. 0x185B20 (from 0x18620C, read): FFF8BB38 = 05F380(rpm) + density FFF8BB32 x this(rpm FFF8CD54), the copy of FFF8AF64 in 0x0C2E70. Copy of Full-Load Reference Brake Torque 05A054 (data 0x049464, axis 0x0494C4). The throttle-monitor module (0x18620C / 0x189DF0 / 0x186290, run from 0x07C408 on one pass in four, each right after its primary 0x0C3D14 / 0x0BE694 / 0x0C3E34, read) repeats the primary computation into its own FFF8BBxx variables with a separate copy of the data and axes. Edit both together, or expect the monitor to disagree with the main path (plausibility fault inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: Full-Load Reference Torque Loss
table.description:
Engine loss torque by rpm added to Full-Load Reference Brake Torque to give the full-load reference the whole throttle/boost model divides by. Probably a mechanical loss at full load (about the same as Friction and Pumping Torque Loss there). Edit the (Monitor) copy too.
Details: Inferred a mechanical loss at the boost limit (not density-scaled; within a few Nm of Friction and Pumping Torque Loss at 120-150 kPa). 0x0C2E70 (task 0x0C3D14): FFF8AF64 = this + density x (Full-Load Reference Brake Torque - 0 ft-lb), density = baro/101.3 kPa x IAT factor. AF64 is the denominator of every torque ratio in the throttle module (0x0C37D8, 0x0C385C) and of the target MAP (0x0C2F0C). Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: read.

table.name: Full-Load Reference Torque Loss (Monitor)
table.description:
Throttle-monitor copy of Full-Load Reference Torque Loss. Keep identical, or expect a plausibility fault (inferred).
Details: When used: always, in the throttle monitor. 0x185B20 (read): added to the density-scaled 05F374 into FFF8BB38, the monitor's full-load indicated torque. Copy of Full-Load Reference Torque Loss 05A048 (data 0x049494). The throttle-monitor module (0x18620C / 0x189DF0 / 0x186290, run from 0x07C408 on one pass in four, each right after its primary 0x0C3D14 / 0x0BE694 / 0x0C3E34, read) repeats the primary computation into its own FFF8BBxx variables with a separate copy of the data and axes. Edit both together, or expect the monitor to disagree with the main path (plausibility fault inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: Friction and Pumping Torque Loss
table.description:
Friction and pumping losses by rpm and manifold pressure, added to every torque request in the throttle/boost model. Cancels out at part throttle; matters near full load, for the torque estimate and limiters (raising it probably opens the throttle and raises target MAP). Edit the (Monitor) copy too.
Details: CORRECTION (end-to-end model, read arithmetic): at part throttle the losses cancel out of the commanded opening (Throttle Required Area is the inverse of Torque Fraction from Throttle Area); this table matters near full load, for the torque estimate and the limiters. 0x0C2FE4 -> FFF8AF76, which 0x0C2B2C adds into FFF8AF62. AF62 is added to every brake-torque request before the throttle ratio (0x0C36A0/0x0C36D0) and subtracted from the modelled delivered torque (0x0C1824), so this table converts brake torque to indicated torque for the throttle/boost model. Raising it opens the throttle and raises the target MAP (0x0C2F0C) for the same torque request (inferred). Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: read.

table.name: Friction and Pumping Torque Loss (Monitor)
table.description:
Throttle-monitor copy of Friction and Pumping Torque Loss. Keep identical, or expect a plausibility fault (inferred).
Details: When used: always, in the throttle monitor. 0x185C34 (from 0x186290, read): FFF8BB44 = this(rpm FFF8CD54, FFF8C5D2 = FFF8AF6E filtered with cal 0x23E08), the copy of the loss term of 0x0C2FE4. Copy of Friction and Pumping Torque Loss 05A060 (data 0x048FE4, axes 0x0494C4/0x048FB4). The throttle-monitor module (0x18620C / 0x189DF0 / 0x186290, run from 0x07C408 on one pass in four, each right after its primary 0x0C3D14 / 0x0BE694 / 0x0C3E34, read) repeats the primary computation into its own FFF8BBxx variables with a separate copy of the data and axes. Edit both together, or expect the monitor to disagree with the main path (plausibility fault inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: Full-Load Reference Torque IAT Factor
table.description:
Intake-temperature correction on the full-load reference torque (and on an upper torque ceiling).
Details: 0x0C24F8 -> FFF8AF54; 0x0C2494 forms FFF8AF52 = cal 0x10720 x baro FFF88668 x AF54 / 2^30 (32768 = 1.0 at 101.3 kPa), the density factor on 05A054 in FFF8AF64 (0x0C2E70). AF54 also scales the 457 ft-lb (619 Nm) ceiling in 0x0BD48C. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: read.

table.name: Ignition Efficiency vs Retard
table.description:
How much torque the engine loses when timing is retarded from base timing (1.0 = no loss). The torque model uses it, and together with its inverse, Torque Reduction Spark Retard, it also decides how far the fired timing is pulled down toward Primary Ignition plus knock advance. Leave alone, or edit together with its inverse.
Details: Ignition efficiency (torque ratio) versus retard below the base timing FFF8A645, 32768 = 1.0. Data 0x023DD0 is shared by 059E7C, 059F18 and 059E88: editing one edits all three. 0x0C13B4 (read): FFF8AF22 = this(A645 - (A789 - 32 [+ KCA/FLKC in combustion modes 3/4])), the efficiency of the timing request; AF22 is the numerator of the spark compensation in 0x0C2514 and feeds 0x0C39DC and FFF8B0E0. It also sets the fired spark: 0x0C39DC folds it into FFF8A64B and 0x0DD568 converts FFF8A64B (pedal pressed) or AF22 >> 7 (pedal released, cylinder cut) back into retard on FFF8A645 through Torque Reduction Spark Retard, this table's exact inverse, so the pair implements fired base timing = min(Base Timing, timing request + KCA + FLKC) (read; min() form computed). Editing this table without the matching inverse shifts the fired timing wherever the request side is lower. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Air Quantity for Torque
table.description:
Air quantity needed for a given torque, by rpm; the torque model uses it to judge how much of the requested air has actually arrived (air-path lag), which feeds spark-based torque reduction and the cylinder-cut level. Only the shape matters. Extend the 277 ft-lb (375 Nm) torque axis if your torque request plus losses exceeds it.
Details: 0x0C34F8 (read): AF74 = Air Quantity for Torque(rpm, AF24); AF68 = AF74 lagged with the air-path lag rate; AF96 = min(1.0, AF68/AF74) is the fraction of the requested air already delivered. 0x0C1854 and 0x0C39DC scale torque by AF96 into AF40 / AF3E (predicted air torque for ignition torque reduction and the cylinder-cut level). The torque axis ends at 277 ft-lb (375 Nm); extend it if requested torque plus losses exceeds that. Only the ratio AF68/AF74 is used, so the data unit does not matter. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Air Quantity Filter Rate
table.description:
Smoothing of the air quantity input to the air-path lag tables (lower = more smoothing).
Details: 0x0C34F8 (read): FFF8AF7A / C558 = air quantity FFF8B4D6 filtered with this coefficient; C558 is the axis of the air-path lag rate tables. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). p16 (read): this torque-model function (0x0C3E34 subtree) runs every 10 ms (0x07C408 <- 0x1DFE3C); 'pass' = 10 ms. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Air-Path Lag Rate (Torque Rising)
table.description:
How fast the modelled air charge catches up with the request (per 10 ms) during a big rise in torque request (over 74 ft-lb, 100 Nm). Used for spark-based torque reduction and the cylinder-cut level, not for throttle. Leave alone unless you know the model.
Details: 0x0C34F8 (read): AF74 = Air Quantity for Torque(rpm, AF24); AF68 = AF74 lagged with the air-path lag rate; AF96 = min(1.0, AF68/AF74) is the fraction of the requested air already delivered. 0x0C1854 and 0x0C39DC scale torque by AF96 into AF40 / AF3E (predicted air torque for ignition torque reduction and the cylinder-cut level). Used after AF24 rose by more than 74 ft-lb (100 Nm) over two passes (cal 0x243CE), until it falls by more than 74 ft-lb (100 Nm) (cal 0x243D0). Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). p16 (read): this torque-model function (0x0C3E34 subtree) runs every 10 ms (0x07C408 <- 0x1DFE3C); 'pass' = 10 ms. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Air-Path Lag Rate (Steady)
table.description:
How fast the modelled air charge catches up with the request (per 10 ms) outside a big torque rise. Used for spark-based torque reduction and the cylinder-cut level, not for throttle. Leave alone unless you know the model.
Details: 0x0C34F8 (read): AF74 = Air Quantity for Torque(rpm, AF24); AF68 = AF74 lagged with the air-path lag rate; AF96 = min(1.0, AF68/AF74) is the fraction of the requested air already delivered. 0x0C1854 and 0x0C39DC scale torque by AF96 into AF40 / AF3E (predicted air torque for ignition torque reduction and the cylinder-cut level). Used outside the rising-torque transient. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). p16 (read): this torque-model function (0x0C3E34 subtree) runs every 10 ms (0x07C408 <- 0x1DFE3C); 'pass' = 10 ms. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Torque Response Filter Weight (Throttle Opening)
table.description:
How quickly the torque model expects delivered torque to follow after the throttle opens quickly (larger = faster), by rpm. Part of the modelled torque used for spark compensation. Leave alone unless you know the model.
Details: 0x0C38E0 (read, 10 ms): FFF8AFAC = this(rpm) once the throttle change AF36 = FFF8CD77 - FFF8CD7A (throttle position now minus 30 ms ago; CD77 = (ETC throttle position FFF8A342 - 10)/4) has risen past +15 counts (about +8 % throttle, scale inferred). After 50 passes (0.5 s) back inside +/-15 it becomes the mean of this and Torque Response Filter Weight (Throttle Closing). AFAC weights the lag of the delivered indicated torque model AF40 (0x0C1854, weight AFAC x AF4E >> 9, per 65536) and of AF58 (0x0C2514). Larger = faster modelled response. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes and Phase 16 (AF36 correction). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Torque Response Filter Weight (Throttle Closing)
table.description:

Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes and Phase 16 (AF36 correction). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Torque Delay
table.description:
Delay, in half crank revolutions by rpm, used by the torque model's spark compensation when a certain event (not identified) starts. Leave alone.
Details: 0x0C3454: FFF8AF8E = this x 15360 / rpm_raw (= this x 3000 / rpm passes of 10 ms, i.e. each count is half a crank revolution, 180 deg, read arithmetic), latched on a rising edge of FFF8A856 bit 5. table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A
table.description:
Torque-model smoothing multiplier by coolant (1.0 = normal; very high values mean no smoothing), used for a while after a combustion-mode change while final timing is still well short of the spark target. Leave alone unless you know the model.

Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Spark Compensation Filter Rate (High Pressure)
table.description:

table.name: Spark Compensation Event Hold Time
table.description:

table.name: Primary Ignition (TGV Closed, AVCS Active)
table.description:
Knock-limited ignition timing by rpm and load for TGVs closed while the cams are under AVCS control. With the knock correction advance and fine learning added it forms one side of the timing limit: the ECU fires the lower of this sum and the Base Timing map.
Details: When used: Weight a (FFF84710) jumps to 255 when both cam controllers are in an active state (intake FFF8AB2C, exhaust FFF8AB1E = 1, 2, 6, or 9 with their bit 5) and falls by 8 per pass otherwise; forced to 0 while FFF88A2D bit 0 (engine stopped) is set (0x0D952C, read). So this table applies while AVCS is controlling. 0x0D952C (from 0x0DE0E0, read): Closed = 05B4A0 x a + 05B4B4 x (1 - a), Open = 05B4C8 x a + 05B4DC x (1 - a), result = Closed x (1 - TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8) + Open x FFF8B3E8, degrees = x/2 - 16, into FFF8A734 (closed blend) / FFF8A737 (open blend) / FFF8A736 (result), output FFF8A735 (optionally smoothed via FFF8C537 when FFF8AA85 bit 0 is set). FFF8A735 feeds the timing request (0x0E0A30 -> FFF8B10E -> FFF8A789) and so the spark target FFF8A72A, and FFF8A74A (0x0DA38C) (read). It sets the fired timing wherever it is the lower side of the timing limit (read, knock routing review 2026-10-31): 0x0E0A30 builds the pedal-pressed request FFF8A78A = this + coolant comp FFF8A787 + IAT comp FFF8A782 + EGR Timing Advance FFF8A769; FFF8A789 adds the enrichment retard (0x0E0910); 0x0C13B4 compares FFF8A789 - 32 + 0.3516 deg x (KCA FFF8A791 + FLKC FFF8A7A7) with base timing FFF8A645, the shortfall becomes the efficiency FFF8AF22 (Ignition Efficiency vs Retard), and 0x0C39DC / 0x0DD568 turn it back into retard on FFF8A645 through the inverse table Torque Reduction Spark Retard. So the fired base FFF8A76A = min(Base Timing + comps, this + comps + EGR advance + KCA + FLKC) less torque-reduction retard (min() form computed), followed by tip-in retard, 0x0DD760, 0x0DA600 and the fired sum 0x0D9E40 (FBKC and retard terms). 0x0D9E40 uses FFF8A735 as the whole fired timing only when cal 0x239AE bit 1 is set, and in limit states FFF8A639 = 0x0B/0x0C/0x19/0x1A/0x1B the spark target FFF8A72A (0x0D9088, built from this request) replaces base timing outright (read). Weight a is a 0-255 ramp kept in FFF84710: +cal 0x2FFB0 (255) per pass while both cam controllers are active, -cal 0x2FFAF (8) per pass otherwise (0x0D952C, read). Axes rpm FFF8CE9C x load FFF8ADE4 (g/rev alternate). TGV polarity (read): 0x0D952C blends its Closed and Open ignition sets as Closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + Open x FFF8B3E8, so FFF8B3E8 is the TGV open fraction; 0x10C948 drives it toward 0 while FFF8A881 bit 4 is set, so that bit set = TGVs closed. p16 (read): 0x0D952C runs every 10 ms, so the weight falls 8 per 10 ms (full blend in about 0.32 s). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Volumetric Efficiency (TGV Closed)
table.description:
Volumetric efficiency by rpm and manifold pressure; feeds the ECU's air-mass model that defines engine load. The ECU blends the TGV Closed and TGV Open tables by actual TGV position. This is the TGVs-closed side. Retune when changing intake, cams or head flow.
Details: Volumetric efficiency, rpm x manifold pressure (psia). 0x11E280 blends Volumetric Efficiency (TGV Closed) x (1 - w) + Volumetric Efficiency (TGV Open) x w, with w = FFF8B3E8/65536 the TGV open fraction, into FFF8B4DA (read). 0x11E308 uses it (as VE = x/32768, rate-limited by cal 0x2B0E8/0x2B0EA). The exception is when cal 0x2C4D0 bit 0 is set and FFF8A83B bit 7 is clear; then it uses Volumetric Efficiency (AVCS Not Ready). table.name: Throttle Flow Function
table.description:
Physics curve for airflow through the throttle versus the pressure ratio across it, used by the manifold model that is corrected toward the MAF. Leave alone: it is an exact physical constant.
Details: When used: every model pass. 0x11DD04 (read), enabled by FFF8A8FB bit 0 (0x11E43C): the modelled throttle flow FFF8C24C = (P_up/101325) x flow function(r) x throttle area FFF8ADEC (= table 0594CC(FFF8CD74), 0x0B8940) x temperature factor x cal 0x2B06C/0x2B06D/64 x 60000 x 2.98e-15, with P_up = FFF8C244 and r = FFF8C240/FFF8C244 (inverted for reverse flow) clamped at 0.53 (choked), then filtered with the ratio-dependent weight. C24C feeds the manifold/airflow observer 0x11DB50, which corrects the estimated pre-throttle pressure C244 so the modelled flow matches the MAF (read). Physical constants of the orifice equation; a tuner should normally leave them alone. Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Flow Temperature Correction
table.description:
Temperature correction for throttle airflow in the manifold model (the standard square-root-of-temperature law). Leave alone: it is exact physics.
Details: When used: every model pass. Input FFF8A8FF = estimated charge air temperature degC + 50 (0x11E0B8: IAT FFF88662 plus a pressure-ratio heating term, capped by FFF888CF, read). 0x11DD04 (read), enabled by FFF8A8FB bit 0 (0x11E43C): the modelled throttle flow FFF8C24C = (P_up/101325) x flow function(r) x throttle area FFF8ADEC (= table 0594CC(FFF8CD74), 0x0B8940) x temperature factor x cal 0x2B06C/0x2B06D/64 x 60000 x 2.98e-15, with P_up = FFF8C244 and r = FFF8C240/FFF8C244 (inverted for reverse flow) clamped at 0.53 (choked), then filtered with the ratio-dependent weight. C24C feeds the manifold/airflow observer 0x11DB50, which corrects the estimated pre-throttle pressure C244 so the modelled flow matches the MAF (read). Physical constants of the orifice equation; a tuner should normally leave them alone. Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Flow Filter Weight
table.description:
Smoothing of the modelled throttle airflow by pressure ratio: when pressures either side of the throttle are nearly equal (small, noisy flow) it is smoothed more. Normally leave alone.
Details: When used: every model pass. C24C = new x w + previous x (1 - w) with w = this(r)/65536 (65535 = 1.0) (read). 0x11DD04 (read), enabled by FFF8A8FB bit 0 (0x11E43C): the modelled throttle flow FFF8C24C = (P_up/101325) x flow function(r) x throttle area FFF8ADEC (= table 0594CC(FFF8CD74), 0x0B8940) x temperature factor x cal 0x2B06C/0x2B06D/64 x 60000 x 2.98e-15, with P_up = FFF8C244 and r = FFF8C240/FFF8C244 (inverted for reverse flow) clamped at 0.53 (choked), then filtered with the ratio-dependent weight. C24C feeds the manifold/airflow observer 0x11DB50, which corrects the estimated pre-throttle pressure C244 so the modelled flow matches the MAF (read). Physical constants of the orifice equation; a tuner should normally leave them alone. Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Area from Throttle Position (Airflow Model)
table.description:
Converts throttle position into effective throttle area (mm^2) for the airflow model and the throttle-based MAP substitute; about 2,150 mm^2 wide open.
Details: When used: always (0x0B8BB0 -> 0x0B8940, read): FFF8ADEC = this(throttle position FFF8CD74). ADEC feeds the throttle flow of the manifold model (0x11D704: C24C = P_up/101325 x flow function x ADEC x temperature factor x cal, which corrects the pre-throttle pressure estimate toward the MAF, my research notes, read), the throttle-flow chain FFF8ADF8/ADF0 (Throttle Flow Curve (Area per RPM, MAP Fallback Model)) and FFF8A61F (its change per pass, 0x0B8A38) (read). Keep it consistent with Throttle Area from Opening (and its Monitor copy) when the throttle body changes (inferred; the code does not compare them). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Throttle Flow Curve (Area per RPM, MAP Fallback Model)
table.description:
Airflow per revolution versus throttle area per rpm. Used for a throttle-based MAP substitute (probably when the MAP sensor is faulted) and as an input to transient (tip-in) fueling. Change only for a different throttle body.
Details: When used: always (0x0B8BB0 -> 0x0B8C74, read): FFF8ADF8 = rpm FFF8CD54 x this(FFF8ADEC x 1024 / CD54) / 32768, with ADEC from Throttle Area from Throttle Position; then 0x0B8980 forms FFF8ADF0 = ADF8 x 0.4/6e7 x cal 0x349C4 (14187) x FFF8CD46 x 0.0349 x 256 (filtered by cal 0x349C6), and when FFF88E28 bit 3 is set the MAP value FFF8913C becomes cal 0x58EA4 (52298) x ADF0 >> 15 instead of the sensor reading (0x1E0000 block, read): a throttle-based MAP substitute. ADF8 x 2 -> FFF8ADF6 -> filtered rate FFF8ADF4, and the rate of ADF0 -> FFF8ADF2, are inputs of the transient-fuel module 0x0F6260 (throttle-rate term and tip-in trigger) (read). table.name: Manifold Pressure Rate Span (RPM)
table.description:
How many samples (10 ms each) the ECU spans, by rpm, when measuring how fast manifold pressure is changing; that rate triggers the manifold model's transient corrections.
Details: When used: every pass of 0x11CAB8 (from the airflow module, read). table.name: Manifold Model Rising Transient Threshold
table.description:

Initial/Recovery/duration values are sampled once at the start of the falling transient. Rising transient: B4CA >= 05D7B8 (in gear) / 05D7C4 (neutral switch FFF88ADA b6 set), or a throttle step >= 05D80C (254, off). Falling transient: B4CA <= 05D7E8 (-6 kPa, hysteresis 05D7D0 +4 kPa) / 05D7F4 (-3 kPa, neutral). Output FFF8A8F9 multiplies the model gain FFF8B4D0 (0x11CC68: B4D0 is proportional to intake temperature x A8F9; 0x11D938 integrates R x B4D0 x (air in - air out) into the modelled pressure FFF8C238 when the model is active, FFF8A8FB b0 = running and rpm >= 100). A8F9 by phase: (1) rising transient and 1 pass after it (cal 0x2AF3B): 05D788(FFF8CDC2) = 179 in gear, cal 0x2C4C6 = 205 in neutral; (2) from the start of a falling transient for a duration from 05D8B8 / 05D890 / 05D8A4: the Initial table; (3) after that, until B4CA > cal 0x2BAD6 (-2 kPa): the Recovery table; (4) otherwise cal 0x2AF3E = 128. Initial/Recovery/duration values are sampled once at the start of the falling transient. Set: neutral switch -> Neutral tables; else TGV closed command FFF8A881 b4 -> TGV Closed tables; else the in-gear TGV-open tables. (For A8F9, 128 = x1.0, the steady-state gain; this table is a duration, not a gain.) Countdown in 10 ms passes, loaded at the start of a falling transient. Confidence: read.

table.name: Manifold Model Start Correction RPM Threshold
table.description:
After start, once rpm passes this value (by coolant at start), the manifold model is pulled onto the MAF reading with the start gain (Manifold Model Start Correction MAF Gain) until model and MAF agree. Below this rpm the gain is 1.0. Normally leave alone.
Details: Manifold-pressure model start phase 0x11C788 (10 ms task, read). Both tables are looked up with coolant at start FFF88A46 (the first stack argument; the disassembly shows R5 = EXTU.W @(40,R15) for 05D74C). FFF8C234 = 05D758 / 64 x 05D764(FFF8C540) / 128 while FFF8A8FC b6 is clear, else 1.0; b6 clears once rpm >= 05D74C x 6.25 after the model started (FFF8A8FB b0 rising) and stays clear until the modelled air FFF8C254 and the MAF value FFF88820/1280 agree within cal 0x2B999 x 0.2 (or FFF886AB b5 falls). C234 is the gain on the (MAF - model) term in 0x11DB50 (read), so the tables shape how fast the model is pulled onto the MAF after start (inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: Manifold Model Start Correction MAF Gain

table.name: Volumetric Efficiency (AVCS Not Ready)
table.description:
VE table that would replace the normal TGV-blended VE while the cams are probably not yet ready.
When that bit is set, 0x11E308 uses this table instead of the Volumetric Efficiency (TGV Closed) / (TGV Open) blend while FFF8A83B bit 7 is clear (read). That bit is an AVCS-ready flag from 0x1050F4 that needs both cam references learned (inferred meaning). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Throttle Flow Coefficient (Forward Flow)
table.description:
Discharge coefficient of the throttle airflow model for normal flow into the manifold. Leave at 1.0 and describe a new throttle body through the area tables instead.
Details: When used: every model pass while the pressure ratio r = FFF8C240/FFF8C244 is at most 1.0 (normal flow into the manifold). 0x11DD04 (read), enabled by FFF8A8FB bit 0 (0x11E43C): modelled throttle flow FFF8C24C [g/min] = (P_up/101325) x Throttle Flow Function(r) x FFF8ADEC (Throttle Area from Throttle Position, 0.05 mm^2) x Throttle Flow Temperature Correction x this x 60000 x 2.98e-15, which feeds the manifold/airflow observer 0x11DB50 / 0x11D938. With the area tables in mm^2 this is the discharge coefficient of the orifice equation; normally leave at 1.0 and correct the area tables instead. Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Flow Coefficient (Reverse Flow)
table.description:
Coefficient of the throttle airflow model when the manifold is above the pre-throttle pressure. Leave alone.
Details: When used: every model pass while r > 1.0 (manifold above the pre-throttle pressure; the ratio is inverted). 0x11DD04 (read), enabled by FFF8A8FB bit 0 (0x11E43C): modelled throttle flow FFF8C24C [g/min] = (P_up/101325) x Throttle Flow Function(r) x FFF8ADEC (Throttle Area from Throttle Position, 0.05 mm^2) x Throttle Flow Temperature Correction x this x 60000 x 2.98e-15, which feeds the manifold/airflow observer 0x11DB50 / 0x11D938. table.name: Exhaust Temperature Estimate 2 Map (No Enrichment)
table.description:
Second exhaust/catalyst temperature estimate (inferred), by rpm and load, with no enrichment active. When it gets high enough the ECU skips the delay before open loop fueling. Raising it brings open loop in sooner.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Base
table.description:
Base exhaust temperature by rpm and load for the A/F sensor's exhaust model, which probably decides when it is safe to heat the front A/F sensor fully (water condensation check). Does not affect fuel or timing.
Details: When used: always. 0x181334 (read): base exhaust temperature from rpm FFF8CD54 and load FFF8BAC4 (= FFF8ADE4, or cal 0x42E7E under FFF88E2A bit 1). Module 0x180C20 (read) is a self-contained exhaust thermal model: its result flags FFF8139F bit 0, which the A/F sensor state machine FFF88AFE reads (0x08492A / 0x0852B2, read); its role as the exhaust-pipe condensation check before full A/F sensor heating is inferred. 0x181334: T = this base x 05F208(final timing)/128 x (05F214(timing retard) + 128)/256 -> FFF8BAA8; FFF8BAC8 follows T with the 05F234 filter (towards coolant temperature while not running). No reader of FFF8BAC8 / FFF8BAA8 outside this module in the decompilation, so it does not affect fuel or timing (read). Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Timing Factor
table.description:
Correction of the A/F sensor exhaust temperature model for ignition timing (later timing = hotter exhaust). Does not affect fuel or timing.
Details: When used: always. 0x181334 (read): multiplies the base exhaust temperature by this(final timing FFF8A744)/128. Module 0x180C20 (read) is a self-contained exhaust thermal model: its result flags FFF8139F bit 0, which the A/F sensor state machine FFF88AFE reads (0x08492A / 0x0852B2, read); its role as the exhaust-pipe condensation check before full A/F sensor heating is inferred. 0x181334: T = this base x 05F208(final timing)/128 x (05F214(timing retard) + 128)/256 -> FFF8BAA8; FFF8BAC8 follows T with the 05F234 filter (towards coolant temperature while not running). No reader of FFF8BAC8 / FFF8BAA8 outside this module in the decompilation, so it does not affect fuel or timing (read). Both factors multiply the absolute temperature (base table + 223.15 K, i.e. Kelvin), not the degC/degF value shown: x1.10 on 800 C (1073 K) gives 907 C. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Retard Factor
table.description:
Correction of the A/F sensor exhaust temperature model for knock-related retard. Does not affect fuel or timing.
Details: When used: always. 0x181334 (read, input checked in the assembly): multiplies the base by (this + 128)/256, input = FFF8A735 + FFF8A7A5 x 180/256 - 32 - FFF8A744 clamped to s8, i.e. base timing plus the maximum knock advance minus final timing (retard below the knock-free maximum, inferred), in half degrees. Module 0x180C20 (read) is a self-contained exhaust thermal model: its result flags FFF8139F bit 0, which the A/F sensor state machine FFF88AFE reads (0x08492A / 0x0852B2, read); its role as the exhaust-pipe condensation check before full A/F sensor heating is inferred. 0x181334: T = this base x 05F208(final timing)/128 x (05F214(timing retard) + 128)/256 -> FFF8BAA8; FFF8BAC8 follows T with the 05F234 filter (towards coolant temperature while not running). No reader of FFF8BAC8 / FFF8BAA8 outside this module in the decompilation, so it does not affect fuel or timing (read). Both factors multiply the absolute temperature (base table + 223.15 K, i.e. Kelvin), not the degC/degF value shown: x1.10 on 800 C (1073 K) gives 907 C. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Filter
table.description:
How quickly the A/F sensor exhaust temperature model follows its target, by coolant. Does not affect fuel or timing. Normally leave alone.
Details: When used: always. 0x181334 (read): FFF8BAC8 = (previous x 32768 + target x k/2)/(32768 + k/2) with k = this(coolant FFF8CD65); target = the modelled exhaust temperature while running (engine state 3), else coolant temperature. Module 0x180C20 (read) is a self-contained exhaust thermal model: its result flags FFF8139F bit 0, which the A/F sensor state machine FFF88AFE reads (0x08492A / 0x0852B2, read); its role as the exhaust-pipe condensation check before full A/F sensor heating is inferred. 0x181334: T = this base x 05F208(final timing)/128 x (05F214(timing retard) + 128)/256 -> FFF8BAA8; FFF8BAC8 follows T with the 05F234 filter (towards coolant temperature while not running). No reader of FFF8BAC8 / FFF8BAA8 outside this module in the decompilation, so it does not affect fuel or timing (read). Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Condensate at Start
table.description:
Modelled water in the exhaust at start, by coolant and intake temperature. If it is above the threshold, full A/F sensor heating waits until the model has dried out. Raise to delay A/F sensor heating on cold starts, lower to allow it earlier.
Details: When used: at ignition on, at the cranking -> running change of FFF8906B, on rising FFF89053 bit 4 and while FFF89053 bit 3 is set (0x1801A4, read). Module 0x180C20 (read) is the exhaust condensation model behind the A/F sensor heater release: 05F158 (by pipe temperature FFF8BAB8, K x 32) is the saturation vapour pressure of water; 0x17F4B8 takes the water partial pressure as cal 0x42333/256 (15 %) of max(MAP, baro) and makes the condensation rate FFF8C448 from flow x factor x (partial - saturation pressure) / total pressure; 0x18065C integrates the net amount into FFF8C48C. The A/F state machine (0x0852B2, read) goes to the protected state 2 when the start value FFF8C478 >= cal 0x4230C (415645) and on to state 3 only when FFF8139F bit 0 clears (0x08492A), which 0x181668 does when the model amount FFF8C47C < 415645. 0x1801A4 (read, args checked in the assembly): FFF8C478 = this(coolant FFF8AC8D, IAT FFF8AC8B; both degC + 50 bytes, cal 0x4234E / 0x42344 = -40 C on sensor fault) + FFF81880 (amount carried over from the last run). Above 415645 the A/F sensor heating waits for the model to dry out; below it the sensor takes the fast path (state 5). Raise to delay A/F sensor heating on cold starts, lower to allow it earlier. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Condensation Flow Factor
table.description:
Scales how fast water is modelled to condense in the exhaust, by exhaust flow (probably 1.0 = normal); more condensation keeps the front A/F sensor in its protected heating state longer. Normally leave alone.
Details: When used: always (module 0x180C20). Module 0x180C20 (read) is the exhaust condensation model behind the A/F sensor heater release: 05F158 (by pipe temperature FFF8BAB8, K x 32) is the saturation vapour pressure of water; 0x17F4B8 takes the water partial pressure as cal 0x42333/256 (15 %) of max(MAP, baro) and makes the condensation rate FFF8C448 from flow x factor x (partial - saturation pressure) / total pressure; 0x18065C integrates the net amount into FFF8C48C. The A/F state machine (0x0852B2, read) goes to the protected state 2 when the start value FFF8C478 >= cal 0x4230C (415645) and on to state 3 only when FFF8139F bit 0 clears (0x08492A), which 0x181668 does when the model amount FFF8C47C < 415645. 0x180BE4 / 0x17F4B8 (read): the condensation rate FFF8C448 is proportional to this(exhaust flow FFF8C4B4) x FFF8C4B4 x cal 0x42DA8 x (water partial pressure - saturation pressure at pipe temperature) / total pressure, so this scales condensation linearly (256 = 1.0 assumed; inferred). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Saturation Vapour Pressure
table.description:
Water vapour pressure versus exhaust pipe temperature for the A/F sensor condensation model, which decides how long the front A/F sensor is kept in protected heating.
Details: When used: always (exhaust condensation model 0x180C20 behind the A/F sensor heater release, read). 0x17F4B8 (read; axis = pipe temperature FFF8BAB8, LF75404S_table_inputs): saturation = this(pipe temperature); total pressure = max(MAP, baro) in kPa x 8192; water partial pressure = total x cal 0x42333/256 (15 %); the condensation rate FFF8C448 = flow FFF8C4B4 x Condensation Flow Factor x cal 0x42DA8 x (partial - saturation) / total, clamped >= 0, and is integrated (minus evaporation) into the condensate amount that holds the A/F sensor in its protected heating state (see A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Condensate at Start). Raising the curve lowers the modelled condensation (shorter heater protection), lowering it lengthens it; the physics argues for leaving it. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 1A (TGV Open, Normal, Altitude)
table.description:
Intake cam advance target (degrees from the fully retarded rest position) by rpm and load for normal driving with the TGVs open, used at altitude (blended in by AVCS Barometric Blend; near sea level the 1B table is used instead). Higher = earlier intake valve timing. The normal vs high-pedal split is inferred from the switching conditions.
Details: Convention (read, see FU_UNITS): crank degrees of intake cam ADVANCE from its learned rest position; 0 = rest (fully retarded, inferred), larger = more advance (earlier valve events). Values below 0 ask for less than the rest position: the OCV then sits at minimum duty and the cam stays at rest (inferred). AVCS target (intake 0x15C250, exhaust 0x16032C, read): target = coolant terms + v x [S_A x w + S_B x (1 - w)] + (1 - v) x [3A x w + (3B + Coolant Offset 3B x Coolant Factor 3 / 128) x (1 - w)], clamped to +/-90 degrees, 364.09 counts per degree. v = FFF8B3E8, the TGV open fraction: sets 1/2 apply with TGVs open, set 3 with TGVs closed. w = FFF8B948 = AVCS Barometric Blend (barometric pressure FFF88668, via 0x15B1E0, read): the A tables apply at altitude, the B tables at sea level. S = set 1 or set 2, chosen by FFF8A8A4 bit 7 (stack argument +24 from 0x15969C, read). That bit is a high-pedal latch (0x11C15C / 0x10F848, read): it sets when the accelerator FFF88A5E is at or above High Pedal Entry Threshold while vehicle speed is not jumping (under cal 0x35B16... per gear) and some status flags (FFF88A2D bit 0, FFF88ADA bit 6, FFF8A8A2 bit 6) are clear, or when FFF8A8A5 bit 2 or 4 is set; it clears once the pedal is below cal 0x36518 (85 %). So set 1 = normal driving and set 2 = near wide-open pedal (meaning inferred from these conditions). The set-3 terms are active because cal 0x3ACF6 = 1 in both images. Set 1, A table (weight w). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 2A (TGV Open, High Pedal, Altitude)
table.description:
Intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used when the pedal is near wide open (about 90 % or more), TGVs open, at altitude. Higher = earlier intake timing. The high-pedal meaning is inferred from the switching conditions.
Details: Convention (read, see FU_UNITS): crank degrees of intake cam ADVANCE from its learned rest position; 0 = rest (fully retarded, inferred), larger = more advance (earlier valve events). Values below 0 ask for less than the rest position: the OCV then sits at minimum duty and the cam stays at rest (inferred). AVCS target (intake 0x15C250, exhaust 0x16032C, read): target = coolant terms + v x [S_A x w + S_B x (1 - w)] + (1 - v) x [3A x w + (3B + Coolant Offset 3B x Coolant Factor 3 / 128) x (1 - w)], clamped to +/-90 degrees, 364.09 counts per degree. v = FFF8B3E8, the TGV open fraction: sets 1/2 apply with TGVs open, set 3 with TGVs closed. w = FFF8B948 = AVCS Barometric Blend (barometric pressure FFF88668, via 0x15B1E0, read): the A tables apply at altitude, the B tables at sea level. table.name: High Pedal Entry Threshold
table.description:
Accelerator position, by barometric pressure, at or above which the ECU switches to the high-pedal cam targets (set 2), provided vehicle speed is steady. Lowering it uses the high-pedal cams earlier. Other functions also read this high-pedal flag.
Details: High-pedal latch FFF8A8A4 bit 7 (0x10F848 -> FFF8B410, 0x11C15C, read): FFF8B410 counts passes with the accelerator FFF88A5E at or above this threshold (by barometric pressure FFF88A42 = FFF88668) while vehicle speed FFF88BE8 changes by less than cal 0x35B16... per pass (by gear FFF888A0) and FFF88A2D bit 0, FFF88ADA bit 6 and FFF8A8A2 bit 6 are clear. The bit sets once FFF8B410 reaches 05D740 (1 pass) and clears after the pedal stays below cal 0x36518 for cal 0x36516 passes. The AVCS uses the bit to pick cam target set 2; 12 other functions read FFF8A8A4 (not reviewed). p16 (read): the pass counter FFF8B410 (0x10F848 <- 0x1140BC <- 0x1E1560) runs in the 80 ms OS task (one pass = 80 ms); the latch 0x11C15C runs every 10 ms. Confidence: read.

table.name: High Pedal Exit Threshold
table.description:
Accelerator position below which the high-pedal flag clears and the cams return to the normal (set 1) targets. Keep it below High Pedal Entry Threshold.
Details: High-pedal latch FFF8A8A4 bit 7 (0x10F848 -> FFF8B410, 0x11C15C, read): FFF8B410 counts passes with the accelerator FFF88A5E at or above this threshold (by barometric pressure FFF88A42 = FFF88668) while vehicle speed FFF88BE8 changes by less than cal 0x35B16... per pass (by gear FFF888A0) and FFF88A2D bit 0, FFF88ADA bit 6 and FFF8A8A2 bit 6 are clear. The bit sets once FFF8B410 reaches 05D740 (1 pass) and clears after the pedal stays below cal 0x36518 for cal 0x36516 passes. The AVCS uses the bit to pick cam target set 2; 12 other functions read FFF8A8A4 (not reviewed). Below this the latch clears. p16 (read): the pass counter FFF8B410 (0x10F848 <- 0x1140BC <- 0x1E1560) runs in the 80 ms OS task (one pass = 80 ms); the latch 0x11C15C runs every 10 ms. Confidence: read.

table.name: High Pedal Tip-In Rate Threshold
table.description:
Pedal-rise rate, by pedal position, that sets the high-pedal flag immediately on a fast stab at the pedal (above about 90 %), for both the high-pedal cam targets and Injection Timing (High Pedal), without waiting for the normal entry delay.
Details: 0x10F7DC (10 ms task, read): when the pedal rise FFF88C5C (= pedal FFF88A5E - the previous pedal sample FFF88C60, 0x09F234) is at or above this(pedal), FFF8B40E is loaded with 05D410 (6 passes) and otherwise counts down; zero while FFF8A8A5 b0 is clear (0x1194DC: neutral switch and two status flags). With B40E nonzero and the pedal at or above 05D6F0 / 05D6E4 (90 %), 0x119500 / 0x119438 set FFF8A8A5 b2 / FFF8A8A3 b0 after cal 0x35B3C (5) passes, and those set the high-pedal latches FFF8A8A4 b7 (AVCS target set 2, 0x11C15C) and b6 (Injection Timing (High Pedal), 0x11C0C4) without waiting for the 80 ms counter of High Pedal Entry Threshold (read). The sample interval of FFF88C5C was not settled. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Intake AVCS Minimum RPM (Oil Temp)
table.description:
Minimum engine speed for intake cam control by oil temperature. Below it the cams are held at rest and ignition fades to the AVCS Inactive timing tables.
Details: When used: always. 0x15CD4C (read): the intake AVCS may run closed-loop (enable status FFF8AB2E = 0) only while rpm FFF8CE9C >= this(oil temperature FFF8B97C) (hysteresis cal 0x3B888 = 100 rpm), rpm below cal 0x3B880, oil above cal 0x3B884 and time since start >= 05E57C; otherwise the cam state FFF8AB2C becomes 4 (held at default) and Primary Ignition fades to the AVCS Inactive tables (my research notes). FFF8B97C is oil temperature: 0x15B1E0 writes it from FFF88E26 (oil temperature, OBD PID 0x5C units) because cal 0x3ACF1 = 1, or from coolant FFF88A44 x 32/41 (the same scale) when that cal is 0 (read). Earlier notes called FFF8B97C battery voltage; that is wrong. Confidence: read.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Minimum RPM (Oil Temp)
table.description:
Minimum engine speed for exhaust cam control by oil temperature; works like Intake AVCS Minimum RPM (Oil Temp).
Details: When used: always. 0x16144C, the exhaust twin of 0x15CD4C (read): exhaust AVCS status FFF8AB20 / state FFF8AB1E, same logic as Intake AVCS Minimum RPM (Oil Temp). FFF8B97C is oil temperature: 0x15B1E0 writes it from FFF88E26 (oil temperature, OBD PID 0x5C units) because cal 0x3ACF1 = 1, or from coolant FFF88A44 x 32/41 (the same scale) when that cal is 0 (read). Earlier notes called FFF8B97C battery voltage; that is wrong. Confidence: read.

table.name: AVCS Activation Delay After Start
table.description:
How long after every start the cams are held at their rest position before cam control begins, by coolant temperature at start. Raise for a longer hold, lower to start cam control sooner.
Details: When used: after every start. 0x15B59C (intake) and 0x15F7C0 (exhaust, descriptor 05E770, same data 0x03AD6A) (read): while FFF88A76 / 2 is below this(coolant at start FFF88A46) the AVCS request FFF8AB2D / FFF8AB1F is 4 (hold at the default position, no closed-loop cam control). FFF88A76 counts 10 ms passes since the engine left cranking (0x07E1AC: +1 per call, saturating at 65535, reset while FFF88A27 bit 0 is set; called once per pass from 0x07D3E4 in the 10 ms task 0x1DFE3C, read), so one table count = 20 ms. Confidence: read.

table.name: AVCS Minimum Oil Temp (IAT at Start)
table.description:
Minimum oil temperature before cam control is allowed, by intake air temperature at start (a proxy for how cold the engine was). Below it the cams stay at rest.
Details: When used: always. 0x15B59C (intake) and 0x15F7C0 (exhaust, descriptor 05E788, same data 0x03AD8A) (read): the active-control request (FFF8AB2D = 1) needs oil temperature FFF8B97C >= this(FFF8CEE6) plus the rpm / pedal windows; otherwise the request is 9 (FFF8AB28 bit 5 / FFF8AB24 bit 5 clear). FFF8CEE6 = intake air temperature latched at start, (IAT + 50 - 10) x 65536/160 (0x06AF58, read), the iat_409 scale. FFF8B97C is oil temperature: 0x15B1E0 writes it from FFF88E26 (oil temperature, OBD PID 0x5C units) because cal 0x3ACF1 = 1, or from coolant FFF88A44 x 32/41 (the same scale) when that cal is 0 (read). Earlier notes called FFF8B97C battery voltage; that is wrong. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake AVCS Fixed Duty Window After Start
table.description:
Appears to set how long after a start (by coolant at start) the intake cam valves are held at a fixed 52 % duty instead of closed-loop control. Only matters if longer than AVCS Activation Delay After Start.
Details: When used: every pass while running; only matters if it is longer than AVCS Activation Delay After Start. Time after start (A76/2, 20 ms counts) during which the intake OCV duty is held at the fixed 52 % (cal 0x3CE52) instead of closed-loop cam control, when the oil-temperature condition (Intake AVCS Fixed Duty Minimum Oil Temp) also holds. Its own data block (0x3D066), not the one of AVCS Activation Delay After Start (Second) (0x3D088). 0x15B59C (intake AVCS request, read; arguments mapped from the call at seg_0x150000.c:7959 and the stack offsets at 0x15B5BC-0x15B68C): 05E420 and 05E414 / 05E408 are read with coolant at start FFF88A46 (R14 at 0x15B664-0x15B674), 05E42C and 05E438 with IAT at start FFF8CEE6 (R12 at 0x15B678-0x15B68C). Output FFF8AB2A bit 3 = 1 unless all of: AVCS enable status FFF8AB2E = 0, FFF88ADA bit 3 clear, FFF8AB27 bit 6 clear, not (rpm CE9C <= cal 0x3AD38 = 450 rpm with FFF88A28 bit 1) and FFF88A76/2 >= Fixed Duty Window. Output FFF8AB2A bit 4 = (Fixed Duty Minimum Oil Temp(IAT at start) <= oil FFF8B97C x 328 >> 16) and FFF8AB28 bit 7 and FFF8AB27 bit 5 and the rpm/angle windows of cals 0x3AD1A-0x3AD46 (same structure as AVCS Minimum Oil Temp (IAT at Start), which sets FFF8AB28 bit 5). In 0x15DF20 (cam 1) and 0x15E63C (cam 2), when both bits are set the duty B8DE is not feedback + hold but max(min(cal 0x3B8FE, cal 0x3CE52), cal 0x3B8FC) = 1300 = 52 % (read); B8DE becomes the OCV output B8EA only in AVCS states 1/6 (FFF8AB28 bit 3, slice D). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Intake AVCS Fixed Duty Minimum Oil Temp (IAT at Start)
table.description:
Appears to set the oil temperature, by intake air temperature at start, above which the intake cam valves are held at a fixed 52 % duty during Intake AVCS Fixed Duty Window After Start instead of closed-loop control. Only acts during Intake AVCS Fixed Duty Window After Start.

In 0x15DF20 (cam 1) and 0x15E63C (cam 2), when both bits are set the duty B8DE is not feedback + hold but max(min(cal 0x3B8FE, cal 0x3CE52), cal 0x3B8FC) = 1300 = 52 % (read); B8DE becomes the OCV output B8EA only in AVCS states 1/6 (FFF8AB28 bit 3, slice D). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Idle, Cam 1)
table.description:
Proportional part of the intake cam 1 oil control valve duty by rpm and cam error, used with the pedal fully released and the car below about 4 km/h; otherwise Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 1) is used.
Details: Axis (read, see FU_UNITS): cam error = target - actual in crank degrees (intake: advance, exhaust: retard). When used: intake cam 1 (0x15DF20, error FFF8B956) at idle / standstill. This is the idle variant, used while the accelerator is fully released (FFF88C64 bit 5) and vehicle speed FFF88BE8 x 9/160 < cal 0x3B904 (4 km/h); otherwise Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 1) is used. 0x15DF20 / 0x15E63C (intake cam 1 / cam 2) and 0x16269C / 0x162D18 (exhaust cam 1 / cam 2), read: duty = learned hold duty (FFF8B8E8 / FFF8B8E6 intake cam 1 / 2, FFF8B8FE / FFF8B8FC exhaust cam 1 / 2) + (P + D) x cal 0x3B90C/100 (exhaust cal 0x3C7E2; both 100 %), clamped 31.9...81.1 % (exhaust 32.1...81.1 %). table.name: Intake AVCS Rate Feedback Duty (Cam 1)
table.description:

Details: When used: intake cam 1 in active control (0x15DF20). D term (read): when |FFF8B952| (the filtered rate of change of the cam error, 0x15CF8C) exceeds 0.5 deg (cal 0x3CCC8), D = (-100 + this(rpm, rate)/327.68 %) x oil factor/128 x 05E5F4(error)/128, added to the P term. table.name: Intake AVCS Rate Feedback Oil Factor
table.description:

table.name: Intake AVCS OCV Battery Voltage Compensation
table.description:
Multiplier on both intake oil control valve outputs by battery voltage, so the valves get the same effective drive as voltage changes. Always used.
Details: When used: always, both intake OCVs (0x15ED58; descriptor 05E6E0 in 0x15F158, same data 0x03BC84). 0x15ED58 / 0x15F158 (intake cam 1 / 2) and 0x163394 / 0x163788 (exhaust cam 1 / 2), read: OCV output = (I term + duty FFF8B8EA x coil factor x adaptation factor) x battery factor, stored x25 into FFF8B8EE (intake cam 1). The adaptation factor (0.5...1.5, cal 0x3BBCE/0x3BBCC) is stepped by the current error = expected current (Expected Current table) - measured FFF88D70 x 2.5/65536 while the duty is >= 20 % (cal 0x3BBC4). The battery factor is this(FFF88C9E, filtered battery voltage). The exhaust OCVs use Exhaust AVCS OCV Battery Voltage Compensation (05E9C8). Confidence: read.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS OCV Battery Voltage Compensation
table.description:
Multiplier on both exhaust oil control valve outputs by battery voltage, so the valves get the same effective drive as voltage changes. Always used.

Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake AVCS OCV Expected Current
table.description:
Expected intake oil control valve current for a given duty; the ECU compares the measured current with it to learn a correction factor.
Details: When used: intake OCVs (0x15ED58 cam 1; descriptor 05E704 in 0x15F158 cam 2, same data 0x03BC92) (read): expected current = this(duty FFF8B8EA) + cal 0x3BBD4 (0), compared with the measured current to step the adaptation factor (Intake AVCS OCV Adaptation Step) and the I term. 0x15ED58 / 0x15F158 (intake cam 1 / 2) and 0x163394 / 0x163788 (exhaust cam 1 / 2), read: OCV output = (I term + duty FFF8B8EA x coil factor x adaptation factor) x battery factor, stored x25 into FFF8B8EE (intake cam 1). The adaptation factor (0.5...1.5, cal 0x3BBCE/0x3BBCC) is stepped by the current error = expected current (Expected Current table) - measured FFF88D70 x 2.5/65536 while the duty is >= 20 % (cal 0x3BBC4). Confidence: read.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS OCV Expected Current
table.description:
Expected exhaust oil control valve current for a given duty; the ECU compares measured current against it to learn a correction. Same role as Intake AVCS OCV Expected Current.
Details: When used: exhaust OCVs (0x163394, duty FFF8B900; descriptor 05EA34 in 0x163788, same data 0x03CB8E) (read): as Intake AVCS OCV Expected Current. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake AVCS OCV Coil Factor (Oil Temp)
table.description:
Multiplier by oil temperature on the intake oil control valve duty, used only for the first moments of cam control after power-up; afterwards the Settled table is used. Probably compensates the valve coil warming with the oil. Edit together with the Settled table.
Details: When used: intake OCVs until FFF8B8DA / 20 >= cal 0x3CE54 (50), i.e. about 50 passes of active control since power-up (FFF8B8DA adds 20 per pass in states 1/6, 0x15CD4C), then 05E6A4 (read; 0x15ED58, descriptor 05E6F8 in 0x15F158). Multiplies the duty request by this(oil FFF8B97C), as the OCV coil warms with the oil (inferred: resistance rises with temperature). 0x15ED58 / 0x15F158 (intake cam 1 / 2) and 0x163394 / 0x163788 (exhaust cam 1 / 2), read: OCV output = (I term + duty FFF8B8EA x coil factor x adaptation factor) x battery factor, stored x25 into FFF8B8EE (intake cam 1). The adaptation factor (0.5...1.5, cal 0x3BBCE/0x3BBCC) is stepped by the current error = expected current (Expected Current table) - measured FFF88D70 x 2.5/65536 while the duty is >= 20 % (cal 0x3BBC4). Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake AVCS OCV Coil Factor (Oil Temp, Settled)
table.description:
Multiplier by oil temperature on the intake oil control valve duty for normal running once cam control has been active a while.
Details: When used: intake OCVs once FFF8B8DA / 20 >= cal 0x3CE54 (about 50 passes of active control since power-up) (read; 0x15ED58, descriptor 05E6EC in 0x15F158). Same role as Intake AVCS OCV Coil Factor (Oil Temp). Confidence: read.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS OCV Coil Factor (Oil Temp)
table.description:
Multiplier by oil temperature on the exhaust oil control valve duty, used only briefly before the first active cam-control pass; afterwards the Settled table is used. Edit together with the Settled table.
Details: When used: exhaust OCVs until the exhaust active-control counter FFF8B8F0 exceeds 19, i.e. only before the first active pass (read; 0x163394, descriptor 05EA28 in 0x163788); afterwards 05E9D4. 0x15ED58 / 0x15F158 (intake cam 1 / 2) and 0x163394 / 0x163788 (exhaust cam 1 / 2), read: OCV output = (I term + duty FFF8B8EA x coil factor x adaptation factor) x battery factor, stored x25 into FFF8B8EE (intake cam 1). The adaptation factor (0.5...1.5, cal 0x3BBCE/0x3BBCC) is stepped by the current error = expected current (Expected Current table) - measured FFF88D70 x 2.5/65536 while the duty is >= 20 % (cal 0x3BBC4). Confidence: read.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS OCV Coil Factor (Oil Temp, Settled)
table.description:
Multiplier by oil temperature on the exhaust oil control valve duty, used for normal running once cam control has been active.
Details: When used: exhaust OCVs once FFF8B8F0 > 19 (after the first active-control pass), i.e. normally (read; 0x163394, descriptor 05EA1C in 0x163788). 0x15ED58 / 0x15F158 (intake cam 1 / 2) and 0x163394 / 0x163788 (exhaust cam 1 / 2), read: OCV output = (I term + duty FFF8B8EA x coil factor x adaptation factor) x battery factor, stored x25 into FFF8B8EE (intake cam 1). The adaptation factor (0.5...1.5, cal 0x3BBCE/0x3BBCC) is stepped by the current error = expected current (Expected Current table) - measured FFF88D70 x 2.5/65536 while the duty is >= 20 % (cal 0x3BBC4). Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake AVCS OCV Adaptation Step (Cam 1)
table.description:
Step size, by valve current error, for learning the intake cam 1 oil control valve current correction (limited to 0.5-1.5). Larger steps learn faster but can hunt. Used while valve duty is at least 20 %.
Details: When used: intake cam 1 OCV (0x15ED58) while the duty is >= 20 % (read): the adaptation factor FFF868F0 moves by this(current error)/32768 per pass, up when the expected current exceeds the measured, down otherwise, limits 0.5...1.5 (cal 0x3BBD0 = 0 enables it). 0x15ED58 / 0x15F158 (intake cam 1 / 2) and 0x163394 / 0x163788 (exhaust cam 1 / 2), read: OCV output = (I term + duty FFF8B8EA x coil factor x adaptation factor) x battery factor, stored x25 into FFF8B8EE (intake cam 1). The adaptation factor (0.5...1.5, cal 0x3BBCE/0x3BBCC) is stepped by the current error = expected current (Expected Current table) - measured FFF88D70 x 2.5/65536 while the duty is >= 20 % (cal 0x3BBC4). Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake AVCS OCV Adaptation Step (Cam 2)
table.description:
Step size, by valve current error, for learning the intake cam 2 oil control valve current correction. Same role as the cam 1 table.
Details: When used: intake cam 2 OCV (0x15F158, current FFF88D72) (read); as Intake AVCS OCV Adaptation Step (Cam 1). Confidence: read.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS OCV Adaptation Step (Cam 1)
table.description:
Step size, by valve current error, for learning the exhaust cam 1 oil control valve current correction. Same role as the intake tables.
Details: When used: exhaust cam 1 OCV (0x163394, current FFF88D84) (read); as the intake table, enable cal 0x3CACC = 0. Confidence: read.

table.description:
Step size, by valve current error, for learning the exhaust cam 2 oil control valve current correction. Same role as the intake tables.
Details: When used: exhaust cam 2 OCV (0x163788, current FFF88D86) (read); as the intake table. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 1)
table.description:
Proportional part of the intake cam 1 oil control valve duty by rpm and cam error (target minus actual) while driving (pedal applied or moving). Larger values move the cam faster but can overshoot.
Details: Axis (read, see FU_UNITS): cam error = target - actual in crank degrees (intake: advance, exhaust: retard). When used: the main (driving) AVCS proportional duty, used whenever the idle variant is not: the accelerator is applied or vehicle speed is at least 4 km/h (FFF88BE8 x 9/160 >= cal 0x3B904) (read, 0x15DF20 / 0x15E63C intake, 0x16269C / 0x162D18 exhaust). Rows rpm, columns cam error (degrees); the duty term is summed with the rate (D) term and scaled by the oil-temperature factor into the OCV duty. 32768 = 0 %. Same shape and scaling as the idle variant (Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Idle, Cam 1)). Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 2)
table.description:

Details: Axis (read, see FU_UNITS): cam error = target - actual in crank degrees (intake: advance, exhaust: retard). Rows rpm, columns cam error (degrees); the duty term is summed with the rate (D) term and scaled by the oil-temperature factor into the OCV duty. 32768 = 0 %. Same shape and scaling as the idle variant (Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Idle, Cam 2)). Confidence: read.

table.description:
Proportional part of the exhaust cam 1 oil control valve duty by rpm and cam error (target minus actual) while driving. Larger values move the cam towards its target faster but can overshoot. The idle variant is used with the pedal released at standstill.
Details: Axis (read, see FU_UNITS): cam error = target - actual in crank degrees (intake: advance, exhaust: retard). Same shape and scaling as the idle variant (Exhaust AVCS Feedback Duty (Idle, Cam 1)). Confidence: read.

When used: the main (driving) AVCS proportional duty, used whenever the idle variant is not: the accelerator is applied or FFF88E7E >= cal 0x3B904 x 128 (FFF88E7E not identified) (read, 0x15DF20 / 0x15E63C intake, 0x16269C / 0x162D18 exhaust). table.name: AVCS Activation Delay After Start (Second)
table.description:
A second start-delay table that can only shorten the AVCS hold after the hold has already ended, so it never changes anything. Edit AVCS Activation Delay After Start instead.
Details: 0x15B59C (read): the hold threshold is 05E408 while the hold flag FFF86848 is set or the engine is stopped (FFF88A76 = 0, which also clears FFF8683B); only after the hold has ended does it become min(05E408, this). Since FFF88A76 only rises while running and coolant at start FFF88A46 is fixed, min(05E408, this) <= 05E408 <= A76/2 can never set the hold again; a stall resets A76 to 0 and restores 05E408 first. So this table has no effect on the output (read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake AVCS OCV Current Integral Step
table.description:
Integral step for the intake oil control valve current loop. a calibration setting forces the integral term to zero.
Details: When used: cal 0x3BBD1 = 90 (non-zero) forces the I term to 0 (0x15ED58, read). Otherwise the I term FFF868EC (limits +/-25 by cal 0x3BBC6/0x3BBC8, then 0...2) moves by this(current error) x cal 0x3BBBC/100 / 32768 per pass and is added before the battery factor. Read by 0x15ED58 (cam 1) and as 05E71C by 0x15F158 (cam 2), same data 0x03BC50. 0x15ED58 / 0x15F158 (intake cam 1 / 2) and 0x163394 / 0x163788 (exhaust cam 1 / 2), read: OCV output = (I term + duty FFF8B8EA x coil factor x adaptation factor) x battery factor, stored x25 into FFF8B8EE (intake cam 1). Confidence: read.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS OCV Current Integral Step
table.description:
Integral step for the exhaust oil control valve current loop. a calibration setting forces the exhaust integral term to zero.
Details: When used: cal 0x3CACD = 90 forces the exhaust I term to 0 (0x163394, read). Same role as Intake AVCS OCV Current Integral Step; read as 05EA4C by 0x163788 (same data 0x03CB4C). Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake OCV Base Duty (Cam 1, Legacy Path)
table.description:
Base intake cam 1 valve duty by rpm for an older, byte-based cam control path.
Base term by rpm of the intake cam 1 OCV duty in the legacy byte-based AVCS path: about 49.2-52.0 % duty before the FFF88AA4 factor; the learned and feedback bytes are added around 128 (= 51.2 %). Module (read): seg 0x100000 0x104xxx-0x106xxx is the byte-based cam path; 0x10466C (intake, called at seg_0x100000.c:3516 with rpm CD54, FFF88AA4, learned bytes FFF8147A/147C/147E, feedback bytes FFF8B368, cam errors B956/B954) forms per cam: B352 = this(rpm) x 026EB0/026EC0(FFF88AA4)/128; B356 = 147A if the cam error >= cal 0x26E82 (364 = 2.0 deg), 147C if <= cal 0x26E84 (-2.0 deg), else 128; B366 = clamp(B368 + B352 + 147E + B356 - 384, 0, 250). 0x106A0C does the same for the exhaust cams (05CF08/05CF14, factors 0298F4/029904, errors B916/B914, thresholds cal 0x298C6/0x298C8) into B380. The OCV duty routines 0x15DF20 / 0x15E63C (intake cam 1 / 2) and 0x16269C / 0x162D18 (exhaust) set duty B8DE = B366[cam] x 10 (B380 for exhaust) only when cal 0x3CCC4 bit 0 is clear (read). FFF88AA4 = (FFF88AE6 >> 8 - 10) x 1.6 (0x060000 area, read); FFF88AE6 not identified. Confidence: inferred.
