table.name: Cruise Integrator Preset (Engage)
table.description:
Value the cruise controller's integral term is preset to when cruise starts controlling or returns to holding speed, by speed and acceleration.
Details: Cruise module 0x165AC4/0x1663AC, 20 ms task (read). Cruise runs on this 6MT ROM: cal 0x57788 = 0x03 enables the analog steering-switch input FFF88E76 (0x08DF14: main switch -> FFF88EC9 b6; two momentary switches -> FFF88EC9 b1 (raises the set speed) and b0 (lowers it), read; 'accelerate'/'coast' are inferred names); no MT-coding gate was found. 0x16AF7C (read): the controller integrator FFF86B48 is preset to (feed-forward + this(speed FFF8B9F4, acceleration FFF8B9C2) x 0.025) / 2 on the pass cruise control starts controlling (FFF8AB40 b5 rising) and on the change from state 0xCF to the hold state 0x33. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Cruise Integrator Preset (After Tap)
table.description:
Value the cruise controller's integral term is preset to after a set-speed switch tap, by speed and acceleration, so speed settles smoothly.
Details: Cruise module 0x165AC4/0x1663AC, 20 ms task (read). Cruise runs on this 6MT ROM: cal 0x57788 = 0x03 enables the analog steering-switch input FFF88E76 (0x08DF14: main switch -> FFF88EC9 b6; two momentary switches -> FFF88EC9 b1 (raises the set speed) and b0 (lowers it), read; 'accelerate'/'coast' are inferred names); no MT-coding gate was found. 0x16AF7C (read): the controller integrator FFF86B48 is preset to (feed-forward + this(speed FFF8B9F4, acceleration FFF8B9C2) x 0.025) / 2 on the change from state 0x23 to 0x33 (enabled by cal 0x3F850 b3 = 1) and from 0xB0 to 0x33 (cal 0x3F850 b4 = 1). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Cruise Vehicle Speed from CAN Speed
table.description:
Converts the CAN vehicle speed into the speed used by cruise control, per meter (market) code, as a straight line (scale and offset). The offsets probably make the set speed match the speedometer.
Details: Cruise module 0x165AC4/0x1663AC, 20 ms task (read). Cruise runs on this 6MT ROM: cal 0x57788 = 0x03 enables the analog steering-switch input FFF88E76 (0x08DF14: main switch -> FFF88EC9 b6; two momentary switches -> FFF88EC9 b1 (raises the set speed) and b0 (lowers it), read; 'accelerate'/'coast' are inferred names); no MT-coding gate was found. 0x16C2D0 (read): while FFF88E28 b0 and the VDC CAN fault FFF88BF9 b0 are clear and FFF88B94 b2 is set, the cruise speed FFF8B9F4 = filter(this(meter code FFF8A88C, CAN speed FFF8B4C2), weight 05F054); otherwise B9F4 = cal 0x4073C (10 km/h). The column axis is 0 and 5333 (300 km/h) followed by 14 points just above 300 km/h (5334-5347) holding the same values, so each row is a straight line: speed x k + offset (edit columns 2-16 together). The row offsets look like speedometer corrections so the set speed matches the meter (inferred). Above 300 km/h the last column holds. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Cruise Vehicle Speed Filter Weight
table.description:
Smoothing weight for the vehicle speed used by cruise control, by speed error and speed. Larger = less smoothing, quicker reaction.
Details: Cruise module 0x165AC4/0x1663AC, 20 ms task (read). Cruise runs on this 6MT ROM: cal 0x57788 = 0x03 enables the analog steering-switch input FFF88E76 (0x08DF14: main switch -> FFF88EC9 b6; two momentary switches -> FFF88EC9 b1 (raises the set speed) and b0 (lowers it), read; 'accelerate'/'coast' are inferred names); no MT-coding gate was found. 0x16C2D0 (read): first-order filter (0x6CEC) of 05F040's output into FFF8B9F4 with this weight. Axis 1 = FFF8B9C4 = speed - cruise target while cruise is controlling, else 0 (0x1693D8, read; shown in km/h); axis 2 = the previous filtered speed. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Cruise Excess Acceleration Threshold (Meter Cruise Option, Alternate)
table.description:
With one cruise option and an alternate flag only: if the car accelerates faster than this (by speed) for 0.2 s while cruise is on without pedal input, cruise ends (probably a runaway check).
Details: Cruise module 0x165AC4/0x1663AC, 20 ms task (read). Cruise runs on this 6MT ROM: cal 0x57788 = 0x03 enables the analog steering-switch input FFF88E76 (0x08DF14: main switch -> FFF88EC9 b6; two momentary switches -> FFF88EC9 b1 (raises the set speed) and b0 (lowers it), read; 'accelerate'/'coast' are inferred names); no MT-coding gate was found. 0x16E6EC (read): used only while FFF811E1 b4 and FFF8AB40 b2 are set (05F080 otherwise, not defined here). Counts passes in FFF8AB5A while cruise is active (FFF88E12 b1) without pedal override (88E12 b5), FFF88E28 b0 / 88A26 b0 clear, manifold pressure FFF88A34 >= cal 0x409FC (53 kPa) and acceleration FFF8B9C2 >= this(speed); more than cal 0x409FE (10 passes, 0.2 s) sets FFF8AB43 b3, which ends cruise via 0x16E314 (inferred: runaway-acceleration check). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Cruise Acceleration Cancel Threshold (Meter Cruise Option)
table.description:
With one cruise option only: if the car accelerates faster than this (by speed) for 3 s while cruise is on, cruise is cancelled and stays unavailable for the rest of the drive (probably a runaway check).
Details: When used: only with the meter flag FFF811E1 bit 4 ('Meter Cruise Option', CAN 0x282) and FFF88BB2 bit 2, while cruise is active (FFF88E12 bit 1) and has been for cal 0x35C02 = 200 passes without FFF88E12 bit 5. 0x119200 (read; 10 ms task via 0x110AAC; arguments from the call at seg_0x110000:601): FFF8A8A4 bit 3 is set after cal 0x35C00 = 300 passes (3 s) of FFF8B3F8 > cal 0x35BFC (24000 = 74 ft-lb, 100 Nm) together with either (a) the acceleration FFF88E78 > this(cruise vehicle speed FFF8B9F4), or (b) speed above the set speed FFF8B9FA by more than cal 0x35BFE (3 km/h) for 200 passes, no raise/lower switch edge (FFF88E11 bits 4/5) for 200 passes and FFF88E78 > cal 0x35BFA (1.75 km/h/s). FFF8A8A4 bit 3 latches FFF88E13 bit 4 for the rest of the drive (0x11BCA8, never cleared, read), which with the meter flag and the main switch sets FFF8AB43 bit 6 (0x16DED0) and that clears the cruise-engaged bit FFF88E12 bit 0 (0x16F194) (read): cruise is cancelled and stays unavailable. FFF8B3F8 = CAN 0x161 bytes 1:0 (FFF88BAE) x 8 - 64000 in torque_nm units (0x10E640, read; which unit sends it is not identified). FFF88E78 = speed change over 1.01 s in km/h x 128 (0x06B526, read). Physical purpose (runaway / unexpected acceleration check) inferred. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Brake Override Pedal Limit Ramp-Down Rate
table.description:

The module sets no DTC (no DTC monitor record points at its RAM, read). 0x182900 (read, lookup by speed FFF8AC95 checked in the assembly at 0x182A6E): limit FFF8BAFA = max(previous limit - this, Brake Override Pedal Limit Floor), capped at cal 0x433B6 = 26214 (40 % pedal); if the pedal is below the limit the limit follows the pedal. FFF88A5E = min(pedal, limit). Larger = faster torque cut when brake and accelerator overlap. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Brake Override Pedal Limit Floor
table.description:
Lowest pedal value, by vehicle speed, that brake override ramps the accelerator signal down to. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.
Details: When used: while brake override is active (FFF8AC8F bit 0). Brake override module 0x181B38 (10 ms task 0x1DFE3C, read): it limits the accelerator pedal that feeds the torque request, FFF88A5E = min(pedal FFF88EE6, limit FFF8BAFA) (0x09E800, read), when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Brake Override Recovery Rate (Pedal Held)
table.description:
How fast, by vehicle speed, the pedal limit is raised again after the brake is released while the driver keeps the accelerator pressed. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.
Details: When used: after the brake is released (recovery FFF8AC90 bit 7) in recovery state FFF8AC8E = 1. Brake override module 0x181B38 (10 ms task 0x1DFE3C, read): it limits the accelerator pedal that feeds the torque request, FFF88A5E = min(pedal FFF88EE6, limit FFF8BAFA) (0x09E800, read), when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. Brake detection: VDC CAN frame 0x0D1 byte 2 (FFF88DF9, slew-limited 8/pass into FFF8AC94; brake pressure, inferred) against a threshold, or discrete input FFF88E2F bit 3 (pin PF10; brake switch, inferred) when the pressure signal is not valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4 clear). Vehicle speed FFF8AC95 = km/h from the wheel speeds or FFF88BE8 x 9/160 (0x182E34, read). The module sets no DTC (no DTC monitor record points at its RAM, read). States 2-4 use 05F264 (655) and state 0 a time-based ramp (Brake Override Recovery Time). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Brake Override Recovery Time
table.description:
Time, by vehicle speed, over which full pedal is restored after brake override ends (recovery ends early if the pedal is released or reached). Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.
Details: When used: at the start of recovery (rising FFF8AC90 bit 7), latched into FFF8BB04 by 0x182DC0 (read; cal 0x43430 = 400 instead while the speed signal is faulty, FFF88E28 bit 0). Brake override module 0x181B38 (10 ms task 0x1DFE3C, read): it limits the accelerator pedal that feeds the torque request, FFF88A5E = min(pedal FFF88EE6, limit FFF8BAFA) (0x09E800, read), when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. Brake detection: VDC CAN frame 0x0D1 byte 2 (FFF88DF9, slew-limited 8/pass into FFF8AC94; brake pressure, inferred) against a threshold, or discrete input FFF88E2F bit 3 (pin PF10; brake switch, inferred) when the pressure signal is not valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4 clear). Vehicle speed FFF8AC95 = km/h from the wheel speeds or FFF88BE8 x 9/160 (0x182E34, read). The module sets no DTC (no DTC monitor record points at its RAM, read). In recovery state 0 0x182900 (read) raises the limit by max((pedal - limit) / (10 x remaining passes), 05F240 = 1 % per pass) with remaining = this - FFF8BAEE (passes spent in state 0, 0x181AB8); 0x1839F0 ends the recovery (FFF8AC90 bit 7 clear) when FFF8BAEE reaches this, when the limit reaches the pedal, or when the pedal is released. table.name: Brake Override Brake Pressure Threshold
table.description:
Brake pressure, by booster vacuum and vehicle speed, above which the brake counts as applied for brake override. Raise to make override need a firmer brake press. Used while the brake-pressure signal from the stability control unit is valid. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.
Details: When used: while the VDC brake-pressure signal is valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4, set after cal 0x435D6 = 100 passes with no CAN/VDC fault, 0x181978 / 0x1839B8). Brake override module 0x181B38 (10 ms task 0x1DFE3C, read): it limits the accelerator pedal that feeds the torque request, FFF88A5E = min(pedal FFF88EE6, limit FFF8BAFA) (0x09E800, read), when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. Brake detection: VDC CAN frame 0x0D1 byte 2 (FFF88DF9, slew-limited 8/pass into FFF8AC94; brake pressure, inferred) against a threshold, or discrete input FFF88E2F bit 3 (pin PF10; brake switch, inferred) when the pressure signal is not valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4 clear). Axis 1 is that vacuum (0-30 kPa = 0-4.35 psi). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Brake Override Delay
table.description:
How long the brake must be pressed over a held accelerator, by pedal position and speed, before brake override starts cutting the pedal signal (above 7 km/h). Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.
Details: When used: while the VDC brake-pressure signal is valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4); 05F2E0 (200 = 2 s, flat) replaces it otherwise. Brake override module 0x181B38 (10 ms task 0x1DFE3C, read): it limits the accelerator pedal that feeds the torque request, FFF88A5E = min(pedal FFF88EE6, limit FFF8BAFA) (0x09E800, read), when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. Brake detection: VDC CAN frame 0x0D1 byte 2 (FFF88DF9, slew-limited 8/pass into FFF8AC94; brake pressure, inferred) against a threshold, or discrete input FFF88E2F bit 3 (pin PF10; brake switch, inferred) when the pressure signal is not valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4 clear). FFF8AC91 bit 1 (or bit 0, the brake-switch path 0x183680) sets the active flag FFF8AC8F bit 0 (0x183B68), which starts the pedal-limit ramp. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Brake Override Deceleration Threshold (No Pressure Signal)

table.description:
Deceleration needed (by pedal and speed) to confirm braking when the brake-pressure signal is not available, so brake override can still act from the brake switch. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.
Details: When used: only while the VDC brake-pressure signal is not valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4 clear) and the brake was applied over the accelerator (FFF8AC90 bit 6). Brake detection: VDC CAN frame 0x0D1 byte 2 (FFF88DF9, slew-limited 8/pass into FFF8AC94; brake pressure, inferred) against a threshold, or discrete input FFF88E2F bit 3 (pin PF10; brake switch, inferred) when the pressure signal is not valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4 clear). FFF8AC91 bit 2 replaces the minimum-pedal condition of Brake Override Delay. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: VDC Torque Request Correction
table.description:
Correction, by the gap between the stability control (VDC) torque request and actual engine torque, that sets how tightly the ECU limits target torque during a VDC torque reduction (VDC meaning inferred).
Details: When used: every 10 ms (0x117778 from 0x110AAC, task 0x1DFE3C), effective while the VDC torque-reduction flag is active. 0x117778 (read; stack arguments checked in the disassembly: param_5 @36 = IAT FFF88A48, param_8 @48 = FFF8B404, param_9 @52 = FFF88B80 bit 2, param_10 @56 = FFF88DF6): on the active network variant (FFF88E0C bit 4) the request R is FFF888B6 = CAN 0x0D2 bytes 3:2 from the VDC unit (signals_rates_can, read), or the TCM limit FFF88DF6 x 20 + 10000 while FFF88B80 bit 2 (always clear on this MT car). Error e = R - FFF8B404 (the reported engine torque, see CAN Engine Torque Fuel-Cut Fade Rate) + 10000, floored at cal 0x35AB2 (-148 ft-lb, -200 Nm) -> FFF8B42A. Output FFF8B47C = R x 05D620(IAT)/128 + this(e) + an integrator FFF8568C (+0.4 ft-lb, +0.6 Nm per pass while e >= +2.2 ft-lb, +3 Nm, -0.4 ft-lb, -0.6 Nm per pass while e < 0, limited to -111..+111 ft-lb, -150..+150 Nm; cals 0x35AA6-0x35AB0) - offsets, floored at 0 ft-lb (read). table.name: Brake Booster Vacuum Model Maximum
table.description:
Upper limit, by barometric pressure, of a modelled brake-booster vacuum.
Brake override module 0x181B38 (10 ms task 0x1DFE3C, read): it limits the accelerator pedal that feeds the torque request, FFF88A5E = min(pedal FFF88EE6, limit FFF8BAFA) (0x09E800, read), when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. Brake detection: VDC CAN frame 0x0D1 byte 2 (FFF88DF9, slew-limited 8/pass into FFF8AC94; brake pressure, inferred) against a threshold, or discrete input FFF88E2F bit 3 (pin PF10; brake switch, inferred) when the pressure signal is not valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4 clear). Vehicle speed FFF8AC95 = km/h from the wheel speeds or FFF88BE8 x 9/160 (0x182E34, read). The module sets no DTC (no DTC monitor record points at its RAM, read). 0x182B28 (read, all stack args checked in the assembly) has three sources for the booster vacuum FFF8BAFC: cal 0x57585 bit 5 set = baro - analog pressure input FFF88D10; else bit 6 = fixed cal 0x43402 (50 kPa); else a model from manifold vacuum baro FFF88668 - MAP FFF88A34: while not braking at low manifold vacuum (FFF8AC90 bit 3 clear) the estimate is filtered (cal 0x43406) up towards the manifold vacuum as long as it is below this(baro); during braking it is reduced by 253 x 13/100 per count of brake-pressure rise (FFF8AC93 - FFF8AC92). Confidence: read.

table.name: Brake Booster Vacuum Model Manifold Threshold
table.description:
Manifold-vacuum threshold, by barometric pressure, for a brake-booster vacuum model.
Brake override module 0x181B38 (10 ms task 0x1DFE3C, read): it limits the accelerator pedal that feeds the torque request, FFF88A5E = min(pedal FFF88EE6, limit FFF8BAFA) (0x09E800, read), when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. Brake detection: VDC CAN frame 0x0D1 byte 2 (FFF88DF9, slew-limited 8/pass into FFF8AC94; brake pressure, inferred) against a threshold, or discrete input FFF88E2F bit 3 (pin PF10; brake switch, inferred) when the pressure signal is not valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4 clear). Vehicle speed FFF8AC95 = km/h from the wheel speeds or FFF88BE8 x 9/160 (0x182E34, read). The module sets no DTC (no DTC monitor record points at its RAM, read). 0x18390C (read): FFF8AC90 bit 3 = brake pressure FFF8AC94 >= cal 0x435BD (1) and FFF88A38 >= this(baro FFF88668) - 12800 (FFF88A38 = (MAP - baro)/2, so MAP - baro >= (this - 12800)/128 kPa), i.e. braking with too little manifold vacuum to recharge the booster. Bit 3 feeds only the brake-pressure latches FFF8AC92 / FFF8AC93 / FFF8BAFE and the manifold-vacuum model of 0x182B28, whose results are unused while cal 0x57585 bit 5 is set and FFF8BB00 has no reader (read, grep). Confidence: read.

table.name: Alternator Command from Target Voltage
table.description:
Alternator control duty by target charging voltage (probably). Changing it changes the charging voltage the alternator actually reaches. Also feeds Idle Air Trim (Charging Command).
Details: When used: every pass of the charging module (0x138BB0, called from the module body at seg 0x130000, read): B71E = clamp(this(target FFF8B6F4), cal 0x397CE = 167, cal 0x397D0 = 1500); B718 = B71E (cal 0x57584 bit 4 clear, 0x1373C8). B718 is written to timer E channel 20 as duty = min(B718, 1667)/1667 (0, below 17) by 0x1E0000 -> 0x1D98AC (read), so 1667 = 100 % duty: the alternator control duty (inferred). B718 also drives Idle Air Trim (Charging Command) and the electrical-load idle logic. B6F4 is the rate-limited charging target (0x136854), starting at cal 0x399B6 = 14300 (mV, inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: Radiator Fan Duty (Coolant)
table.description:
Radiator fan duty by coolant for an alternate (duty-based) fan control path.
With cal 0x1D0AE bit 0 set, 0x0F8AAC (read) uses this when received byte FFF88BAA (CAN 0x282 byte 3) < cal 0x342EC (148, 146 to fall back) and FFF8A807 bit 5 is clear: duty B27C = this(coolant FFF88A44) once coolant >= cal 0x342DC (95 C, falls off 3 C lower), 100 % from cal 0x342E4 (100 C); used in fan mode 1 (0x0F7A88). Radiator fan module 0x0F7618 (40 ms task, read): the fan stage FFF8A805 (0/1/2) drives timer E channel 10 fully on for stage >= 1 (FFF9981C bit 0, 0x0F8F08 -> 0x1E417C -> 0x1D9B8E) and port PF6 for stage 2 (FFF9981C bit 4, 0x0F8E70 -> 0x1D4E56 -> PFDR), and feeds the idle air (0x0ECE60, 0x0F5248) and torque adders (0x0C2B2C); the stages follow coolant and the A/C request (0x0F8764), so a two-relay radiator fan (inferred). With the bit set, A805 = stage from the duty FFF8B278 (0x0F7EC4: stage 1 from 40 %, stage 2 from 70 %). Confidence: read.

table.name: Radiator Fan Duty (A/C, CAN 0x280 Value)

table.name: Engine Torque from Load (CAN, DAM 1.0)
table.description:
Engine torque by rpm and load at DAM 1.0, blended with the DAM 0 table by DAM. Only affects the maximum-available torque value the ECU sends over CAN to other modules (inferred meaning); it does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost. table.name: CAN Engine Torque Fuel-Cut Fade Rate
table.description:
How fast, by rpm, the engine torque reported over CAN to other modules (for example stability control) fades out at a fuel cut and returns after it. It does not change fuelling or throttle.
Details: When used: always while running, 10 ms (0x10ED6C from 0x111AB8, task 0x1DFE3C, read). Axis FFF8CE9C (rpm; the function's param_1, read). A weight w = FFF854FC moves toward 0 while the cylinder fuel cut FFF8A64C bit 0 is set and toward 0xFF00 otherwise, by (target - w) x this/255 per pass (read). The DAM-blended engine torque FFF8B48A (= DAM x B490/16 + (16 - DAM) x B4A2/16, DAM FFF811AE) is scaled by w/0xFF00 about the 16000 zero point (B48E, read), and FFF8B404 = (that - 16000 - (05D3E4(rpm, FFF88AE6) + FFF8B46E + FFF8AF62 - 48000))/8 + 10000, i.e. faded torque minus loss terms in 10000 + 10 x Nm (read). FFF8B404 is packed into the engine CAN TX frames (0x08B1B6 / 0x08C220, bytes FFF8CC91/92) and is the 'actual torque' of the VDC torque-request loop 0x117778 (VDC Torque Request Correction); B48E and A8F0 (= w >> 8) have no readers (ram_xref, read). So this only shapes how fast the torque reported to the other control units falls at a fuel cut and returns after it; it does not change fuelling or the throttle directly. Confidence: read.

table.name: MAF Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts MAF sensor voltage to airflow (g/s) in 64 fixed steps from 0 to 4.92 V; this airflow drives the ECU's air model, load and fuel. Rescale every point when fitting a bigger intake or a different MAF, and keep peak flow below the P0103 voltage limit. An internal 218 g/s cap on one copy of the airflow affects only purge, TGV, monitors and similar side functions, not fuel, load or timing.
Details: When used: always (4 ms task prefix 0x1E2CB4, read). ADC channel 2 (0xFFFFE844) -> FFF8C990 (10-bit) x ADC trim FFF82038 / 32768, capped at 1023, x 64 -> FFF8CA48 -> FFF88A1A (0x1D87C8, read). FFF82038 is a per-unit gain trim copied at start from a stored data block (FFF81050, 0x1CF324) and used only within 125/128...131/128, else 1.0 (cals 0x28BA2 / 0x28BA3 / 0x28BA0, read); 65536 = 5 V (inferred). 0x06CA98 subtracts a start-up correction (only while FFF88CE5 is set) and floors at MAF Sensor Voltage Floor -> FFF88CFA; 0x06C9F8 looks up FFF88CFA >> 2 in this 64-point u32 table (boot routine 0x68EC: index = input / 256 with linear interpolation, input capped at 0x3F00, so above 4.92 V the last point holds) -> FFF8921C -> FFF88820. g/s = value / 76800 (OBD PID 0x10 chain, read). The axis is implicit: point n is at n x 0.078125 V (0...4.92 V). FFF88820 feeds the manifold/airflow model 0x11D704 / 0x11D4E4, which the load and fuel calculations use, and the torque model 0x0C3E34 (read). For a bigger housing or another MAF, rescale every point to the new g/s at that voltage and keep peak flow below MAF Sensor Voltage High Limit. Limits elsewhere (read): the scan-tool/OBD MAF value FFF88A4A saturates at 300 g/s, and FFF8B4D6, a u16 copy of the model's air quantity (g/s x 300), saturates at 218 g/s (0x11DEE0). That 218 g/s cap does not limit fuel, load, ignition or boost. The base fuel quantity (0x0B8030) and engine load (0x0B7EFC) are computed from the unsaturated cylinder flow FFF8C250, and no ignition routine reads FFF8B4D6. Its readers are: the evap purge module (0x0D4C14, 0x0D4E78: purge flow = purge rate x air) and the evap monitor 0x18C3B0; TGV request logic and TGV transition fuel (0x10D93C, 0x0CA144); the EGR fresh-air option; the torque model's air-path lag lookup (0x0C34F8, axis ends at 208 g/s); the exhaust temperature model's filter and fuel-cut terms (0x0C9878, axis ends at 210 g/s); catalyst/rear-O2 heater energy and OBD monitor enables (0x101CF0, 0x134374, 0x1B3280, 0x1B3A48, 0x1259EC, 0x09FE44); charging control (0x136CD8, 0x13741C); the 'air since start' sum 0x10A270; and the CAN full-load air estimate 0x110444. All of these use thresholds far below 218 g/s, or axes whose last breakpoint is below it. The only one that can still change above 218 g/s is the CAN estimate, which takes the larger of FFF8B4D6 and its own value (inferred: little effect). The limits that matter at high airflow are the 4.92 V end of this table, MAF Sensor Voltage High Limit, the 256 % (3.31 g/rev) ceiling of engine load (0x0B7EFC) and Base Fuel Quantity Limit; the model's cylinder flow FFF8C250 itself does not saturate. Identical in both images. Confidence: read.

table.name: MAP Sensor Multiplier
table.description:
Gain of the manifold pressure sensor conversion, in kPa per volt. For a 3-bar or larger sensor set it to the new sensor's slope and set MAP Sensor Offset to match. The ECU's MAP value cannot go above 256 kPa absolute (about 22 psi boost at sea level) whatever sensor is fitted, so anything higher reads as 256 kPa.
Details: When used: always (2 ms task prefix 0x1E2AA2; also 0x1E220A / 0x1E4D00 at start-up, read). MAP (kPa x 256) = ADC channel 18 sample FFF88D3A (16-bit left-justified 10-bit value, not corrected by the ADC trim FFF82038) x this >> 8 + MAP Sensor Offset, limited to 0...65535 (0x6E00, read) -> FFF8913C, the MAP the engine uses (-> FFF88A34 -> FFF88666; FFF8869C for the airflow model) and FFF89040 / FFF89A32 (OBD MAP). FFF89140 = the same minus 0xD4C (13.3 kPa), limited the same way, is the boost-control pressure FFF88FF4. With 65536 = 5 V (inferred) the unit is kPa per volt = value / 5. Hard limit (read): the MAP value cannot exceed 255.99 kPa absolute (about 22.3 psi gauge at sea level) whatever sensor is fitted. To fit a different (e.g. 3-bar) sensor: this = sensor slope in kPa per V x 5, and MAP Sensor Offset = sensor kPa at 0 V x 256; example 0.5 V = 20 kPa, 4.5 V = 300 kPa -> 70 kPa/V -> 350, offset -15 kPa -> -3840. Readings above 256 kPa are still clipped. Range faults use raw voltage: P0107 below MAP Sensor Voltage Low Limit, P0108 above MAP Sensor Voltage High Limit; while the MAP fault flag FFF88E28 bit 3 is set MAP = cal 0x58EA4 x FFF8ADF0 / 32768 instead (read). The TMAP's temperature element is probably Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 (change that table too if the new sensor's thermistor differs). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: MAP Sensor Offset
table.description:
Offset of the manifold pressure sensor conversion, i.e. the sensor's reading extrapolated to 0 V. Set it together with MAP Sensor Multiplier when fitting a different MAP sensor. The result is still limited to 256 kPa absolute.
Details: When used: always (2 ms task prefix 0x1E2AA2, read): offset of the MAP conversion in kPa x 256, added to sample x MAP Sensor Multiplier >> 8 before the result is limited to 0...65535 (255.99 kPa). Equals the sensor's (extrapolated) reading at 0 V. For a different sensor: offset = kPa at 0 V x 256 = (kPa at V1 - slope x V1) x 256; example 0.5 V = 20 kPa, 4.5 V = 300 kPa -> -15 kPa -> -3840. Confidence: read.

table.name: MAF Sensor Voltage Floor
table.description:
Lowest value the corrected MAF voltage may reach after the ECU subtracts its post-start MAF correction (a decaying start-up offset); it applies at all times after the first pass. Normally leave alone.
Details: Lower limit of the dynamically corrected MAF voltage FFF88CFA (0x06CA98, read). The correction (voltage minus a gain x rate term, cal 0x5758E/0x57590/0x57587) only runs while FFF88CE5 is set. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts the main intake air temperature sensor voltage to degrees; this IAT feeds the timing, boost and fuel compensations and the scan-tool reading. Its voltage axis is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling, so edit only the temperatures when fitting a different sensor.
Details: When used: always (10 ms task prefix 0x1E2F20 / 0x06AF58, read). ADC channel 19 (0xFFFFE864, untrimmed) -> FFF88D38 -> FFF88F30, filtered by cal 0x579B6 -> FFF88F34 / FFF88F32, looked up here (boot lookup 0x7250) to give FFF88662 = degC + 50: the OBD IAT FFF8CEE5, the IAT behind FFF88A48 (the IAT axis of the timing, boost, throttle and fuel compensation tables) and the IAT read by fuel 0x0C589C and purge 0x0D4E78 (for Purge Air Density (IAT, Baro), 0x0D44DC) (read). This is IAT sensor 1 (P0112 / P0113, read), probably the element in the MAF housing (inferred). The voltage axis (0x579FC, 32 points 0...4.96 V in 0.16 V steps; 65536 = 5 V inferred) is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling: change only the temperature values for a different thermistor, or both sensors move. While the sensor is faulted (FFF88E28 bit 2) the fixed voltage cal 0x579BA x 256 is used. Descriptor boot 0579DC. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling
table.description:
Converts the second intake temperature sensor's voltage to degrees. This is the air temperature the ECU's airflow model uses to work out air density, and it probably comes from the manifold pressure (TMAP) sensor, so update it when you swap that sensor for one with a different thermistor. Its voltage axis is shared with the main IAT table; change only the temperatures.
Details: When used: always (10 ms task prefix 0x1E2F20 / 0x06B304, read). ADC channel 20 (0xFFFFE868, untrimmed) -> FFF88D40 -> FFF88F36, filtered by cal 0x579B8 -> FFF88F38 / FFF88F3A, looked up here (boot lookup 0x7250) into FFF888CF (degC + 50; FFF888D4 from the unfaulted value). This is IAT sensor 2 (P0097 / P0098 monitors on the same voltage, read). FFF888CF is the air temperature of the speed-density airflow model (0x11DF4C: density from MAP and IAT 2 + 223 K) and is also read by requested torque 0x0BE694, ignition 0x0D98F8 / 0x0D9A10 / 0x0DE0E0 and AVCS 0x15969C (read), so a wrong curve shifts the modelled air and load. Probably the thermistor of the manifold TMAP sensor (inferred from its use as the manifold air temperature): when fitting a different TMAP / MAP sensor with its own thermistor, change these temperature values. The voltage axis (0x579FC) is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor Scaling, so change only the data. While faulted (FFF88FCD bit 2) the fixed voltage cal 0x579BB x 256 is used. Descriptor boot 0579E8. Confidence: read.

table.name: Coolant Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts coolant temperature sensor voltage to degrees. Every coolant-based table and the scan-tool coolant reading use this. Change only when fitting a different sensor.
Details: When used: always (40 ms task prefix 0x1E43FE / 0x06BA46, read). Coolant sensor voltage FFF8865E (input 0 of the 8-way multiplexer on ADC channel 21, untrimmed, 65536 = 5 V inferred) is filtered by cal 0x56EE8 (65535 = no filter) into FFF88ADC and looked up here (boot lookup 0x73BC) into FFF88AE8 / FFF88AE0 (256 x (degC + 50)): FFF8CD65 (coolant byte, degC + 50), the OBD coolant value and FFF88A44 (the coolant axis of most tables). While the sensor is faulted (FFF88E28 bit 1) a warm-up model from cals 0x56EEC-0x56EF2 replaces it. Range faults: P0117 below Coolant Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit, P0118 above Coolant Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit. Change only when fitting a different sensor. Descriptor boot 057A00. Confidence: read.

table.name: Oil Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts oil temperature sensor voltage to degrees; this oil temperature feeds the AVCS and idle tables and the scan-tool reading. Change only when fitting a different sensor.
Details: When used: always (40 ms task prefix 0x1E43FE / 0x06BEA0, read). Oil temperature sensor voltage FFF88AA2 (input 7 of the 8-way multiplexer on ADC channel 21, untrimmed) is filtered by cal 0x56F76 (65535 = no filter) into FFF88AE4 and looked up here (boot lookup 0x73BC). Output unit 256 x (degC + 50), read: FFF88E24 = (output - 0xA00) x 256 / 205 and OBD PID 0x5C reports FFF88E24 x 205 / 65536 = degC + 40. FFF88E24 / FFF88E26 is the oil temperature of the AVCS and idle tables (oil_temp_obd axis). Range faults: P0197 below Oil Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit, P0198 above Oil Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit. Descriptor boot 057A0C. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Sensor Scaling (Wide Range)
table.description:
Converts the front wideband A/F sensor signal to lambda when the reading is outside about lambda 0.90-1.37. This is the measured lambda used by closed loop fueling.
Details: When used: Used while FFF88AFB bit 4 is clear: the A/F signal is outside about lambda 0.90-1.37 (window -800..1000 with hysteresis 333, 0x0843F8, read); gain cal 0x571F0 = 2. 0x06C1A8 (read): the A/F sensor signal FFF88B2E is looked up here (boot lookup 0x6A0C) into FFF88AF6, the measured lambda of the closed loop (B308 = 43194 x 32768 / FFF88AF6, 0x0FF3CC). Descriptor boot 057A18. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Sensor Scaling (Near Stoich)
table.description:
Converts the front A/F sensor signal to lambda when it reads within about lambda 0.90-1.37, at a higher gain.
Details: When used: Used while the A/F signal is within about lambda 0.90-1.37 (FFF88AFB bit 4 set, 0x0843F8, read); higher gain cal 0x571F1 = 9 (gain reading inferred). Second A/F sensor table in 0x06C1A8 (read); shares the axis with A/F Sensor Scaling (Wide Range). Descriptor boot 057A24. Confidence: read.

table.name: Fuel Level Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts the fuel sender reading, which the instrument cluster sends to the ECU over CAN, to fuel level (219 = 100 %). The ECU averages it and reports it as fuel level to a scan tool.
Details: When used: always (0x06C336, read). Input: the fuel sender reading sent by the combination meter on CAN 0x282 bytes 0-1 (10-bit, FFF88E04 -> 0x1108B8 -> FFF8B43C; not an ECU analog input). 0x06C336 forms FFF88BD0 = FFF8B43C x 2867 / (FFF8B43C + cal 0x572E0 (720)), filters it into FFF88BCC and looks it up here (boot lookup 0x7250) into FFF88BD4; FFF88BD7 is its average over cal 0x572E6 samples taken while FFF88A76 is at least cal 0x572E4, kept in backup RAM FFF806BB/806BC, and reported by OBD PID 0x2F as x 255 / 219 (read). So this is the fuel level curve, 219 = 100 %. P0463 / P0462 when FFF88BCC is above cal 0x572DA / below cal 0x572DE (0x0714E0 / 0x071548, read). Descriptor boot 057A30. Confidence: read.

table.name: MAP Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0107)
table.description:
Sensor voltage below which the MAP sensor is flagged as shorted low (P0107) and a substitute MAP is used. It works on raw voltage, so it does not change when you rescale the MAP sensor.
Details: When used: always while the monitor is enabled (FFF88E66 bit 1, FFF89183 = 0). 0x06FC80 (read): P0107 (FFF89B0B bit 2, record slot of P0107) is set when the MAP sensor sample FFF88D3A (ADC channel 18, 16-bit left-justified, not trimmed) stays below this for cal 0x56702 (200) passes; while set the ECU replaces MAP by cal 0x58EA4 x FFF8ADF0 / 32768 (fault flag FFF88E28 bit 3, read in 0x1E2AA2). It compares raw voltage, so it does not move when MAP Sensor Multiplier / Offset are changed. A replacement sensor whose lowest output (engine-off vacuum is not reached, so the lowest is about 20-30 kPa) is above this needs no change. Confidence: read.

table.name: MAP Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0108)
table.description:
Sensor voltage above which the MAP sensor is flagged as shorted high (P0108). Raw voltage, independent of the MAP scaling.
Details: When used: always while the monitor is enabled (FFF88E66 bit 1, FFF89183 = 0). 0x06FC80 (read): P0108 (FFF89B0B bit 1) is set when the MAP sensor sample FFF88D3A stays above this for cal 0x56703 (200) passes; the substitute MAP is then used (FFF88E28 bit 3). Raw voltage, independent of MAP Sensor Multiplier / Offset. Note the MAP value itself is limited to 255.99 kPa (see MAP Sensor Multiplier) whatever the voltage. Confidence: read.

table.name: MAF Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0102)
table.description:
MAF voltage below which the MAF circuit-low code P0102 is set.
Details: When used: with the ignition/run input on (FFF8A297 bit 1) for at least cal 0x5700D (26) passes and FFF88E66 bit 1 set. 0x070048 (read): P0102 (FFF89AFC bit 6) is set when the MAF voltage FFF88D48 (ADC channel 2 sample x 64, before the ADC trim and before the start-up correction) has been below this for cal 0x57007 (13) passes, cleared after cal 0x57008 (13) passes above. Confidence: read.

table.name: MAF Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0103)
table.description:
MAF voltage above which the MAF circuit-high code P0103 is set.
Details: When used: with the ignition/run input on (FFF8A297 bit 1) for at least cal 0x57009 (26) passes and FFF88E66 bit 1 set. 0x06FF70 (read): P0103 (FFF89AFC bit 5) is set when the MAF voltage FFF88D48 (ADC channel 2 x 64, untrimmed) has been above this for cal 0x57007 (13) passes, cleared after cal 0x57008 (13) passes below. With a larger MAF housing make sure peak flow stays below this voltage (the scaling table itself stops at 4.92 V); raising it towards 4.9 V is possible but leaves less margin to detect a shorted signal (inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0112)
table.description:
Voltage below which the main IAT sensor is flagged as shorted (reads impossibly hot, P0112).
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF89185 = 0. 0x070310 (read): P0112 (IAT circuit low, FFF89AFD bit 6) is set when the IAT sensor voltage FFF88D38 (ADC channel 19 x 64, untrimmed) is below this for cal 0x566F0 (13) passes. Low voltage = very hot reading (NTC). While the IAT is faulted (FFF88E28 bit 2) the ECU looks up the fixed voltage cal 0x579BA x 256 instead (0x06AF58, read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0113)
table.description:
Voltage above which the main IAT sensor is flagged as open (reads impossibly cold, P0113).
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF89185 = 0. 0x0702A8 (read): P0113 (IAT circuit high, FFF89AFD bit 5) is set when the IAT sensor voltage FFF88D38 (ADC channel 19) is above this for cal 0x566F1 (13) passes. High voltage = open circuit / very cold. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Voltage Low Limit (P0097)
table.description:
Voltage below which the second intake temperature sensor is flagged as shorted (P0097).
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF89188 = 0. 0x0703D4 (read): P0097 (IAT sensor 2 circuit low, FFF89B17 bit 0) is set when the IAT 2 sensor voltage FFF88D40 (ADC channel 20 x 64, untrimmed) is below this for cal 0x57014 (13) passes. While IAT 2 is faulted (FFF88FCD bit 2) the fixed voltage cal 0x579BB x 256 is used (0x06B304, read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Voltage High Limit (P0098)
table.description:
Voltage above which the second intake temperature sensor is flagged as open (P0098).
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF89188 = 0. 0x070378 (read): P0098 (IAT sensor 2 circuit high, FFF89B17 bit 1) is set when the IAT 2 sensor voltage FFF88D40 (ADC channel 20) is above this for cal 0x57010 (13) passes. Confidence: read.

table.name: Coolant Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0117)
table.description:
Voltage below which the coolant sensor is flagged as shorted (P0117).
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF8918B = 0. 0x070520 (read): P0117 (FFF89AFC bit 1) is set when the coolant sensor voltage FFF8865E (multiplexed ADC channel 21, input 0, untrimmed) is below this for cal 0x566F2 (13) passes. While the coolant sensor is faulted (FFF88E28 bit 1) the coolant value follows a warm-up model instead (cals 0x56EEC-0x56EF2, 0x06BA46, read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Coolant Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0118)
table.description:
Voltage above which the coolant sensor is flagged as open (P0118).
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF8918B = 0. 0x0704B8 (read): P0118 (FFF89AFC bit 0) is set when the coolant sensor voltage FFF8865E is above this for cal 0x566F3 (13) passes. Confidence: read.

table.name: Oil Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0197)
table.description:
Voltage below which the oil temperature sensor is flagged as shorted (P0197).
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF8919F = 0. 0x0705E4 (read): P0197 (FFF89B1D bit 6) is set when the oil temperature sensor voltage FFF88AA2 (multiplexed ADC channel 21, input 7, untrimmed) is below this for cal 0x5703A (13) passes. Confidence: read.

table.name: Oil Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0198)
table.description:
Voltage above which the oil temperature sensor is flagged as open (P0198).
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF8919F = 0. 0x070588 (read): P0198 (FFF89B1D bit 7) is set when the oil temperature sensor voltage FFF88AA2 is above this for cal 0x57037 (13) passes. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0192)
table.description:
Rail pressure sensor voltage below which P0192 (circuit low) is set.
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF891D1 = 0. 0x06FDF8 (read): P0192 (FFF89B17 bit 6) is set when the rail pressure sensor sample FFF88D44 (ADC channel 17, 16-bit, untrimmed) is below this for cal 0x56710 (250) passes. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0193)
table.description:
Rail pressure sensor voltage above which P0193 (circuit high) is set.
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF891D1 = 0. 0x06FDF8 (read): P0193 (FFF89B17 bit 7) is set when the rail pressure sensor sample FFF88D44 is above this for cal 0x56711 (250) passes. Raise it only together with a sensor or pump change. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Zero-Pressure Voltage
table.description:
Rail pressure sensor voltage that reads as zero pressure. Change it with Rail Pressure Sensor Gain only when fitting a different rail pressure sensor.
Details: When used: always (0x06D43A, read). Rail pressure FFF88F82 = Rail Pressure Sensor Gain x max(0, FFF88AAA - this) / 2, where FFF88AAA is the 10-bit sample of ADC channel 17 (FFF88D44 >> 6, 2 ms task 0x1E2AA2); the result is limited to Rail Pressure Sensor Maximum and becomes FFF88AAC and (filtered when FFF8A29C bit 0 is set) FFF88886, the rail pressure used by injection, the HPFP and the rail-pressure DTCs (read). For a different rail pressure sensor set this to its zero-pressure output. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Gain
table.description:
Slope of the rail pressure sensor conversion. Change it only for a different rail pressure sensor.
Details: When used: always (0x06D43A, read; a byte, read with MOVU.B). Rail pressure counts per 10-bit ADC count = this / 2 (counts of 0.61 kPa, 1639.34 per MPa). For a different sensor: this = sensor MPa per V / 0.062464. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Maximum
table.description:
Highest rail pressure the sensor conversion can report.
Details: When used: always (0x06D43A, read): the converted rail pressure is limited to this (unsigned min, 0x753C) before it becomes FFF88AAC / FFF88886. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Fault Value
table.description:
Rail pressure the ECU assumes while the rail pressure sensor is faulted. Normally leave alone.
Details: When used: while FFF88E2C bit 2 or FFF88EDA bit 7 is set (rail pressure sensor fault, inferred from the flags' use) the converted rail pressure is replaced by this (0x06D43A, read). Normally leave alone. Confidence: read.

table.name: Barometric Sensor Multiplier
table.description:
Gain of the ECU's barometric pressure sensor conversion, in kPa per volt. This sensor is probably inside the ECU; leave alone.
Details: When used: always (0x1D886A, read). Barometric pressure FFF8D060 (kPa x 256) = filtered sample FFF8D062 x this >> 8 + Barometric Sensor Offset, limited to 0...65535; FFF8D062 is a 3:1 running average of multiplexer channel 3 of ADC channel 12 (FFF8CA32, untrimmed). With 65536 = 5 V (inferred) the unit is kPa per volt = value / 5. FFF8D060 -> FFF8CE60 -> FFF88668 (rate-limited by cals 0x1D0B2 / 0x1D0B4 = 34 per pass), the barometric pressure every baro table and gauge-pressure conversion uses (read). The sensor is not one of the externally wired inputs (inferred: no harness connector was identified); normally leave alone. Confidence: read.

table.name: Barometric Sensor Offset
table.description:
Offset of the barometric pressure sensor conversion. Leave alone.
Details: When used: always (0x1D886A, read): offset of the barometric pressure conversion in kPa x 256 (see Barometric Sensor Multiplier). While the barometric sensor fault flag FFF88E2A bit 0 is set (passed to the driver as FFF8CA4C bit 7 by 0x1D766E, read) FFF8D060 is forced to 0x654C = 101.3 kPa. Confidence: read.

table.name: Barometric Sensor Enable
table.description:
When set, the ECU uses its barometric pressure sensor. When cleared, it assumes sea-level pressure (101.3 kPa) everywhere, so altitude compensation stops working.
Details: When used: always. 0x06AA54 (via 0x06B66A, read): with this bit set the barometric pressure FFF88668 follows the sensor value FFF8CE60 (rate-limited by cals 0x1D0B2 / 0x1D0B4); with it clear FFF88668 is fixed at 0x654C = 101.3 kPa and FFF886DE / FFF886DA are not updated (0x1E220A, 0x06B650, read). Clearing it makes every baro compensation assume sea level. Confidence: read.

table.name: P0088 Rail Pressure High Limit
table.description:
Fuel rail pressure limit for P0088 (rail pressure too high): the code trips when actual pressure exceeds this value plus a 2.5 MPa hysteresis for about 2 seconds, and also triggers fail-safe; after a trip, pressure must drop back to this value to recover. If you raise target rail pressure, keep peak actual pressure below this plus 2.5 MPa.
Details: 0x0752A8 (read): the absolute high-pressure test fails while actual FFF88884 > this + hysteresis cal 0x574DE (4098 = 2.5 MPa; the hysteresis widens the limit while the test is in its normal state, 0x6C4C) for cal 0x574E2 (200) passes, and recovers only when actual <= this; it sets FFF89BDE bit 2 -> P0088 and the fail-safe flag FFF88EDA bit 6 (0x080B96). If you raise target rail pressure, keep peak actual pressure below this + 2.5 MPa, and keep this above the normal operating pressure so a tripped test can recover. p16 (read): 0x0752A8 (<- 0x0A1D2C <- 0x1DFE3C) runs every 10 ms; 200 passes = 2 s, 1000 passes = 10 s. Confidence: read.

table.name: P0087 Rail Pressure Deviation Limit
table.description:
How far actual rail pressure may fall below target (in normal high-pressure pump operation) before P0087 sets, after about 10 seconds. Raising it makes the code harder to set.
Details: 0x0752A8 (read): in HPFP state FFF8AB35 = 3, target - actual > this for cal 0x574E6 (1000) passes sets P0087 (FFF89BDE bit 7 via bit 1); outside state 3 the limit is cal 0x577BA (65535 = off). p16 (read): 0x0752A8 (<- 0x0A1D2C <- 0x1DFE3C) runs every 10 ms; 200 passes = 2 s, 1000 passes = 10 s. Confidence: read.

table.name: P0088 Rail Pressure Deviation Limit
table.description:
How far actual rail pressure may rise above target (in normal high-pressure pump operation) before P0088 sets, after about 10 seconds. Raising it makes the code harder to set.
Details: 0x0752A8 (read): in HPFP state 3, actual - target > this for cal 0x574E8 (1000) passes sets P0088 (FFF89BDE bit 6 via bit 0); otherwise cal 0x577BC (off). p16 (read): 0x0752A8 (<- 0x0A1D2C <- 0x1DFE3C) runs every 10 ms; 200 passes = 2 s, 1000 passes = 10 s. Confidence: read.

table.name: P0087 Rail Pressure Low Limit
table.description:
Rail pressure floor by rpm for P0087 (rail pressure too low): the code counts a fault when actual pressure stays more than 0.30 MPa (hysteresis cal) below this value for about 10 seconds, and recovers when pressure is back at this value.
Details: 0x0752A8 (read, boot lookup 0x72AC): the absolute low-pressure test fails while actual rail pressure FFF88884 < this(rpm FFF8CD56) - hysteresis cal 0x574DA for cal 0x574E0 passes -> P0087. p16 (read): 0x0752A8 (<- 0x0A1D2C <- 0x1DFE3C) runs every 10 ms; 200 passes = 2 s, 1000 passes = 10 s. Descriptor boot 057B44. Confidence: read.

table.name: Cold Start Timing Monitor Band (Coolant)
table.description:
Diagnostic threshold, not a tuning table: how far final timing may exceed the cold-start spark target, by coolant, before the P050B cold-start timing monitor counts a fault. One entry edits all three copies.
Details: When used: one data block (0x04B0B2) read through three descriptors: 05B428, 0607FC and 060808 - this entry edits all three. (1) P050B cold-start timing monitor (0x1CB088 group): 0x1CB66C counts the passes where final timing FFF8A744 minus the active spark target FFF8A647 exceeds this (coolant FFF88A44), and 0x1CB6BC the passes where it does not, while the monitor runs (FFF8ADE2 bit 0) (read); see my research notes. (2) 0x0D8FC8: in the scan-tool mode set by UDS 0x2E DID 0x2004 (FFF89042 = 0xF0..0xF5, written by 0x0B0E6C, read) FFF8A729 = this + 0..10, added to the alternate timing path of 0x0D9E40 (read). Diagnostic, not a tuning table. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 1
table.description:
First reference for the P219A (A/F imbalance) monitor: how much the front A/F sensor reading may swing, by rpm and load, over the 25-second test window. Raising it makes P219A harder to set. A fault also needs A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 1 to be exceeded. Above about 4000 rpm the reference climbs steeply (interpolating to the 4500 rpm row, which is effectively infinite), so running above about 4000 rpm during the window stops the test from failing.
Details: P219A also needs the crank-roughness confirmation: the channel judgements 0x18F980 / 0x18F928 report "exceeded" only when this reference is exceeded and the roughness latch from A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 1 / 2 (05FC7C / 05FCDC) is set (read, Phase 19). When used: while the P219A monitor runs (FFF8ACCE bits 0 and 1). A/F imbalance monitor 0x18FF34 (10 ms task 0x1DFE3C) sets P219A (result FFF8ACCF bit 0, DTC monitor record slot 623, read). Over a window of cal 0x436D4 = 2500 passes (25 s) while its conditions FFF8ACCE bits 0/1 hold it sums the A/F-sensor swings, |change| of lambda x 8192 FFF88AF8 over each rising and falling run (FFF8C4E8, 0x18DB0C / 0x18DCCC, read), and two references. At the window end measured > reference x coolant factor gives FFF8ACCE bit 4 / bit 2 (0x1913E0 / 0x19154C), judgements FFF8ACCB / FFF8ACCA = 2 and FFF8ACCF bit 1 / bit 3; either of these sets the P219A result in 0x19198C (read). This is the first reference (judgement FFF8ACCB, enabled by cal 0x436C0 = 1). Raising it makes P219A harder to set. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 2
table.description:
Second, higher reference for the P219A (A/F imbalance) monitor, used with A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 2 as confirmation. Raising it makes P219A harder to set. Above about 4000 rpm the reference climbs steeply (interpolating to the 4500 rpm row, which is effectively infinite), so running above about 4000 rpm during the window stops the test from failing.
Details: P219A also needs the crank-roughness confirmation: the channel judgements 0x18F980 / 0x18F928 report "exceeded" only when this reference is exceeded and the roughness latch from A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 1 / 2 (05FC7C / 05FCDC) is set (read, Phase 19). When used: while the P219A monitor runs (FFF8ACCE bits 0 and 1). A/F imbalance monitor 0x18FF34 (10 ms task 0x1DFE3C) sets P219A (result FFF8ACCF bit 0, DTC monitor record slot 623, read). Over a window of cal 0x436D4 = 2500 passes (25 s) while its conditions FFF8ACCE bits 0/1 hold it sums the A/F-sensor swings, |change| of lambda x 8192 FFF88AF8 over each rising and falling run (FFF8C4E8, 0x18DB0C / 0x18DCCC, read), and two references. At the window end measured > reference x coolant factor gives FFF8ACCE bit 4 / bit 2 (0x1913E0 / 0x19154C), judgements FFF8ACCB / FFF8ACCA = 2 and FFF8ACCF bit 1 / bit 3; either of these sets the P219A result in 0x19198C (read). This is the second reference (judgement FFF8ACCA, enabled by cal 0x436C1 = 1); it is higher than Threshold 1 and its judgement additionally needs FFF8ACD6 / FFF8ACDB (FFF8ACDB = the crank-roughness latch of A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 2, 0x191920; FFF8ACD6 not decoded) instead of FFF8ACD4 / FFF8ACD8. Confidence: read.

table.name: EGR Enable
table.description:
Master switch for EGR. Clearing it is expected to keep EGR off, so the EGR-off variants of base timing, closed loop target and throttle tables become the live ones (inferred).
One of the EGR enable conditions computed by 0x0FAAFC (FFF8A811 bit 0), with coolant, rpm and load windows, engine running and normal combustion mode (read). Clearing it is expected to keep EGR off, so the EGR-off table variants (Base Timing (EGR Off,...), Closed Loop Target (..., EGR Off), the non-EGR Throttle Opening from Target Torque tables) become the live ones (inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: Transmission Coding: Automatic/CVT
table.description:
Tells the ECU whether it is in a manual or an AT/CVT car (clear = manual in every manual image). It decides gear calculation, the gear torque limits and whether the AT/CVT Coding table variants are used. Do not change on a manual car.
Details: Clear in every manual image (byte 0xFD) and set in the 2016 CVT image LF75300G (0xFB) (read, my research notes). While Transmission Coding: From Input Port is clear, FFF886AB bit 7 (manual coding) = NOT this bit (read, 0x06A38C at 0x06A73A..0x06A824). The bit is also read directly, whatever From Input Port says, by 0x0B83F8 (0x0B8544 / 0x0B8514 -> FFF8A618 bits 0/1 -> 0x0B8154, read; meaning not identified). With the manual coding: gear is computed from the rpm/speed ratio (0x0B914C), Requested Torque uses its A tables only, the gear torque limit table applies (0x0BB1AC), and the flag-set table variants are the live ones; with automatic/CVT coding the gear and a torque limit come from a received CAN frame and the AT/CVT Coding table variants are used (read; meaning inferred). Do not change on a manual car. Confidence: read.

table.name: Transmission Coding: From Input Port
table.description:
When set, the manual/automatic coding is read from a hardware input instead of Transmission Coding: Automatic/CVT.
When set, the transmission coding (FFF886AB bit 7) is taken from a latched input-port bit (FFF80238 bit 7, set once port bit FFF8A2A4 bit 7 is seen) instead of Transmission Coding: Automatic/CVT (read, 0x06A38C). Leave clear. Confidence: read.

table.name: Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B
table.description:
Enables the second (Path B) tip-in torque shaping. Leave clear unless you calibrate the whole Path B set.
The torque module 0x0BE694 passes this bit to the rise shaping 0x0BB958 (BLD.B #6 at 0x0BF3D0, stack argument 11, read), and the torque monitor call passes it to 0x1877B4 (read). When set, Path B of the target-torque rise shaping can act (all "Target Torque Rise..." tables), and a request below Path B Start Torque passes unshaped. Leave clear unless the whole Path B set is calibrated. Bit 7 of the same byte is a separate switch passed to another torque routine (seg_0x0B0000.c:9252). Confidence: read.

table.name: Open Loop Fueling: Use Alternate Map
table.description:
When set, Primary Open Loop Fueling (Alternate) probably replaces the normal open loop fueling strategy.
Passed by the open-loop fueling readers 0x0CE854 and 0x0CE5E8 (read): when set, Primary Open Loop Fueling (Alternate) is used in place of the base + DAM-scaled knock additive strategy (inferred). Leave clear unless you have filled that table. Confidence: read.

table.name: VE: Use AVCS-Not-Ready Table
table.description:
When set, Volumetric Efficiency (AVCS Not Ready) is used while the cams are probably not yet under control.
0x11E308 uses Volumetric Efficiency (AVCS Not Ready) only when this bit is set and FFF8A83B bit 7 is clear (read); FFF8A83B bit 7 = AVCS ready (inferred). Leave clear. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing: Pedal-Released Tables Enable
table.description:
Clear it to use the normal base timing tables off-throttle too.
With this bit set and FFF8A774 bit 0 (pedal released) set, Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Closed/Open) replaces the EGR Active/Off base timing tables (read, 0x0C2C08). Clear it to use the normal base timing tables with the pedal released. Confidence: read.

table.name: Multi-Injection Allowed During High-Pedal Latch 1
table.description:
Allows double/triple injection while one of the high-pedal latches is set.
The multi-injection enable FFF8A775 bit 0 (0x10B650) requires the high-pedal latch FFF8A8A3 bit 6 to be clear unless this bit is set (read; the pairing of bit and latch follows the argument order at the call in 0x109008, inferred). Only matters if the double/triple injection windows are opened. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Multi-Injection Allowed During High-Pedal Latch 2
table.description:
Allows double/triple injection while a second high-pedal latch is set.
The multi-injection enable FFF8A775 bit 0 (0x10B650) requires the high-pedal latch FFF8A8A4 bit 6 to be clear unless this bit is set (read; the pairing of bit and latch follows the argument order at the call in 0x109008, inferred). Only matters if the double/triple injection windows are opened. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Multi-Injection Allowed During High-Pedal Latch 3
table.description:
Allows double/triple injection while a third high-pedal latch is set.
The multi-injection enable FFF8A775 bit 0 (0x10B650) requires the high-pedal latch FFF8A8A4 bit 7 to be clear unless this bit is set (read; the pairing of bit and latch follows the argument order at the call in 0x109008, inferred). Only matters if the double/triple injection windows are opened. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Fallback)
table.description:
Rail pressure target in combustion mode 1 after a warm-up fallback has latched.
Details: When used: Used only while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set, a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch (0x081EFC) gated by cal 0x59134 bit 0. 0x165180 (read): target in combustion mode FFF8A85C = 1 while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set (else Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1)); coolant FFF88A44. LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05EB84 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N303J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 056240. Confidence: read.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling
table.description:
Base open-loop (power enrichment) AFR target by rpm and load, used once the exhaust temperature estimate is high enough. The ECU uses the richer of this and the Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV..., AVCS...) group: to lean, edit both; to richen, either. Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor (Outside Closed Loop).
Details: Note: the ECU has a second open-loop fuel path: the four "Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV..., AVCS...)" tables 05ABB0..05ABEC, blended by TGV and AVCS (0x0CE5E8 -> FFF8A681); 0x0CEA80 takes the richer of the two (max). To lean the open-loop target edit both sets; richening works with either (read, my research notes). Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor. Base open-loop enrichment target, 0x0CE854. Used only while the exhaust temperature estimate FFF8AFD0 (see Exhaust Temperature Model Map A/B) is >= cal 0x18DD4 (39322, hysteresis cal 0x18DD6 = 2185), or its integral FFF8C03C >= cal 0x18DD8 (65535); otherwise this path contributes 0 (read). While cal 0x2F79A bit 4 is clear, the additive term (Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive x DAM multiplier) is added, minus Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive x Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier(DAM)/128. The result is rate-limited (FFF84424) into FFF8A682, and FFF8A684 = max(FFF8A682, other enrichments) feeds commanded lambda. LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05AC6C by the code that reads it (read). LV9N303J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 052634. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive
table.description:
Extra open-loop enrichment added to Primary Open Loop Fueling, scaled by its DAM multiplier: full at DAM 0, none at DAM 1. Probably the classic knock-dependent extra fuel. Edit with Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive (TGV/AVCS Group).
Details: Extra enrichment added to Primary Open Loop Fueling, scaled by the DAM multiplier table (full at DAM 0, none at DAM 1) - the classic knock-dependent additive enrichment (role inferred, arithmetic read). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05ACA8 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N303J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 052670. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive
table.description:
Fuel removed from Primary Open Loop Fueling, scaled by its DAM multiplier (negative cells add fuel). It only leans the target where the TGV/AVCS group is not richer.
Enrichment removed from Primary Open Loop Fueling, scaled by Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier. Same 1/256-of-stoich-fuel unit as the Additive (inferred). To use it, set both this table and its DAM multiplier. Because 0x0CEA80 takes the richer of the two open-loop paths, removing fuel here leans the target only where the TGV/AVCS group is not richer. 0x0CE854 (read; called from 0x0C589C with cal 0x2F79A bit 4, exhaust temperature estimate FFF8AFD0, its integral FFF8C03C, rpm FFF8CD54, load FFF8A616, DAM FFF811AE): while the exhaust-temperature condition holds (FFF8AFD0 >= cal 0x18DD4, hysteresis 0x18DD6, or FFF8C03C >= cal 0x18DD8) and cal 0x2F79A bit 4 is clear, FFF8A683 = clamp((Primary Open Loop Fueling x 128 + Additive x Additive DAM Multiplier(DAM)) / 128 - Subtractive x Subtractive DAM Multiplier(DAM) / 128, 0, 255) (0x0CE934..0x0CE9A0, read: signed 16-bit table, same rpm x load inputs as the Additive, product shifted arithmetically, so negative cells add fuel). The result is rate-limited (FFF84424) into FFF8A682; 0x0CEA80 takes max(FFF8A682, the TGV/AVCS group FFF8A681) into the commanded-lambda enrichment FFF8A684 (read). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05AC94 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N303J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 05265C. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (Alternate)
table.description:
Replacement for Primary Open Loop Fueling plus its knock additive, used only when the calibration switch 'Open Loop Fueling. Edit with Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate) if you enable it.
Details: When used: only when cal 0x2F79A bit 4 is set (read; 2017 0x36B76, 2018 0x37FF2). The bit is the first argument of 0x0CE854 (call in 0x0C589C, read). With it set, 0x0CE854 uses this table + cal 0x18DDC in place of the base table plus the DAM-scaled additive, while DAM16 FFF811AE < cal 0x18DDD; otherwise Primary Open Loop Fueling + cal 0x18DDC (read). The TGV/AVCS group has its own alternate (Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate)); edit both if you enable the switch. LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05AC80 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N303J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 052648. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Additional Enrichment A
table.description:
Extra enrichment added to the open-loop enrichment at higher coolant and lower rpm.
Details: When used: A applies when coolant >= cal 0x13E18 and rpm < cal 0x13E0E, B when coolant < 0x13E1A or rpm >= 0x13E0C (in between the last value is held); the whole term needs FFF8A654 bit 1, whose thresholds (cal 0x13E08, 0x13E14) are 65535, and both tables are zero. Source of FFF8AFE8 (0x0CAF70, with B), a term of the commanded lambda and of the fuel factor FFF8AFBC, where it is added to the open-loop enrichment (0x0C558C, read). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05A804 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N303J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 052294. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Additional Enrichment B
table.description:
Second table of the additional enrichment, used at low coolant or high rpm.
Details: When used: see Additional Enrichment A: B applies when coolant < cal 0x13E1A or rpm >= cal 0x13E0C (A when coolant >= cal 0x13E18 and rpm < cal 0x13E0E; in between the last value is held), and the whole term needs FFF8A654 bit 1. Second source table of FFF8AFE8. LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05A818 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N303J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0522A8. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Closed Loop Target Cold-Start Trim (TGVs Closed)
table.description:
Small trim to the closed-loop target after a cold start, by start coolant and air used since start, with the TGVs closed.
Details: When used: TGVs forced closed (FFF8A881 bit 4 set). 0x0FFA0C (read): FFF8B326 = 32768 + (this - 32768) x (05CDF0/05CE04(rpm, load) / 2979) x (05CE18/05CE24(FFF8AF12) / 255); B326 - 32768 is added to the closed-loop target (0x0FF468, see Closed Loop Target). Axes: coolant at start FFF89224 x accumulated air since start FFF81818 (0x10A270). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05CDDC by the code that reads it (read). LV9N303J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0547B8. Confidence: read.

table.name: Closed Loop Target (Catalyst Monitor Active)
table.description:
Closed-loop target used instead of the four Closed Loop Target tables while the P0420 catalyst monitor test runs; not limited or trimmed by the other target tables.
Details: When used: while FFF8AA60 bit 3 is set: the P0420 catalyst monitor test is running (set by 0x135D18 inside 0x134374, read; needs closed loop, speed >= 40 km/h, an airflow window). 0x0FF468 (read): used instead of the four Closed Loop Target tables, and its value goes straight to FFF8B30A, without the lean limit, Low-DAM Enrichment or cold-start trim. Axes rpm (FFF8CD56) x load % (FFF8A616). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05CD38 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N303J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 054714. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment 1 (TGV Open)
table.description:
Start-path after-start enrichment by coolant, faded to zero by its decay table; the largest of the three after-start terms is used, scaled by After-Start Enrichment RPM Multiplier. Used with the TGVs open.
Details: Enrichment amount FFF843EA (0x0CD834, read); this TGV Open table is used when TGV state flag FFF8A881 bit 4 (passed in by 0x0C73D0, read) is clear. Faded to zero by After-Start Enrichment Decay 1 (TGV Open), the three faded terms' maximum is scaled by the RPM multiplier into FFF8B012/B016/B01A/B01E (read), and FFF8B012 adds to the start-path fuel factor (B012 + A828 + B02C)/256 + 0.5 (0x0D1400, read). Coolant axis is the value latched at start (FFF843F4) or the current one (read). Unit 1/256 of base fuel (inferred). TGV polarity (read): 0x0D952C blends its Closed and Open ignition sets as Closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + Open x FFF8B3E8, so FFF8B3E8 is the TGV open fraction; 0x10C948 drives it toward 0 while FFF8A881 bit 4 is set, so that bit set = TGVs closed. LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05A958 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N303J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0523DC. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment 1 (TGV Closed)
table.description:
Start-path after-start enrichment by coolant, faded to zero by its decay table; the largest of the three after-start terms is used, scaled by After-Start Enrichment RPM Multiplier. Used with the TGVs closed.
Details: Enrichment amount FFF843EA (0x0CD834, read); this TGV Closed table is used when TGV state flag FFF8A881 bit 4 (passed in by 0x0C73D0, read) is set. Faded to zero by After-Start Enrichment Decay 1 (TGV Closed), the three faded terms' maximum is scaled by the RPM multiplier into FFF8B012/B016/B01A/B01E (read), and FFF8B012 adds to the start-path fuel factor (B012 + A828 + B02C)/256 + 0.5 (0x0D1400, read). Coolant axis is the value latched at start (FFF843F4) or the current one (read). Unit 1/256 of base fuel (inferred). TGV polarity (read): 0x0D952C blends its Closed and Open ignition sets as Closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + Open x FFF8B3E8, so FFF8B3E8 is the TGV open fraction; 0x10C948 drives it toward 0 while FFF8A881 bit 4 is set, so that bit set = TGVs closed. LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05A96C by the code that reads it (read). LV9N303J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0523F0. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment Decay 1 (TGV Open)
table.description:
Fade time for After-Start Enrichment 1: the enrichment falls linearly to zero over this time after start (unfaded while cranking). Larger = longer enrichment. Used with the TGVs open.
Details: Fade time FFF843F0 for After-Start Enrichment 1 (0x0CD834, read): the enrichment falls linearly from full to zero after 8 x this many counts of FFF8B06A (read). In cranking mode (FFF8906B = 2) the enrichment is used unfaded (read). TGV polarity (read): 0x0D952C blends its Closed and Open ignition sets as Closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + Open x FFF8B3E8, so FFF8B3E8 is the TGV open fraction; 0x10C948 drives it toward 0 while FFF8A881 bit 4 is set, so that bit set = TGVs closed. LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05A9D0 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N303J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 052454. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment Decay 1 (TGV Closed)
table.description:
Fade time for After-Start Enrichment 1: the enrichment falls linearly to zero over this time after start (unfaded while cranking). Larger = longer enrichment. Used with the TGVs closed.
Details: Fade time FFF843F0 for After-Start Enrichment 1 (0x0CD834, read): the enrichment falls linearly from full to zero after 8 x this many counts of FFF8B06A (read). In cranking mode (FFF8906B = 2) the enrichment is used unfaded (read). TGV polarity (read): 0x0D952C blends its Closed and Open ignition sets as Closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + Open x FFF8B3E8, so FFF8B3E8 is the TGV open fraction; 0x10C948 drives it toward 0 while FFF8A881 bit 4 is set, so that bit set = TGVs closed. LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05A9E4 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N303J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 052468. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment 2 (TGV Open)
table.description:
Start-path after-start enrichment by coolant, faded to zero by its decay table; the largest of the three after-start terms is used, scaled by After-Start Enrichment RPM Multiplier. Used with the TGVs open.

table.name: Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Base ignition timing map for the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration) with the TGVs closed. It is only an upper limit: the ECU fires the lower of this map and Closed-Pedal Timing Target (plus its corrections).

The result is rate-limited (cals 0x1058C / 0x1058E) and the IAT compensation FFF8A782 and Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation FFF8A788 are added (0x0C2C08) to give base timing FFF8A645, which is only the upper limit of the fired timing: with the pedal released 0x0DD568 sets FFF8A76A = FFF8A645 - Torque Reduction Spark Retard(FFF8AF22 >> 7), where FFF8AF22 (0x0C13B4) is the efficiency of the closed-pedal timing request (Closed-Pedal Timing Target + FFF8A788 + FFF8A782 + Post-Start Closed-Pedal Timing Advance, 0x0E0A30) plus KCA + FLKC, so in effect FFF8A76A = min(FFF8A645, that request + KCA + FLKC) (read; min() form computed from the inverse tables). FFF8A76A then goes through 0x0DD760, 0x0DA600 and 0x0D9E40 to FFF8A744. The F2 selector is FFF8A881 bit 4, set by the TGV module 0x10CAE0 (0x10DEFC) - set = TGVs closed (see below). TGV polarity (read): 0x0D952C blends its Closed and Open ignition sets as Closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + Open x FFF8B3E8, so FFF8B3E8 is the TGV open fraction; 0x10C948 drives it toward 0 while FFF8A881 bit 4 is set, so that bit set = TGVs closed. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (TGV Closed)
table.description:
Version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier A used while the TGVs are closed.
Details: 0x0C1EA8 (read): AF4E multiplies the rpm-based filter coefficient AFAC (0x0C38E0) in 0x0C2514 (AF58), 0x0C1854 (predicted air torque AF40) and 0x0C39DC (AF3E): k = AF4E x AFAC/512. 512 = 1.0; values that push k past 65535 mean no lag. Selected in state S2: after combustion-mode change 1 -> 3, while spark target - final timing > 4 deg (7 deg with A7E2 bit 0) and FFF886AB bit 5. TGV closed (A881 bit 4), A7E2 bit 0 clear. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 059ED0 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N303J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 051A80. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor
table.description:
On a hot restart, the A/F sensor exhaust model starts from the pipe temperature stored at engine stop, multiplied by this factor by how much the coolant has dropped since. Normally leave alone.
Details: When used: before the engine runs (FFF8906B != 3) on a hot restart: coolant at start >= 60 C (50 C to stay, cals 0x4234D/0x4234C) and last running coolant FFF8069B >= 80 C (cal 0x4234F = 130). Module 0x180C20 (read) is the exhaust condensation model behind the A/F sensor heater release: 05F158 (by pipe temperature FFF8BAB8, K x 32) is the saturation vapour pressure of water; 0x17F4B8 takes the water partial pressure as cal 0x42333/256 (15 %) of max(MAP, baro) and makes the condensation rate FFF8C448 from flow x factor x (partial - saturation pressure) / total pressure; 0x18065C integrates the net amount into FFF8C48C. The A/F state machine (0x0852B2, read) goes to the protected state 2 when the start value FFF8C478 >= cal 0x4230C (415645) and on to state 3 only when FFF8139F bit 0 clears (0x08492A), which 0x181668 does when the model amount FFF8C47C < 415645. 0x1802F4 (read): the modelled exhaust pipe temperature FFF8BAB8 (K x 32) starts at the value stored at the last engine stop FFF815BA (0x1802D4) x this(coolant drop since the engine last ran)/256; on other starts it starts at min(IAT, coolant) - 05F1F0. FFF8069B is the coolant copied every pass while running (0x06BA46, read). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05F1E4 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N303J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 056894. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake Cam Coolant Offset 3B
table.description:
Extra intake cam advance (degrees) added to Intake Cam Target 3B (TGVs closed, sea level), scaled by Intake Cam Coolant Factor 3 so it can act only when cold. Positive = more advance.
Details: Convention (read, see FU_UNITS): adds to the intake cam target in crank degrees of ADVANCE; positive = more advance, negative = less. AVCS target (intake 0x15C250, exhaust 0x16032C, read): target = coolant terms + v x [S_A x w + S_B x (1 - w)] + (1 - v) x [3A x w + (3B + Coolant Offset 3B x Coolant Factor 3 / 128) x (1 - w)], clamped to +/-90 degrees, 364.09 counts per degree. v = FFF8B3E8, the TGV open fraction: sets 1/2 apply with TGVs open, set 3 with TGVs closed. w = FFF8B948 = AVCS Barometric Blend (barometric pressure FFF88668, via 0x15B1E0, read): the A tables apply at altitude, the B tables at sea level. S = set 1 or set 2, chosen by FFF8A8A4 bit 7 (stack argument +24 from 0x15969C, read). That bit is a high-pedal latch (0x11C15C / 0x10F848, read): it sets when the accelerator FFF88A5E is at or above High Pedal Entry Threshold while vehicle speed is not jumping (under cal 0x35B16... per gear) and some status flags (FFF88A2D bit 0, FFF88ADA bit 6, FFF8A8A2 bit 6) are clear, or when FFF8A8A5 bit 2 or 4 is set; it clears once the pedal is below cal 0x36518 (85 %). So set 1 = normal driving and set 2 = near wide-open pedal (meaning inferred from these conditions). The set-3 terms are active because cal 0x3ACF6 = 1 in both images. table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Fallback Latch)
table.description:
Idle target ramp rate (by coolant) used when a warm-up fallback flag is set (manual-car version).
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00).
