table.name: TGV Coolant Minimum (Warm-Up Fallback)
table.description:
Minimum coolant for TGV closing used only while a warm-up fallback flag is set.
TGV request logic 0x10D93C (read): the request byte FFF8A888 is 3 unless all of these hold: coolant FFF88A44 at or above TGV Coolant Minimum, requested torque FFF8AEE2 (0x0BA868, Nm = x/80 - 200) below the rpm-based TGV Torque Threshold (it must fall below the Enter table and then rise above the Exit table to clear), air quantity FFF8B4D6 below TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Enter 0x37A4A, Exit 0x37A48), and FFF8A88D = 0. When they hold, FFF8A888 = 1, or 2 if the intake air temperature FFF88A48 is below TGV IAT Threshold (vehicle speed) or FFF88E28 bit 0/2 is set; FFF8A888 = 2 also while combustion mode FFF8A85C is below cal 0x37B48. State 1 requests TGV close: it runs the timer FFF8B3E0 (0x10C3D0) and FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is set once the timer reaches TGV Close Delay. States 2 (close blocked: cold intake air, FFF88E28 bit 0/2, or combustion mode below cal 0x37B48) and 3 (close conditions not met) reset the timer, so the TGVs stay open (read). Which threshold pair is used depends on FFF8A8C1 (1, 2, 3 or other) and FFF8A8A2 bit 5 (not identified). Each threshold is table(rpm FFF8CE9C) + TGV Torque Threshold Offset(rpm, FFF88AE6) - 16000, so the offset table is centred on 16000 (0 ft-lb). Used while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set. LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 037A46 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N303J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (2 reads)). Address 035498. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 1
table.description:
Crankshaft roughness level, by rpm and load, that confirms channel 1 of the P219A A/F imbalance monitor. It sets no code by itself; P219A needs both this and A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 1 exceeded. Raising cells makes a fault harder (the maximum value = never).
Details: When used: once per combustion event (0x1908E4, crank-synchronous list 0x1E1D1C) while the P219A monitor runs (FFF8ACD1). Confirms channel 1 of P219A (A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 1). 0x18E130 (read): threshold FFF8BC5E = this(rpm FFF8CE9C, load FFF8A616) x 05FCB0(coolant)/8192 x 05FCBC/128 x 1.0 (float constants 1000/2^33 and 8.192, 0x18E23C / 0x18E248, read); x 100 instead (capped at 65535, so during that window any cell >= 336 can never be exceeded) until the neutral input FFF88ADA bit 6 has been unchanged for cal 0x4496E = 150 passes (1.5 s; FFF8ACCD bit 5, 0x1912B4) - the A/C-state stability bit 6 (0x191324, cal 0x436B2 = 0) is always set; 65535 while FFF88A2D bit 0; 05FC90 (all 65535) replaces it near standstill with the pedal released (FFF8ACCD bit 0: FFF88C64 bit 5 and speed < 2 km/h) and 05FC68 (all 65535) while FFF8AA3F is set. 0x18F14C sets FFF8ACC5 = 2 when the crank fluctuation FFF8BC5C - 0x8000 > threshold x 250/256 (so an event counts when the fluctuation exceeds 0.977 x the cell value). 0x18D180... count those events per cylinder (FFF8ACC2 = 1..4, cylinder inferred) into FFF8BC24/28/2C/30 and in total FFF8BC48; at the end of a 2000-event window (FFF8BC20 = cal 0x436F0) 0x18F364 judges FFF8ACC7 = 2 'rough' when a cylinder count > cal 0x436F4 (17) or the total > cal 0x436F6 (17) (with a cylinder share > cal 0x43704 = 0) (read). That latches FFF8ACD8 (0x191850). The channel 1 judgement 0x18F980 gives FFF8ACCB = 2 (exceeded, which sets FFF8ACCF bit 1 and through it the P219A result in 0x19198C) only when the A/F swing exceeded its reference (FFF8ACCE bit 4) AND FFF8ACD8 (or FFF8ACD4) is set; FFF8ACCB = 1 (passed) when the swing passed (FFF8ACCE bit 5, cal 0x436C0 = 1) (read). So the roughness test is a required confirmation: a channel 1 P219A needs both the A/F swing and this crank roughness. The largest count and its limit are also Mode $06 values FFF815CE / FFF815D0 (0x18EB24 / 0x18EBA8, test 0xDC in the 0x0A0000 reporter, read). Raising cells makes the confirmation harder (65535 = never), lowering makes it easier; it does not set a DTC by itself. LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05FC7C by the code that reads it (read). LV9N303J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 05729C. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 2
table.description:
Crankshaft roughness level that confirms channel 2 of the P219A monitor (paired with A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 2). Lower than Threshold 1, so more sensitive. Sets no code by itself; raising cells makes a fault harder (the maximum value = never).
Details: When used: as A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 1, for channel 2 of P219A (A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 2). 0x18E250 (read): same gating and scaling (x 05FD10(coolant)/8192 x 05FD1C/128, both 1.0) into FFF8BC60 -> FFF8BC64; 0x18F0F8 sets FFF8ACC4 = 2 on an exceedance; per-cylinder counters FFF8BC32..BC44 (0x18D4C8...) and the 2000-event window judgement FFF8ACC6 (0x18F1A0: a cylinder count > cal 0x436FC (17) or the total > cal 0x436FE (17) gives 2 'rough') latch FFF8ACDB (0x191920). The channel 2 judgement 0x18F928 gives FFF8ACCA = 2 (exceeded: FFF8ACCF bit 3 -> P219A result) only when the swing exceeded (FFF8ACCE bit 2) AND FFF8ACDB (or FFF8ACD6) is set; = 1 (passed) when the swing passed (FFF8ACCE bit 3, cal 0x436C1 = 1) (read). Mode $06 values FFF815D2 / FFF815D4 (0x18EFCC / 0x18F050, read). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05FCDC by the code that reads it (read). LV9N303J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0572FC. Confidence: read.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Fallback)
table.description:
Rail pressure target in combustion mode 1 after a warm-up fallback has latched.
Details: When used: Used only while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set, a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch (0x081EFC) gated by cal 0x59134 bit 0. 0x165180 (read): target in combustion mode FFF8A85C = 1 while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set (else Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1)); coolant FFF88A44. LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05EB84 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N340J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 056240. Confidence: read.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling
table.description:
Base open-loop (power enrichment) AFR target by rpm and load, used once the exhaust temperature estimate is high enough. The ECU uses the richer of this and the Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV..., AVCS...) group: to lean, edit both; to richen, either. Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor (Outside Closed Loop).
Details: Note: the ECU has a second open-loop fuel path: the four "Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV..., AVCS...)" tables 05ABB0..05ABEC, blended by TGV and AVCS (0x0CE5E8 -> FFF8A681); 0x0CEA80 takes the richer of the two (max). To lean the open-loop target edit both sets; richening works with either (read, my research notes). Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor. Base open-loop enrichment target, 0x0CE854. Used only while the exhaust temperature estimate FFF8AFD0 (see Exhaust Temperature Model Map A/B) is >= cal 0x18DD4 (39322, hysteresis cal 0x18DD6 = 2185), or its integral FFF8C03C >= cal 0x18DD8 (65535); otherwise this path contributes 0 (read). While cal 0x2F79A bit 4 is clear, the additive term (Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive x DAM multiplier) is added, minus Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive x Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier(DAM)/128. The result is rate-limited (FFF84424) into FFF8A682, and FFF8A684 = max(FFF8A682, other enrichments) feeds commanded lambda. LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05AC6C by the code that reads it (read). LV9N340J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 052634. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive
table.description:
Extra open-loop enrichment added to Primary Open Loop Fueling, scaled by its DAM multiplier: full at DAM 0, none at DAM 1. Probably the classic knock-dependent extra fuel. Edit with Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive (TGV/AVCS Group).
Details: Extra enrichment added to Primary Open Loop Fueling, scaled by the DAM multiplier table (full at DAM 0, none at DAM 1) - the classic knock-dependent additive enrichment (role inferred, arithmetic read). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05ACA8 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N340J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 052670. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive
table.description:
Fuel removed from Primary Open Loop Fueling, scaled by its DAM multiplier (negative cells add fuel). It only leans the target where the TGV/AVCS group is not richer.
Enrichment removed from Primary Open Loop Fueling, scaled by Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier. Same 1/256-of-stoich-fuel unit as the Additive (inferred). To use it, set both this table and its DAM multiplier. Because 0x0CEA80 takes the richer of the two open-loop paths, removing fuel here leans the target only where the TGV/AVCS group is not richer. 0x0CE854 (read; called from 0x0C589C with cal 0x2F79A bit 4, exhaust temperature estimate FFF8AFD0, its integral FFF8C03C, rpm FFF8CD54, load FFF8A616, DAM FFF811AE): while the exhaust-temperature condition holds (FFF8AFD0 >= cal 0x18DD4, hysteresis 0x18DD6, or FFF8C03C >= cal 0x18DD8) and cal 0x2F79A bit 4 is clear, FFF8A683 = clamp((Primary Open Loop Fueling x 128 + Additive x Additive DAM Multiplier(DAM)) / 128 - Subtractive x Subtractive DAM Multiplier(DAM) / 128, 0, 255) (0x0CE934..0x0CE9A0, read: signed 16-bit table, same rpm x load inputs as the Additive, product shifted arithmetically, so negative cells add fuel). The result is rate-limited (FFF84424) into FFF8A682; 0x0CEA80 takes max(FFF8A682, the TGV/AVCS group FFF8A681) into the commanded-lambda enrichment FFF8A684 (read). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05AC94 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N340J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 05265C. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (Alternate)
table.description:
Replacement for Primary Open Loop Fueling plus its knock additive, used only when the calibration switch 'Open Loop Fueling. Edit with Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate) if you enable it.
Details: When used: only when cal 0x2F79A bit 4 is set (read; 2017 0x36B76, 2018 0x37FF2). The bit is the first argument of 0x0CE854 (call in 0x0C589C, read). With it set, 0x0CE854 uses this table + cal 0x18DDC in place of the base table plus the DAM-scaled additive, while DAM16 FFF811AE < cal 0x18DDD; otherwise Primary Open Loop Fueling + cal 0x18DDC (read). The TGV/AVCS group has its own alternate (Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate)); edit both if you enable the switch. LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05AC80 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N340J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 052648. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Additional Enrichment A
table.description:
Extra enrichment added to the open-loop enrichment at higher coolant and lower rpm.
Details: When used: A applies when coolant >= cal 0x13E18 and rpm < cal 0x13E0E, B when coolant < 0x13E1A or rpm >= 0x13E0C (in between the last value is held); the whole term needs FFF8A654 bit 1, whose thresholds (cal 0x13E08, 0x13E14) are 65535, and both tables are zero. Source of FFF8AFE8 (0x0CAF70, with B), a term of the commanded lambda and of the fuel factor FFF8AFBC, where it is added to the open-loop enrichment (0x0C558C, read). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05A804 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N340J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 052294. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Additional Enrichment B
table.description:
Second table of the additional enrichment, used at low coolant or high rpm.
Details: When used: see Additional Enrichment A: B applies when coolant < cal 0x13E1A or rpm >= cal 0x13E0C (A when coolant >= cal 0x13E18 and rpm < cal 0x13E0E; in between the last value is held), and the whole term needs FFF8A654 bit 1. Second source table of FFF8AFE8. LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05A818 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N340J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0522A8. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Closed Loop Target Cold-Start Trim (TGVs Closed)
table.description:
Small trim to the closed-loop target after a cold start, by start coolant and air used since start, with the TGVs closed.

table.name: Purge Valve Duty
table.description:

The final duty is A713 + (100 % - A713) x this, with A713 = Purge Valve Minimum Duty (0x0D6118, read), and 0 when this is 0. B0C0 = purge rate x air quantity FFF8B4D6 / 256, in the air-quantity unit (read). Higher vacuum needs less duty for the same flow. table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 1, Channel 2)
table.description:
This software version (function 0x0D6CAC, read against the longer version of the function): the table is the step only on the pass where the window flag sets. On the pass where it clears, the longer version subtracts the table; this one adds the fixed value at cal 0x026B6E instead (s16; the row for the event is Knock Background Clear Step (Event 1)).
Knock signal processing for event slot 1, channel 2 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock. Larger = that event less likely to count as knock. Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.
Details: When used: event slot FFF8CDC0 = 1 (Event 1), knock channel 2 of 8, on the knock window where FFF8A7C2 changes. Background step for this channel, added to (window extended) or subtracted from (window back to nominal) the channel background FFF8C180[1] for that one event; overlap-flag FFF8A7D2, gain curve cal 0x26F6F. Knock signal processing 0x0E51E4 (read; called once per knock window from 0x0E43B8 with load FFF8A616, after the event chain 0x0E433C): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4, the slot of the Knock Threshold tables) each of 8 knock channels i gets a reference ref_i = 32 x step_i + g x background_i, and the channel ratio is 256 x FFF8CDB0[i] / (ref_i / 32), i.e. measured / reference with 256 = equal (0x0E51E4 tail, read). Channels with their bit set in cal 0x1B97C..0x1B97F give 0; a channel flagged in FFF8CEED (driver flag, value at its lower limit, inferred) gives 256. The ratios are sorted and the largest min(cal 0x1B988, 5) = 3 are summed into the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot], which 0x0E80B4/0x0E8654 compare with Knock Threshold (read). The measured channels come from the knock sensor ADC: 0x1E7868 DMA-collects 32-sample blocks, 0x1E725A runs FFT-style butterflies, 0x1E73A4 takes sqrt(re^2+im^2) of 8 selected bins (pointer tables 0x34A88/0x34AA8), and 0x1E7724 sums them over the window into FFF8D1D4[8] -> FFF8CDB0[8] (read), so the 8 channels are 8 frequency bins of the knock sensor signal (inferred). background_i is the per-slot channel background FFF8C180.. (slot 1) / C190.. / C1A0.. / C1B0.. (slot 4), a lag filter of the measured channel kept by 0x0E4500 when the event is not knocking, floored at the per-channel rpm curve FFF8C0D8 (0x0E22A4) (read). step_i is this table family: it is non-zero only on the one event where the slot's window-length flag changes: +table when the flag goes 0 -> 1 (window switched to the extended length) and -table when it goes 1 -> 0 (back to the nominal length); on that event the reference is also floored at 32 x FFF8C0D8[i] (read). The flag is set when the extended knock window is used (0x0E20E0, read: B11A = nominal + Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 <= Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold and the extended window ends before the event angle). The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). Axes: rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500, 500-4000 rpm) x load FFF8A616 (read). Confidence: inferred.

This software version (function 0x0D6CAC, read against the longer version of the function): the table is the step only on the pass where the window flag sets. On the pass where it clears, the longer version subtracts the table; this one adds the fixed value at cal 0x026B80 instead (s16; the row for the event is Knock Background Clear Step (Event 2)).
Knock signal processing for event slot 2, channel 3 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.
Details: When used: event slot FFF8CDC0 = 2 (Event 2), knock channel 3 of 8, on the knock window where FFF8A7C3 changes. Background step for this channel, added to (window extended) or subtracted from (window back to nominal) the channel background FFF8C190[2] for that one event; overlap-flag FFF8A7D3, gain curve cal 0x26F7F. Knock signal processing 0x0E51E4 (read; called once per knock window from 0x0E43B8 with load FFF8A616, after the event chain 0x0E433C): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4, the slot of the Knock Threshold tables) each of 8 knock channels i gets a reference ref_i = 32 x step_i + g x background_i, and the channel ratio is 256 x FFF8CDB0[i] / (ref_i / 32), i.e. measured / reference with 256 = equal (0x0E51E4 tail, read). Channels with their bit set in cal 0x1B97C..0x1B97F give 0; a channel flagged in FFF8CEED (driver flag, value at its lower limit, inferred) gives 256. The ratios are sorted and the largest min(cal 0x1B988, 5) = 3 are summed into the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot], which 0x0E80B4/0x0E8654 compare with Knock Threshold (read). The measured channels come from the knock sensor ADC: 0x1E7868 DMA-collects 32-sample blocks, 0x1E725A runs FFT-style butterflies, 0x1E73A4 takes sqrt(re^2+im^2) of 8 selected bins (pointer tables 0x34A88/0x34AA8), and 0x1E7724 sums them over the window into FFF8D1D4[8] -> FFF8CDB0[8] (read), so the 8 channels are 8 frequency bins of the knock sensor signal (inferred). background_i is the per-slot channel background FFF8C180.. (slot 1) / C190.. / C1A0.. / C1B0.. (slot 4), a lag filter of the measured channel kept by 0x0E4500 when the event is not knocking, floored at the per-channel rpm curve FFF8C0D8 (0x0E22A4) (read). step_i is this table family: it is non-zero only on the one event where the slot's window-length flag changes: +table when the flag goes 0 -> 1 (window switched to the extended length) and -table when it goes 1 -> 0 (back to the nominal length); on that event the reference is also floored at 32 x FFF8C0D8[i] (read). The flag is set when the extended knock window is used (0x0E20E0, read: B11A = nominal + Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 <= Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold and the extended window ends before the event angle). The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). Axes: rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500, 500-4000 rpm) x load FFF8A616 (read). Confidence: inferred.

On the pass where it clears, the longer version subtracts the table; this one adds the fixed value at cal 0x026B94 instead (s16; the row for the event is Knock Background Clear Step (Event 3)).
Knock signal processing for event slot 3, channel 5 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.
Details: When used: event slot FFF8CDC0 = 3 (Event 3), knock channel 5 of 8, on the knock window where FFF8A7C4 changes. Background step for this channel, added to (window extended) or subtracted from (window back to nominal) the channel background FFF8C1A0[4] for that one event; overlap-flag FFF8A7D4, gain curve cal 0x26F8F. Knock signal processing 0x0E51E4 (read; called once per knock window from 0x0E43B8 with load FFF8A616, after the event chain 0x0E433C): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4, the slot of the Knock Threshold tables) each of 8 knock channels i gets a reference ref_i = 32 x step_i + g x background_i, and the channel ratio is 256 x FFF8CDB0[i] / (ref_i / 32), i.e. measured / reference with 256 = equal (0x0E51E4 tail, read). Channels with their bit set in cal 0x1B97C..0x1B97F give 0; a channel flagged in FFF8CEED (driver flag, value at its lower limit, inferred) gives 256. The ratios are sorted and the largest min(cal 0x1B988, 5) = 3 are summed into the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot], which 0x0E80B4/0x0E8654 compare with Knock Threshold (read). The measured channels come from the knock sensor ADC: 0x1E7868 DMA-collects 32-sample blocks, 0x1E725A runs FFT-style butterflies, 0x1E73A4 takes sqrt(re^2+im^2) of 8 selected bins (pointer tables 0x34A88/0x34AA8), and 0x1E7724 sums them over the window into FFF8D1D4[8] -> FFF8CDB0[8] (read), so the 8 channels are 8 frequency bins of the knock sensor signal (inferred). background_i is the per-slot channel background FFF8C180.. (slot 1) / C190.. / C1A0.. / C1B0.. (slot 4), a lag filter of the measured channel kept by 0x0E4500 when the event is not knocking, floored at the per-channel rpm curve FFF8C0D8 (0x0E22A4) (read). step_i is this table family: it is non-zero only on the one event where the slot's window-length flag changes: +table when the flag goes 0 -> 1 (window switched to the extended length) and -table when it goes 1 -> 0 (back to the nominal length); on that event the reference is also floored at 32 x FFF8C0D8[i] (read). The flag is set when the extended knock window is used (0x0E20E0, read: B11A = nominal + Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 <= Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold and the extended window ends before the event angle). The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). Axes: rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500, 500-4000 rpm) x load FFF8A616 (read). Confidence: inferred.

On the pass where it clears, the longer version subtracts the table; this one adds the fixed value at cal 0x026B6C instead (s16; the row for the event is Knock Background Clear Step (Event 1)).
Knock-detection background step for event slot 1, frequency channel 1.
Details: event slot FFF8CDC0 = 1 (Event 1), knock channel 1 of 8 (index 0 of FFF8CDB0), which is masked: bit 0 of cal 0x1B97C is set (0xC1 = channels 1, 7 and 8 off for every slot). 0x0E51E4 (read) then writes a fixed ratio for the channel instead of 256 x measured/reference, and the reference ref_0 (the only place this step enters, statics FFF84AB4..FFF84AD0 read only by 0x0E51E4, ram_xref) is not used; the reference copies FFF8C130.. have no reader. So editing it has no effect unless that cal bit is cleared, which would make the channel count (then this would be the background step for FFF8C180[0] when FFF8A7C2 changes; overlap flag FFF8A7D2, gain curve cal 0x26F6F). Knock signal processing 0x0E51E4 (read; called once per knock window from 0x0E43B8 with load FFF8A616, after the event chain 0x0E433C): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4, the slot of the Knock Threshold tables) each of 8 knock channels i gets a reference ref_i = 32 x step_i + g x background_i, and the channel ratio is 256 x FFF8CDB0[i] / (ref_i / 32), i.e. measured / reference with 256 = equal (0x0E51E4 tail, read). Channels with their bit set in cal 0x1B97C..0x1B97F give 0; a channel flagged in FFF8CEED (driver flag, value at its lower limit, inferred) gives 256. The ratios are sorted and the largest min(cal 0x1B988, 5) = 3 are summed into the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot], which 0x0E80B4/0x0E8654 compare with Knock Threshold (read). The measured channels come from the knock sensor ADC: 0x1E7868 DMA-collects 32-sample blocks, 0x1E725A runs FFT-style butterflies, 0x1E73A4 takes sqrt(re^2+im^2) of 8 selected bins (pointer tables 0x34A88/0x34AA8), and 0x1E7724 sums them over the window into FFF8D1D4[8] -> FFF8CDB0[8] (read), so the 8 channels are 8 frequency bins of the knock sensor signal (inferred). background_i is the per-slot channel background FFF8C180.. (slot 1) / C190.. / C1A0.. / C1B0.. (slot 4), a lag filter of the measured channel kept by 0x0E4500 when the event is not knocking, floored at the per-channel rpm curve FFF8C0D8 (0x0E22A4) (read). step_i is this table family: it is non-zero only on the one event where the slot's window-length flag changes: +table when the flag goes 0 -> 1 (window switched to the extended length) and -table when it goes 1 -> 0 (back to the nominal length); on that event the reference is also floored at 32 x FFF8C0D8[i] (read). The flag is set when the extended knock window is used (0x0E20E0, read: B11A = nominal + Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 <= Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold and the extended window ends before the event angle). The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). Axes: rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500, 500-4000 rpm) x load FFF8A616 (read). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Base ignition timing map for the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration) with the TGVs closed. It is only an upper limit: the ECU fires the lower of this map and Closed-Pedal Timing Target (plus its corrections).
Details: When used: Used while the accelerator is fully released (FFF8A774 bit 0: pedal-zero flag FFF88C64 bit 5 in engine state 2/3, vehicle speed FFF99835 at or below cal 0x2FDB2 = 200 km/h (inferred); 0x0E127C / 0x09FF9A, read), TGVs closed; enabled by cal 0x1071E bit 0, set in all four images. Base ignition timing. 0x0C2C08 uses this 16x16 table when cal 0x1071E bit 0 and FFF8A774 bit 0 are both set, and F2 set (F2 = FFF8A881 bit 4). The result is rate-limited (cals 0x1058C / 0x1058E) and the IAT compensation FFF8A782 and Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation FFF8A788 are added (0x0C2C08) to give base timing FFF8A645, which is only the upper limit of the fired timing: with the pedal released 0x0DD568 sets FFF8A76A = FFF8A645 - Torque Reduction Spark Retard(FFF8AF22 >> 7), where FFF8AF22 (0x0C13B4) is the efficiency of the closed-pedal timing request (Closed-Pedal Timing Target + FFF8A788 + FFF8A782 + Post-Start Closed-Pedal Timing Advance, 0x0E0A30) plus KCA + FLKC, so in effect FFF8A76A = min(FFF8A645, that request + KCA + FLKC) (read; min() form computed from the inverse tables). FFF8A76A then goes through 0x0DD760, 0x0DA600 and 0x0D9E40 to FFF8A744. The F2 selector is FFF8A881 bit 4, set by the TGV module 0x10CAE0 (0x10DEFC) - set = TGVs closed (see below). TGV polarity (read): 0x0D952C blends its Closed and Open ignition sets as Closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + Open x FFF8B3E8, so FFF8B3E8 is the TGV open fraction; 0x10C948 drives it toward 0 while FFF8A881 bit 4 is set, so that bit set = TGVs closed. LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05A034 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N340J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 051BE4. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1, AT/CVT, Warm-Up Fallback)
table.description:
AT/CVT warm-up fallback copy of Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1).
Details: When used: FFF8A7E2 bit 0 clear, FFF899D7 bit 0 set. 0x108BAC (catalyst-heating module, read) writes FFF8A854, which 0x0C3200 selects as the spark target FFF8A647 in fuel mode FFF8A852 = 2 (combustion mode FFF8A85C 1 or 3, 0x108B08). A647 is the spark the torque model compensates for (0x0C2514, 0x0C1EA8) and the reference of the cold-start retard monitors (0x1CB70C, 0x132568: A72A - A854) (read); the fired spark in this mode follows FFF8A74C/FFF8A76B (0x0DA428), not A854 (read). In combustion mode 1 (A85C < 2), at <= 4000 rpm (cal 0x1CBD8), with the pedal released (FFF886AB bit 5) and speed below cal 0x2A0C1 (2 km/h): A854 = Base(rpm FFF8CD5C, coolant) + Torque Adder(FFF8A85E, coolant) + Run-Time Adder(passes since the engine state became running, coolant) + Re-Entry Adder(passes since mode 1 was re-entered from normal mode 4, coolant), saturated to a byte; the set is chosen by FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (set = the manual tables, clear = the "AT/CVT" tables; always set on the manual coding, Phase 14) and FFF899D7 bit 0 (set = the "Warm-Up Fallback" tables): a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch set by 0x081EFC only when cal 0x59134 bit 0 is set. Otherwise in mode 1 A854 = 05D0BC x 05D0A8 / 256 + FFF8A789 - 32; in mode 3 A854 = A72A (normal target) (read). with cal 0x2996C bit 6 set A854 is forced to cal 0x2A0C0. Units: A854 is compared with A72A and final timing in 0.5 degree units (inferred). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05D044 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N340J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 054A14. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Throttle Opening Map Reference Torque
table.description:
Torque by rpm that counts as 100 % in the Throttle Opening from Target Torque maps: at or above it they give wide-open throttle. Raise it together with Full-Load Reference Brake Torque for a higher-torque tune. Edit together with Throttle Opening Map Reference Torque (Monitor).
Details: 0x0C0010 (read): normalises the target brake torque FFF8AECA into the column index of the eight Throttle Opening from Target Torque tables (idx = 255 x AECA / this); at or above this torque every table gives 100 % (wide open). Raising it with 05A054 keeps the WOT point of the opening tables and the full-load excess term (0x0BDAA0) together. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Closed)
table.description:
This is where part-throttle feel is set: the commanded throttle opening is essentially this map (by rpm and target torque) plus the idle air. Used with the TGVs closed and no EGR (blended by TGV position and EGR amount). Edit together with Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Closed, Monitor).
Details: 0x0C0010 (called from torque module 0x0BE694): column index = 255 x target torque FFF8AECA / Throttle Opening Map Reference Torque 059DD0(rpm); result blended by TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 and EGR realisation FFF8B290 (min 256) into FFF8AF12, which 059D2C/059D64/05A148/05A0BC turn back into the commanded throttle, so at part throttle the commanded opening is essentially this map plus the idle area (read, numeric check in TD.md). Weight (1 - TGV open) x (1 - EGR) on the normal (non-cruise) path. THIS is where part-throttle feel is set: the commanded opening is about this table plus the idle area (end-to-end model, my research notes). Confidence: inferred.

table.description:

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (TGV Closed)
table.description:
Version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier A used while the TGVs are closed.
Details: 0x0C1EA8 (read): AF4E multiplies the rpm-based filter coefficient AFAC (0x0C38E0) in 0x0C2514 (AF58), 0x0C1854 (predicted air torque AF40) and 0x0C39DC (AF3E): k = AF4E x AFAC/512. 512 = 1.0; values that push k past 65535 mean no lag. Selected in state S2: after combustion-mode change 1 -> 3, while spark target - final timing > 4 deg (7 deg with A7E2 bit 0) and FFF886AB bit 5. TGV closed (A881 bit 4), A7E2 bit 0 clear. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 059ED0 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N340J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (between exact neighbours (72 bytes below, 48 above, both moved by the same amount; inferred)). Descriptor 051A80. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Spark Air Compensation Limiter
table.description:
Limits, by requested amount and coolant, how much the throttle model may add air to make up for retarded spark (TGVs not closed). Large compensation is cut more when cold. Leave alone unless you know the model. On 2017+ ROMs edit the "(Alt)" version instead.
Details: 0x0C2AD8 (read): A644 = this(AF58, coolant); AF5E = max(1.0, AF58 x A644/256) is the spark compensation actually allowed and is the normal value of the cap AF56 in 0x0C37D8. Used while TGVs are not forced closed (FFF8A881 bit 4 clear). Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 059FA8 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N340J: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 051B58. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor
table.description:

table.name: Injector 2/4 Rail Pressure Offset
table.description:
Pressure offset added to measured rail pressure before looking up Injector Flow Compensation (Injectors 2/4), by rpm and load; probably the pressure difference of the rail without the sensor.
Details: 0x06D43A (read): FFF89222 = sat(rail pressure FFF88886 + this(rpm FFF8CE9C, load FFF8A616)), interpolated by 0x00671C (descriptor 0x0608E4: data, u16 axis, u8 axis, 16, 16; row = rpm, read). FFF89222 indexes the injector flow compensation 05A844 used only for injectors 2 and 4 (0x0CB0C8, read); injectors 1 and 3 use 05A838 with FFF88886. Likely the pressure difference of the rail without the sensor (inferred from the boxer layout). Signed, in the rail-pressure unit. Descriptor boot 061548. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 4, Start Delay)
Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Released)
Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied)
Primary Open Loop Fueling
table.description:
Base open-loop (power enrichment) AFR target by rpm and load, used once the exhaust temperature estimate is high enough. The ECU uses the richer of this and the Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV..., AVCS...) group: to lean, edit both; to richen, either. Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor (Outside Closed Loop).
Details: Note: the ECU has a second open-loop fuel path: the four "Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV..., AVCS...)" tables 05ABB0..05ABEC, blended by TGV and AVCS (0x0CE5E8 -> FFF8A681); 0x0CEA80 takes the richer of the two (max). To lean the open-loop target edit both sets; richening works with either (read, my research notes). Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor. Base open-loop enrichment target, 0x0CE854. table.name: Additional Enrichment A
table.description:

Details: When used: while FFF8AA60 bit 3 is set: the P0420 catalyst monitor test is running (set by 0x135D18 inside 0x134374, read; needs closed loop, speed >= 40 km/h, an airflow window). 0x0FF468 (read): used instead of the four Closed Loop Target tables, and its value goes straight to FFF8B30A, without the lean limit, Low-DAM Enrichment or cold-start trim. Axes rpm (FFF8CD56) x load % (FFF8A616). LF76400Q: same code as LF75404S; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 05D9D8. Confidence: inferred.

LTFT Load Range Boundary 2
table.description:
Load boundary 2 of the 10 long-term fuel trim cells (5 load ranges x 2 rpm ranges); load range 2 is below this value.
Details: Long-term fuel trim (0x0C589C -> 0x0CECA8 and 0x0FD76C -> 0x0FD3E4, read). The trim used in the fuel quantity, FFF8A689 (OBD PID 0x07, 128 = 0 %), is FFF811D9 (backup RAM), capped at cal 0x384D6 only when coolant FFF8CD65 is below cal 0x384D7. 0x0FD3E4 builds FFF811D9 from ten learned cells FFF81466[0..9] (backup RAM, cleared to 0 by 0x0FC054): cell = load range (FFF8A616 against the four LTFT Load Range Boundaries, 1-5) + 5 if engine speed FFF8CE9C >= LTFT RPM Range Boundary; FFF8A823 = cell. The cell value is filtered (cal 0x4B16C) into FFF8C53C and then scaled by coolant: FFF811D9 = 128 + (FFF8C53C - 128) x LTFT Coolant Scaling (Positive or Negative)(coolant FFF88A44) / 128. How the cells themselves are learned (0x0FCAF0 / 0x0FC400 / 0x0FC5C0, from the closed-loop integrators FFF8B2B0/B2FA) is not decoded. Load range 2 is below this; range 5 is at or above boundary 4. Confidence: read.

Injection Timing (Double Injection, 1st)
table.description:
Angle of the first pulse when two injections per cycle are used.
Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the compression TDC, stored directly (0x0CFC20: code = 1440 - x, then clamped to 0.5-540 BTDC; read). Same scale as every other Injection Timing / injection-angle table. When used: Angle of the first pulse when two injections per cycle are used, in normal fuel mode (0x0CB394, read). Injection angle for FFF8B054 (0x0C589C via 0x0CFC20-style helper, read): computed only while FFF99844 is 2 or 3 (otherwise a fixed 0x1FE) (0x0CFC20, read). 0x0CB394 uses B054 for two injections and B058 for three in normal fuel mode (read); the Double Injection tables cover 1100-3200 rpm, the Triple Injection tables 600-1300 rpm. LF76400Q: same code as LF75404S; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 05BC5C. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Injection Timing (Double Injection, 2nd)
table.description:
Angle of the second pulse with two injections per cycle.
Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the compression TDC, stored directly (0x0CFC20: code = 1440 - x, then clamped to 0.5-540 BTDC; read). Same scale as every other Injection Timing / injection-angle table. When used: Angle of the second pulse with two injections per cycle (0x0CB604, read). Injection angle for FFF8B056 (0x0C589C via 0x0CFC20-style helper, read): computed only while FFF99844 is 2 or 3 (otherwise a fixed 0x1FE) (0x0CFC20, read). 0x0CB394 uses B054 for two injections and B058 for three in normal fuel mode (read); the Double Injection tables cover 1100-3200 rpm, the Triple Injection tables 600-1300 rpm. LF76400Q: same code as LF75404S; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 05BC70. Confidence: inferred.

Purge Valve Duty
table.description:
Purge valve duty needed for a target purge flow at a given manifold vacuum; higher vacuum needs less duty. Applied above Purge Valve Minimum Duty. Change only for a different purge valve.
Details: When used: every 80 ms pass (0x0D60FC, read): A70A = this(target purge flow FFF8B0C0, manifold vacuum FFF8CDFA). The final duty is A713 + (100 % - A713) x this, with A713 = Purge Valve Minimum Duty (0x0D6118, read), and 0 when this is 0. B0C0 = purge rate x air quantity FFF8B4D6 / 256, in the air-quantity unit (read). Higher vacuum needs less duty for the same flow. Purge module (inferred: canister purge): 0x0D4E78 (80 ms task 0x1E1560) and 0x0D4C14 (20 ms task 0x1E0AE8) (read). Chain (read): purge rate A70C (limits A6FD/A70F, ramp A709, cut B0A0) -> purge flow B0C0 = A70C x air FFF8B4D6/256 -> valve duty A70A = 05B314(B0C0, vacuum) -> A70B with minimum duty A713 -> A707 -> timer E channel 22 (0x1D98D6); A707 is also checked by the circuit monitor 0x072090 (driver status FFF88BF4 bits 10/11). Fuel: A71A = filtered purge rate x learned concentration FFF81412 (0x0D688C) is subtracted from the fuel factor (0x0D15EC). LF76400Q: same code as LF75404S; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 05BF50. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing IAT Compensation
table.description:
Timing added (negative = retard) for hot intake air, by intake air temperature, scaled by Base Timing IAT Compensation Multiplier. Applied once the engine is running above about 800 rpm and feeds into base timing.
Details: When used: FFF8A782 = rate-limited (cals 0x32DE2/0x32DE4 = 65535, i.e. none) value, enabled once FFF8CD5C >= cal 0x37F9E (800 rpm) in running mode FFF8866C = 3 (0x0E0184, read; cal 0x239AE bit 3 clear, so the knock-limit min() is not applied). FFF8A782 is added to the torque-model base timing FFF8A645 (0x0C2C08, A-D path with FFF8A787; E/F path with FFF8A788; my research notes, Ghidra stack args) and to the timing request FFF8A78A/FFF8B10E -> FFF8A789 (0x0E0A30, register args, read), which becomes the spark target FFF8A72A (0x0D9088). It is not a separate term of the final timing sum FFF8A744, but it reaches the fired timing through FFF8A645 (FFF8A645 -> FFF8A76A -> FFF8A76D -> FFF8A74B -> FFF8A744, 0x0DD568 / 0x0DD760 / 0x0DA600 / 0x0D9E40, read). Value = this(IAT FFF88A48) x Base Timing IAT Compensation Multiplier(rpm, load) / 128 (read). LF76400Q: 0x0DFD68 (pair of LF75404S 0x0E0184): the first curve, multiplied by Base Timing IAT Compensation Multiplier 05C8F4 (read; the transfer had put this name on 05C964, which is the second curve). Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing IAT Compensation 2

Knock Background Window Step (Event 1, Channel 2)
table.description:
This software version (function 0x0E5098, read against the longer version of the function): the table is the step only on the pass where the window flag sets. On the pass where it clears, the longer version subtracts the table; this one adds the fixed value at cal 0x02953A instead (s16; the row for the event is Knock Background Clear Step (Event 1)).
Knock signal processing for event slot 1, channel 2 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock. Larger = that event less likely to count as knock. Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.
Details: When used: event slot FFF8CDC0 = 1 (Event 1), knock channel 2 of 8, on the knock window where FFF8A7C2 changes. Background step for this channel, added to (window extended) or subtracted from (window back to nominal) the channel background FFF8C180[1] for that one event; overlap-flag FFF8A7D2, gain curve cal 0x26F6F. Knock signal processing 0x0E51E4 (read; called once per knock window from 0x0E43B8 with load FFF8A616, after the event chain 0x0E433C): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4, the slot of the Knock Threshold tables) each of 8 knock channels i gets a reference ref_i = 32 x step_i + g x background_i, and the channel ratio is 256 x FFF8CDB0[i] / (ref_i / 32), i.e. measured / reference with 256 = equal (0x0E51E4 tail, read). Channels with their bit set in cal 0x1B97C..0x1B97F give 0; a channel flagged in FFF8CEED (driver flag, value at its lower limit, inferred) gives 256. The ratios are sorted and the largest min(cal 0x1B988, 5) = 3 are summed into the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot], which 0x0E80B4/0x0E8654 compare with Knock Threshold (read). The measured channels come from the knock sensor ADC: 0x1E7868 DMA-collects 32-sample blocks, 0x1E725A runs FFT-style butterflies, 0x1E73A4 takes sqrt(re^2+im^2) of 8 selected bins (pointer tables 0x34A88/0x34AA8), and 0x1E7724 sums them over the window into FFF8D1D4[8] -> FFF8CDB0[8] (read), so the 8 channels are 8 frequency bins of the knock sensor signal (inferred). background_i is the per-slot channel background FFF8C180.. (slot 1) / C190.. / C1A0.. / C1B0.. (slot 4), a lag filter of the measured channel kept by 0x0E4500 when the event is not knocking, floored at the per-channel rpm curve FFF8C0D8 (0x0E22A4) (read). step_i is this table family: it is non-zero only on the one event where the slot's window-length flag changes: +table when the flag goes 0 -> 1 (window switched to the extended length) and -table when it goes 1 -> 0 (back to the nominal length); on that event the reference is also floored at 32 x FFF8C0D8[i] (read). The flag is set when the extended knock window is used (0x0E20E0, read: B11A = nominal + Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 <= Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold and the extended window ends before the event angle). The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). Axes: rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500, 500-4000 rpm) x load FFF8A616 (read). 0x0E5098: same descriptor sequence as in LF76401R, where the exact map and its neighbours place these tables (inferred by position). Confidence: inferred.

(slot 4), a lag filter of the measured channel kept by 0x0E4500 when the event is not knocking, floored at the per-channel rpm curve FFF8C0D8 (0x0E22A4) (read). step_i is this table family: it is non-zero only on the one event where the slot's window-length flag changes: +table when the flag goes 0 -> 1 (window switched to the extended length) and -table when it goes 1 -> 0 (back to the nominal length); on that event the reference is also floored at 32 x FFF8C0D8[i] (read). The flag is set when the extended knock window is used (0x0E20E0, read: B11A = nominal + Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 <= Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold and the extended window ends before the event angle). The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). Axes: rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500, 500-4000 rpm) x load FFF8A616 (read). Confidence: read.

Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1, AT/CVT)
table.description:
AT/CVT copy of Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1).
Details: When used: FFF8A7E2 bit 0 clear (never on the manual coding), FFF899D7 bit 0 clear. 0x108BAC (catalyst-heating module, read) writes FFF8A854, which 0x0C3200 selects as the spark target FFF8A647 in fuel mode FFF8A852 = 2 (combustion mode FFF8A85C 1 or 3, 0x108B08). A647 is the spark the torque model compensates for (0x0C2514, 0x0C1EA8) and the reference of the cold-start retard monitors (0x1CB70C, 0x132568: A72A - A854) (read); the fired spark in this mode follows FFF8A74C/FFF8A76B (0x0DA428), not A854 (read). In combustion mode 1 (A85C < 2), at <= 4000 rpm (cal 0x1CBD8), with the pedal released (FFF886AB bit 5) and speed below cal 0x2A0C1 (2 km/h): A854 = Base(rpm FFF8CD5C, coolant) + Torque Adder(FFF8A85E, coolant) + Run-Time Adder(passes since the engine state became running, coolant) + Re-Entry Adder(passes since mode 1 was re-entered from normal mode 4, coolant), saturated to a byte; the set is chosen by FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (set = the manual tables, clear = the "AT/CVT" tables; always set on the manual coding, Phase 14) and FFF899D7 bit 0 (set = the "Warm-Up Fallback" tables): a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch set by 0x081EFC only when cal 0x59134 bit 0 is set. Otherwise in mode 1 A854 = 05D0BC x 05D0A8 / 256 + FFF8A789 - 32; in mode 3 A854 = A72A (normal target) (read). with cal 0x2996C bit 6 set A854 is forced to cal 0x2A0C0. Units: A854 is compared with A72A and final timing in 0.5 degree units (inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: Start Spark Signal Upper Threshold (Baro)
table.description: Below the rpm limit cal 0x1C9B8. The start spark function compares a 16-bit signal (FFF8B25C, not identified) with two thresholds looked up by barometric pressure: at or below Start Spark Signal Lower Threshold (plus cal 0x2B0C4 once met) for cal 0x2B0C8 passes, and at or above Start Spark Signal Upper Threshold (minus cal 0x2B0C2 once met) for cal 0x2B0C9 passes; Start Spark Offset Step is added per pass to the offset counter FFF85440 that is added to the start spark target (0x109254, read on the Ghidra lift of LF76401R, 2026-11-13). Raw units. Descriptor 05DCEC. Confidence: read.

Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Below Idle Target)
table.description:
Version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier A used while rpm is far below the idle target (later software versions).
Details: When used: Only while the below-idle latch (in later software versions) is set: rpm - idle target <= cal 0x11AF4 (with hysteresis). LF79100P: a table LF75404S does not have; scaling and axes as Torque Model Filter Multiplier A. Evidence: table new in 2017+ builds, read by 0x0D0D6C in state S2 when the latch FFF84250 is set (rpm FFF8D424 - idle target FFF8B8B2 <= cal 0x11AF4, hysteresis 0x11AF6); Alt flag clear, TGV normal (read). LF76400Q: 0x0C1740: A-state, Alt argument clear, below-idle flag FFF84244 set (rpm - idle target <= cal 0x11AF4, + 0x11AF6 once set) (read). This build has no TGV split of these tables. Descriptor 05AB40. Confidence: read.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Alt)
table.description:
Alternate version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier A, used when an unidentified flag is set. Leave alone unless you know the model.
Details: 0x0C1EA8 (read): AF4E multiplies the rpm-based filter coefficient AFAC (0x0C38E0) in 0x0C2514 (AF58), 0x0C1854 (predicted air torque AF40) and 0x0C39DC (AF3E): k = AF4E x AFAC/512. 512 = 1.0; values that push k past 65535 mean no lag. Selected in state S2: after combustion-mode change 1 -> 3, while spark target - final timing > 4 deg (7 deg with A7E2 bit 0) and FFF886AB bit 5. TGVs normal, A7E2 bit 0 set. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: read.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Alt, Below Idle Target)
table.description:
Version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Alt) used while rpm is far below the idle target (later software versions).
Details: When used: Only while the below-idle latch (in later software versions) is set: rpm - idle target <= cal 0x11AF4 (with hysteresis). LF79100P: a table LF75404S does not have; scaling and axes as Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Alt). Evidence: table new in 2017+ builds, read by 0x0D0D6C in state S2 when the latch FFF84250 is set (rpm FFF8D424 - idle target FFF8B8B2 <= cal 0x11AF4, hysteresis 0x11AF6); Alt flag set, TGV normal (read). LF76400Q: 0x0C1740: A-state, Alt argument set, below-idle flag FFF84244 set (read). This build has no TGV split of these tables. Descriptor 05AB34. Confidence: read.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier C (Alt)
table.description:
Alternate version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier C, used when an unidentified flag is set. Leave alone.
Details: 0x0C1EA8 (read): AF4E multiplies the rpm-based filter coefficient AFAC (0x0C38E0) in 0x0C2514 (AF58), 0x0C1854 (predicted air torque AF40) and 0x0C39DC (AF3E): k = AF4E x AFAC/512. 512 = 1.0; values that push k past 65535 mean no lag. Selected in state S3: after combustion-mode change 1 -> 3, while in mode 3, FFF886AB bit 5 clear and final timing not yet within 3 deg of the spark target (A64C bit 5). TGVs normal, A7E2 bit 0 set. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: read.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier C
table.description:
Torque-model smoothing multiplier by coolant (1.0 = normal; very high values mean no smoothing), used after a combustion-mode change until timing reaches the spark target. Leave alone.
Details: 0x0C1EA8 (read): AF4E multiplies the rpm-based filter coefficient AFAC (0x0C38E0) in 0x0C2514 (AF58), 0x0C1854 (predicted air torque AF40) and 0x0C39DC (AF3E): k = AF4E x AFAC/512. 512 = 1.0; values that push k past 65535 mean no lag. Selected in state S3: after combustion-mode change 1 -> 3, while in mode 3, FFF886AB bit 5 clear and final timing not yet within 3 deg of the spark target (A64C bit 5). TGVs normal, A7E2 bit 0 clear. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Confidence: read.

table.name: Spark Air Compensation Limiter
table.description:
Limits, by requested amount and coolant, how much the throttle model may add air to make up for retarded spark (TGVs not closed). Large compensation is cut more when cold. Leave alone unless you know the model. On 2017+ ROMs edit the "(Alt)" version instead.
Details: 0x0C2AD8 (read): A644 = this(AF58, coolant); AF5E = max(1.0, AF58 x A644/256) is the spark compensation actually allowed and is the normal value of the cap AF56 in 0x0C37D8. Used while TGVs are not forced closed (FFF8A881 bit 4 clear). Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). LF75200T: located from LF75404S 059FA8 by the code that reads it (read). LF76400Q: 0x0C23E0 reads this one table (read). In this software version the result is also multiplied by a third argument (x arg / 16384), as with the baro factor of later versions. Descriptor 05ABF4. Confidence: read.

Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (No Enrichment)
table.description:
Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map A is the fast-reacting part, by rpm and load, used while no open loop enrichment is active. Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it.
Details: When used: always while running. Map A while no open-loop enrichment is active. 0x0C9878 (read): with no open-loop enrichment (FFF8A684 = 0) S = Map A (No Enrichment) x Retard Multiplier A (No Enrichment)/256 and U = Map B (No Enrichment) x Retard Multiplier B (No Enrichment)/256; with enrichment the (Enriched) tables are used; with FFF8A8A5 bit 4 set (flag from 0x11B2A4 on vehicle speed, pedal and load; not decoded) the (FFF8A8A5 Bit 4) tables. Maps are rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8A616. FFF8C562 = S filtered (weight 05A578 while FFF8AFCC is rising, 05A5A0 while falling, by rpm x load); FFF8C564 = (U - S + fuel-cut term FFF8B040) filtered (weights 05A680 / 05A6A8 by air quantity FFF8B4D6 x FFF8B066); estimate FFF8AFD0 = FFF8C562 + FFF8C564, so in steady state FFF8AFD0 tends to Map B. 0x0CE854 enables Primary Open Loop Fueling while FFF8AFD0 >= cal 0x18DD4 (39322, hysteresis cal 0x18DD6 = 2185), and 0x0C5880 integrates 05A82C(FFF8AFD0) into FFF8C03C, the second enable path (read). Reading FFF8AFD0 as an exhaust/catalyst temperature estimate is inferred: the enriched maps are lower than the stoichiometric ones, retard raises the value (multiplier 0.75 at 25 degrees advanced to 1.2 at 20 degrees retarded) and the value gates the enrichment. Raising these maps brings Primary Open Loop Fueling in earlier (lower load); lowering them delays it. LF76400Q: same code as LF75404S; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 05B19C. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (Enriched)
table.description:
Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map A is the fast-reacting part, by rpm and load, used while open loop enrichment is active. Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it.
Details: When used: always while running. Map A while open-loop enrichment FFF8A684 is active. 0x0C9878 (read): with no open-loop enrichment (FFF8A684 = 0) S = Map A (No Enrichment) x Retard Multiplier A (No Enrichment)/256 and U = Map B (No Enrichment) x Retard Multiplier B (No Enrichment)/256; with enrichment the (Enriched) tables are used; with FFF8A8A5 bit 4 set (flag from 0x11B2A4 on vehicle speed, pedal and load; not decoded) the (FFF8A8A5 Bit 4) tables. Maps are rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8A616. Details: When used: at the start of each cylinder fuel cut (rising edge of FFF8A64C bit 0, i.e. FFF8A643 != 0, my research notes). 0x0C9878 (read): FFF8B040 = this(air quantity FFF8B4D6, FFF8B066) at the edge, then FFF8B040 = previous x Fuel Cut Decay(FFF8B4D6)/65535 each pass; FFF8B040 is added into the FFF8C564 part of the estimate. 0x0C9878 (read): with no open-loop enrichment (FFF8A684 = 0) S = Map A (No Enrichment) x Retard Multiplier A (No Enrichment)/256 and U = Map B (No Enrichment) x Retard Multiplier B (No Enrichment)/256; with enrichment the (Enriched) tables are used; with FFF8A8A5 bit 4 set (flag from 0x11B2A4 on vehicle speed, pedal and load; not decoded) the (FFF8A8A5 Bit 4) tables. Maps are rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8A616. FFF8C562 = S filtered (weight 05A578 while FFF8AFCC is rising, 05A5A0 while falling, by rpm x load); FFF8C564 = (U - S + fuel-cut term FFF8B040) filtered (weights 05A680 / 05A6A8 by air quantity FFF8B4D6 x FFF8B066); estimate FFF8AFD0 = FFF8C562 + FFF8C564, so in steady state FFF8AFD0 tends to Map B. 0x0CE854 enables Primary Open Loop Fueling while FFF8AFD0 >= cal 0x18DD4 (39322, hysteresis cal 0x18DD6 = 2185), and 0x0C5880 integrates 05A82C(FFF8AFD0) into FFF8C03C, the second enable path (read). Reading FFF8AFD0 as an exhaust/catalyst temperature estimate is inferred: the enriched maps are lower than the stoichiometric ones, retard raises the value (multiplier 0.75 at 25 degrees advanced to 1.2 at 20 degrees retarded) and the value gates the enrichment. Raising these maps brings Primary Open Loop Fueling in earlier (lower load); lowering them delays it. LF76400Q: same code as LF75404S; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 05B2A4. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Estimate 2 Map (Standstill High Load)
A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Base
A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Timing Factor
A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Retard Factor
A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Filter
A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Condensate at Start
A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Condensation Flow Factor
A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Saturation Vapour Pressure
A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor (2D)
table.description:
Later-software version of A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor: on a hot restart the exhaust model starts from the stored pipe temperature times this factor, by stored temperature and coolant drop. Normally leave alone.
Details: When used: before the engine runs, on a hot restart: coolant at start high enough (cals 0x4B638/0x4B639 = 10/110, i.e. the same >= 60 C, 50 C to stay test as LF75404S cals 0x4234C/D) and last running coolant FFF8069B >= cal 0x4B63B (130 = 80 C). Later-software replacement of the 1D table A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor (05F1E4), which these images do not have. LF79002P 0x1866D8 (counterpart of LF75404S 0x1802F4; stack arguments checked in the LF79002P disassembly: param_9 @72 = FFF81678, called at 0x18716A, read): the modelled exhaust pipe temperature (K x 32) starts at max(FFF81678 x this(FFF81678, coolant drop)/256, min(IAT, coolant) (C150/C152)). FFF81678 is the pipe temperature latched when the engine stops (0x1866B8, read; = LF75404S FFF815BA). Axis 1 = that stored pipe temperature (u16, K x 32; the lookup 0x1B0D7C clamps it and the drop to the axis ends), axis 2 = the coolant drop since the engine last ran, FFF8069B - FFF88D96 x 160/65536 - 10 (s8, degC) (read). Data u8, unsigned interpolation in 0x1B0D7C, layout [stored-temperature index x 8 + drop index] (read). The starting temperature drives the exhaust condensation model behind the A/F sensor heater release (see A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Saturation Vapour Pressure). LF79100P: a table LF75404S does not have. Evidence: Phase 19 group X (my research notes): reader 0x186818, call site 1868D0; replaces the 1D hot-restart factor of the 2015 code (read). LF76400Q: 0x18166C: the lookup whose result is written to the factor output; a 2D table by a 16-bit temperature and the temperature drop, as in the later software versions (read). Descriptor 05FE5C. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 1A (TGV Open, Normal, Altitude)
Intake Cam Target 1B (TGV Open, Normal, Sea Level)
table.description:
Main intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load for normal driving with the TGVs open near sea level: above light part throttle, above about 5200 rpm, or cold. Higher = earlier intake timing. At light part throttle the TGVs close and Intake Cam Target 3B is used instead. Normal vs high-pedal split is inferred.
Details: Convention (read, see FU_UNITS): crank degrees of intake cam ADVANCE from its learned rest position; 0 = rest (fully retarded, inferred), larger = more advance (earlier valve events). Values below 0 ask for less than the rest position: the OCV then sits at minimum duty and the cam stays at rest (inferred). AVCS target (intake 0x15C250, exhaust 0x16032C, read): target = coolant terms + v x [S_A x w + S_B x (1 - w)] + (1 - v) x [3A x w + (3B + Coolant Offset 3B x Coolant Factor 3 / 128) x (1 - w)], clamped to +/-90 degrees, 364.09 counts per degree. v = FFF8B3E8, the TGV open fraction: sets 1/2 apply with TGVs open, set 3 with TGVs closed. w = FFF8B948 = AVCS Barometric Blend (barometric pressure FFF88668, via 0x15B1E0, read): the A tables apply at altitude, the B tables at sea level. S = set 1 or set 2, chosen by FFF8A8A4 bit 7 (stack argument +24 from 0x15969C, read). That bit is a high-pedal latch (0x11C15C / 0x10F848, read): it sets when the accelerator FFF88A5E is at or above High Pedal Entry Threshold while vehicle speed is not jumping (under cal 0x35B16... per gear) and some status flags (FFF88A2D bit 0, FFF88ADA bit 6, FFF8A8A2 bit 6) are clear, or when FFF8A8A5 bit 2 or 4 is set; it clears once the pedal is below cal 0x36518 (85 %). So set 1 = normal driving and set 2 = near wide-open pedal (meaning inferred from these conditions). Exhaust set 2 differs mainly below 1.03 g/rev. The altitude (A) sets differ only below 0.52 g/rev. The set-3 terms are active because cal 0x3ACF6 = 1 in both images. Set 1, B table (weight 1 - w). This is the sea-level target while the TGVs are open (above the TGV torque / air-quantity thresholds, above 5200 rpm, or cold); at light part throttle the TGVs are closed and Intake Cam Target 3B is used. LF76400Q: same code as LF75404S; address from the same instruction (similarity port (code)). Descriptor 05F134. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Intake Cam Target Limit
table.description: While FFF8A8B0 bit 7 is set, the intake cam target is capped at Intake Cam Target Limit(rpm, load) + Intake Cam Target Limit Temperature Offset(rpm, load) x Intake Cam Target Limit Temperature Factor(temperature byte FFF88A1F) / 128. That bit is a high-pedal latch (0x11C15C / 0x10F848, read): it sets when the accelerator FFF88A5E is at or above High Pedal Entry Threshold while vehicle speed is not jumping (under cal 0x35B16... per gear) and some status flags (FFF88A2D bit 0, FFF88ADA bit 6, FFF8A8A2 bit 6) are clear, or when FFF8A8A5 bit 2 or 4 is set; it clears once the pedal is below cal 0x36518 (85 %). So set 1 = normal driving and set 2 = near wide-open pedal (meaning inferred from these conditions). The set-3 terms are active because cal 0x3ACF6 = 1 in both images. This table is w itself: the share of every A table (the B tables get the rest), by barometric pressure FFF88668 (0x15B1E0 looks it up and stores FFF8B948, read). LF76400Q: same code as LF75404S; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 05F0A0. Confidence: read.

table.description:
Requested torque, by rpm, below which the TGVs may close in drive mode 3. The TGVs probably close at light load: requested torque must fall below the Enter table to close them and rise above the matching Exit table to reopen (with coolant and air-flow conditions).
Details: When used: Drive mode 3 (0x10D93C / 0x11A8B0, read). TGV request logic 0x10D93C (read): the request byte FFF8A888 is 3 unless all of these hold: coolant FFF88A44 at or above TGV Coolant Minimum, requested torque FFF8AEE2 (0x0BA868, Nm = x/80 - 200) below the rpm-based TGV Torque Threshold (it must fall below the Enter table and then rise above the Exit table to clear), air quantity FFF8B4D6 below TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Enter 0x37A4A, Exit 0x37A48), and FFF8A88D = 0. When they hold, FFF8A888 = 1, or 2 if the intake air temperature FFF88A48 is below TGV IAT Threshold (vehicle speed) or FFF88E28 bit 0/2 is set; FFF8A888 = 2 also while combustion mode FFF8A85C is below cal 0x37B48. State 1 requests TGV close: it runs the timer FFF8B3E0 (0x10C3D0) and FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is set once the timer reaches TGV Close Delay. States 2 (close blocked: cold intake air, FFF88E28 bit 0/2, or combustion mode below cal 0x37B48) and 3 (close conditions not met) reset the timer, so the TGVs stay open (read). Which threshold pair is used depends on FFF8A8C1 (1, 2, 3 or other) and FFF8A8A2 bit 5 (not identified). Each threshold is table(rpm FFF8CE9C) + TGV Torque Threshold Offset(rpm, FFF88AE6) - 16000, so the offset table is centred on 16000 (0 ft-lb). used for mode 3, and for other modes (not 1/2) while FFF8A8A2 bit 5 is set. Confidence: inferred.

Which threshold pair is used depends on FFF8A8C1 (1, 2, 3 or other) and FFF8A8A2 bit 5 (not identified). table.description:
Road speed per 1000 rpm for each gear, used only by the gear advice function. The values do not match the 6MT and probably belong to another transmission.

table.name: Gear Advice Consumption Map
table.description:
Fuel consumption map by torque and rpm (probably g/kWh) for a gear-shift advice function that picks the most economical gear. One table edits all three copies.
Gear advice module 0x116A0C. With the bit set it takes the current power (torque x rpm / 9549.3), the engine speed in the gear below (FFF8B434, gear FFF8A8BA = gear - 1, 0x114360) and in the gear above (FFF8B436, gear FFF8A8BC = gear + 1, 0x1143CC), looks up the consumption map at the three points and advises the gear with the lowest value (FFF85678 / FFF85679, biases cal 0x36E4E/0x36E50 = 3 %). 'Alternate' tables are used when FFF8A8C3 = 2. Descriptors 05D4D8, 05D504 and 05D518 share this data block (037352): 05D4D8 at the current torque FFF8B468 = DAM-blended torque FFF8B48A - FFF8A8CC x 128 (0x1161DC) and rpm, 05D504 / 05D518 at the torque needed for the same power in the lower / upper gear (read). One entry edits all three. LF76400Q: same code as LF75404S; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 05E0A0. Confidence: inferred.

'Alternate' tables are used when FFF8A8C3 = 2. 0x116A0C (read): FFF85648 = this(lower gear FFF8A8BA); the lower gear is advised (FFF85679 = 1) only if its engine speed FFF8B434 <= FFF85648. 05D5B8 (normal) is 31232 = 6100 rpm for every gear. table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts the main intake air temperature sensor voltage to degrees; this IAT feeds the timing, boost and fuel compensations and the scan-tool reading. Its voltage axis is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling, so edit only the temperatures when fitting a different sensor.
Details: When used: always (10 ms task prefix 0x1E2F20 / 0x06AF58, read). ADC channel 19 (0xFFFFE864, untrimmed) -> FFF88D38 -> FFF88F30, filtered by cal 0x579B6 -> FFF88F34 / FFF88F32, looked up here (boot lookup 0x7250) to give FFF88662 = degC + 50: the OBD IAT FFF8CEE5, the IAT behind FFF88A48 (the IAT axis of the timing, boost, throttle and fuel compensation tables) and the IAT read by fuel 0x0C589C and purge 0x0D4E78 (for Purge Air Density (IAT, Baro), 0x0D44DC) (read). This is IAT sensor 1 (P0112 / P0113, read), probably the element in the MAF housing (inferred). The voltage axis (0x579FC, 32 points 0...4.96 V in 0.16 V steps; 65536 = 5 V inferred) is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling: change only the temperature values for a different thermistor, or both sensors move. While the sensor is faulted (FFF88E28 bit 2) the fixed voltage cal 0x579BA x 256 is used. Descriptor boot 0614B4. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling
table.description:
Converts the second intake temperature sensor's voltage to degrees. This is the air temperature the ECU's airflow model uses to work out air density, and it probably comes from the manifold pressure (TMAP) sensor, so update it when you swap that sensor for one with a different thermistor. Its voltage axis is shared with the main IAT table; change only the temperatures.
Details: When used: always (10 ms task prefix 0x1E2F20 / 0x06B304, read). ADC channel 20 (0xFFFFE868, untrimmed) -> FFF88D40 -> FFF88F36, filtered by cal 0x579B8 -> FFF88F38 / FFF88F3A, looked up here (boot lookup 0x7250) into FFF888CF (degC + 50; FFF888D4 from the unfaulted value). This is IAT sensor 2 (P0097 / P0098 monitors on the same voltage, read). FFF888CF is the air temperature of the speed-density airflow model (0x11DF4C: density from MAP and IAT 2 + 223 K) and is also read by requested torque 0x0BE694, ignition 0x0D98F8 / 0x0D9A10 / 0x0DE0E0 and AVCS 0x15969C (read), so a wrong curve shifts the modelled air and load. Probably the thermistor of the manifold TMAP sensor (inferred from its use as the manifold air temperature): when fitting a different TMAP / MAP sensor with its own thermistor, change these temperature values. The voltage axis (0x579FC) is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor Scaling, so change only the data. While faulted (FFF88FCD bit 2) the fixed voltage cal 0x579BB x 256 is used. Descriptor boot 0614C0. Confidence: read.

table.name: Coolant Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts coolant temperature sensor voltage to degrees. Every coolant-based table and the scan-tool coolant reading use this. Change only when fitting a different sensor.
Details: When used: always (40 ms task prefix 0x1E43FE / 0x06BA46, read). Coolant sensor voltage FFF8865E (input 0 of the 8-way multiplexer on ADC channel 21, untrimmed, 65536 = 5 V inferred) is filtered by cal 0x56EE8 (65535 = no filter) into FFF88ADC and looked up here (boot lookup 0x73BC) into FFF88AE8 / FFF88AE0 (256 x (degC + 50)): FFF8CD65 (coolant byte, degC + 50), the OBD coolant value and FFF88A44 (the coolant axis of most tables). While the sensor is faulted (FFF88E28 bit 1) a warm-up model from cals 0x56EEC-0x56EF2 replaces it. Range faults: P0117 below Coolant Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit, P0118 above Coolant Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit. Change only when fitting a different sensor. Descriptor boot 0614D8. Confidence: read.

table.name: Oil Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts oil temperature sensor voltage to degrees; this oil temperature feeds the AVCS and idle tables and the scan-tool reading. Change only when fitting a different sensor.
Details: When used: always (40 ms task prefix 0x1E43FE / 0x06BEA0, read). Oil temperature sensor voltage FFF88AA2 (input 7 of the 8-way multiplexer on ADC channel 21, untrimmed) is filtered by cal 0x56F76 (65535 = no filter) into FFF88AE4 and looked up here (boot lookup 0x73BC). Output unit 256 x (degC + 50), read: FFF88E24 = (output - 0xA00) x 256 / 205 and OBD PID 0x5C reports FFF88E24 x 205 / 65536 = degC + 40. FFF88E24 / FFF88E26 is the oil temperature of the AVCS and idle tables (oil_temp_obd axis). Range faults: P0197 below Oil Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit, P0198 above Oil Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit. Descriptor boot 0614E4. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Sensor Scaling (Wide Range)
table.description:
Converts the front wideband A/F sensor signal to lambda when the reading is outside about lambda 0.90-1.37. This is the measured lambda used by closed loop fueling.
Details: When used: Used while FFF88AFB bit 4 is clear: the A/F signal is outside about lambda 0.90-1.37 (window -800..1000 with hysteresis 333, 0x0843F8, read); gain cal 0x571F0 = 2. 0x06C1A8 (read): the A/F sensor signal FFF88B2E is looked up here (boot lookup 0x6A0C) into FFF88AF6, the measured lambda of the closed loop (B308 = 43194 x 32768 / FFF88AF6, 0x0FF3CC). Descriptor boot 0614F0. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Sensor Scaling (Near Stoich)
table.description:
Converts the front A/F sensor signal to lambda when it reads within about lambda 0.90-1.37, at a higher gain.
Details: When used: Used while the A/F signal is within about lambda 0.90-1.37 (FFF88AFB bit 4 set, 0x0843F8, read); higher gain cal 0x571F1 = 9 (gain reading inferred). Second A/F sensor table in 0x06C1A8 (read); shares the axis with A/F Sensor Scaling (Wide Range). Descriptor boot 0614FC. Confidence: read.

table.name: Fuel Level Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts the fuel sender reading, which the instrument cluster sends to the ECU over CAN, to fuel level (219 = 100 %). The ECU averages it and reports it as fuel level to a scan tool.
Details: When used: always (0x06C336, read). Input: the fuel sender reading sent by the combination meter on CAN 0x282 bytes 0-1 (10-bit, FFF88E04 -> 0x1108B8 -> FFF8B43C; not an ECU analog input). 0x06C336 forms FFF88BD0 = FFF8B43C x 2867 / (FFF8B43C + cal 0x572E0 (720)), filters it into FFF88BCC and looks it up here (boot lookup 0x7250) into FFF88BD4; FFF88BD7 is its average over cal 0x572E6 samples taken while FFF88A76 is at least cal 0x572E4, kept in backup RAM FFF806BB/806BC, and reported by OBD PID 0x2F as x 255 / 219 (read). So this is the fuel level curve, 219 = 100 %. P0463 / P0462 when FFF88BCC is above cal 0x572DA / below cal 0x572DE (0x0714E0 / 0x071548, read). Descriptor boot 061508. Confidence: read.

table.name: Battery Temperature Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts the battery temperature sensor voltage to degrees for the charging-voltage control. It is probably the temperature half of the battery sensor, whose current signal the ECU also reads. Leave alone unless the battery sensor is changed.
Details: When used: always (10 ms task prefix 0x1E2F20 / 0x06C768, read). ADC channel 9 (0xFFFFE852, untrimmed) -> FFF8939A, filtered by cal 0x590F0 into FFF8939E (cal 0x590EE replaces the input while FFF88BCA bit 2 or 3 is set) and looked up here (boot lookup 0x7250) into FFF893A0 (degC + 50), read only by the charging-voltage control 0x136CD8 (temperature-compensated voltage targets); the unfiltered value gives FFF893A1, reported by SSM as x - 10 (0x11F0E8, read). Identity (inferred): its companion input ADC channel 4 (FFF89390, 0x06C554) is a linear signal centred on 2.5 V (FFF89396 = 12800 - 0.488 x (sample - 32768); SSM x/128 + 28 puts zero at 2.5 V, about -50 A per volt), i.e. a bidirectional battery current, read by charging control 0x136BC0 and idle 0x0EE338; the two inputs share their filter cal block and their range monitors (FFF88BCA bits 2-5, 0x0715B0-0x07175C) are both enabled by cal 0x57584 bit 4. A current + temperature pair used only for charging is the battery sensor, so this is battery temperature. Leave alone unless the battery sensor is changed. LF75200T: located from LF75404S 0608B0 by the code that reads it (read). LF76400Q: same code as LF75200T; address from the same instruction (exact (2 reads), descriptor words read from the image). Descriptor boot 061514. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Rear O2 Sensor Ready Heater Energy Threshold
table.description:
How much heater energy, by coolant temperature at start, the rear O2 sensor must have received before it is treated as warmed up and ready. Raising it delays the rear O2 sensor (and its diagnostics) becoming active.
Details: When used: while the engine runs (run state FFF8906B = 3). 0x1028D0 (read; called from 0x101CF0): FFF8A833 bit 7 is set (and held until the run state leaves 3) when the accumulated rear O2 heater drive FFF88E6E > this(coolant at start FFF88A46; the -40 C row is used when the coolant sensor is faulted, FFF88E28 bit 1), or when FFF8881E >= cal 0x4B900 (9437) for cal 0x4B904 (50) passes. Rear O2 identity: the heater output FFF9980E bit 2 is driven by 0x06EC70 for FFF8CE0B of every 24 40-ms passes, and 0x073570 monitors that output against FFF8CE0B into FFF89CB4 bits 0/1, the P0037 / P0038 (heater circuit, bank 1 sensor 2) monitor records (dtc_monitors slots 182 / 180, read). FFF88E6E sums FFF8CE0B every 40 ms (0x06ED92, read), so it is heater energy since start; FFF8CE0B = 0 while the heater is held off (initial delay from 0x608F4, high load, battery out of range; 0x06E7D8, read). FFF8881E = 2 x (ADC channel 11 - ADC channel 25) (0x1E0000 task, read); it is the oxygen-sensor signal that gates Fuel Cut Recovery Enrichment (0x0CAE40: FFF8881E < cal 0x14F5C, read), so the second path is 'sensor already reads rich' (inferred). FFF8A833 bit 7 feeds the catalyst/rear-O2 module 0x101CF0 (0x1023E0, 0x102B58) and the rear O2 diagnostics 0x1B8890 / 0x1B902C (P0137, result FFF8AD93 bit 7) and 0x123C68 (read). Meaning 'sensor ready / warmed up' inferred. Raising it delays the rear O2 sensor being treated as ready. LF76400Q: same code as LF75404S; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 05DB1C. Confidence: inferred.
