table.name: FLKC Range Boundary Load 1
table.description:
One of the four load boundaries that split fine learning knock correction (FLKC) into load ranges; each learning cell covers one rpm range by one load range. Moving it changes which conditions share a learned correction. Keep them in increasing order.
Details: Fine learning knock correction cells (0x0E1C58, read): the cell FFF8A790 = 5 x rpm range + load range (0...34). Seven rpm ranges are split at the six boundaries 0x1C24A...0x1C254 on FFF8CE9C, five load ranges at the four boundaries 0x1C240...0x1C246 on FFF8ADE4, each with a hysteresis band (0x1C256 rpm, 0x1C248 load). The learned value for the cell is FFF81414[cell] (s16, x 256); 0x0E73CC applies FFF8A7A7 = min(that, KCA Max x (16 - DAM) x 16) / 256, in 0.3516 degree counts; it is not added to the fired timing directly: like KCA it enters the timing request (0x0C13B4 -> FFF8AF22 -> 0x0C39DC / 0x0DD568), so fired base timing = min(Base Timing + comps, request + KCA + FLKC), and in limit states 0x0B/0x0C/0x19/0x1A/0x1B through the spark target FFF8A72A (0x0D9088). A negative learned value therefore retards the spark only where the request side is the lower one; where Base Timing is lower it is hidden until it pulls the request below Base Timing. Feedback knock correction is the only knock term added directly (0x0D9E40). load boundary. Confidence: inferred.

Subtracted per pass in state 6. p16 (read): the FBKC logic 0x0E2F94 (0x0E402C <- 0x07D0E0 <- 0x1E1CBC) is crank-synchronous: one pass per combustion event (180 deg CA, dispatched at tooth position 70 via the ATU-J0 software interrupt 0x0A7390), not per time. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: FLKC Counted-Cell Learned Value Threshold
table.description:
By DAM: a fine-knock-learning cell is counted when its learned value is at or above this, and the count sets an internal flag.
0x0E7DF8 (read): one cell per pass, it counts the FLKC cells whose flag FFF811AF[cell] is 1 and whose learned value FFF81414[cell] is at or above this(DAM FFF811AE); after all 35 cells the count goes to FFF8A792 and FFF8A7A3 bit 1 = count >= cal 0x1C699 (4). 0x0E7D0C (read) uses that bit only together with DAM inside cal 0x1C698..0x1C697 (32..48 in DAM x 16 units), which DAM (0..16) never reaches. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Secondary Knock Threshold (Event 1)
table.description:
Second knock detector level by rpm for event slot 1; a signal above it triggers the secondary knock retard steps. Unit: sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background (3.0 = all at background).
Details: Knock decision (0x0E8654 / 0x0E80B4, read): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4) the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot] (output of the signal processing 0x0E51E4) is compared with two thresholds. Knock B, FFF8A7B5 = intensity > Knock Threshold (this family, FFF8C1CC[slot] by 0x0E77E0) or FFF8CDC4[slot] >= cal 0x1BD92 (65535, off). Knock A, FFF8A7AD = intensity > Secondary Knock Threshold (FFF8C1D4[slot] by 0x0E78E4). Each event also sets bits of FFF8A79D (0x10/0x20/0x30/0x40 by slot). Slot vs cylinder number not mapped. 0x0E78E4 looks this 16-point curve up by FFF8CDC2 with the implicit-axis routine 0x7304 (0...240 in steps of 16 = 500...8,000 rpm, read). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 1, Channel 2)
table.description:
This software version (function 0x0EFD6C, read against the longer version of the function): the table is the step only on the pass where the window flag sets. On the pass where it clears, the longer version subtracts the table; this one adds the fixed value at cal 0x0310E2 instead (s16; the row for the event is Knock Background Clear Step (Event 1)).
Knock signal processing for event slot 1, channel 2 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock. Larger = that event less likely to count as knock. Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.
Details: When used: event slot FFF8CDC0 = 1 (Event 1), knock channel 2 of 8, on the knock window where FFF8A7C2 changes. Background step for this channel, added to (window extended) or subtracted from (window back to nominal) the channel background FFF8C180[1] for that one event; overlap-flag FFF8A7D2, gain curve cal 0x26F6F. Knock signal processing 0x0E51E4 (read; called once per knock window from 0x0E43B8 with load FFF8A616, after the event chain 0x0E433C): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4, the slot of the Knock Threshold tables) each of 8 knock channels i gets a reference ref_i = 32 x step_i + g x background_i, and the channel ratio is 256 x FFF8CDB0[i] / (ref_i / 32), i.e. measured / reference with 256 = equal (0x0E51E4 tail, read). Channels with their bit set in cal 0x1B97C..0x1B97F give 0; a channel flagged in FFF8CEED (driver flag, value at its lower limit, inferred) gives 256. The ratios are sorted and the largest min(cal 0x1B988, 5) = 3 are summed into the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot], which 0x0E80B4/0x0E8654 compare with Knock Threshold (read). The measured channels come from the knock sensor ADC: 0x1E7868 DMA-collects 32-sample blocks, 0x1E725A runs FFT-style butterflies, 0x1E73A4 takes sqrt(re^2+im^2) of 8 selected bins (pointer tables 0x34A88/0x34AA8), and 0x1E7724 sums them over the window into FFF8D1D4[8] -> FFF8CDB0[8] (read), so the 8 channels are 8 frequency bins of the knock sensor signal (inferred). background_i is the per-slot channel background FFF8C180.. (slot 1) / C190.. / C1A0.. / C1B0.. (slot 4), a lag filter of the measured channel kept by 0x0E4500 when the event is not knocking, floored at the per-channel rpm curve FFF8C0D8 (0x0E22A4) (read). step_i is this table family: it is non-zero only on the one event where the slot's window-length flag changes: +table when the flag goes 0 -> 1 (window switched to the extended length) and -table when it goes 1 -> 0 (back to the nominal length); on that event the reference is also floored at 32 x FFF8C0D8[i] (read). The flag is set when the extended knock window is used (0x0E20E0, read: B11A = nominal + Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 <= Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold and the extended window ends before the event angle). The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). Axes: rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500, 500-4000 rpm) x load FFF8A616 (read). Confidence: inferred.

The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). table.description:
Base ignition timing map for the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration) with the TGVs closed. It is only an upper limit: the ECU fires the lower of this map and Closed-Pedal Timing Target (plus its corrections).
Details: When used: Used while the accelerator is fully released (FFF8A774 bit 0: pedal-zero flag FFF88C64 bit 5 in engine state 2/3, vehicle speed FFF99835 at or below cal 0x2FDB2 = 200 km/h (inferred); 0x0E127C / 0x09FF9A, read), TGVs closed; enabled by cal 0x1071E bit 0, set in all four images. Base ignition timing. 0x0C2C08 uses this 16x16 table when cal 0x1071E bit 0 and FFF8A774 bit 0 are both set, and F2 set (F2 = FFF8A881 bit 4). The result is rate-limited (cals 0x1058C / 0x1058E) and the IAT compensation FFF8A782 and Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation FFF8A788 are added (0x0C2C08) to give base timing FFF8A645, which is only the upper limit of the fired timing: with the pedal released 0x0DD568 sets FFF8A76A = FFF8A645 - Torque Reduction Spark Retard(FFF8AF22 >> 7), where FFF8AF22 (0x0C13B4) is the efficiency of the closed-pedal timing request (Closed-Pedal Timing Target + FFF8A788 + FFF8A782 + Post-Start Closed-Pedal Timing Advance, 0x0E0A30) plus KCA + FLKC, so in effect FFF8A76A = min(FFF8A645, that request + KCA + FLKC) (read; min() form computed from the inverse tables). FFF8A76A then goes through 0x0DD760, 0x0DA600 and 0x0D9E40 to FFF8A744. The F2 selector is FFF8A881 bit 4, set by the TGV module 0x10CAE0 (0x10DEFC) - set = TGVs closed (see below). TGV polarity (read): 0x0D952C blends its Closed and Open ignition sets as Closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + Open x FFF8B3E8, so FFF8B3E8 is the TGV open fraction; 0x10C948 drives it toward 0 while FFF8A881 bit 4 is set, so that bit set = TGVs closed. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 05A034 by the code that reads it (read). LF9B003U: same code as LF9C000C; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 008580. Confidence: inferred.

table.description:
AT/CVT warm-up fallback copy of Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1).
Details: When used: FFF8A7E2 bit 0 clear, FFF899D7 bit 0 set. 0x108BAC (catalyst-heating module, read) writes FFF8A854, which 0x0C3200 selects as the spark target FFF8A647 in fuel mode FFF8A852 = 2 (combustion mode FFF8A85C 1 or 3, 0x108B08). A647 is the spark the torque model compensates for (0x0C2514, 0x0C1EA8) and the reference of the cold-start retard monitors (0x1CB70C, 0x132568: A72A - A854) (read); the fired spark in this mode follows FFF8A74C/FFF8A76B (0x0DA428), not A854 (read). In combustion mode 1 (A85C < 2), at <= 4000 rpm (cal 0x1CBD8), with the pedal released (FFF886AB bit 5) and speed below cal 0x2A0C1 (2 km/h): A854 = Base(rpm FFF8CD5C, coolant) + Torque Adder(FFF8A85E, coolant) + Run-Time Adder(passes since the engine state became running, coolant) + Re-Entry Adder(passes since mode 1 was re-entered from normal mode 4, coolant), saturated to a byte; the set is chosen by FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (set = the manual tables, clear = the "AT/CVT" tables; always set on the manual coding, Phase 14) and FFF899D7 bit 0 (set = the "Warm-Up Fallback" tables): a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch set by 0x081EFC only when cal 0x59134 bit 0 is set. Otherwise in mode 1 A854 = 05D0BC x 05D0A8 / 256 + FFF8A789 - 32; in mode 3 A854 = A72A (normal target) (read). with cal 0x2996C bit 6 set A854 is forced to cal 0x2A0C0. Units: A854 is compared with A72A and final timing in 0.5 degree units (inferred). LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 05D044 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). LF9B003U: same code as LF9C000C; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 00BE30. Confidence: inferred.

Rev Limit Full Cut RPM
table.description:
At or above this rpm, once the rev limit has started, every injector is cut on every firing (a hard fuel cut). Keep it equal to Rev Limit RPM; set higher, the range between them gets only the throttle cap, probably a softer limit.
Set rpm of the full-cut latch (part 2): at or above it, while state 0x0B is active, the torque cap is zero and all four injectors are cut every combustion event (part 3). On its own it does not start a cut; Rev Limit RPM does. Set above Rev Limit RPM, the range between them gets only the throttle cap (part 5; a soft stage, inferred). Rev limiter and limit-state cuts (LF75404S; read unless marked). The rev limiter is a fuel cut. (1) Limit state, 0x0BE140 (10 ms torque module 0x0BE694): the rev latch FFF8416A sets when rpm FFF8CD54 > Rev Limit RPM (the comparator FFF84169 then uses Rev Limit Reset RPM) and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Reset RPM and MAP FFF88FF4 < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. The overboost latch FFF84167 sets when MAP >= Overboost Limit (compensated, FFF8A851) + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) and releases below that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). Either latch gives limit state FFF8A639 = 0x0B. Priority: not running = 1, FFF8A640 bit 0 = 0x19, latch FFF8416C = 0x1B (cals 0x22FB2-0x22FBC, not decoded), then 0x0B, then the vehicle-speed latch = 0x0C (see Vehicle Speed Limit). (2) Full-cut latch, 0x0BAE98: FFF840C4 sets when rpm >= Rev Limit Full Cut RPM and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM and MAP < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. In state 0x0B the final torque cap FFF8AE54 (0x0B9DC8) is limited to FFF8AE8A: zero indicated torque (32000 - losses FFF8AF62) while this latch or the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) is set, otherwise FFF8AF3A = the current air torque minus losses, i.e. no reduction. (3) Fuel: 0x0C4BA0 turns the cap into the torque ratio FFF8A64F; in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C and 0x18-0x1B, 0x0C1AC8 turns the ratio into the number of cylinders to cut FFF8A643 (Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio thresholds; a zero cap gives 4). Once per combustion event (crank-synchronous list 0x07D0E0) 0x0C4B84 makes a cut decision FFF8A648 from the count and the last three decisions (4 = every event, 3 = three in four, 2 = every second, 1 = one in four; the pattern is in code, not a cal). 0x0C88C8 (list 0x07D1C2) latches it into the cut flag of the cylinder being scheduled (FFF8A6F5-FFF8A6F8). For a flagged cylinder the fuel time is 0 (0x0D1D7C/0x0D1FB8) and both start angles are 0x1FE (0x0CB394/0x0CB604), which the injector driver 0x1DCA04 treats as no pulse. So the cut is a true injector cut, all four cylinders, every event. (4) Spark is neither cut nor retarded: the coil scheduler 0x1DB804 only checks FFF8C6F4 (set at the first injection after sync, cleared only on stop), and with Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut set 0x0DD568 uses the normal spark target FFF8A72A in state 0x0B instead of Torque Reduction Spark Retard. (5) Throttle: with Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable set 0x0BDA84 caps the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C in state 0x0B by 0x0BAFA8: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Stage 1) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM (held while > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold)) or MAP FFF8AF70 > Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 MAP (held while > Stage 1 Reset MAP); else (Stage 2) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) (held while > Rev Limit RPM) or MAP > Stage 1 Reset MAP (held while > Stage 2 Hold MAP); else (Base). The torque monitor (0x186F0C) repeats this with the same data. A hard cut; stage 2 is never selected because its thresholds equal stage 1's. To move the limit, set Rev Limit RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 rpm lower. Setting the Full Cut pair above Rev Limit RPM gives a throttle-only soft stage between them (inferred). The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. Confidence: inferred.

Overboost Flag Reset Margin
table.description:
Once set, the overboost flag clears only when boost falls to Overboost Limit plus this.
Details: When used: always. 0x0C0FE0 (read): once set, the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) stays set until MAP FFF88FF4 <= Overboost Limit + this. The flag forces the zero torque cap in the overboost/rev cut state (0x0BAE98 -> FFF8AE8A, applied in limit state 0x0B; Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State)) and also feeds 0x1B8310 (0x1B828C / 0x1B83CC, the overboost diagnostic, inferred in my research notes), so this margin also sets how long that monitor sees overboost. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed
table.description:
Speed at which the active speed limiter cuts fuel to all cylinders; without it the limiter does nothing.
Details: When used: only in limit state 0x0C (vehicle-speed latch, see Vehicle Speed Limit). 0x0C058C (read): latch FFF84188 sets when vehicle speed FFF99835 >= this (minus Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed Hysteresis while above it) and holds until speed is below and MAP <= Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP; while set, FFF8AF1A = zero torque, which in state 0x0C cuts fuel on all four cylinders every event (0x0B9DC8, 0x0C1AC8). Without it state 0x0C reduces nothing. Confidence: inferred.

table.description:
Version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier A used while rpm is far below the idle target (later software versions).
Details: When used: Only while the below-idle latch (in later software versions) is set: rpm - idle target <= cal 0x11AF4 (with hysteresis). LF9C000C: a table LF75404S does not have; scaling and axes as Torque Model Filter Multiplier A. LF9B003U: same code as LF9C000C; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0083E0. Confidence: read.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (TGV Closed)
table.description:
Version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier A used while the TGVs are closed.
Details: 0x0C1EA8 (read): AF4E multiplies the rpm-based filter coefficient AFAC (0x0C38E0) in 0x0C2514 (AF58), 0x0C1854 (predicted air torque AF40) and 0x0C39DC (AF3E): k = AF4E x AFAC/512. 512 = 1.0; values that push k past 65535 mean no lag. Selected in state S2: after combustion-mode change 1 -> 3, while spark target - final timing > 4 deg (7 deg with A7E2 bit 0) and FFF886AB bit 5. TGV closed (A881 bit 4), A7E2 bit 0 clear. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 059ED0 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). LF9B003U: same code as LF9C000C; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0083B0. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (No Enrichment)
table.description:
Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map A is the fast-reacting part, by rpm and load, used while no open loop enrichment is active. Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it.
Details: When used: always while running. Map A while no open-loop enrichment is active. 0x0C9878 (read): with no open-loop enrichment (FFF8A684 = 0) S = Map A (No Enrichment) x Retard Multiplier A (No Enrichment)/256 and U = Map B (No Enrichment) x Retard Multiplier B (No Enrichment)/256; with enrichment the (Enriched) tables are used; with FFF8A8A5 bit 4 set (flag from 0x11B2A4 on vehicle speed, pedal and load; not decoded) the (FFF8A8A5 Bit 4) tables. Maps are rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8A616. FFF8C562 = S filtered (weight 05A578 while FFF8AFCC is rising, 05A5A0 while falling, by rpm x load); FFF8C564 = (U - S + fuel-cut term FFF8B040) filtered (weights 05A680 / 05A6A8 by air quantity FFF8B4D6 x FFF8B066); estimate FFF8AFD0 = FFF8C562 + FFF8C564, so in steady state FFF8AFD0 tends to Map B. 0x0CE854 enables Primary Open Loop Fueling while FFF8AFD0 >= cal 0x18DD4 (39322, hysteresis cal 0x18DD6 = 2185), and 0x0C5880 integrates 05A82C(FFF8AFD0) into FFF8C03C, the second enable path (read). Reading FFF8AFD0 as an exhaust/catalyst temperature estimate is inferred: the enriched maps are lower than the stoichiometric ones, retard raises the value (multiplier 0.75 at 25 degrees advanced to 1.2 at 20 degrees retarded) and the value gates the enrichment. Raising these maps brings Primary Open Loop Fueling in earlier (lower load); lowering them delays it. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 05A564 by the code that reads it (read). LF9B003U: same code as LF9C000C; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 008D58. Confidence: inferred.

table.description:
Later-software version of A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor: on a hot restart the exhaust model starts from the stored pipe temperature times this factor, by stored temperature and coolant drop. Normally leave alone.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 1A (TGV Open, Normal, Altitude)
Intake Cam Target 1B (TGV Open, Normal, Sea Level)
table.description:
Main intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load for normal driving with the TGVs open near sea level: above light part throttle, above about 5200 rpm, or cold. Higher = earlier intake timing. At light part throttle the TGVs close and Intake Cam Target 3B is used instead. Normal vs high-pedal split is inferred.
Details: Convention (read, see FU_UNITS): crank degrees of intake cam ADVANCE from its learned rest position; 0 = rest (fully retarded, inferred), larger = more advance (earlier valve events). Values below 0 ask for less than the rest position: the OCV then sits at minimum duty and the cam stays at rest (inferred). AVCS target (intake 0x15C250, exhaust 0x16032C, read): target = coolant terms + v x [S_A x w + S_B x (1 - w)] + (1 - v) x [3A x w + (3B + Coolant Offset 3B x Coolant Factor 3 / 128) x (1 - w)], clamped to +/-90 degrees, 364.09 counts per degree. v = FFF8B3E8, the TGV open fraction: sets 1/2 apply with TGVs open, set 3 with TGVs closed. w = FFF8B948 = AVCS Barometric Blend (barometric pressure FFF88668, via 0x15B1E0, read): the A tables apply at altitude, the B tables at sea level. S = set 1 or set 2, chosen by FFF8A8A4 bit 7 (stack argument +24 from 0x15969C, read). That bit is a high-pedal latch (0x11C15C / 0x10F848, read): it sets when the accelerator FFF88A5E is at or above High Pedal Entry Threshold while vehicle speed is not jumping (under cal 0x35B16... per gear) and some status flags (FFF88A2D bit 0, FFF88ADA bit 6, FFF8A8A2 bit 6) are clear, or when FFF8A8A5 bit 2 or 4 is set; it clears once the pedal is below cal 0x36518 (85 %). So set 1 = normal driving and set 2 = near wide-open pedal (meaning inferred from these conditions). Exhaust set 2 differs mainly below 1.03 g/rev. The altitude (A) sets differ only below 0.52 g/rev. The set-3 terms are active because cal 0x3ACF6 = 1 in both images. Set 1, B table (weight 1 - w). This is the sea-level target while the TGVs are open (above the TGV torque / air-quantity thresholds, above 5200 rpm, or cold); at light part throttle the TGVs are closed and Intake Cam Target 3B is used. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 05E4A8 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). LF9B003U: same code as LF9C000C; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 00D428. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts the main intake air temperature sensor voltage to degrees; this IAT feeds the timing, boost and fuel compensations and the scan-tool reading. Its voltage axis is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling, so edit only the temperatures when fitting a different sensor.

This is IAT sensor 1 (P0112 / P0113, read), probably the element in the MAF housing (inferred). The voltage axis (0x579FC, 32 points 0...4.96 V in 0.16 V steps; 65536 = 5 V inferred) is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling: change only the temperature values for a different thermistor, or both sensors move. While the sensor is faulted (FFF88E28 bit 2) the fixed voltage cal 0x579BA x 256 is used. Descriptor boot 0633E4. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling
table.description:
Converts the second intake temperature sensor's voltage to degrees. This is the air temperature the ECU's airflow model uses to work out air density, and it probably comes from the manifold pressure (TMAP) sensor, so update it when you swap that sensor for one with a different thermistor. Its voltage axis is shared with the main IAT table; change only the temperatures.

ADC channel 20 (0xFFFFE868, untrimmed) -> FFF88D40 -> FFF88F36, filtered by cal 0x579B8 -> FFF88F38 / FFF88F3A, looked up here (boot lookup 0x7250) into FFF888CF (degC + 50; FFF888D4 from the unfaulted value). This is IAT sensor 2 (P0097 / P0098 monitors on the same voltage, read). FFF888CF is the air temperature of the speed-density airflow model (0x11DF4C: density from MAP and IAT 2 + 223 K) and is also read by requested torque 0x0BE694, ignition 0x0D98F8 / 0x0D9A10 / 0x0DE0E0 and AVCS 0x15969C (read), so a wrong curve shifts the modelled air and load. The voltage axis (0x579FC) is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor Scaling, so change only the data. While faulted (FFF88FCD bit 2) the fixed voltage cal 0x579BB x 256 is used. Descriptor boot 0633F0. Confidence: read.

table.name: Coolant Temp Sensor Scaling

table.name: Fuel Level Sensor Scaling

table.name: Rear O2 Sensor Ready Heater Energy Threshold

Descriptor boot 063610. Confidence: read.

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 1, Channel 2)
table.description:
This software version (function 0x0EFE94, read against the longer version of the function): the table is the step only on the pass where the window flag sets. On the pass where it clears, the longer version subtracts the table; this one adds the fixed value at cal 0x0310E2 instead (s16; the row for the event is Knock Background Clear Step (Event 1)).
Knock signal processing for event slot 1, channel 2 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock. Larger = that event less likely to count as knock. Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.
Details: When used: event slot FFF8CDC0 = 1 (Event 1), knock channel 2 of 8, on the knock window where FFF8A7C2 changes. Background step for this channel, added to (window extended) or subtracted from (window back to nominal) the channel background FFF8C180[1] for that one event; overlap-flag FFF8A7D2, gain curve cal 0x26F6F. Knock signal processing 0x0E51E4 (read; called once per knock window from 0x0E43B8 with load FFF8A616, after the event chain 0x0E433C): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4, the slot of the Knock Threshold tables) each of 8 knock channels i gets a reference ref_i = 32 x step_i + g x background_i, and the channel ratio is 256 x FFF8CDB0[i] / (ref_i / 32), i.e. measured / reference with 256 = equal (0x0E51E4 tail, read). Channels with their bit set in cal 0x1B97C..0x1B97F give 0; a channel flagged in FFF8CEED (driver flag, value at its lower limit, inferred) gives 256. The ratios are sorted and the largest min(cal 0x1B988, 5) = 3 are summed into the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot], which 0x0E80B4/0x0E8654 compare with Knock Threshold (read). The measured channels come from the knock sensor ADC: 0x1E7868 DMA-collects 32-sample blocks, 0x1E725A runs FFT-style butterflies, 0x1E73A4 takes sqrt(re^2+im^2) of 8 selected bins (pointer tables 0x34A88/0x34AA8), and 0x1E7724 sums them over the window into FFF8D1D4[8] -> FFF8CDB0[8] (read), so the 8 channels are 8 frequency bins of the knock sensor signal (inferred). background_i is the per-slot channel background FFF8C180.. (slot 1) / C190.. / C1A0.. / C1B0.. (slot 4), a lag filter of the measured channel kept by 0x0E4500 when the event is not knocking, floored at the per-channel rpm curve FFF8C0D8 (0x0E22A4) (read). step_i is this table family: it is non-zero only on the one event where the slot's window-length flag changes: +table when the flag goes 0 -> 1 (window switched to the extended length) and -table when it goes 1 -> 0 (back to the nominal length); on that event the reference is also floored at 32 x FFF8C0D8[i] (read). The flag is set when the extended knock window is used (0x0E20E0, read: B11A = nominal + Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 <= Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold and the extended window ends before the event angle). The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). Axes: rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500, 500-4000 rpm) x load FFF8A616 (read). Confidence: inferred.

On the pass where it clears, the longer version subtracts the table; this one adds the fixed value at cal 0x031108 instead (s16; the row for the event is Knock Background Clear Step (Event 3)).
Knock signal processing for event slot 3, channel 5 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.
Details: When used: event slot FFF8CDC0 = 3 (Event 3), knock channel 5 of 8, on the knock window where FFF8A7C4 changes. Background step for this channel, added to (window extended) or subtracted from (window back to nominal) the channel background FFF8C1A0[4] for that one event; overlap-flag FFF8A7D4, gain curve cal 0x26F8F. Knock signal processing 0x0E51E4 (read; called once per knock window from 0x0E43B8 with load FFF8A616, after the event chain 0x0E433C): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4, the slot of the Knock Threshold tables) each of 8 knock channels i gets a reference ref_i = 32 x step_i + g x background_i, and the channel ratio is 256 x FFF8CDB0[i] / (ref_i / 32), i.e. measured / reference with 256 = equal (0x0E51E4 tail, read). Channels with their bit set in cal 0x1B97C..0x1B97F give 0; a channel flagged in FFF8CEED (driver flag, value at its lower limit, inferred) gives 256. The ratios are sorted and the largest min(cal 0x1B988, 5) = 3 are summed into the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot], which 0x0E80B4/0x0E8654 compare with Knock Threshold (read). The measured channels come from the knock sensor ADC: 0x1E7868 DMA-collects 32-sample blocks, 0x1E725A runs FFT-style butterflies, 0x1E73A4 takes sqrt(re^2+im^2) of 8 selected bins (pointer tables 0x34A88/0x34AA8), and 0x1E7724 sums them over the window into FFF8D1D4[8] -> FFF8CDB0[8] (read), so the 8 channels are 8 frequency bins of the knock sensor signal (inferred). background_i is the per-slot channel background FFF8C180.. (slot 1) / C190.. / C1A0.. / C1B0.. (slot 4), a lag filter of the measured channel kept by 0x0E4500 when the event is not knocking, floored at the per-channel rpm curve FFF8C0D8 (0x0E22A4) (read). step_i is this table family: it is non-zero only on the one event where the slot's window-length flag changes: +table when the flag goes 0 -> 1 (window switched to the extended length) and -table when it goes 1 -> 0 (back to the nominal length); on that event the reference is also floored at 32 x FFF8C0D8[i] (read). The flag is set when the extended knock window is used (0x0E20E0, read: B11A = nominal + Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 <= Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold and the extended window ends before the event angle). The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). Axes: rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500, 500-4000 rpm) x load FFF8A616 (read). Confidence: inferred.

On the pass where it clears, the longer version subtracts the table; this one adds the fixed value at cal 0x0310E0 instead (s16; the row for the event is Knock Background Clear Step (Event 1)).
Knock-detection background step for event slot 1, frequency channel 1.
Details: event slot FFF8CDC0 = 1 (Event 1), knock channel 1 of 8 (index 0 of FFF8CDB0), which is masked: bit 0 of cal 0x1B97C is set (0xC1 = channels 1, 7 and 8 off for every slot). 0x0E51E4 (read) then writes a fixed ratio for the channel instead of 256 x measured/reference, and the reference ref_0 (the only place this step enters, statics FFF84AB4..FFF84AD0 read only by 0x0E51E4, ram_xref) is not used; the reference copies FFF8C130.. have no reader. So editing it has no effect unless that cal bit is cleared, which would make the channel count (then this would be the background step for FFF8C180[0] when FFF8A7C2 changes; overlap flag FFF8A7D2, gain curve cal 0x26F6F). Knock signal processing 0x0E51E4 (read; called once per knock window from 0x0E43B8 with load FFF8A616, after the event chain 0x0E433C): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4, the slot of the Knock Threshold tables) each of 8 knock channels i gets a reference ref_i = 32 x step_i + g x background_i, and the channel ratio is 256 x FFF8CDB0[i] / (ref_i / 32), i.e. measured / reference with 256 = equal (0x0E51E4 tail, read). Channels with their bit set in cal 0x1B97C..0x1B97F give 0; a channel flagged in FFF8CEED (driver flag, value at its lower limit, inferred) gives 256. The ratios are sorted and the largest min(cal 0x1B988, 5) = 3 are summed into the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot], which 0x0E80B4/0x0E8654 compare with Knock Threshold (read). The measured channels come from the knock sensor ADC: 0x1E7868 DMA-collects 32-sample blocks, 0x1E725A runs FFT-style butterflies, 0x1E73A4 takes sqrt(re^2+im^2) of 8 selected bins (pointer tables 0x34A88/0x34AA8), and 0x1E7724 sums them over the window into FFF8D1D4[8] -> FFF8CDB0[8] (read), so the 8 channels are 8 frequency bins of the knock sensor signal (inferred). background_i is the per-slot channel background FFF8C180.. (slot 1) / C190.. / C1A0.. / C1B0.. (slot 4), a lag filter of the measured channel kept by 0x0E4500 when the event is not knocking, floored at the per-channel rpm curve FFF8C0D8 (0x0E22A4) (read). step_i is this table family: it is non-zero only on the one event where the slot's window-length flag changes: +table when the flag goes 0 -> 1 (window switched to the extended length) and -table when it goes 1 -> 0 (back to the nominal length); on that event the reference is also floored at 32 x FFF8C0D8[i] (read). The flag is set when the extended knock window is used (0x0E20E0, read: B11A = nominal + Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 <= Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold and the extended window ends before the event angle). The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). Axes: rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500, 500-4000 rpm) x load FFF8A616 (read). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Injector 2/4 Rail Pressure Offset
table.description:
Pressure offset added to measured rail pressure before looking up Injector Flow Compensation (Injectors 2/4), by rpm and load; probably the pressure difference of the rail without the sensor.
Details: 0x06D43A (read): FFF89222 = sat(rail pressure FFF88886 + this(rpm FFF8CE9C, load FFF8A616)), interpolated by 0x00671C (descriptor 0x0608E4: data, u16 axis, u8 axis, 16, 16; row = rpm, read). FFF89222 indexes the injector flow compensation 05A844 used only for injectors 2 and 4 (0x0CB0C8, read); injectors 1 and 3 use 05A838 with FFF88886. Likely the pressure difference of the rail without the sensor (inferred from the boxer layout). Signed, in the rail-pressure unit. Descriptor boot 0656F8. Confidence: inferred.

Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied)
Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, AT/CVT Coding)

AT/CVT version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1). Only used with the automatic/CVT transmission coding; no effect on a manual car.

Details: 0x165180 (read): fixed target in combustion mode FFF8A85C = 2 (stratified catalyst heating). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Rail Pressure Fail-Safe Target A
table.description:

table.name: Rail Pressure Fail-Safe Target B
table.description:
Second fail-safe rail pressure target; the lower of A and B is used when both apply. Nothing that activates it was found, so it probably never applies.
Details: 0x165180 (read): target while FFF88F4A bit 2 is set. No setter of that bit was found in either image. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Fallback)
table.description:
Rail pressure target in combustion mode 1 after a warm-up fallback has latched.
Details: When used: Used only while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set, a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch (0x081EFC) gated by cal 0x59134 bit 0. 0x165180 (read): target in combustion mode FFF8A85C = 1 while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set (else Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1)); coolant FFF88A44. LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05EB84 by the code that reads it (read). LF9D000d: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 00DF30. Confidence: read.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Fallback, AT/CVT Coding)

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling
table.description:
Base open-loop (power enrichment) AFR target by rpm and load, used once the exhaust temperature estimate is high enough. The ECU uses the richer of this and the Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV..., AVCS...) group: to lean, edit both; to richen, either. Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor (Outside Closed Loop).
Details: Note: the ECU has a second open-loop fuel path: the four "Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV..., AVCS...)" tables 05ABB0..05ABEC, blended by TGV and AVCS (0x0CE5E8 -> FFF8A681); 0x0CEA80 takes the richer of the two (max). To lean the open-loop target edit both sets; richening works with either (read, my research notes). Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor. Base open-loop enrichment target, 0x0CE854. Used only while the exhaust temperature estimate FFF8AFD0 (see Exhaust Temperature Model Map A/B) is >= cal 0x18DD4 (39322, hysteresis cal 0x18DD6 = 2185), or its integral FFF8C03C >= cal 0x18DD8 (65535); otherwise this path contributes 0 (read). While cal 0x2F79A bit 4 is clear, the additive term (Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive x DAM multiplier) is added, minus Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive x Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier(DAM)/128. The result is rate-limited (FFF84424) into FFF8A682, and FFF8A684 = max(FFF8A682, other enrichments) feeds commanded lambda. LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05AC6C by the code that reads it (read). LF9D000d: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 00985C. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Closed, AVCS Inactive)
table.description:

Details: When used: TGVs forced closed (FFF8A881 bit 4 set). 0x0FFA0C (read): FFF8B326 = 32768 + (this - 32768) x (05CDF0/05CE04(rpm, load) / 2979) x (05CE18/05CE24(FFF8AF12) / 255); B326 - 32768 is added to the closed-loop target (0x0FF468, see Closed Loop Target). Axes: coolant at start FFF89224 x accumulated air since start FFF81818 (0x10A270). LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05CDDC by the code that reads it (read). LF9D000d: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 00BE38. Confidence: read.

table.name: Closed Loop Target (Catalyst Monitor Active)
table.description:
Closed-loop target used instead of the four Closed Loop Target tables while the P0420 catalyst monitor test runs; not limited or trimmed by the other target tables.
Details: When used: while FFF8AA60 bit 3 is set: the P0420 catalyst monitor test is running (set by 0x135D18 inside 0x134374, read; needs closed loop, speed >= 40 km/h, an airflow window). 0x0FF468 (read): used instead of the four Closed Loop Target tables, and its value goes straight to FFF8B30A, without the lean limit, Low-DAM Enrichment or cold-start trim. Axes rpm (FFF8CD56) x load % (FFF8A616). LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 05CD38 by the code that reads it (read). LF9D000d: same code as LF9C000C; address from the same instruction (between exact neighbours (100 bytes below, 20 above, both moved by the same amount; inferred)). Descriptor 00BD94. Confidence: inferred.

LTFT RPM Range Boundary
table.description:
Engine speed that splits the long-term fuel trim cells into a low-rpm and a high-rpm set.
Details: Long-term fuel trim (0x0C589C -> 0x0CECA8 and 0x0FD76C -> 0x0FD3E4, read). The trim used in the fuel quantity, FFF8A689 (OBD PID 0x07, 128 = 0 %), is FFF811D9 (backup RAM), capped at cal 0x384D6 only when coolant FFF8CD65 is below cal 0x384D7. 0x0FD3E4 builds FFF811D9 from ten learned cells FFF81466[0..9] (backup RAM, cleared to 0 by 0x0FC054): cell = load range (FFF8A616 against the four LTFT Load Range Boundaries, 1-5) + 5 if engine speed FFF8CE9C >= LTFT RPM Range Boundary; FFF8A823 = cell. The cell value is filtered (cal 0x4B16C) into FFF8C53C and then scaled by coolant: FFF811D9 = 128 + (FFF8C53C - 128) x LTFT Coolant Scaling (Positive or Negative)(coolant FFF88A44) / 128. How the cells themselves are learned (0x0FCAF0 / 0x0FC400 / 0x0FC5C0, from the closed-loop integrators FFF8B2B0/B2FA) is not decoded. Cells 6-10 are used at or above this engine speed. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: LTFT Floor (Restricted)

Details: Long-term fuel trim (0x0C589C -> 0x0CECA8 and 0x0FD76C -> 0x0FD3E4, read). The trim used in the fuel quantity, FFF8A689 (OBD PID 0x07, 128 = 0 %, one count = 0.39 % of fuel: 0x171978 reports A689 >> 1 + 64 and 0x0D15EC applies (A689 + 128)/256, read), is FFF811D9 (backup RAM), capped at cal 0x384D6 only when coolant FFF8CD65 is below cal 0x384D7. 0x0FD3E4 builds FFF811D9 from ten learned cells FFF81466[0..9] (backup RAM, cleared to 0 by 0x0FC054): cell = load range (FFF8A616 against the four LTFT Load Range Boundaries, 1-5) + 5 if engine speed FFF8CE9C >= LTFT RPM Range Boundary; FFF8A823 = cell. The cell value is filtered (cal 0x4B16C) into FFF8C53C and then scaled by coolant: FFF811D9 = 128 + (FFF8C53C - 128) x LTFT Coolant Scaling (Positive or Negative)(coolant FFF88A44) / 128. How the cells themselves are learned (0x0FCAF0 / 0x0FC400 / 0x0FC5C0, from the closed-loop integrators FFF8B2B0/B2FA) is not decoded. table.description:
Start-path after-start enrichment by coolant, faded to zero by its decay table; the largest of the three after-start terms is used, scaled by After-Start Enrichment RPM Multiplier. Used with the TGVs open.
Details: Enrichment amount FFF843EA (0x0CD834, read); this TGV Open table is used when TGV state flag FFF8A881 bit 4 (passed in by 0x0C73D0, read) is clear. Faded to zero by After-Start Enrichment Decay 1 (TGV Open), the three faded terms' maximum is scaled by the RPM multiplier into FFF8B012/B016/B01A/B01E (read), and FFF8B012 adds to the start-path fuel factor (B012 + A828 + B02C)/256 + 0.5 (0x0D1400, read). Coolant axis is the value latched at start (FFF843F4) or the current one (read). Unit 1/256 of base fuel (inferred). TGV polarity (read): 0x0D952C blends its Closed and Open ignition sets as Closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + Open x FFF8B3E8, so FFF8B3E8 is the TGV open fraction; 0x10C948 drives it toward 0 while FFF8A881 bit 4 is set, so that bit set = TGVs closed. LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05A958 by the code that reads it (read). LF9D000d: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 009368. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Closed, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description:
AT/CVT version of Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Closed). Only used with the automatic/CVT transmission coding; no effect on a manual car.
Details: When used: Only with the automatic/CVT transmission coding (Cal Switches: Transmission Coding: Automatic/CVT); unused on a manual car (read). LF9F000R: a table LF75404S does not have; scaling and axes as Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Closed). LF9D000d: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 009E6C. Confidence: read.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base (TGV Normal)
Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base (TGV Closed)
table.description:
First-pulse (intake stroke) injection angle in catalyst-heating phase 2 and the start sequence, by rpm and coolant, limited to 180.5-360 BTDC. Used when the TGVs are closed.
Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the injected cylinder's compression TDC (0 = firing TDC, 180 = intake BDC (start of compression), 360 = gas-exchange TDC, 540 = expansion BDC); larger = earlier. Same scale as every Injection Timing table. First pulse of the phase 2 split; clamped to 180.5-360 BTDC (code 720-1079, 0x0D00A8, read), i.e. the intake stroke. When used: while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs forced closed) is set, with 05B07C/05B0A4/05B0F4 in place of the other terms. 0x0D00A8 (called from 0x0C589C, args read): in fuel state FFF8906B 2/3, FFF8B05E = this(rpm FFF8CD54, coolant FFF88A44) + 05B068(rpm, load) x 05B090(FFF88A9D, IAT)/255 + 05B0E0(spark FFF8A76B, coolant), clamped 720..1079; under FFF88E28 bit 2 or FFF88E2B bit 5 only the TGV Normal base 05B0B8 is used (this table is skipped even with the TGVs forced closed); cal 0x38448 bit 5 (clear) would force cal 0x1208A. 0x0CB394 uses FFF8B05E - 720 as the injection angle of cylinders in injector mode 2 (fuel mode 2 = combustion modes 1 and 3, the catalyst-heating phase 2 / start sequence) (read). Axes 850-1600 rpm x coolant. LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05B0CC by the code that reads it (read). LF9D000d: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 009DE0. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base Adder (TGV Normal)
Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base Adder (TGV Closed)
table.description:
Rpm x load correction to the phase 2 first-pulse angle with the TGVs closed; positive = later.
Details: When used: catalyst-heating phase 2 first pulse while the TGVs are closed (FFF8A881 bit 4 set); then it replaces the TGV Normal adder and 05B0A4 replaces the multiplier (0x0D00A8, read). 0x0D00A8 (called from 0x0C589C with (906B, cal 0x38448 bit 5, rpm FFF8CD54, load FFF8A616, FFF88E28 bit 2, FFF88E2B bit 5, FFF88A9D, IAT FFF88662, coolant FFF88A44, spark target FFF8A76B, TGV closed FFF8A881 bit 4, &FFF8B05E), read): in fuel states 2/3 FFF8B05E = Base(rpm, coolant) + Base Adder(rpm, load) x multiplier(FFF88A9D, IAT)/255 + Base Spark Adder(spark, coolant), clamped to code 720-1079 (180.5-360 BTDC); with FFF88E28 bit 2 or FFF88E2B bit 5 set only the Base is used (read). Units (FU_UNITS): added to the code angle, so a positive value moves the pulse LATER (fewer degrees BTDC), x/2 degrees (fu_units_inj_delta_later). LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05B07C by the code that reads it (read). LF9D000d: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 009D90. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base Spark Adder (TGV Normal)
Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base Spark Adder (TGV Closed)
table.description:
Correction by spark target and coolant to the phase 2 first-pulse angle, TGVs closed; positive = later.
Details: When used: as the TGV Normal spark adder, while the TGVs are closed (FFF8A881 bit 4) (0x0D00A8, read). 0x0D00A8 (called from 0x0C589C with (906B, cal 0x38448 bit 5, rpm FFF8CD54, load FFF8A616, FFF88E28 bit 2, FFF88E2B bit 5, FFF88A9D, IAT FFF88662, coolant FFF88A44, spark target FFF8A76B, TGV closed FFF8A881 bit 4, &FFF8B05E), read): in fuel states 2/3 FFF8B05E = Base(rpm, coolant) + Base Adder(rpm, load) x multiplier(FFF88A9D, IAT)/255 + Base Spark Adder(spark, coolant), clamped to code 720-1079 (180.5-360 BTDC); with FFF88E28 bit 2 or FFF88E2B bit 5 set only the Base is used (read). Units (FU_UNITS): added to the code angle, so a positive value moves the pulse LATER (fewer degrees BTDC), x/2 degrees (fu_units_inj_delta_later). LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05B0F4 by the code that reads it (read). LF9D000d: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 009E08. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Adder (TGV Normal)
Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Adder (TGV Closed)
table.description:
Correction to the phase 2 second-pulse angle with the TGVs closed; positive = later.
Details: When used: catalyst-heating phase 2 second pulse while the TGVs are closed (FFF8A881 bit 4); scaled by 05B16C/255. 0x0D023C (called from 0x0C589C with (906B, spark target FFF8A76B, rpm/50 FFF8CD56, cal 0x38448 bit 4, FFF88E28 bit 2, FFF88E2B bit 5, FFF88A9D, IAT FFF88662, rpm FFF8CD54, TGV closed FFF8A881 bit 4, &FFF8B060, &FFF8B00A), read): unless rpm > cal 0x1CBD8 (20480 = 4000 rpm), FFF8B060 = Phase 2 Injection Angle(rpm/50, spark) + this adder(rpm/50, spark) x multiplier(FFF88A9D, IAT)/255 (adder skipped while FFF88E28 bit 2 or FFF88E2B bit 5), clamped to code 1080-1439 (180-0.5 BTDC) in fuel states 2/3 (read). FFF8B060 is the second-pulse angle in fuel mode 2 (0x0CB604, segment 3, read). Units (FU_UNITS): added to the code angle, so a positive value moves the pulse LATER (fewer degrees BTDC), x/2 degrees (fu_units_inj_delta_later). LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05B11C by the code that reads it (read). LF9D000d: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 009E30. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Start Split Injection Second Share (Idle, Alternate)
table.description:
Share of fuel moved into the second (compression-stroke) pulse during the start / catalyst-heating phase 2, by rpm and coolant (0 = single injection).
Details: When used: fuel mode 2, pedal released and stopped, FFF899D7 bit 0 set. 0x10A604 (read) writes FFF8A85F = this at <= 4000 rpm (cal 0x1CBD8); 0 when FFF8A657 bit 7 or FFF8A857 bit 7, cal 0x2A340 (51) if cal 0x2996C bit 4 (clear). 0x0D0A7C-0x0D0C14 copy A85F into the per-injector split FFF8A6D6...A6D9 when that injector's fuel mode FFF8A858...A85B is 2 (combustion modes 1 and 3, 0x108B08) (read); the second pulse gets A6D6/256 of the quantity (0x0D1FB8) at the Catalyst Heating Phase 2 injection angle B060, and A6D6 = 0 means no second pulse (my research notes) (read). Selection: pedal released (FFF886AB bit 5) and speed below cal 0x2A389 (2 km/h) -> 05D1A0 (05D1C8 if FFF899D7 bit 0), otherwise 05D1B4 (read). The same data blocks are also read by 0x10BF88 through descriptors 05D224 / 05D238 / 05D24C, so one entry covers both. LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05D1C8 by the code that reads it (read). LF9D000d: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 00C25C. Confidence: read.

Purge Valve Duty
table.description:
Purge valve duty needed for a target purge flow at a given manifold vacuum; higher vacuum needs less duty. Applied above Purge Valve Minimum Duty. Change only for a different purge valve.
Details: When used: every 80 ms pass (0x0D60FC, read): A70A = this(target purge flow FFF8B0C0, manifold vacuum FFF8CDFA). The final duty is A713 + (100 % - A713) x this, with A713 = Purge Valve Minimum Duty (0x0D6118, read), and 0 when this is 0. B0C0 = purge rate x air quantity FFF8B4D6 / 256, in the air-quantity unit (read). Higher vacuum needs less duty for the same flow. Purge module (inferred: canister purge): 0x0D4E78 (80 ms task 0x1E1560) and 0x0D4C14 (20 ms task 0x1E0AE8) (read). Chain (read): purge rate A70C (limits A6FD/A70F, ramp A709, cut B0A0) -> purge flow B0C0 = A70C x air FFF8B4D6/256 -> valve duty A70A = 05B314(B0C0, vacuum) -> A70B with minimum duty A713 -> A707 -> timer E channel 22 (0x1D98D6); A707 is also checked by the circuit monitor 0x072090 (driver status FFF88BF4 bits 10/11). Fuel: A71A = filtered purge rate x learned concentration FFF81412 (0x0D688C) is subtracted from the fuel factor (0x0D15EC). LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05B314 by the code that reads it (read). LF9D000d: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 00A068. Confidence: read.

FBKC Retard Step (Knock, State 0x0E)
table.description:
Timing pulled by feedback knock correction for each knock event detected above Knock Threshold, in the main knock case. Applied once per combustion event, to all cylinders (there is no per-cylinder knock retard).
Details: Feedback knock correction (0x0E2BE4, read): FFF8A79A is an s8 integrator kept at or below 0 and added directly to the fired timing (x 0.3516 degrees, 0x0D9E40): it is the only knock term of that sum, and FFF8A79A is one value for the whole engine, so a knock event on any cylinder retards all four (the fired timing FFF8A744 is recomputed per event for the next cylinder, but no per-cylinder knock retard exists; read). The state FFF8A79C (set once per combustion event by 0x0E2F94 from that event's knock results FFF8A7AD / FFF8A7B5; FFF8A7C1 is the knock-window-length flag (1 = extended window), used there only to reload per-cylinder hold counters FFF84920...FFF84930 from cal 0x27014 when it changes, purpose inferred) picks the action: states 0x0E, 0x0D, 7 and 6 subtract a step (floor = minus FBKC Maximum Retard); states 0x0C, 2, 0 (outside the rpm window) and the other non-knock states (0x0A outside the window, 0x0B) add the recovery step 0x1C271; 0x10 (inside the rpm window, no knock, fewer than cal 0x1C288 = 100 events since the last knock) holds the correction unchanged; 0x0F (inside the window, no knock, >= 100 events) adds 0x1C270, 8/9 add 0x1C272 (capped at 0); 5 = FFF8A79B x 0x1C26E / 128; 3 and 4 load the fixed values 0x1C26F / 0x1C278; 1 = 0. States (0x0E2F94, read, in priority order): 1 = knock control off (cal 0x56EE7 bit 7); 2 = FFF886AB bit 5 or load FFF8ADE4 <= cal 0x1C27E (0); 3 / 4 = FFF88E29 bit 3 / FFF88E2A bit 6 (fixed -14 counts = -4.9 degrees, inferred knock-sensor fault default); 5 = engine speed above FBKC Window RPM Maximum (hold); inside the rpm window: 6 / 0x0D = knock A with / without FFF8AA85 bit 0, 7 / 0x0E = knock B (FFF8A7B5, intensity > Knock Threshold, the active one); 0x0F = no knock and FFF8B130 (events since the last knock, 0x0E7C7C) >= cal 0x1C288 (100), 0x10 = no knock, fewer events; 8 / 9 hold; 0x0A / 0x0B / 0x0C other conditions (0x0B: A/F FFF88AF6 above a lambda threshold). Subtracted per pass in state 0x0E. p16 (read): the FBKC logic 0x0E2F94 (0x0E402C <- 0x07D0E0 <- 0x1E1CBC) is crank-synchronous: one pass per combustion event (180 deg CA, dispatched at tooth position 70 via the ATU-J0 software interrupt 0x0A7390), not per time. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: FBKC Recovery Step
table.description:
Timing given back by feedback knock correction per combustion event in the non-knock states other than normal knock-free running: when rpm is outside the FBKC window (for example below FBKC Window RPM Minimum), in the closed-pedal / low-load state, and in a few other special states. Inside the window, after knock stops the correction is held for 100 knock-free events and then recovered by FBKC Recovery Step (State 0x0F), not by this value.
Details: Feedback knock correction (0x0E2BE4, read): FFF8A79A is an s8 integrator kept at or below 0 and added directly to the fired timing (x 0.3516 degrees, 0x0D9E40): it is the only knock term of that sum, and FFF8A79A is one value for the whole engine, so a knock event on any cylinder retards all four (the fired timing FFF8A744 is recomputed per event for the next cylinder, but no per-cylinder knock retard exists; read). The state FFF8A79C (set once per combustion event by 0x0E2F94 from that event's knock results FFF8A7AD / FFF8A7B5; FFF8A7C1 is the knock-window-length flag (1 = extended window), used there only to reload per-cylinder hold counters FFF84920...FFF84930 from cal 0x27014 when it changes, purpose inferred) picks the action: states 0x0E, 0x0D, 7 and 6 subtract a step (floor = minus FBKC Maximum Retard); states 0x0C, 2, 0 (outside the rpm window) and the other non-knock states (0x0A outside the window, 0x0B) add the recovery step 0x1C271; 0x10 (inside the rpm window, no knock, fewer than cal 0x1C288 = 100 events since the last knock) holds the correction unchanged; 0x0F (inside the window, no knock, >= 100 events) adds 0x1C270, 8/9 add 0x1C272 (capped at 0); 5 = FFF8A79B x 0x1C26E / 128; 3 and 4 load the fixed values 0x1C26F / 0x1C278; 1 = 0. States (0x0E2F94, read, in priority order): 1 = knock control off (cal 0x56EE7 bit 7); 2 = FFF886AB bit 5 or load FFF8ADE4 <= cal 0x1C27E (0); 3 / 4 = FFF88E29 bit 3 / FFF88E2A bit 6 (fixed -14 counts = -4.9 degrees, inferred knock-sensor fault default); 5 = engine speed above FBKC Window RPM Maximum (hold); inside the rpm window: 6 / 0x0D = knock A with / without FFF8AA85 bit 0, 7 / 0x0E = knock B (FFF8A7B5, intensity > Knock Threshold, the active one); 0x0F = no knock and FFF8B130 (events since the last knock, 0x0E7C7C) >= cal 0x1C288 (100), 0x10 = no knock, fewer events; 8 / 9 hold; 0x0A / 0x0B / 0x0C other conditions (0x0B: A/F FFF88AF6 above a lambda threshold). Added per pass (toward 0) in states 0x0C and 2, in state 0 (rpm outside the FBKC window, e.g. below FBKC Window RPM Minimum) and in 0x0A (outside the window) / 0x0B; NOT in state 0x10: inside the window with no knock the correction is held until 100 knock-free events, after which FBKC Recovery Step (State 0x0F) applies. p16 (read): the FBKC logic 0x0E2F94 (0x0E402C <- 0x07D0E0 <- 0x1E1CBC) is crank-synchronous: one pass per combustion event (180 deg CA, dispatched at tooth position 70 via the ATU-J0 software interrupt 0x0A7390), not per time. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: FLKC Range Boundary Load 2
table.description:
One of the four load boundaries that split fine learning knock correction (FLKC) into load ranges; each learning cell covers one rpm range by one load range. Moving it changes which conditions share a learned correction. Keep them in increasing order.
Details: Fine learning knock correction cells (0x0E1C58, read): the cell FFF8A790 = 5 x rpm range + load range (0...34). Seven rpm ranges are split at the six boundaries 0x1C24A...0x1C254 on FFF8CE9C, five load ranges at the four boundaries 0x1C240...0x1C246 on FFF8ADE4, each with a hysteresis band (0x1C256 rpm, 0x1C248 load). The learned value for the cell is FFF81414[cell] (s16, x 256); 0x0E73CC applies FFF8A7A7 = min(that, KCA Max x (16 - DAM) x 16) / 256, in 0.3516 degree counts; it is not added to the fired timing directly: like KCA it enters the timing request (0x0C13B4 -> FFF8AF22 -> 0x0C39DC / 0x0DD568), so fired base timing = min(Base Timing + comps, request + KCA + FLKC), and in limit states 0x0B/0x0C/0x19/0x1A/0x1B through the spark target FFF8A72A (0x0D9088). A negative learned value therefore retards the spark only where the request side is the lower one; where Base Timing is lower it is hidden until it pulls the request below Base Timing. Feedback knock correction is the only knock term added directly (0x0D9E40). load boundary. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: FBKC Retard Step (Secondary Knock, State 0x0D)
table.description:
Timing pulled per event by feedback knock correction when the secondary knock detector fires.
Details: Feedback knock correction (0x0E2BE4, read): FFF8A79A is an s8 integrator kept at or below 0 and added directly to the fired timing (x 0.3516 degrees, 0x0D9E40): it is the only knock term of that sum, and FFF8A79A is one value for the whole engine, so a knock event on any cylinder retards all four (the fired timing FFF8A744 is recomputed per event for the next cylinder, but no per-cylinder knock retard exists; read). The state FFF8A79C (set once per combustion event by 0x0E2F94 from that event's knock results FFF8A7AD / FFF8A7B5; FFF8A7C1 is the knock-window-length flag (1 = extended window), used there only to reload per-cylinder hold counters FFF84920...FFF84930 from cal 0x27014 when it changes, purpose inferred) picks the action: states 0x0E, 0x0D, 7 and 6 subtract a step (floor = minus FBKC Maximum Retard); states 0x0C, 2, 0 (outside the rpm window) and the other non-knock states (0x0A outside the window, 0x0B) add the recovery step 0x1C271; 0x10 (inside the rpm window, no knock, fewer than cal 0x1C288 = 100 events since the last knock) holds the correction unchanged; 0x0F (inside the window, no knock, >= 100 events) adds 0x1C270, 8/9 add 0x1C272 (capped at 0); 5 = FFF8A79B x 0x1C26E / 128; 3 and 4 load the fixed values 0x1C26F / 0x1C278; 1 = 0. States (0x0E2F94, read, in priority order): 1 = knock control off (cal 0x56EE7 bit 7); 2 = FFF886AB bit 5 or load FFF8ADE4 <= cal 0x1C27E (0); 3 / 4 = FFF88E29 bit 3 / FFF88E2A bit 6 (fixed -14 counts = -4.9 degrees, inferred knock-sensor fault default); 5 = engine speed above FBKC Window RPM Maximum (hold); inside the rpm window: 6 / 0x0D = knock A with / without FFF8AA85 bit 0, 7 / 0x0E = knock B (FFF8A7B5, intensity > Knock Threshold, the active one); 0x0F = no knock and FFF8B130 (events since the last knock, 0x0E7C7C) >= cal 0x1C288 (100), 0x10 = no knock, fewer events; 8 / 9 hold; 0x0A / 0x0B / 0x0C other conditions (0x0B: A/F FFF88AF6 above a lambda threshold). Subtracted per pass in state 0x0D. p16 (read): the FBKC logic 0x0E2F94 (0x0E402C <- 0x07D0E0 <- 0x1E1CBC) is crank-synchronous: one pass per combustion event (180 deg CA, dispatched at tooth position 70 via the ATU-J0 software interrupt 0x0A7390), not per time. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Secondary Knock Threshold (Event 1)
table.description:
Second knock detector level by rpm for event slot 1; a signal above it triggers the secondary knock retard steps. Unit: sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background (3.0 = all at background).
Details: Knock decision (0x0E8654 / 0x0E80B4, read): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4) the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot] (output of the signal processing 0x0E51E4) is compared with two thresholds. Knock B, FFF8A7B5 = intensity > Knock Threshold (this family, FFF8C1CC[slot] by 0x0E77E0) or FFF8CDC4[slot] >= cal 0x1BD92 (65535, off). Knock A, FFF8A7AD = intensity > Secondary Knock Threshold (FFF8C1D4[slot] by 0x0E78E4). Each event also sets bits of FFF8A79D (0x10/0x20/0x30/0x40 by slot). Slot vs cylinder number not mapped. 0x0E78E4 looks this 16-point curve up by FFF8CDC2 with the implicit-axis routine 0x7304 (0...240 in steps of 16 = 500...8,000 rpm, read). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Knock Window Start Minimum
table.description:
Lower limit on Knock Window Start.
Details: Knock window (0x0E2090 / 0x0E20E0, read): window start FFF8B118 = clamp(Knock Window Start(rpm), 0x1C210...0x1C212); nominal length FFF8B11C = Knock Window Length(rpm). The length used, FFF8B11A, is the nominal length plus Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 is at or below Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold (with hysteresis; MOVRT at 0x0E216E) and the extended window end (0x0E20E0 computes it from nominal + extension with the same formula 0x0E7CB0 uses for the window end FFF8A7AB) ends before the per-event angle FFF8C0E8 (built by 0x0E39C0 from FFF88860/FFF81478, inferred to be the next spark); if either fails the nominal length is used. Either way the length used is clamped to Knock Window Length Minimum...Maximum (0x1C1EC...0x1C1EE; 0x0E211E-0x0E2130 for the extended length, 0x0E21C0-0x0E21E8 for the nominal one, read). FFF8A7C1 / FFF8A7C2...C5 = 1 while the extended length is used (read, 0x0E20E0 at 0x0E21AA-0x0E21EC; corrected 2026-10-30). 0x0E7C00 / 0x0E7C24 scale start and length by FFF8CD46 into FFF8B12A / FFF8B12C for the window timer (1E5202, read). The rpm axis is FFF8CDC2 (rpm = x x 31.25 + 500, read). Degrees are crank degrees after the firing cylinder's TDC (reference inferred). Lower clamp on Knock Window Start. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 1, Channel 2)
table.description:
Knock signal processing for event slot 1, channel 2 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock. Larger = that event less likely to count as knock. Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.

table.description:
Base ignition timing map for the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration) with the TGVs closed. It is only an upper limit: the ECU fires the lower of this map and Closed-Pedal Timing Target (plus its corrections).
Details: When used: Used while the accelerator is fully released (FFF8A774 bit 0: pedal-zero flag FFF88C64 bit 5 in engine state 2/3, vehicle speed FFF99835 at or below cal 0x2FDB2 = 200 km/h (inferred); 0x0E127C / 0x09FF9A, read), TGVs closed; enabled by cal 0x1071E bit 0, set in all four images. Base ignition timing. 0x0C2C08 uses this 16x16 table when cal 0x1071E bit 0 and FFF8A774 bit 0 are both set, and F2 set (F2 = FFF8A881 bit 4). The result is rate-limited (cals 0x1058C / 0x1058E) and the IAT compensation FFF8A782 and Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation FFF8A788 are added (0x0C2C08) to give base timing FFF8A645, which is only the upper limit of the fired timing: with the pedal released 0x0DD568 sets FFF8A76A = FFF8A645 - Torque Reduction Spark Retard(FFF8AF22 >> 7), where FFF8AF22 (0x0C13B4) is the efficiency of the closed-pedal timing request (Closed-Pedal Timing Target + FFF8A788 + FFF8A782 + Post-Start Closed-Pedal Timing Advance, 0x0E0A30) plus KCA + FLKC, so in effect FFF8A76A = min(FFF8A645, that request + KCA + FLKC) (read; min() form computed from the inverse tables). FFF8A76A then goes through 0x0DD760, 0x0DA600 and 0x0D9E40 to FFF8A744. The F2 selector is FFF8A881 bit 4, set by the TGV module 0x10CAE0 (0x10DEFC) - set = TGVs closed (see below). TGV polarity (read): 0x0D952C blends its Closed and Open ignition sets as Closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + Open x FFF8B3E8, so FFF8B3E8 is the TGV open fraction; 0x10C948 drives it toward 0 while FFF8A881 bit 4 is set, so that bit set = TGVs closed. LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05A034 by the code that reads it (read). LF9D000d: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0086B4. Confidence: inferred.

table.description:
AT/CVT warm-up fallback copy of Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1).
Details: When used: FFF8A7E2 bit 0 clear, FFF899D7 bit 0 set. 0x108BAC (catalyst-heating module, read) writes FFF8A854, which 0x0C3200 selects as the spark target FFF8A647 in fuel mode FFF8A852 = 2 (combustion mode FFF8A85C 1 or 3, 0x108B08). A647 is the spark the torque model compensates for (0x0C2514, 0x0C1EA8) and the reference of the cold-start retard monitors (0x1CB70C, 0x132568: A72A - A854) (read); the fired spark in this mode follows FFF8A74C/FFF8A76B (0x0DA428), not A854 (read). In combustion mode 1 (A85C < 2), at <= 4000 rpm (cal 0x1CBD8), with the pedal released (FFF886AB bit 5) and speed below cal 0x2A0C1 (2 km/h): A854 = Base(rpm FFF8CD5C, coolant) + Torque Adder(FFF8A85E, coolant) + Run-Time Adder(passes since the engine state became running, coolant) + Re-Entry Adder(passes since mode 1 was re-entered from normal mode 4, coolant), saturated to a byte; the set is chosen by FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (set = the manual tables, clear = the "AT/CVT" tables; always set on the manual coding, Phase 14) and FFF899D7 bit 0 (set = the "Warm-Up Fallback" tables): a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch set by 0x081EFC only when cal 0x59134 bit 0 is set. Otherwise in mode 1 A854 = 05D0BC x 05D0A8 / 256 + FFF8A789 - 32; in mode 3 A854 = A72A (normal target) (read). with cal 0x2996C bit 6 set A854 is forced to cal 0x2A0C0. Units: A854 is compared with A72A and final timing in 0.5 degree units (inferred). LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05D044 by the code that reads it (read). LF9D000d: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 00C0A0. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Boost IAT Compensation
table.description:

Details: 0x108778: FFF8B3B2 = 2 x Target Boost Baro Compensation x this x FFF8A84B / 128 (32768 = x1), the factor on the absolute boost target and Boost Limit (read). Implicit 16-point u8 table (boot lookup 0x71E0, axis 0..240 step 16) on FFF88663 = (IAT_c50 x 410 - 3972) / 256 from 0x06AF58, where IAT_c50 = FFF88662 = intake air temperature + 50 degC (the OBD IAT source, read); axis = -40.3 + 9.99 x n degC, shown in degF. 128 = x1.0. Confidence: inferred.

Rev Limit Reset RPM
table.description:
End of the rev-limit state: the throttle cap stays until rpm falls to this and boost is below Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP, while fuel already returns at Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM. Keep it about 100 rpm below Rev Limit RPM.
Details: When used: always. Release rpm of the rev latch (part 1): once Rev Limit RPM is exceeded, state 0x0B (and its throttle cap) stays until rpm <= this and MAP < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. The fuel cut itself ends at Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM. Keep it below Rev Limit RPM. Rev limiter and limit-state cuts (LF75404S; read unless marked). The rev limiter is a fuel cut. (1) Limit state, 0x0BE140 (10 ms torque module 0x0BE694): the rev latch FFF8416A sets when rpm FFF8CD54 > Rev Limit RPM (the comparator FFF84169 then uses Rev Limit Reset RPM) and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Reset RPM and MAP FFF88FF4 < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. The overboost latch FFF84167 sets when MAP >= Overboost Limit (compensated, FFF8A851) + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) and releases below that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). Either latch gives limit state FFF8A639 = 0x0B. Priority: not running = 1, FFF8A640 bit 0 = 0x19, latch FFF8416C = 0x1B (cals 0x22FB2-0x22FBC, not decoded), then 0x0B, then the vehicle-speed latch = 0x0C (see Vehicle Speed Limit). (2) Full-cut latch, 0x0BAE98: FFF840C4 sets when rpm >= Rev Limit Full Cut RPM and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM and MAP < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. In state 0x0B the final torque cap FFF8AE54 (0x0B9DC8) is limited to FFF8AE8A: zero indicated torque (32000 - losses FFF8AF62) while this latch or the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) is set, otherwise FFF8AF3A = the current air torque minus losses, i.e. no reduction. (3) Fuel: 0x0C4BA0 turns the cap into the torque ratio FFF8A64F; in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C and 0x18-0x1B, 0x0C1AC8 turns the ratio into the number of cylinders to cut FFF8A643 (Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio thresholds; a zero cap gives 4). Once per combustion event (crank-synchronous list 0x07D0E0) 0x0C4B84 makes a cut decision FFF8A648 from the count and the last three decisions (4 = every event, 3 = three in four, 2 = every second, 1 = one in four; the pattern is in code, not a cal). 0x0C88C8 (list 0x07D1C2) latches it into the cut flag of the cylinder being scheduled (FFF8A6F5-FFF8A6F8). For a flagged cylinder the fuel time is 0 (0x0D1D7C/0x0D1FB8) and both start angles are 0x1FE (0x0CB394/0x0CB604), which the injector driver 0x1DCA04 treats as no pulse. So the cut is a true injector cut, all four cylinders, every event. (4) Spark is neither cut nor retarded: the coil scheduler 0x1DB804 only checks FFF8C6F4 (set at the first injection after sync, cleared only on stop), and with Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut set 0x0DD568 uses the normal spark target FFF8A72A in state 0x0B instead of Torque Reduction Spark Retard. (5) Throttle: with Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable set 0x0BDA84 caps the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C in state 0x0B by 0x0BAFA8: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Stage 1) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM (held while > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold)) or MAP FFF8AF70 > Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 MAP (held while > Stage 1 Reset MAP); else (Stage 2) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) (held while > Rev Limit RPM) or MAP > Stage 1 Reset MAP (held while > Stage 2 Hold MAP); else (Base). The torque monitor (0x186F0C) repeats this with the same data. A hard cut; stage 2 is never selected because its thresholds equal stage 1's. To move the limit, set Rev Limit RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 rpm lower. Setting the Full Cut pair above Rev Limit RPM gives a throttle-only soft stage between them (inferred). The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP
table.description:
The rev-limit fuel cut and state cannot end while manifold pressure is at or above this, even below their reset rpm. Raise it if you want the cut to release on rpm alone at high boost.
Details: When used: always. Neither the rev latch (part 1) nor the full-cut latch (part 2) releases while MAP FFF88FF4 is at or above this, even below its reset rpm, so at high boost the fuel cut lasts until the closed throttle has pulled the manifold below it. At 65535 the release depends on rpm only (read: the test is MAP < this). Rev limiter and limit-state cuts (LF75404S; read unless marked). The rev limiter is a fuel cut. (1) Limit state, 0x0BE140 (10 ms torque module 0x0BE694): the rev latch FFF8416A sets when rpm FFF8CD54 > Rev Limit RPM (the comparator FFF84169 then uses Rev Limit Reset RPM) and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Reset RPM and MAP FFF88FF4 < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. The overboost latch FFF84167 sets when MAP >= Overboost Limit (compensated, FFF8A851) + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) and releases below that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). Either latch gives limit state FFF8A639 = 0x0B. Priority: not running = 1, FFF8A640 bit 0 = 0x19, latch FFF8416C = 0x1B (cals 0x22FB2-0x22FBC, not decoded), then 0x0B, then the vehicle-speed latch = 0x0C (see Vehicle Speed Limit). (2) Full-cut latch, 0x0BAE98: FFF840C4 sets when rpm >= Rev Limit Full Cut RPM and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM and MAP < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. In state 0x0B the final torque cap FFF8AE54 (0x0B9DC8) is limited to FFF8AE8A: zero indicated torque (32000 - losses FFF8AF62) while this latch or the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) is set, otherwise FFF8AF3A = the current air torque minus losses, i.e. no reduction. (3) Fuel: 0x0C4BA0 turns the cap into the torque ratio FFF8A64F; in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C and 0x18-0x1B, 0x0C1AC8 turns the ratio into the number of cylinders to cut FFF8A643 (Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio thresholds; a zero cap gives 4). Once per combustion event (crank-synchronous list 0x07D0E0) 0x0C4B84 makes a cut decision FFF8A648 from the count and the last three decisions (4 = every event, 3 = three in four, 2 = every second, 1 = one in four; the pattern is in code, not a cal). 0x0C88C8 (list 0x07D1C2) latches it into the cut flag of the cylinder being scheduled (FFF8A6F5-FFF8A6F8). For a flagged cylinder the fuel time is 0 (0x0D1D7C/0x0D1FB8) and both start angles are 0x1FE (0x0CB394/0x0CB604), which the injector driver 0x1DCA04 treats as no pulse. So the cut is a true injector cut, all four cylinders, every event. (4) Spark is neither cut nor retarded: the coil scheduler 0x1DB804 only checks FFF8C6F4 (set at the first injection after sync, cleared only on stop), and with Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut set 0x0DD568 uses the normal spark target FFF8A72A in state 0x0B instead of Torque Reduction Spark Retard. The torque monitor (0x186F0C) repeats this with the same data. A hard cut; stage 2 is never selected because its thresholds equal stage 1's. To move the limit, set Rev Limit RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 rpm lower. Setting the Full Cut pair above Rev Limit RPM gives a throttle-only soft stage between them (inferred). The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. Confidence: inferred.
